### Printed p. 146

*Running head: [146 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये । (*pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |*)
आत्मानं वस्को अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥ (*ātmānaṃ vasko abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutaṃ ‖*)
(म. सं १०-९२-१३) (*(ma. saṃ 10-92-13)*)

in this ṛk Pūṣan and then Apāṃ Napāt are prayed to along with the Viśve Devāḥ. In the second ṛk of this sūkta ((ऋ. सं. १०-९२-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-92-2)*)) Agni is praised as the increaser of the sacrifice. In the thirteenth ṛk of the seventy-fifth sūkta of the seventh Maṇḍala the deities Aja Ekapād, Ahirbudhnya, Samudra, Apāṃ Napāt and Pṛśni are invoked together; Indra and Agni in the first ṛk, and Agni alone in the fourth ṛk. In the fourteenth ṛk of the fifty-second sūkta of the sixth Maṇḍala other deities are invoked with Apāṃ Napāt; in the sixth and twelfth ṛks Agni is prayed to. Similarly in the thirty-first sūkta of the second Maṇḍala and the fiftieth sūkta of the sixth Maṇḍala Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are named separately. In none of these ṛks can it be said that Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are one deity by identity.

The thirty-fifth sūkta of the second Maṇḍala is addressed to Apāṃ Napāt alone. Only in the fifteenth ṛk is Agni addressed; in the other ṛks, to the end, the name of Agni does not occur at all. Even so, if they can be interpreted as relating to Agni, only the eleventh and twelfth ṛks can; but the description there too does not apply to Agni himself. Taking these examples, the scholar Bloomfield has given his opinion in this way:

While Agni became more and more conpsicions [sic], Apan Napat seems to have waned in popnlarity [sic], nntil [sic] he was so far forgotten that a confusion arose concerning the two uses of the expression अपांनशात् (*apāṃnaśāt*) [?] " the son of the waters" was swallowed np [sic] in Agni, a son of the waters as he was occasionally (twice in the Rik) called, since he too. because of his original lightning nature, was supposed to have been born of the rain-clouds. To the same source is te be traced the myth of his hiding in the waters, for this myth probably had no connection originally with Apan Napat, beyond the mere fact that both he and Agni were forms of lightning which, appearing when the thunderstorm was at its hight [sic] seemed to disappear in the clouds from which they came. The conclusion seems to be warranted, therefore, that Agni and Apan Napat were once distinct Gods-Gods, of the lightning, who were, however, associated with each other and were much alike in certain particulars and that this association, and resemblance nlii-mately resulted, possibly at the close of the Vedic Period, in a confusion and union of the two, as a result of which Apan Napat was absorbed by Agni- (Journal of American Oriental Society Vol. XIX (2) p. 144)

*[The page break of the print (p. 146/147) falls inside this English quotation, at "nlii-" / "mately"; the quotation is given unbroken above.]*

### Printed p. 147

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 147 (as supplied, "ಅ. ೨ ಅ. ೫. ವ. ೪").*

मनोजुवः (*manojuvaḥ*) — मन इव वेगयुक्तः (*mana iva vegayuktaḥ*): "swift like the mind". The mind can think of an object however far away in an instant; therefore when indicating great speed the custom of using the comparison "swift as the mind" is found in the Ṛgveda.

इंद्रवायू मनोजुवा विप्रा हवंत ऊतॆये । सहस्राक्षा धियॆस्सती ॥ (*iṃdravāyū manojuvā viprā havaṃta ūtèye | sahasrākṣā dhiyèssatī ‖*)
(ऋ सं. १-२३-३) (*(ṛ saṃ. 1-23-3)*)

in these and similar ṛks the word *manojuva* is used in the sense stated above.

वृषण: (*vṛṣaṇa:*) — वर्षका मेघाः (*varṣakā meghāḥ*): Sāyaṇa's explanation is "the clouds that pour rain".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

आहिः (*āhiḥ*) [as printed with the long ā] (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*)): by आजि श्रिहनिभ्यांह्रस्वश्च (उ सू. ४-५;७७) (*āji śrihanibhyāṃhrasvaśca (u sū. 4-5;77)*) the suffix *iṇ*; shortening of the *ā*; because the suffix is marked *ḍ* the *ṭi* (*an*) of the root is lost; the form is *ahi*. बुध्न्यः (*budhnyaḥ*): बुध्नमहर्तिति बुध्न्यः (*budhnamahartiti budhnyaḥ*) ("he who deserves the atmosphere"): the Vedic suffix *yat* in the sense "deserving"; by the sūtra यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*) loss of *a*; by तित्‌स्वरितम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५) (*titsvaritam (pā. sū. 6-1-185)*) the *svarita* accent occurs. कॆः (*kèḥ*) [as printed, for *kaḥ*] (root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*)): by छंदसि लुज्लज्लिटः (*chaṃdasi lujlajliṭaḥ*) *laṅ* in the sense of the imperative; when *tip* comes, by इतश्च (*itaśca*) loss of *i*; by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *luk* of the thematic suffix; guṇa with *r* of the *ṛ* of the root because of *tip*; by हल्ज्याभ्योदीर्घा—(पा सू. (*haljyābhyodīrghā—(pā sū.*) ६-१-६८) (*6-1-68)*) the loss of *tip*; *visarga* for the *r* because of the pause; by the Vedic rule the augment *aṭ* does not occur; the *nighāta* accent arises. पिप्युषी (*pipyuṣī*) (root ओप्यायी वृद्धौ (*opyāyī vṛddhau*)): when the Vedic *liṭ* comes, by क्वसुश्च (पा. सू. (*kvasuśca (pā. sū.*) ३-२-१०७) (*3-2-107)*) the substitute *kvasu*; by लिड्यजोश्च (पा. सू. ६-१-२९) (*liḍyajośca (pā. sū. 6-1-29)*) the substitute *pī* for the root; doubling and so on of the root because of the suffix; in the feminine, by उगितश्च (*ugitaśca*) *ṅīp*; because of the *bha* designation *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *v* of the suffix, the earlier form; *yaṇ* substitution for the *ī* of the root; by शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. सू, ८-३-६०) (*śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (pā. sū, 8-3-60)*) *ṣ* for the *s* of the suffix; from the first-syllable acute of the suffix the word becomes middle-acute. [The window ends here, in the middle of the Ṛk 5 grammar page.]

### Printed p. 148

*Running head: [148 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186]. The window continues the Ṛk 5 grammar page of Sūkta 186 from p. 147, after the *pipyuṣī* entry.*

वेति (*veti*) (root वी गत्यादिषु (*vī gatyādiṣu*)): *leṭ*, third person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent arises. नपातम् (*napātam*): by नभ्राण् नपात्—(पा सू. ६-३-७५) (*nabhrāṇ napāt—(pā sū. 6-3-75)*) the non-loss of *n* is an irregular form; the accent of the earlier member after *nañ* arises. अपाम् (*apām*): by ऊडिदंपदादि—(पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) (*ūḍidaṃpadādi—(pā. sū. 6-1-171)*) the genitive plural ending is acute. जुनाम (*junāma*) (root जु गतौ (*ju gatau*), "to go"; the sūtra only is named): *kryādi* imperative, first person plural; since the prohibition of *nighāta* arises through यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (*yadvṛttānityam*) the word is middle-acute by the accent of the suffix. वहंति (*vahaṃti*): because of the relative *yat* there is no *nighāta*; by तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) (*tāsyanudāttet—(pā. sū. 6-1-186)*) the *laḥ sārvadhātuka* is unaccented, so the accent of the root remains.

#### Ṛk 6

*[In the supplied text the Saṃhitā and Pada of this ṛk were a picture; the picture was viewed and agrees with the machine text, which has been used.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उ॒त न॑ ईं॒ त्वष्टा गं॒त्वच्छा॒ स्मत्सू॒रिभि॑रभिपि॒त्वे स॒जोषाः॑ ।
> आ वृ॑त्र॒हेंद्र॑श्चर्षणि॒प्रास्तु॒ विष्ट॑मो न॒रां न॑ इ॒ह ग॑म्याः ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । नः । ईं । त्वष्टा । आ । गंतु । अच्छ । स्मत् । सूरिभिः । अभिपित्वे । सजोषाः ।
> आ । वृत्रहा । इंद्रः । चर्षणिप्राः । तुविःतमः।नरां।नः । इह । गम्याः ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> त्वष्टा देवोऽपि नोऽस्मानच्छाभिप्राप्तमीमिदानीमिमं यज्ञं वा गंतु ।
> आगत्य च । स्मत्सहार्थे प्राशस्त्ये ना वर्तते । अत्र प्रशंसायां । प्रशस्तं यथा
> तथाभिपित्वेऽभिगंतव्ये यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः सजोषाः
> समानप्रीतिर्भवश्विति शेषः । तथा वृत्रहा वृत्रघाती चर्षणिप्राः । चर्षणयो
> मनुष्या यजमानाः । कामैस्तेषां पूरकस्तु विष्टमो बहुतमो महत्तम इहा-
> स्मिन्कर्मणि नरां नृणां नोऽस्माकमुक्तगुणोपेतः सन्ना गम्याः । आगच्छतु ॥

*Gist:* May Tvaṣṭṛ come to our sacrifice, in accord with the priests; and may Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, who fills the wishes of men, come to us.

### Printed p. 149

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 149 (as supplied, "೨. ೨. ಅ. ೫. ವ. ೪.").*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

उत—मत्तु (*uta—mattu*). त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ. नः अभि (*naḥ abhi*) — towards us. ईं (*īṃ*) — to this sacrifice. आ गंतु (*ā gaṃtu*) — may he come; (then) अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*) — at this sacrifice being performed forthwith. सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*) — with his praisers, the priests. सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — being of equal affection. स्मत् (*smat*) — may he make the sacrifice excellent. चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*) — fulfiller of men's wishes. तुविष्टमः (*tuviṣṭamaḥ*) — of the greatest might. वृताहा [?] (*vṛtāhā [?]*) — the Vṛtra-slayer. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*) — Indra. इह (*iha*) — in this rite. नरां नः (*narāṃ naḥ*) — towards us men. आ गम्याः (*ā gamyāḥ*) — may he come.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ come towards us to this sacrifice. At this sacrifice being performed now, being of equal affection with his praisers the priests, may he make the sacrifice excellent; and may Indra, the fulfiller and protector of men's wishes, of the greatest might and the slayer of Vṛtra, come in this rite towards us men.

**Printed English translation**

Or may Twashtri come to this sacrifice, equally well pleased with those who praise (him) at the excellent (rite) at which he is present : may the most potent Indra the protector of man, the destroyer of Vritra, come to the (solemnity) of our leadrs.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads विषयगळु: (*viṣayagaḷu:*); standard label inserted.]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra are praised. We have already spoken of Tvaṣṭṛ, famous as the craftsman of the gods.

त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — Yāska in his Nirukta has stated the derivation of this word as follows:

त्वष्टा त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वास्याद्वीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा (*tvaṣṭā tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervāsyādvīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā*)
स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः। माध्यमिकस्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । (*syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ| mādhyamikasvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ |*)
अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*)
(सि. ८-१४) (*(si. 8-14)*)

that is, the Nirukta-authors say that *tvaṣṭā* is "one who pervades swiftly"; or "one who shines", or "one who does works (craftsman's works)"; some say he is *mādhyamika*, that is, one who is between heaven and earth; Śākapūṇi says he is Agni (printed "ಸಿ." for "ನಿ.").

### Printed p. 150

*Running head: [150 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24. Sū. 186] (the print has "ಆ." for the second abbreviation, as supplied).*

Some also say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods; for in the ṛk that Yāska gave as an example:

यॆ इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । (*yè ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā |*)
तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान्देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् । (*tamadya hotariṣito yajīyāndevaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |*)
(म. सं. १०-११०-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-110-9)*)

Tvaṣṭṛ is said to be the maker of heaven and earth and the cause of the form, beauty, prosperity, growth and so on suited to the beings in all the worlds. Besides, Śruti (Yajurveda) sentences such as त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानाग्ं रूपकृत् (*tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāgṃ rūpakṛt*) ((तै. सं. ६-१-८-५) (*(tai. saṃ. 6-1-8-5)*)), त्वष्टा रूपाणामधिपतिः (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāmadhipatiḥ*) ((तै सं. ३-३) (*(tai saṃ. 3-3)*)) and त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) affirm Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things. And:

मध्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुं । (*madhyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjannapi kratuṃ |*)
(मु. वं. १०-४८-३) (*(mu. vaṃ. 10-48-3)*)

Indra says that Tvaṣṭṛ made for him a thunderbolt of steel (printed "ಮು. ವಂ." for the reference "ಋ. ಸಂ."); many mantras of the Ṛgveda say that he made for the gods the sacrificial materials they need and many other things. Tvaṣṭṛ is a very skilful workman. He has made various things that show his skill. In fact there are no workmen as skilful as he. Therefore:

त्वष्टा यद्वज्रं सुकृतं हिरण्ययं सहस्रभृष्टिं स्वपा अवर्तयत् । (*tvaṣṭā yadvajraṃ sukṛtaṃ hiraṇyayaṃ sahasrabhṛṣṭiṃ svapā avartayat |*)
धत्त इंद्रो नर्यपांसि कर्तवेऽहन् वृत्रं निरपामौज्ज दर्णवं ॥ (*dhatta iṃdro naryapāṃsi kartave 'han vṛtraṃ nirapāmaujja darṇavaṃ ‖*)
(म. प. १-८५-९) (*(ma. pa. 1-85-9)*)

in this ṛk it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ made a very excellent thunderbolt, golden-bright, with a thousand edges, and gave it to Indra, and by it Indra killed Vṛtra.

त्वष्टा माया वेदपसामपस्तमो बिभ्रत्पात्रा देवपानानि शंतमा । (*tvaṣṭā māyā vedapasāmapastamo bibhratpātrā devapānāni śaṃtamā |*)
शिशीते नूनं परशुं स्वायसं येन वृश्चादेतशो ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥ (*śiśīte nūnaṃ paraśuṃ svāyasaṃ yena vṛścādetaśo brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖*)
(पु. सं. १०-५३-९) (*(pu. saṃ. 10-53-9)*)

in this ṛk, since Tvaṣṭṛ is a very intelligent workman, it is said that he not only made drinking vessels for the gods to drink Soma, but also sharpened the steel axe of Brahmaṇaspati... [the window ends mid-sentence: "ಮಾಡಿ"].

### Printed p. 151

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 151 (as supplied, "ಅ, ೨. ಅ. ೫. ವ. ೫"; the Varga number changes here from 4 to 5). The window continues the Tvaṣṭṛ note in the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 of Sūkta 186 from p. 150, in mid-sentence.*

... [he sharpened the steel axe of Brahmaṇaspati and] gave it: so there is a description. Since there is much to say about Tvaṣṭṛ, it will be explained at length later.

सूरिभिः-सूरिस्तव स्तोता (*sūribhiḥ-sūristava stotā*) — "your praiser": the meaning is "praiser". Since it is read among the thirteen names of the praiser, such as *rebhaḥ*, *jaritā* and *kāruḥ* ((नि. ३-१९) (*(ni. 3-19)*)), *sūrayaḥ* means praisers, devotees who recite praises. The word *sūri* is also used in many places where the sense "learned, discerning, wise" is meant. When used of the ṛṣis who have the supernatural power of vision, bodily and mental, by which they grasp the true nature of the gods and the secret principles of the universe, this epithet gives a special sense.

तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः । दिवीव चॆक्षुराततं ॥ (*tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ | divīva cèkṣurātataṃ ‖*)
(म. सं. १-२२-२०) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-22-20)*)

in such contexts it indicates not merely those who praise but the extraordinary power of vision of the ṛṣis. And it is used not only of ṛṣis but also as an epithet of Indra and the other gods.

महिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥ (*mahiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai ‖*)
(म. सं. १-६३-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-63-3)*)

in these and similar ṛks the words विपश्चितमिंद्रं (*vipaścitamiṃdraṃ*) indicate the wisdom of Indra and other gods. Besides, the word *sūri* is used when the sense "lord, inciter, leader on the good path" is indicated. For example:

जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः । (*jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१२२-८) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-122-8)*)
असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिंद्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता । (*asadyathā jaritra uta sūririṃdro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā |*)
(ऋ सं. ६-२३-१०) (*(ṛ saṃ. 6-23-10)*)
मुह्यंत्वन्ये अभिटो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥ (*muhyaṃtvanye abhiṭo janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-८१-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-81-6)*)

in these and similar contexts this epithet describes the qualities of the gods who are lords and leaders on the good path, Indra and the rest.

आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः । (*ādasya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathādīṣate vayaḥ |*)
(ऋ. सुं. १-१४१-८) (*(ṛ. suṃ. 1-141-8)*)

(printed "ಋ. ಸುಂ." for "ಋ. ಸಂ.") in a few such places only the sense "path" arises.

### Printed p. 152

*Running head: [152 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) (root त्वक्षू तनूकरणे (*tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe*)): the suffix *tṛn* in the agent sense; because it is marked *n* the first syllable is acute; nominative singular form. गंतु (*gaṃtu*) (root गम्‌ल्य गत् (*gamlya gat*)): imperative, third person singular, with *tu*; by एरुः (*eruḥ*) *u*; by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *luk* of the thematic suffix; anusvāra of the *m* of the root, and the homorganic nasal; the verb-*nighāta* accent. अच्छ (*accha*): by निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१-३६) (*nipātasya ca (pā. sū. 6-3-1-36)*) [as printed] lengthening in the Saṃhitā. सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) (root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*)): the Uṇādi suffix *asun*; "he whose joy is the same"; by the sūtra समानस्य छंदसि (*samānasya chaṃdasi*) the substitute *sa* for *samāna*; nominative singular form. वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*)): by ब्रह्मभ्रूण—(पा. सू. ३-२-८७) (*brahmabhrūṇa—(pā. sū. 3-2-87)*) *kvip* when *vṛtra* is the upapada; "who has slain Vṛtra"; in the compound the accent of the *kṛt* later member. चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*) (root प्रा, पूरणे (*prā, pūraṇe*)): by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) *kvip*; it becomes a word ending in *a*; the accent of the later member. नराम् (*narām*) (root नृ नये (*nṛ naye*)): *kvip*; genitive plural; by सावेकाचस्तृ- (*sāvekācastṛ-*) तीयादिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) (*tīyādiḥ (pā. sū. 6-1-168)*) the ending is acute. गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) (root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*)): optative; by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) the second-person singular ending in place of the third-person singular; by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *luk* of the thematic suffix; the augment *yāsuṭ* for *sip*; *ruttva* and visarga for the *s*; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमिां॒ [?] गिरो॒ जन॑यो॒ न पत्निः॑ सुर॒भिष्ट॑मं न॒रां न॑संत ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> उतापि चेमेनं तरुणं नित्ययुवानमिंद्रं मतयोऽस्मदुद्धयोऽश्वयोगा
> अश्वसमानप्राप्तयो रिहंति । आस्वादयंति । स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः गावो
> दोग्यो धेनवः शिशुं न शिशुमिव वत्समिव तं यथा लिहंति तद्वत् । तदेवाह ।
> तमीं तमेवैनं नरां नराणां यजमानानां सुरभिष्टममतिशयेन सुरभिं जनयः
> फलस्योत्पादयित्र्यो गिरः स्तुतयो नसंत । व्याप्नुवंति । नसतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । जनयो नोत्पादयित्र्यः पत्निः पत्न्यः पतिमिव ॥

*Gist:* Our minds, yoked like horses, lick and praise the ever-young Indra as cows lick their calves; our praises encompass him as wives their husbands.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

उत—मत्तु (*uta—mattu*). ईं तरुणं (*īṃ taruṇaṃ*) — this ever-youthful Indra. अश्वयोगाः (*aśvayogāḥ*) — yoked together like horses. नः मतयः (*naḥ matayaḥ*) — our minds. गावः (*gāvaḥ*) — milch cows. शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*) — as they lick their calves. रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) — lick (they praise Indra lovingly). तं ईं (*taṃ īṃ*) — that very Indra. नरां (*narāṃ*) — of men, the sacrificers. सुरभिष्टमं (*surabhiṣṭamaṃ*) — the most fragrant fruit. जनयः (*janayaḥ*) — producing; (capable of producing sons). गिरः (*giraḥ*) — words of praise. पत्निः न (*patniḥ na*) — as wives join their husbands. नसंत—प्यापिसुत्तवॆ [?] (*nasaṃta—pyāpisuttavè [?]*) — they pervade ("ಪ್ಯಾಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ" for *vyāpisuttave*, as supplied).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Our minds, yoked together like horses, lovingly encompass and praise the ever-young Indra, as milch cows lick their calves; and the praises of the men, producing the most fragrant fruit, encompass the same Indra, as wives capable of bearing sons join their husbands.

**Printed English translation**

For our minds, yoked together like horses, tend to the ever youthful Indra, as cows to their calves : and the praises of men, (addressed) to him, are generating most fragrant (fruit), as wives bear (children to their hus-bands).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अश्वयोगा (*aśvayogā*) — as horses are yoked together to a chariot, so may our minds dwell with attachment on Indra, or praise him: this is the main idea [the window ends here, in the middle of the note].

### Printed p. 154

*Running head: [154 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186]. The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 7 of Sūkta 186 from p. 153, after the beginning of the *aśvayogā* note.*

गावः शिशुं न रिहंति (*gāvaḥ śiśuṃ na rihaṃti*) — "as milch cows lovingly lick their calves, so may our minds serve Indra": thus the comparison is stated.

तरुणं—नित्ययुवानमिंद्रं (*taruṇaṃ—nityayuvānamiṃdraṃ*) — Indra who is ever like a youth, or ever young. On Indra being young:

पुरां भिंदुर्युवा कविरमितौजा अजायत । (*purāṃ bhiṃduryuvā kaviramitaujā ajāyata |*)
(म. सं. १-११-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-11-4)*)

in these and similar ṛks it is said that Indra is a youth and exceedingly brilliant.

ईं (*īṃ*) — the short words *kam*, *īm*, *it* and *u* are used to fill out a pāda. On this matter Yāska:

अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूर- (*atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūra-*)
णास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति ॥ (*ṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti ‖*)
(३-९) (*(3-9)*)

explains that the words *kam*, *īm*, *it* and *u* are used to fill out a sentence in prose that has no metre (*amitākṣara*), and to fill out a pāda in metrical ṛks or mantras (*mitākṣara*); therefore these words need not have any definite meaning. In this ṛk Indra is praised.

गिरः (*giraḥ*) — "words", that is, words in the form of praise. Yāska, stating the derivation of the word *giraḥ* as स्तुतयः गिरो गृणातेः (*stutayaḥ giro gṛṇāteḥ*) ((नि. १-१०) (*(ni. 1-10)*)), has given the meaning "praises".

जनयः — नोत्पादयित्र्यः (*janayaḥ — notpādayitryaḥ*) — [the supplied text has "ನೋತ್ಪಾದಯಿತ್ರ್ಯಃ" as in the bhāṣya] young women who have not yet borne children but are capable of bearing them. The comparison is given: as such wives join their husbands with desire of the heart, so may our praises join Indra.

### Printed p. 155

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 155 (as supplied, "ವ. ೧ ಅ. ೨. ಆ ೫").*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

अश्वयोगाः (*aśvayogāḥ*) ("those whose yoking is like the yoking of a horse"): by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) the accent of the earlier member. तरु (*taru*) (root प्लवनतरणयोः (*plavanataraṇayoḥ*)): by त्रोरश्चलोपा (उ. सू ४-३३४) (*troraścalopā (u. sū 4-334)*) the suffix *unan*; [the text of the sūtra is broken in the supplied text, and the page break falls here]; by अट् कुप्वाज् (*aṭ kupvāj*) *ṇatva* of the *n*; because the suffix is marked *n* the first syllable is acute. रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) (root लिह आस्वादने (*liha āsvādane*), "to lick"): *adādi*; present, third person plural; by *vyatyaya* the substitute *l* for the *r* of the root [as written]; because it follows a non-verb the *nighāta* accent arises. जनयः (*janayaḥ*) (root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*)): by सर्वधातुभ्य इन् (*sarvadhātubhya in*) the suffix *in*; because it is marked *n* the first syllable is acute. सुरभिष्टमम् (*surabhiṣṭamam*): by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठसौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhasau*) the suffix *tamap*; because it is marked *p* it is unaccented. नसंत (*nasaṃta*) (root णस कौटिल्ये (*ṇasa kauṭilye*)): *bhvādi*; by णोनः (*ṇonaḥ*) *n* for the initial; by छंदसि लुज्- लज् लिटः (पा सू. ३-४-६) (*chaṃdasi luj- laj liṭaḥ (pā sū. 3-4-6)*) *laṅ* in the sense of the present; third person plural; by बहुलं छंद— (*bahulaṃ chaṃda—*) the augment *aṭ* does not occur; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 156

*Running head: [156 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 23. Sū. 186] (the print has "೨೩" for "೨೪", as supplied).*

> यद्वा । अवनयो रक्षका रथा इव स्थिताः । रिशादसः । रिशाः शत्रवः । तेषामत्तारो
> मित्रयुजो देवा न मैत्रीयुक्ता व्यवहर्तार ऋत्विज इव । यद्वा । मैत्रीयुक्ता
> अन्ये देवा यथा गच्छंति तद्वत् ॥

*Gist:* May the Maruts, of great strength, of one mind, with spotted horses, like chariots and devourers of foes, come with Heaven and Earth to our sacrifice like friendly gods.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

उत—मत्तु (*uta—mattu*). वृद्धसेनाः (*vṛddhasenāḥ*) — of great strength. समनसः (*samanasaḥ*) — of one mind. पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*) — having horses of variegated colour. अवनयः रथाः न (*avanayaḥ rathāḥ na*) — like protecting chariots, or possessing chariots. रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) — devourers of enemies. मरुतः स्मत् (*marutaḥ smat*) — the Maruts also. मित्रयुजः (*mitrayujaḥ*) — joined with friends. देवाः न (*devāḥ na*) — like other gods. रोदसी (*rodasī*) — from the side of earth and atmosphere. नः (*naḥ*) — our. ईं (*īṃ*) — to this sacrifice. सदंतु (*sadaṃtu*) — may they come. (रोदसी (*rodasī*) may Heaven and Earth come too.)

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the Maruts, of great strength, of one mind, with variegated horses, possessing protecting chariots and devouring foes, come to this our sacrifice from the side of earth and atmosphere, like the other gods joined with friends. May Heaven and Earth come with them.

**Printed English translation**

Or may the Maruts, being of one mind, come from heaven and earth (to the sacrifice); they who are a mighty host, who have parti-coloured steeds, who are like protecting chariots, and who are devourers of foes, may they come like friendly deities.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk the Maruts and Heaven and Earth are praised.

पृषदश्वासः—पृषद्वर्णाश्वाः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ—pṛṣadvarṇāśvāḥ*) — "having horses of spotted colour": the meaning is those who have the horses called *pṛṣatī* of many kinds of colour. About the vehicles of the various gods Yāska says:

हरी इंद्रस्य । रोहितोऽग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः (*harī iṃdrasya | rohito 'gneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ | ajāḥ*)
पूष्णः । पृषत्यो मरुतां । अरुण्यो गाव उषसः । श्यावाः सवितुः । (*pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣatyo marutāṃ | aruṇyo gāva uṣasaḥ | śyāvāḥ savituḥ |*)
विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोः । (*viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyoḥ |*)
(नि. 9-28) (*(ni. 9-28)*)

(the Nirukta reference is printed "(ನಿ. 9-28)" with a Latin 9, as supplied) from what is said, it is well known that the spotted deer called *pṛṣatī*, of variegated colour, are the vehicle of the Maruts.

(ऋ. सं. १-३७-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-37-2)*)
उपो रथेषु पृषतीरयुग्त्वं प्रष्ठिर्वहति रोहितः । (*upo ratheṣu pṛṣatīrayugtvaṃ praṣṭhirvahati rohitaḥ |*)

प्रयद्रथेषु पृषतीरयुग्त्वं वाजे अद्रिं मरुतो रंहयंतः । (*prayadratheṣu pṛṣatīrayugtvaṃ vāje adriṃ maruto raṃhayaṃtaḥ |*)

(ऋ. सं ८-७-२८) (*(ṛ. saṃ 8-7-28)*)

in these and similar ṛks the yoking of the spotted deer called *pṛṣatī* to the chariot of the Maruts is mentioned.

रिशादसः-रिशाः शत्रवः । तेषामत्तारो मरुतः (*riśādasaḥ-riśāḥ śatravaḥ | teṣāmattāro marutaḥ*) (the supplied text repeats this headword line, the second time with a dash "—") — *riśaḥ* means enemies; those who devour them, that is, those who crush and destroy them, destroyers of enemies: this is the meaning. The word *riśādasaḥ* is used of many gods in the sense "destroyers of enemies".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

वृद्धसेनाः (*vṛddhasenāḥ*) ("those whose army is great"): by बहुव्रीहौप्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhauprakṛtyā*) the accent of the earlier member. समनसः (*samanasaḥ*): by समानस्यछंदस्यमूर्ध (*samānasyachaṃdasyamūrdha*) the substitute *sa* for *samāna*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the accent of the earlier member. सदंतु (*sadaṃtu*) (root षद्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadlya viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*)): by धात्वादेः षः सः (पा. सू. ६- (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (pā. sū. 6-*) १-६४) (*1-64)*) *s* for the initial; imperative, third person plural; the substitute *anta* for *jhi*; by एरुः (*eruḥ*) *u*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* *luk* of the thematic suffix; therefore the substitute *sīda* for the root does not occur; the verb-*nighāta* accent. पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*): by अज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू ७-१-५०) (*ajjaserasuk (pā. sū 7-1-50)*) the augment *āsuk*. अवनयः (*avanayaḥ*) (root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*)): by अर्तिसृधृधम्य—(उ. सू. २-२५४) (*artisṛdhṛdhamya—(u. sū. 2-254)*) the suffix *asi*; the first syllable of the suffix is acute. रथा: (*rathā:*) — when *matup* comes in the sense "having that", by the Vedic rule there is *luk* of *matup*. रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) ("they eat the *riśa*"; root अद . भक्षणे (*ada . bhakṣaṇe*)): by सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् (उ. सू ४-६२८) (*sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (u. sū 4-628)*) the suffix *asun*; by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the first syllable is acute; in the compound the accent of the *kṛt* later member.

> एषां मरुतां महिना महिमा वृष्टिलक्षणो यद्यस्माद्य चिकित्से प्रज्ञायते ।

> यथा सर्वमावृणोति तथा मरुत्सेना वृष्टा सर्वमूषरं करोति ! यद्वा । मरु-
> न्महिमा वृष्टिर्भवति । तदा सस्यादिसमृद्धौ सत्यां प्रयोगं कुर्वंति । यदा यजंति

*Gist:* The Maruts' rain-greatness is known; their rain-bearing armies fill the whole world, even the barren soil, as light fills a fine day; so the priests perform their rites with fine praises.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

आथ—अनंतर (*ātha—anaṃtara*). सुदिने-मेघावरणदिंद रहितवाद सुदिनगळल्लि (*sudine-meghāvaraṇadiṃda rahitavāda sudinagaḷalli*) — on fine days free of cloud cover. शरुः न (*śaruḥ na*) — as light spreads everywhere. यत् (*yat*) — because. एषां (*eṣāṃ*) — of these Maruts. सेनाः (*senāḥ*) — the rain-producing forces (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 159

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 159 (as supplied, "ಅ ೫").*

इरिणं (*iriṇaṃ*) — as one waters barren land. विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*) — the whole world. आ पुषायंत (*ā puṣāyaṃta*) — they fill with water; (and) यत् (*yat*) — because एषां (*eṣāṃ*) — of these Maruts महिना (*mahinā*) — the greatness in the form of rain प्र चिकित्से (*pra cikitse*) — is well known. [Or: because by the greatness of these Maruts the rites to be performed are well known.] ते (*te*) — the knowing sacrificers सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) — with fine praises प्रयुजां (*prayujāṃ*) — the several rites प्र युंजते (*pra yuṃjate*) — perform.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As light spreads everywhere on fine days free of cloud cover, the rain-producing forces of the Maruts fill the whole world with water, wetting even barren soil; and thereby their rain-greatness is well known. For this reason the sacrificers, knowing their duties well, perform the several prescribed rites with fine praises.

**Printed English translation**

For, verily, their greatness is well known, (as) they diligently dis-charge their functions ; by which their sport pours rain upon every arid soil, as light spreads (universally) on a fine day.

*[The label of the Special Topics is missing in the supplied text; the standard label was inserted.]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

नु—नु ऎंब शब्दक्कॆ यास्कर विवरणॆयु ई रीति इदॆ (*nu—nu èṃba śabdakkè yāskara vivaraṇèyu ī rīti idè*) —

तीत्यनुपृष्टे । नन्नेवकार्षिदिति च । अथाप्युपमार्थे भवति । (*tītyanupṛṣṭe | nannevakārṣiditi ca | athāpyupamārthe bhavati |*)

(the reference is printed in the supplied text in Telugu-script digits; transcribed in Kannada digits as (२ १-४) [?] (*(2 1-4) [?]*), marked [?]). The word *nu* is used in many senses; and saying that it is used also in explaining the reason and in the sense of comparison,

वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यू ३ तयो रुरुहुरिंद्र पूर्विः । (*vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vyū 3 tayo ruruhuriṃdra pūrviḥ |*)

सुदिने—मेघावरणादिरहिते दिने (*sudine—meghāvaraṇādirahite dine*) — the bhāṣyakāra says that a day with clear sunshine without clouds is a *sudina*; this is also the usage in practice. मेघच्छ- (*meghaccha-*)

हैदुर्दिनं (*haidurdinaṃ*) — "a day on which clouds cover the sky and the sun's rays do not fall is a *durdina*": so the lexicon explains. Therefore *sudina* means a day free of clouds and full of the sun's light.

करु:- (*karu:-*) [?] — Yāska says शरुमान् ऎंदरॆ हिंसावान् (*śarumān èṃdarè hiṃsāvān*) ("*śarumān* means one who injures") ((नि. ५-१२) (*(ni. 5-12)*); the supplied text begins the headword with "ಕರು:", marked [?]). In the present ṛk the bhāṣyakāra explains अंधकारहिंसकः प्रकाशकः (*aṃdhakārahiṃsakaḥ prakāśakaḥ*) — "the destroyer of darkness, the giver of light", that is, the Sun who destroys darkness and makes light. The illustration given is: as on a day free of clouds the Sun drives away darkness and spreads his light everywhere, so the Maruts pour rain, wet all regions and even barren land, and make them favourable to the growth of plants and the like: thus the greatness of the Maruts is described.

इरिणं—ऊषरप्रदेशं (*iriṇaṃ—ūṣarapradeśaṃ*) — the bhāṣyakāra's explanation is "barren land in which nothing grows". On this matter Yāska in his Nirukta:

प्रावेपा मा बृहतो मादयंति प्रवातेजा इरिणे वर्वृतानाः । (*prāvepā mā bṛhato mādayaṃti pravātejā iriṇe varvṛtānāḥ |*)
सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जागृविर्मह्यमच्छान् ॥ (*somasyeva maujavatasya bhakṣo vibhīdako jāgṛvirmahyamacchān ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ११-५४-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 11-54-1)*)

having quoted this ṛk (the reference is printed "೧೧-೫೪-೧", as supplied) he explains the word *iriṇe* in it:

इरिणं निर्यणं ऋणातेरपार्णं भवति । अपरता अस्मादोषधय इति वा ॥ (*iriṇaṃ niryaṇaṃ ṛṇāterapārṇaṃ bhavati | aparatā asmādoṣadhaya iti vā ‖*)
(नि. ९-८) (*(ni. 9-8)*)

that is, *iriṇa* or *apārṇa* means "without debt", or, since there is no water in this region (*arṇa* means water, *apārṇa* land without water) herbs and trees do not grow; therefore he has explained it as a region without water, a desert. The main point to note here is that causing abundant rain even in a desert where nothing grows because there is no water, and making plants and the like grow there in abundance, is described as one of the glories of the Maruts.

दिवा चित्तमः कृण्वंति पर्जन्येनोदवाहेन । यत्पृथीविं व्युंदंति ॥ (*divā cittamaḥ kṛṇvaṃti parjanyenodavāhena | yatpṛthīviṃ vyuṃdaṃti ‖*)
(ऋ. सुं. १-३८-९) (*(ṛ. suṃ. 1-38-9)*)

(printed "ಋ. ಸುಂ.") in this ṛk it is said that the Maruts make even the day dark by covering it with clouds, pour rain, make streams of water flow, and wet the whole earth.

पिन्वंत्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो धृतवद्विधथेष्वाभुवः । (*pinvaṃtyapo marutaḥ sudānavaḥ payo dhṛtavadvidhatheṣvābhuvaḥ |*)
(ऋ सं. १-६४-६) (*(ṛ saṃ. 1-64-6)*)

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

महिना (*mahinā*) (the word *mahat*): because it belongs to the *pṛthv-ādi* group the suffix *imanic*; by टेः (*ṭeḥ*) loss of *ṭi* (*at*); the word *mahiman* results; when the ending *su* follows, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) the substitute *ā*; by *vyatyaya*, because it has the *bha* designation, loss of the *a* of *anin*; the loss of *m* is Vedic. चिकित्त्रॆ [?] (*cikittrè [?]*) (root कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*)): Vedic *liṭ* in the passive; third person plural; by लिटस्तझयो—(पा. सू. ३-४-८१) (*liṭastajhayo—(pā. sū. 3-4-81)*) the substitute *irec*; by इरयोरे (पा. सू. ६-४-७६) (*irayore (pā. sū. 6-4-76)*) the substitute *re* for it; because of the relative *yat* there is no *nighāta*; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. युंजते (*yuṃjate*) (root युजिर् योगे (*yujir yoge*)): present, third person plural; the verb-*nighāta* accent. सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*): by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) *luk* for the genitive plural. शरुः (*śaruḥ*) (root श्य हिंसायां (*śya hiṃsāyāṃ*)): by तृस्वस्निहित्रपि—(उ. सू. १-१०) (*tṛsvasnihitrapi—(u. sū. 1-10)*) the suffix *un*; by सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa of the *ṛ*; because it is marked *n* the first syllable is acute. इरिणम् (*iriṇam*) (root ऋ गत् (*ṛ gat*)): by आर्तेःकिदिच्च (उ. सू. २-२०९) (*ārteḥkidicca (u. sū. 2-209)*) the suffix *inan*; because the suffix is marked *k* the root takes *i*, with *r*; by अट् कुप्वाज् (*aṭ kupvāj*) *ṇatva* of the suffix *n*; by इत्यादिनिर्नित्यम् (*ityādinirnityam*) the first syllable is acute. पुषायंत (*puṣāyaṃta*) (root पु, ष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेषु (*pu, ṣa snehanasecanapūraṇeṣu*), *kryādi*): Vedic *laṅ*; when the *śnā* suffix comes, by छंदसिशायजपि (पा. सू. ३-१-८४) (*chaṃdasiśāyajapi (pā. sū. 3-1-84)*) the substitute *śāyac*; because the suffix is marked *j* there is no guṇa of the penultimate short vowel; third person plural; because of the relative *yat* there is no *nighāta*; the suffix *śāyac*, being marked *c*, is acute on the last syllable; the augment *aṭ* does not occur by the Vedic rule.

> रिंद्रश्च । एतानपि प्र कृणुध्वं । अतोऽहं स्वायत्तबलान् सर्वानपि देवान् सुम्नाय
> सुखायाच्छाभिमुख्येन ववृतीय । स्तोत्रैरभिवर्तयेयं ॥

*Gist:* O priests, praise the Aśvins and Pūṣan for our protection, and Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Indra and the other self-powered gods; I too will turn all the gods towards me with praises for happiness.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(O priests) अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*) — the Aśvin deities. पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*) — the nourishing deity Pūṣan, (addressing them). अवसे (*avase*) — for our protection. प्रो कृणुध्वं (*pro kṛṇudhvaṃ*) — praise fully. अद्वेषः (*adveṣaḥ*) — free from hatred. विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) — and pervading Viṣṇu. वातः (*vātaḥ*) — the Vāyu who moves everywhere. ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*) — Indra, the lord. स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*) — the other gods of independent strength. संति हि (*saṃti hi*) — they exist indeed (praise them too). देवान् (*devān*) — all the gods. सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*) — for happiness. अच्छ (*accha*) — that they may be turned towards me. ववृतीय (*vavṛtīya*) — (by praises) I make them turn towards me.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O priests, praise for our protection the Aśvin deities and the nourishing deity Pūṣan; and praise Viṣṇu, who is free from hatred and pervading, and Vāyu who moves everywhere, and Indra the lord, and the other gods of independent strength.

### Printed p. 163

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5 ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 163 (as supplied, with tabs).*

I too, for the sake of my own happiness, praise all the gods so that they may turn towards me.

**Printed English translation**

Propitiate the Ashwins and Pushan, for my protection ; (propitiate) those (deities), who are of independent powers, as Vishnu, devoid of hatred, Vayu, and Ribhukshin, and may I influence the gods to be present for my felicity.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk the Aśvin deities, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Vāta, Indra and other gods are praised.

ऋभुक्षा: (*ṛbhukṣā:*) — the Nirukta-author himself has given two meanings for this word: उरुक्षयणः इंद्रः (*urukṣayaṇaḥ iṃdraḥ*) ("Indra who dwells in the wide atmosphere"), as an epithet of Indra, or ऋभूणां राजा (*ṛbhūṇāṃ rājā*) ("king of the Ṛbhus", or of the shining gods) ((नि. ९-३) (*(ni. 9-3)*)). Or, as Sāyaṇa explains, since the word is read among the names of the great ((नि. ३-१३) (*(ni. 3-13)*)) it may mean Indra, the great-souled.

वातः (*vātaḥ*) — for this word the Nirukta of Yāska is वातो वातीति सतः (*vāto vātīti sataḥ*): because it blows, this deity is called *vāta* (wind) ((नि. १०-३४) (*(ni. 10-34)*)). The two words *vāyu* and *vāta* are used in the sense of the god Vāyu and of the wind; but Vāyu is the deity and *vāta* the wind. There are two sūktas addressed to the deity Vāta ((ऋ. सं. १०-१६८ मत्तु १०-१८६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-168 mattu 10-186)*)), some portions of other sūktas, and about twelve sūktas together with Indra. The two words *vāyu* and *vāta* also occur in one ṛk:

ते नो रुद्रः सरस्वती सजोषा माळ्हुष्मंतो विष्णुर्मृळंतु वायुः । (*te no rudraḥ sarasvatī sajoṣā māḷhuṣmaṃto viṣṇurmṛḷaṃtu vāyuḥ |*)
ऋभुक्षा वाजो दैव्यू विधाता पर्जन्यावाता पिप्यकामिषं नः ॥ (*ṛbhukṣā vājo daivyū vidhātā parjanyāvātā pipyakāmiṣaṃ naḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-५०.१२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-50.12)*)
प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये । (*pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |*)
आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥ (*ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutaṃ ‖*)
(मि. सं. १०-९२-१३) (*(mi. saṃ. 10-92-13)*)

[the window ends here].

### Printed p. 164

*Running head: [164 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 186]. The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 10 of Sūkta 186 from p. 163, after the two verses with Vāyu and Vāta.*

In these two ṛks both the deities Vāyu and Vāta are praised. Of Vāyu and Vāta, it is Vāyu who is praised together with Indra:

इंद्रवायू इमे सुता उप प्रयोभिरा गतं । इंदवो वामुशंति हि ॥ (*iṃdravāyū ime sutā upa prayobhirā gataṃ | iṃdavo vāmuśaṃti hi ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-2-4)*)

in these and similar ṛks Indra and Vāyu are praised together. Vāta is generally connected with Parjanya:

पर्जन्यवाता वृषभा पृथिव्याः पुरीषाणि जिन्वतमप्यानि । (*parjanyavātā vṛṣabhā pṛthivyāḥ purīṣāṇi jinvatamapyāni |*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-४९-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-49-6)*)
(म. सं. ६-४९-६) (*(ma. saṃ. 6-49-6)*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-४९-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-49-6)*)

(the reference is printed three times, as "ಋ. ಸಂ.", "ಮ. ಸಂ." and "ಋ. ಸಂ."). In these and similar ṛks Parjanya and Vāta are praised together. The epithets used for the two are generally different; the epithets of Vāta indicate especially speed and violence.

प्रूषणं- प्रूषा [?] यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति (*prūṣaṇaṃ- prūṣā [?] yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati*) ((नि १२-६) (*(ni 12-6)*)) — the Nirukta says that because he nourishes with rays (*raśmi-poṣa*) this deity is called Pūṣan [the supplied text prints the headword "ಪ್ರೂಷಣಂ" and the first "ಪ್ರೂಷಾ"; marked [?]]. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:

इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीदं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किंचॆ । (*iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃcè |*)
(श. ब्रा. १४-४-२-२५) (*(śa. brā. 14-4-2-25)*)

it is said that because this deity nourishes everything he is called Pūṣan. This kind of meaning supports the view that Pūṣan is one of the twelve Ādityas.

पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः । (*puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ |*)
तेनैनमस्तौत्पोषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पंचभिः ॥ (*tenainamastautpoṣeti bharadvājastu paṃcabhiḥ ‖*)
(बृ. दे. २-६३) (*(bṛ. de. 2-63)*)

— because, destroying darkness, he nourishes the earth so that it prospers, he has the name Pūṣan. There is a statement of the Bṛhaddevatā that the ṛṣi Bharadvāja praised this deity in the five sūktas 53, 54, 55, 56 and 58 of the sixth Maṇḍala.

The name of this deity occurs in the Ṛgveda in about 120 places. There are eight sūktas that praise this deity: in the first Maṇḍala 2 sūktas, in the sixth Maṇḍala 5 sūktas and in the tenth Maṇḍala 1 sūkta praise Pūṣan. In the sūkta ऋ. सं. ६-५७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 6-57*) he is praised with Indra and in ऋ. सं. २-४० (*ṛ. saṃ. 2-40*) with Soma.

Since Pūṣan knows all the ways he is called the protector of the roads. He is prayed to drive away from the road (or at the time of travelling) the troubles, the wolves and the robbers that may be met on the way ((ऋ. सं. १-४२-१ रिंद ३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-42-1 riṃda 3)*)).

### Printed p. 165

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 55] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 165 (as supplied, "ವ. ೫೫" for the Varga number).*

(The sentence of p. 164 ends with "…the robbers", and continues here:) from the roads. In this same context he has the name विमुचोनपात् (*vimuconapāt*), "son of discrimination (release)"; this epithet occurs also in ऋ. सं. ६-५५-१ (*ṛ. saṃ. 6-55-1*).

वि पथो वाजसातये चिनुहि वि मृधो जहि । साधंतामुग्र नो धियः । (*vi patho vājasātaye cinuhi vi mṛdho jahi | sādhaṃtāmugra no dhiyaḥ |*)
(म. सं. ६-५३-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 6-53-4)*)

in this ṛk, and in the ṛks ऋ सं. १-४२-७, ८ (*ṛ saṃ. 1-42-7, 8*), there is the prayer: "wipe out the enemies, make the road clear, and may the road reach a place with good pasture." In many places it is prayed that he remove the difficulties that may come on the way and make the way auspicious. In the ṛks ऋ. सं. ६-४९-८ ; ६-५३-१ (*ṛ. saṃ. 6-49-8 ; 6-53-1*) it is said that he alone is the protector of all ways and the guide on the road. Therefore everyone who sets out on a journey should worship Pūṣan, the maker of roads, reciting the sūkta ऋ सं. ६-५३ (*ṛ saṃ. 6-53*); and all who have lost their way should take refuge in Pūṣan alone: so it is said in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra ३-६-८ (*3-6-8*) and the Sāṅkhyāyana Śrauta Sūtra ३-४-९ (*3-4-9*) and other places.

Pūṣan, prayed to seek, as one seeks a strayed animal, found the lost and hidden king: so it is said in ऋ. सं. १-२३-१४. १५ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-23-14. 15*) and तै. सं. ३-३-९-१ (*tai. saṃ. 3-3-9-1*) and other places. Therefore whatever is lost, worship should be offered to Pūṣan ((आ. गृ. सु. ३-७-९) (*(ā. gṛ. su. 3-7-9)*)). Likewise following the cattle and protecting them is a special mark of Pūṣan. He saves them from falling into pits and being hurt, and drives them back home safe; he brings back the strayed ((ऋ. सं. ६-५४-७ मत्तु १०) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-54-7 mattu 10)*)). His goad drives the cattle straight. He protects horses. He is the creator of cattle ((मै. सं. ४-३-७ ; तै. ब्रा. १-७-२-४) (*(mai. saṃ. 4-3-7 ; tai. brā. 1-7-2-4)*)). Such descriptions are many in the Ṛgveda. The praise-verses of Pūṣan to be used when cattle have gone grazing and strayed are given in the Sāṅkhyāyana Gṛhya Sūtra ((सां. गृ. सू. ३-९) (*(sāṃ. gṛ. sū. 3-9)*)).

विष्णु: (*viṣṇu:*) — though in the Brāhmaṇas and Purāṇas Viṣṇu is regarded as a very chief deity, in the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu is not so prominent. Five sūktas and some part of one sūkta only are addressed to Viṣṇu. Besides, his name is mentioned here and there in many places with other deities, chiefly with Indra. The main prowess of Viṣṇu is said to be the setting of three steps; these three strides are in heaven, atmosphere and earth. Besides, Viṣṇu's *paramapada* (highest abode) is regarded as the most excellent station.

### Printed p. 166

*Running head: [166 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

In the Ṛgveda the relation of Viṣṇu with Indra seems more special than with other gods. When Indra is about to slay the demon Vṛtra he seeks Viṣṇu's help. In the Yajurveda the matter of Viṣṇu is described in many ways; there are many mantras explaining that Viṣṇu is the lord of sacrifice and of mountains, the form of sacrifice, and the leader of all the gods. Yāska has given the derivation of the word *viṣṇu* in this way:

विष्णुः— अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा, (*viṣṇuḥ— atha yadviṣito bhavati tadviṣṇurbhavati viṣṇurviśatervā,*)
व्यश्नोतेर्वा । (*vyaśnotervā |*)
(सि. १२-१८) (*(si. 12-18)*)

because he pervades everything, or enters and pervades everything, or pervades everything with rays, he is called Viṣṇu; therefore *viṣṇu* may also be said to mean the Sun (Āditya): so the word *viṣṇu* is explained.

The great act of Viṣṇu in the Ṛgveda is the *trivikramaṇa*, the striding of three steps. There is a difference of opinion as to what these three strides are and where. Western scholars have taken them to mean the three states of the Sun: rising, culmination and setting.

[This stepping of Vishnu is emblamatic [sic] of the rising, the culminating and setting of the sun.]
[Max Muller. Sacred Books of the East. Vol. XXXII. p. 133]

It is known from a Nirukta sentence that ancient scholars such as Aurṇavābha also supported this meaning:

समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यार्णवाभः । (*samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasītyārṇavābhaḥ |*)
(नि. ८२-९) (*(ni. 82-9)*)

(the reference is printed "(ನಿ. ೮೨-೯)") thus the opinion of Aurṇavābha is stated. On this sentence Durgācārya explains समारोहणे—उदय (*samārohaṇe—udaya*) गिरावुद्यन् पदमेकं निधत्ते । विष्णुपदे माध्यंदिनेंतरिक्षे । गयशिरसि—अस्तंगिरा (*girāvudyan padamekaṃ nidhatte | viṣṇupade mādhyaṃdineṃtarikṣe | gayaśirasi—astaṃgirā*): the one step placed at the rising mountain at sunrise, the other step at the culmination in the atmosphere at midday, and the third step placed at the setting mountain at sunset are indicated by the sentence त्रेधा निदधे पदं (*tredhā nidadhe padaṃ*); this is the opinion of Aurṇavābha, the Nirukta-authors have stated. Besides,

विष्णु स्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभानाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । (*viṣṇu stridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhānāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ |*)
(२ ८-८९) (*(2 8-89)*)

[the window ends here, with this sentence of Śākapūṇi and its reference].

### Printed p. 167

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 167 (as supplied, "ಆ" for the second abbreviation). The window continues the Viṣṇu note in the Special Topics of Ṛk 10 of Sūkta 186 from p. 166, after the sentence of Śākapūṇi and its reference.*

(It is also stated that) according to Śākapūṇi these three strides indicate the three states of the Sun moving through the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven. On this Durgācārya explains प्रार्थिवोऽग्निर्भूत्वा पृथिव्यां यत्किंचिदस्ति तद्विक्रमते । अंतरिक्षे (*prārthivo 'gnirbhūtvā pṛthivyāṃ yatkiṃcidasti tadvikramate | aṃtarikṣe*) विद्युदात्मना दिवि सूरात्मना (*vidyudātmanā divi sūrātmanā*): "becoming the terrestrial Agni he strides over whatever is on the earth; in the atmosphere in the form of lightning; in heaven in the form of the Sun"; that is, he pervades the three worlds in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and the Sun. In support of this very sense:

विष्णुमुखा वै देवाश्चंदोभिरिमांल्लोकाननपजय्यमभ्यजयन् यद्वि- (*viṣṇumukhā vai devāścaṃdobhirimāṃllokānanapajayyamabhyajayan yadvi-*)
ष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते विष्णुरेव भूत्वा यजमानश्चंदोभिरिमांल्लोकाननप- (*ṣṇukramānkramate viṣṇureva bhūtvā yajamānaścaṃdobhirimāṃllokānanapa-*)
जय्यमभिजयति विष्णोः क्रमोस्यभिमातिहेत्याह गायत्री वै पृथिवी (*jayyamabhijayati viṣṇoḥ kramosyabhimātihetyāha gāyatrī vai pṛthivī*)
त्रैष्टुभमंतरिक्षं जागती द्यौरानुष्टुभीर्दिशश्चंदोभिरेवेमांल्लोकान् (*traiṣṭubhamaṃtarikṣaṃ jāgatī dyaurānuṣṭubhīrdiśaścaṃdobhirevemāṃllokān*)
यथापूर्वमभिजयति । (*yathāpūrvamabhijayati |*)
(कृ. सं. १-७-५-४) (*(kṛ. saṃ. 1-7-5-4)*)

अन्या देवतासीथ्योऽब्रवीद्विष्णवे हीदमा हरिष्यावो येनायमिदमिति स (*anyā devatāsīthyo 'bravīdviṣṇave hīdamā hariṣyāvo yenāyamidamiti sa*)
विष्णुस्त्रेधात्मानं वि न्यधत्त पृथिव्यां तृतीयमंतरिक्षे तृतीयं दिवि तृती- (*viṣṇustredhātmānaṃ vi nyadhatta pṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamaṃtarikṣe tṛtīyaṃ divi tṛtī-*)
यमभिपर्यावर्ताद्द्यबिभेद्यत्पृथिव्यां तृतीयमासीत्तेनेंद्रो वज्रमुद- (*yamabhiparyāvartāddyabibhedyatpṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamāsītteneṃdro vajramuda-*)
यच्छद्विष्णवनुस्थितस्सोऽब्रवीन्मा मे प्र हारस्ति वा इदं ॥ (*yacchadviṣṇavanusthitasso 'bravīnmā me pra hārasti vā idaṃ ‖*)
(कृ. सं. २-४-१२-३) (*(kṛ. saṃ. 2-4-12-3)*)

in such Saṃhitā sentences too, and in

यद्वेव विष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते! यज्ञो वै विष्णुः स देवेभ्य इमां विक्रांतिं (*yadveva viṣṇukramānkramate! yajño vai viṣṇuḥ sa devebhya imāṃ vikrāṃtiṃ*)
विचक्रमे यैषामियं विक्रांतिरिदमेव प्रथमेन पदेन पस्पाराथेद- (*vicakrame yaiṣāmiyaṃ vikrāṃtiridameva prathamena padena paspārātheda-*)
मंतरिक्षं द्वितीयेन दिवमुत्तमेनैतामेवैष एतस्मै विष्णुर्यज्ञं विक्रांतिं (*maṃtarikṣaṃ dvitīyena divamuttamenaitāmevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajñaṃ vikrāṃtiṃ*)
विक्रमते तस्माद्विष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते । (*vikramate tasmādviṣṇukramānkramate |*)
(श ब्रा, १-९-३-९) (*(śa brā, 1-9-3-9)*)

यद्वेव विष्णुक्रमवात्सप्रे भवतः । विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरिमं लोकम- (*yadveva viṣṇukramavātsapre bhavataḥ | viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatirimaṃ lokama-*)
सृजत वात्सप्रेणाग्निं विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरंतरिक्षमसृजत वात्सप्रेण- (*sṛjata vātsapreṇāgniṃ viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatiraṃtarikṣamasṛjata vātsapreṇa-*)
वायुं विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिर्दिवमसृजत वात्सप्रेणादित्यं । (*vāyuṃ viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatirdivamasṛjata vātsapreṇādityaṃ |*)
(श. ब्रा. ६-७-४-२) (*(śa. brā. 6-7-4-2)*)

such Brāhmaṇa sentences, it is shown, in accordance with the opinion of Śākapūṇi, that the three steps of Viṣṇu are related to earth, atmosphere and heaven, and to the deities Agni, Vāyu and the Sun. And

आ यो विवाय सचथाय दैव्य इंद्राय विष्णुः सुकृते सुकृत्तरः । (*ā yo vivāya sacathāya daivya iṃdrāya viṣṇuḥ sukṛte sukṛttaraḥ |*)
वेधा अजिन्वत्रिषधस्थ आर्यमृतस्य भागे यजमानमाभजत् ॥ (*vedhā ajinvatriṣadhastha āryamṛtasya bhāge yajamānamābhajat ‖*)
(म. सं. १-१५६-५) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-156-5)*)

### Printed p. 168

*Running head: [168 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 186].*

in this ṛk it is said that Viṣṇu himself strides over the three worlds beginning with the earth. As said in the mantra ६-७-४-७ (*6-7-4-7*) of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa quoted above, the three strides of Viṣṇu are the cause of the creation and maintenance of the worlds, earth and the rest; this is praised in the ṛk (ऋ. सं १-१५४-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ 1-154-2)*) with the words अधिक्षि (*adhikṣi*) यंति भुवनानि विश्वा (*yaṃti bhuvanāni viśvā*): all the worlds rest on the support in the form of the three strides of Viṣṇu; so the greatness of Viṣṇu's strides is praised.

In the Purāṇas and similar works Viṣṇu has an important place. Since he pervades the whole universe, Viṣṇu is called Parameśvara and Parabrahman; or, among the Trimūrti (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara) who carry on the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the world, Viṣṇu is famed as the one who protects the world. For this task of protecting the world Viṣṇu had to take many incarnations, and it is the opinion of the bhāṣyakāra and other scholars that the incarnation of Vāmana or Trivikrama is the one described in this ṛk. But Western and modern scholars hold that, since incarnations of Viṣṇu are not indicated in the Ṛgveda, and since the divine acts found here and there in the Veda are described in a special way in the Purāṇas, and the source of the Purāṇic stories is the Veda itself, it is not right to interpret the incarnations in the Purāṇas by fitting them to the Vedic mantras.

According to the story told in the Purāṇas, when the asura emperor Bali was ruling after defeating the gods, the defeated gods appealed to Viṣṇu, and in order to protect them Viṣṇu took the incarnation of Vāmana and went to Bali while he had undertaken the sacrificial consecration and asked for as much earth as three steps; Bali agreed and said he would give it. Then Viṣṇu, from the form of Vāmana, took the incarnation of Trivikrama, that is, assumed a gigantic form pervading earth and atmosphere, and covered the whole earth with one step and the atmosphere with another, and asked Bali where to place the third step; since the king was true to his word he prayed that, as there was no other place, he should place the third step on his own head and bless him; accordingly Trivikrama placed his third foot on Bali's head, made him go to the nether world, rule there and live happily, and gave him the boon he wished: so there is a lengthy description.

अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*) — we have explained the Aśvin deities many times before. Here we shall state briefly only a short introduction of them and the help they gave to those who praised them.

There are two Aśvin deities. Though one of them is named Dasra and the other Nāsatya, both are often called by the name Dasra or Nāsatya alone.

### Printed p. 169

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5. ।] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 169 (as supplied, with a danda).*

Their chariot is golden, and its wheels, axle and other parts are all made of gold (ऋ सं. ४-४४-४, १-१८०-१, ८-५-२९, ८-२२-५ (*ṛ saṃ. 4-44-4, 1-180-1, 8-5-29, 8-22-5*) and others); it is a peculiar chariot. It has three wheels, three felloes, and some other parts also in threes. It has the speed of thought. A three-wheeled chariot belongs to them alone.

यदयाशं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यमुप । (*yadayāśaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryamupa |*)
क्वैकं चक्रं नामासीत् क्व देष्वाप्यय तस्थतुः ॥ (*kvaikaṃ cakraṃ nāmāsīt kva deṣvāpyaya tasthatuḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-८५-१५) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-85-15)*)

in this it is said that when they went to the wedding of the goddess Sūryā one wheel of the chariot was lost. Although the word *aśvinau* means "possessors of horses (*aśva*)", it is nowhere said that this name came to them because they are horse-riders. The animals that draw their chariot are said to be horses (ऋ. सं. १-११७-२ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-2*)), birds (६-६३-६ (*6-63-6*)), swans (४-४५-४ (*4-45-4*)), eagles (१-११८-४ (*1-118-4*)), hawk-shaped horses (८-५-७ (*8-5-7*)). But their chief vehicle, as Yāska says, is रासभावश्विनोः (*rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ*): asses are the vehicles of the Aśvin deities ((नि. २-२८) (*(ni. 2-28)*)).

कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः । (*kadā yogo vājino rāsabhasya yena yajñaṃ nāsatyopayāthaḥ |*)
(म. सं. १-३४-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-34-9)*)
शद्रासभो [?] नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय । (*śadrāsabho [?] nāsatyā sahasramājā yamasya pradhane jigāya |*)
(म. सं. १-११६-२) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-116-2)*)

in these and similar ṛks it is stated plainly that the ass (*rāsabha*) is the vehicle of the Aśvin deities. Those who perform sacrifice always invoke them at dawn. They have a relation with the daughter of the Sun; Sūryā herself chose them (ऋ सं ७-६९-४ (*ṛ saṃ 7-69-4*)); both are her husbands (४-४३-६ (*4-43-6*)); Sūryā mounted their chariot (५-७३-५ ; ८-८-१० (*5-73-5 ; 8-8-10*)); the daughter of the Sun mounts their chariot (ऋ. सं. १-३४-५ ; १-११६-१७ ; १-११८-५ ; ६-६३-५ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-34-5 ; 1-116-17 ; 1-118-5 ; 6-63-5*)); they regard Sūryā as their own (७-६८-३ (*7-68-3*)) and she goes with them in the chariot (८-२९-८ (*8-29-8*)): there are such descriptions.

There are many stories to show that they help people in distress. These have been explained at length in their places; of them we have explained only a few important ones here.

जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वन्रिं प्रामुंचतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् । (*jujuruṣo nāsatyota vanriṃ prāmuṃcataṃ drāpimiva cyavānāt |*)
प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनां ॥ (*prātirataṃ jahitasyāyurdasrāditpatimakṛṇutaṃ kanīnāṃ ‖*)
(म. सं. १-१३६-११) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-136-11)*)

[the window ends here with the verse and its reference].

### Printed p. 170

*Running head: [170 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186]. The window continues the *aśvinau* note of the Special Topics of Ṛk 10 of Sūkta 186 from p. 169, after the verse "ಜುಜುರುಷೋ ನಾಸತ್ಯೋತ…".*

The ṛṣi Cyavana became very old, his body decrepit and without strength, and his people abandoned him. When this ṛṣi prayed to the Aśvin deities they came, removed his decrepit body, made him young and dear to his wife, and increased his life. The same matter is stated in:

युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । (*yuvaṃ cyavānamaśvinā jaraṃtaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-११७-८३) [?] (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-83) [?]*)
निष्पौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात् पुनश्चवानं चक्रथुर्युवानं । (*niṣpaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrāt punaścavānaṃ cakrathuryuvānaṃ |*)
ऋ. सं. १-११८-६) (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-6)*)
प्र च्यवानाज्जु जुरुषो वत्रिमत्कं न मुंचथः । (*pra cyavānājju juruṣo vatrimatkaṃ na muṃcathaḥ |*)
युवा यदी कृथः पुनरा काममृण्वे वध्वः ॥ (*yuvā yadī kṛthaḥ punarā kāmamṛṇve vadhvaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ सं. ५-७४-५) (*(ṛ saṃ. 5-74-5)*)
उत त्यद्वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय प्रतीत्यं हविर्दे । (*uta tyadvāṃ jurate aśvinā bhūccyavānāya pratītyaṃ havirde |*)
(ऋ. सं. ७-६८-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 7-68-6)*)
युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वं । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ jaraso 'mumuktaṃ ni pedava ūhathurāśumaśvaṃ |*)
(ऋ. सं. ७-७१-५) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 7-71-5)*)
युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरथाय तक्षथुः । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryuvānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-३९-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-4)*)

(the reference of the second verse is printed with a missing opening parenthesis). In these ṛks too there is the description of the aged ṛṣi Cyavana being made young. There is a long history on this subject in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too. Likewise:

युवं विप्रस्य जरणा मुपेयुषः पुनः कलेरकृणुतं युवद्वयः । (*yuvaṃ viprasya jaraṇā mupeyuṣaḥ punaḥ kalerakṛṇutaṃ yuvadvayaḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-३९-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-2)*)

in this ṛk there is the mention of removing the old age of one Kali and making him young.

याभिर्वम्रं विपिपानमुपस्तुतं कलिं याभिर्वित्तजानिं दुवस्यथः । (*yābhirvamraṃ vipipānamupastutaṃ kaliṃ yābhirvittajāniṃ duvasyathaḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-११२-१५) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-15)*)

in this ṛk, which names the same Kali, it is said that when he took a wife and married, they gave him their help and did many services.

They granted for the young women, wives of Vimada, a chariot ((१-११२-१९) (*(1-112-19)*)), or one wife to him ((१-११७-१) (*(1-117-1)*)). It seems she was the wife of Puramitra ((ऋ. सं. १-११३-२० ; १०-३९-७) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-113-20 ; 10-39-7)*)), and her name was Kamadhyu ((१०-६५-१२) (*(10-65-12)*))

...they brought back to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, his lost son and gave him over ((ऋ सं. १-११६-२३; १-११७-७ ; १०-६५-१२) (*(ṛ saṃ. 1-116-23; 1-117-7 ; 10-65-12)*)). In the ṛks ऋ. सं. ८-७५-१ रिंद ३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 8-75-1 riṃda 3*) the names Viśvaka and Viṣṇāpu are indicated.

The story of Bhujyu is told again and again. Bhujyu is the son of a king named Tugra. While he was making a sea voyage and was sinking, Bhujyu held a piece of wood and floated amid the waves. Then he took refuge in the Aśvin deities. In a ship with a hundred oars on the great ocean whose depth could not be known, the Aśvin deities seated him and took him home. In a ship without leaks that seemed to fly through the sky, or in four boats with wings, or in three flying chariots with a hundred feet and six horses, or in their chariot swift as thought, with the help of their horses that fly swiftly, they brought Bhujyu seated and delivered him to his house. ((१-११६-३, ४-५ , १-११७-१४, १५ ; (*(1-116-3, 4-5 , 1-117-14, 15 ;*) १-१८२-५, ६, ७ ; ७-६८-७ ; १-११२-६, २० ; १.-११८-६ ; १-११९-४ ; १-१५८-३ ; ६-६२-६ ; (*1-182-5, 6, 7 ; 7-68-7 ; 1-112-6, 20 ; 1.-118-6 ; 1-119-4 ; 1-158-3 ; 6-62-6 ;*) ७-६९-७ ; ८-५-२२ ; १०-३९-४ ; १०-४७-७ ; १०-६५-१२ ; १०-१४३-५ ) (*7-69-7 ; 8-5-22 ; 10-39-4 ; 10-47-7 ; 10-65-12 ; 10-143-5 )*))

When a woman named Viśpalā had her leg cut off in battle and prayed to the Aśvin deities, they came and provided her with an iron leg and saved her; this is said in the ṛks ऋ. सं. १-११२-१० ; १.१.६- (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-10 ; 1.1.6-*) १५ ; १-११७-११ ; १-११८-८ ; १०-३९-८ (*15 ; 1-117-11 ; 1-118-8 ; 10-39-8*) [as printed; the second reference has stray full stops].

(When the ass, the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, was in the form of a wolf) one Ṛjrāśva cut a hundred sheep from the flock he was tending and gave them as food to the wolf. His father, angered by this, had Ṛjrāśva's eyes pulled out and made him blind. Then the wolf praised the Aśvin deities; they were pleased and gave Ṛjrāśva eyes ((ऋ. सं. १-११६-१६; १-११७-१७, १८) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-16; 1-117-17, 18)*)). In the ṛk ऋ. सं. १-१००-१७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-100-17*) there is mention of Ṛjrāśva praising Indra.

One Pārāvṛja was blind and lame, and was an outcaste. The Aśvin deities gave him the sight of the eyes and the power of walking, that is, they granted eyes and legs ((ऋ सं १-११२-८) (*(ṛ saṃ 1-112-8)*)); the name of Pārāvṛja is mentioned, when Indra is the subject, in the ṛks ऋ. सं. २-१३-१२ ; २-१५-७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 2-13-12 ; 2-15-7*).

The ṛṣi Rebha was bound hand and foot by wicked people and thrown into a well; for nine days and ten nights he lay there on the point of death. The Aśvin deities lifted him out of the well as one lifts soma-juice with a ladle and gave him life ((ऋ. सं. (*(ṛ. saṃ.*) १-११२-५; १-११६-२४; १-११७-२; १-११७-४; १-११८-६; १-११९-६; १०-३९-९) (*1-112-5; 1-116-24; 1-117-2; 1-117-4; 1-118-6; 1-119-6; 10-39-9)*)).

One Vandana, likewise carried off by wicked people and thrown into a pit in a dark place, was rescued by the Aśvin deities from the danger and brought into the light ((ऋ. सं १-११२-५; १-११६-११; १-११७-५; १-११८-६; १०-३९-८' १-११९-६, ७) (*(ṛ. saṃ 1-112-5; 1-116-11; 1-117-5; 1-118-6; 10-39-8 ' 1-119-6, 7)*)).

To Kakṣīvat of the Pajra family they gave boons at will and made hundreds of jars of *surā* (liquor) or honey pour from a horse's hoof as through a sieve ((ऋ. सं. १-११६-७ ; १-११७-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-7 ; 1-117-6)*)).

When the ṛṣi Atri, thrown into a great pit darkened by hatred and envy and blazing with fire, was in distress and prayed to the Aśvin deities, they came, quenched the fire with frost, comforted him with food and the like, and rescued him from that state ((१-११२-७; १-११६-८; १-११७-३; १-११८-७; १-११९-६; ५-७८-४ रिंद ६) (*(1-112-7; 1-116-8; 1-117-3; 1-118-7; 1-119-6; 5-78-4 riṃda 6)*) ७-७१-५ ; ८-६२-३ , ७ रिंद ९ ; १०-३९-९) (*7-71-5 ; 8-62-3 , 7 riṃda 9 ; 10-39-9)*)). In the ṛk ऋ. सं. १०-८०-३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-80-3*) it is indicated that Agni protected Atri.

Vadhrimatī, being childless and barren, prayed to the Aśvin deities, and they granted her a son named Hiraṇyahasta ((ऋ. सं. १-११६-१३ ; १-११७-२४ ; ६-६२-७ ; (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-13 ; 1-117-24 ; 6-62-7 ;*) १०.३९-७) (*10.39-7)*)).

Ghoṣā, who remained unmarried in her father's house, was granted at her prayer a suitable husband by the Aśvin deities ((ऋ. सं १-११७-७; १०-३९-३, ६; १०-४-५) (*(ṛ. saṃ 1-117-7; 10-39-3, 6; 10-4-5)*)). In the bhāṣya on the ṛk ऋ. सं. १-११७-७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-7*) Sāyaṇa says that this woman Ghoṣā was suffering from leprosy and that the Aśvin deities cured that disease. In the tenth Maṇḍala (१०-३९ (*10-39*)) there is a sūkta seen by this Ghoṣā.

When the cow of Śayu was old and bore no calf, they gave her the power of giving milk ((ऋ. सं. १-११६-२२; १-११७-२०; १-११८-८; १-११९-६; १०-३९-१३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-22; 1-117-20; 1-118-8; 1-119-6; 10-39-13)*)).

To the king Pedu the Aśvin deities gave a white horse, as strong as Indra, and with it he conquered his enemies and obtained much wealth, vehicles and the like ((ऋ. सं. १-११६-६ ; १-११७-९ ; १-११८-९ ; १-११९-१० ; ७-२१-५ ; १०-३९-१०) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-6 ; 1-117-9 ; 1-118-9 ; 1-119-10 ; 7-21-5 ; 10-39-10)*)).

Besides, as said in the sūktas 112 (printed "೧ ೨"), 116, 117, 118 and 119 of the first Maṇḍala, the Aśvin deities have helped many men, and have also been of service to animals, birds and so on. In this context it is said that when a wolf was carrying off a sparrow they freed it from the wolf's mouth at the sparrow's prayer, as in the ṛks ऋ.सं. (*ṛ.saṃ.*)
