*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5 ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 173 (as supplied).*

१-११६-१४ ; १-११७-१६ ; १-११८-८ ; १० ३९-१३ (*1-116-14 ; 1-117-16 ; 1-118-8 ; 10 39-13*). Besides these matters there are many more connected with the Aśvin deities; they will be explained in their several contexts.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

कृणुद्धम् (*kṛṇuddham*) (root कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च (*kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca*)): imperative, second person plural; the verb-*nighāta* accent. स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*) ("those whose own strength"): by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) the accent of the earlier member. संति (*saṃti*) (root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*)): present, third person plural; by हिच (पा. सू. (*hica (pā. sū.*) ८-१-३४) (*8-1-34)*) the prohibition of *nighāta* applies, so the first-syllable acute of the suffix remains. अद्वेषः (*adveṣaḥ*): by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) (*nañsubhyām (pā. sū. 6-2-172)*) the last syllable of the later member is acute. वातः (*vātaḥ*) (root वा गतिगंधनयोः (*vā gatigaṃdhanayoḥ*)): by हसिमृग्रिण्व—(उ. सू. ३-३६६) (*hasimṛgriṇva—(u. sū. 3-366)*) the suffix *tan*; because it is marked *n* the first syllable is acute. अच्छॆ (*acchè*): by निपातस्य चॆ (उ. सू. ६-३-१२६) (*nipātasya cè (u. sū. 6-3-126)*) [as printed, "ಉ. ಸೂ."] lengthening in the Saṃhitā. ववृतीय (*vavṛtīya*) (root वृतु वर्तनॆ? (*vṛtu vartanè?*)): optative, first person singular, with the suffix *iṭ*; by इटोत् (पा सू. ३-४-१०६) (*iṭot (pā sū. 3-4-106)*) *at* for it; by लिजिः सीयुट् (पा. सू. ३-४-१०२ (*lijiḥ sīyuṭ (pā. sū. 3-4-102*) the augment *sīyuṭ*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *ślu*; doubling of the root because of *ślu*; by लिजिः सलोपो—(पा. सू. ७-२-७९) (*lijiḥ salopo—(pā. sū. 7-2-79)*) the loss of *s*; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

#### Ṛk 11

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads कंठ काव्यं (*kaṃṭha kāvyaṃ*); standard label inserted. The Saṃhitā lines were joined.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इ॒यं सा वो॑ अ॒स्मे दीधि॑तिर्यजत्रा अपि॒प्राणी॑ च॒ सद॑नी च भूयाः ।
> नि या दे॒वेषु॒ यत॑ते वसू॒युर्वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥ ११ ॥

> *iyaṃ sā vo asme dīdhitiryajatrā apiprāṇī ca sadanī ca bhūyāḥ |*
> *ni yā deveṣu yatate vasūyurvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

### Printed p. 174

*Running head: [174 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186]. The window opens with the Pada of Ṛk 11 of Sūkta 186, after the Saṃhitā on p. 173.*

*[As supplied, the label line reads १ शरणागति (*1 śaraṇāgati*); standard label inserted. Two readings are marked [?]: the Pada's आपि [?] (*āpi [?]*) against the Saṃhitā's *apiprāṇī*, and वसुयुः [?] (*vasuyuḥ [?]*) against the Saṃhitā's *vasūyuḥ*.]*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इयं । सा । वः । अस्मे इति । दीधितिः । यजत्राः । आपि [?] प्राणी । च । सदनी । च । भूयाः ।
> नि । या । देवेषु । यतते । वसुयुः [?] । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरदानुं ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे यजत्रा यष्टव्या देवाः वो युष्मत्संबंधिनी सेयं प्रसिद्धा दीधिति-
> र्दिप्तिरस्मे अस्माकमपिप्राणी सर्वदा चेष्टयित्रि सदनी च निवासवती च भूयाः ।
> भूयात् । भवतु । या दीधितीर्वसूयुर्वसुमती देवेषु नि यतते नियमेन
> प्रयत्नं करोति । तानपि प्रकाशितुं सैव भूयात् । विद्यामेति गतः ॥

*Gist:* O gods worthy of sacrifice, may this your effulgence give us life and shelter, the effulgence that strives among the gods for wealth; may we gain food, strength and long life.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यजत्रा (*yajatrā*) — O gods worthy of sacrifice. या (*yā*) — which effulgence. वसूयुः (*vasūyuḥ*) — richly furnished with wealth. देवेषु (*deveṣu*) — among the gods. नि युतते (*ni yutate*) — regularly attains the nature of an oblation. सा (*sā*) — the world-famed one, वः (*vaḥ*) — yours. इयं दीधिति (*iyaṃ dīdhiti*) — this effulgence. अस्मे (*asme*) — to us. अपि प्राणी च (*api prāṇī ca*) — ever giving us life. सदनी च (*sadanī ca*) — and having a dwelling. भूयाः (*bhūyāḥ*) — may it be. इषं (*iṣaṃ*) — food. वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) — strength. जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) — long life. विद्याम (*vidyāma*) — may we obtain.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O gods worthy of sacrifice, may that effulgence of yours, which is furnished with wealth and world-famed and manifests itself in you, ever give us life and give us shelter. May we, by your grace, obtain food, strength and long life.

**Printed English translation**

Objects of admiration, may that wealth-abounding effulgence which manifests itself amongst the gods, give animation to our existence, and (per-manence to) our dwellings; that we may (thence) obtain food, strength, and long life.

### Printed p. 175

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 175 (as supplied).*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अष्टे [?] (*aṣṭe [?]*) [the headword is evidently *asme*, printed "ಅಷ್ಟೇ"; marked [?]] — this word is used in the sense of all seven cases. For example:

1. (१) अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥ (*1. (1) asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖*) (printed "1. (೧)" with a stray "1.")

अस्मे इत्यतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यंतं । तस्मादनेकार्थं । एकमेव ह्यतच्छब्दरूपं (*asme ityatatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyaṃtaṃ | tasmādanekārthaṃ | ekameva hyatacchabdarūpaṃ*) सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । तद्यथा— (*saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā—*): "the word *asme* ends in all the cases; therefore it has many senses; one and the same form of this word occurs in the senses of all seven cases; its determination is by the context and the like. Thus:"

प्रथमायास्तावत्—अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः (*prathamāyāstāvat—asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ*) — that is, the word *asme* is used in the senses of the seven cases according to the context: according to the context any of the seven case-senses can be given to the word. In the sentence *asme te bandhuḥ* the word *asme* means "we"; this is the example of the nominative sense.

(२) अस्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । अस्मानित्यर्थः ॥ (*(2) asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | asmānityarthaḥ ‖*)

*Dvitīyā*: the word *asme* has the accusative sense *asmān*, "us". As an example:

आ शैनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । (*ā śainasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ |*)
हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमाया उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥ (*have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-११८-११) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-11)*)

he has given this ṛk; the word *asme* in it means *asmān*, "us".

(३) अस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । अस्माभिरित्यर्थः ॥ (*(3) asme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | asmābhirityarthaḥ ‖*)

*Tṛtīyā*: here *asme* means *asmābhiḥ*, "by us", the instrumental sense (the supplied text had Devanagari letters in the word तृतीयाविभक्त्यर्थवु [?] (*tṛtīyāvibhaktyarthavu [?]*); they were rewritten in Kannada script, marked [?]). On this matter:

भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । (*bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ |*)
भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेंद्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥ (*bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭheṃdra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१६५-७) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-165-7)*)

he has given this ṛk as an example. Here *asme* means *asmābhiḥ*, "by us".

(४) अस्मे प्रयंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन् । अस्मभ्यमित्यर्थः ॥ (*(4) asme prayaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣin | asmabhyamityarthaḥ ‖*)

*Caturthī*: here *asme* means *asmabhyam*, "for us", the dative sense. An example:

अस्मे प्र यंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निंद्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । (*asme pra yaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣinniṃdra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ |*)
अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराइश्त्वत इंद्र शिप्रिन् ॥ (*asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāiśtvata iṃdra śiprin ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ३-३६-१०) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-36-10)*)

### Printed p. 176

*Running head: [176 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. . A. 24. Sū. 186] (the print has "ಮಂ. ." with the numeral missing, as supplied).*

For the words *asme* in this ṛk, the sense is *asmabhyam*, "for us": the dative sense.

1. (५) अस्मे आराच्चिद्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु । अस्मदित्यर्थः । (*1. (5) asme ārāccidveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu | asmadityarthaḥ |*) (printed "1. (೫)")

*Pañcamī*: here *asme* means *asmāt*, "from us". An example:

तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्जियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । (*tasya vayaṃ sumatau yajjiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma |*)
स सुत्रामा स्ववा इंद्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥ (*sa sutrāmā svavā iṃdro asme ārāccidveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-13)*)

for the word *asme* in this ṛk the sense is *asmat*, "from us", the ablative.

(६) ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे । अस्माकमित्यर्थः । (*(6) ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme | asmākamityarthaḥ |*)

*Ṣaṣṭhī*: here *asme* means *asmākam*, "of us, to us". For this explanation:

आ नो भर भगमिंद्र द्युमंतं नि ते देष्टस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । (*ā no bhara bhagamiṃdra dyumaṃtaṃ ni te deṣṭasya dhīmahi prareke |*)
ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनां ॥ (*ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnāṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ३-३०-१९) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-30-19)*)

he has quoted this ṛk. For the word *asme* in it the sense is *asmākam*, "our, to us": the genitive sense.

(७) अस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि । अस्मास्वित्यर्थः ॥ (*(7) asme dhatta vasavo vasūni | asmāsvityarthaḥ ‖*)

*Saptamī*: here *asme* means "in us". An example:

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । (*agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho |*)
अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥ (*asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं १-२९-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ 1-29-4)*)

for the word *asme* in this ṛk the sense is *asmāsu*, "in us": the locative sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

अस्मे (*asme*): by सुपां सुलुक्—(पा. सू. ७-१-३४) (*supāṃ suluk—(pā. sū. 7-1-34)*) the substitute *śe* for the genitive plural [as printed]. यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*) (root यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*)): by अमिनक्षियजि—(उ. सू. (*aminakṣiyaji—(u. sū.*) ३-३८५) (*3-385)*) the suffix *atran*; in the vocative the *āmantrita-nighāta* accent. सदनी (*sadanī*) (root षद्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadlya viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*)): when the suffix *lyuṭ* comes, the substitute *ana* for it; by लिति (पा. सू ६-१-१९३) (*liti (pā. sū 6-1-193)*) the syllable before the suffix is acute; in the feminine, because it is marked *ṭ*, the suffix *ṅīp* comes.

### Printed p. 177

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 5. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 177 (as supplied, "ಆ" for the second abbreviation). The window continues the Ṛk 11 grammar page of Sūkta 186 from p. 176, after the *sadanī* entry.*

भूयाः (*bhūyāḥ*) (root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*)): by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) the second-person singular ending in place of the third-person singular of the optative; because it follows a non-verb the *nighāta* accent arises. यतते (*yatate*) (root यती प्रयत्ने (*yatī prayatne*)): present, third person singular; by यद्वृत्ता- (*yadvṛttā-*) न्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) (*nnityam (pā. sū. 8-1-66)*) the prohibition of *nighāta*; by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) the *laḥ sārvadhātuka* is unaccented, so the accent of the root remains. वसूयुः (*vasūyuḥ*): when the sense "he wishes for wealth (*vasūni*)" is intended, by सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (पा. सू. ३-१-८) (*supa ātmanaḥ kyac (pā. sū. 3-1-8)*) the suffix *kyac*; by क्याच्छंदसि (पा. सू, ३-२-१२०) (*kyācchaṃdasi (pā. sū, 3-2-120)*) the suffix *u* after it [as printed]; by अतो लोपः (*ato lopaḥ*) loss of the *a* of *kyac*; by the Vedic rule lengthening of the earlier vowel in the Saṃhitā; by the suffix accent it is acute on the last syllable.

नूर ऎंभत्तेळनॆय सूक्तवु. (*nūra èṃbhatteḷanèya sūktavu.*) ("The hundred and eighty-seventh sūkta.")

*[A stray line in the supplied text: पि ९ रि कॆ. [?] (*pi 9 ri kè. [?]*) ; marked [?].]*

The deity of this sūkta is the praise of food (*anna-stuti*). As Śaunaka says in his Ṛgvidhāna ((ऋग्वि. १-२७) (*(ṛgvi. 1-27)*)), it is the practice of the Āryas from of old to worship and revere food with devotion, then give a small portion to guests and others, and only afterwards eat oneself. It is necessary here to make a little inquiry into the greatness of food. The word *anna* is formed from the root आद-भक्षणे (*āda-bhakṣaṇe*) (*ad*, "to eat"). On the origin of food:

तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः संभूतः । अकाशाद्वायुः । वायोरग्निः । (*tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ | akāśādvāyuḥ | vāyoragniḥ |*)
अग्नेरापः । अद्भ्यः पृथिवी । पृथिव्या ओषधयः । ओषधीभ्योऽन्नं । (*agnerāpaḥ | adbhyaḥ pṛthivī | pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadhībhyo 'nnaṃ |*)
अन्नात्पुरुषः ॥ (*annātpuruṣaḥ ‖*)
(कृ. उ. २-१) (*(kṛ. u. 2-1)*)

so says the Śruti sentence. At the creation of the universe, or of the five elements, from the supreme Brahman (the Supreme Self) first came space, from space air, from air fire, from fire water, from water the earth, from the earth the herbs (plants and the like), from the herbs food; from such food arose man (and other beings too).

*[Stray lines in the supplied text, twice: "[12] Vol. 14".]*

### Printed p. 178

*[Page break of the print; the supplied text prints the header "178 ಸಾಯಣಭಾನ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೪. ಸೂ. ೧೮೭" in the middle of the sentence, with no page marker. The sūkta number is 187.]*

...arose man (and other beings too), it is said. And the answers to the questions "what is the excellence of food? what is the use of food? why is food called *anna*?" are given there too:

अन्नाद्वै प्रजाः प्रजायंते । याः काश्च पृथिवीग् श्रिताः । अथो अन्नेनैव (*annādvai prajāḥ prajāyaṃte | yāḥ kāśca pṛthivīg śritāḥ | atho annenaiva*)
जीवंति । अध्यैनदपियंत्यंततः । अन्नग्ंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठं । तस्मात्सर्वौ- (*jīvaṃti | adhyainadapiyaṃtyaṃtataḥ | annagṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ | tasmātsarvau-*)
षधमुच्यते । सर्वं वै तेऽन्नमाप्नुवंति । येऽन्नं ब्रह्मोपासते । (*ṣadhamucyate | sarvaṃ vai te 'nnamāpnuvaṃti | ye 'nnaṃ brahmopāsate |*)
अन्नग्ंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठं । तस्मात्सर्वौषधमुच्यते । अन्नाद्भूतानि (*annagṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ | tasmātsarvauṣadhamucyate | annādbhūtāni*)
जायंते । जातान्यन्नेन वर्धंते । आद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं (*jāyaṃte | jātānyannena vardhaṃte | ādyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ*)
तदुच्यत इति ॥ (*taducyata iti ‖*)
(कृ. उ. २-२) (*(kṛ. u. 2-2)*)

that is, all creatures that depend on the earth (all living beings too) are born from food, live by food, and in the end are dissolved in it. Among the *bhūtas* (or among things created in the five great elements) food is the eldest of all; therefore it is called *sarvauṣadha* ("the remedy for all"). Those who worship Brahman in the form of food obtain all food, that is, food comes to them in plenty. Food is the eldest of all *bhūtas*.

The *bhūtas* are the five great elements: earth, water, fire, air and space. These five great elements exist as food in their basic form. How? Earth means solid substance. In the food we eat there are always solid things such as grain; these are of the earth part. The second is water. We drink water; besides, in the other things we eat or drink (milk and the like) there is always the part of water. Animals need water more than the earthy (solid) food; in our body too the water part (the blood) is the greater. The third is fire (*tejas*), that is, heat. Animals cannot live without heat; we get heat from the food we take and from the warmth in the sunshine, wind and so on around us. As soon as the heat in the body ceases, death occurs. From birth till death there must be heat in the body; so there is no need to say how necessary heat or *tejas* is. We need one portion more of fire than of water. The fourth is air. When we breathe in, we draw the outside air into the body. We cannot be even a moment without breathing; as soon as breathing stops the life-breath also goes, that is, death occurs. From birth to death air is absolutely necessary for all animals, and it is needed in greater quantity than the solid food, water and fire mentioned before.

### Printed p. 179

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 6.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 179 (as supplied; the Varga number changes here from 5 to 6).*

The fifth is space (*ākāśa*, room). Without space neither we nor other creatures could exist at all. Space is needed for our movements and for the body. Although the three things fire, air and space are not visible to our eyes, they are absolutely necessary for the nourishment of our body; and besides, we (and animals too) need water in one portion more than the earthy solid food; fire more than water; air more than fire; space more than air; and another special point is that in the food belonging to the earth part water, fire, air and space are mingled; in fire there are air and space; in air space is mingled. In this way the five elements and their mixtures, that is, herbs and trees, are arranged as food for animals. Such food is called *anna*; therefore it is called *sarvauṣadha*.

From food the *bhūtas* (living beings) are born. Those born grow and prosper by food alone. It is eaten, and it also eats the beings. Therefore it is called *anna*. Here an explanation is necessary for the last sentence (that food is eaten and that it eats living beings). For the animals that move about in the world, apart from the five elements such as water in their original form, all other food is produced from living beings. There is no food except what relates to living beings. For example, carnivorous animals eat herbivorous animals; herbivores eat plants; plants too have life (how could a plant grow if it were lifeless?); moving living beings must live by eating one another. Since the plant kind does not belong to the moving class, they take their food directly from the earth or from the five elements and grow. Therefore moving beings cannot live without food derived from living beings or from plants. That is why beings eat food and food eats beings, that is, food arises from beings, as said above. The main point is that in the world moving beings (men too) must live by eating one another; without food derived from living beings they cannot live at all. This is the idea stated in the sentences आद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यते (*ādyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyate*) ("it is eaten and it eats beings; therefore it is called *anna*").

There are Śruti sentences also on the matter that food should be worshipped and regarded with respect:

अन्नं न निंद्यात् । तद्व्रतं । प्राणो वा अन्नं । शरीरमन्नादं । प्राणे (*annaṃ na niṃdyāt | tadvrataṃ | prāṇo vā annaṃ | śarīramannādaṃ | prāṇe*)
शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितं । शरीरे प्राणः प्रतिष्ठितः । तदेतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं । (*śarīraṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ | śarīre prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ | tadetadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ |*)

### Printed p. 180

*Running head: [180 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 187].*

स य एतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति । अन्नवानन्नादो भवति । (*sa ya etadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati | annavānannādo bhavati |*)
महान्भवति प्रजया पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन । महान्कीर्त्या ॥ (*mahānbhavati prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena | mahānkīrtyā ‖*)
(कृ. उ. ३-७) (*(kṛ. u. 3-7)*)

One should not disparage food; that is a vow. Life-breath is food. The body eats food and grows by it. The body is established in the life-breath; the life-breath is established in the body. Therefore the life-breath and the body are mutually related. Both are established in food, that is, the growth and protection of body and life-breath come from food alone. Without food neither body nor life-breath can exist. One who knows that food is established in food (in food-form Parabrahman) is honoured. He becomes rich in food and an enjoyer of food. He becomes endowed with offspring, cattle, the radiance of Brahman and fame, and becomes eminent and honoured among men.

अन्नं न परिचक्षीत । तद्व्रतं । आपो वा अन्नं । ज्योतिरन्नादं । अप्पु (*annaṃ na paricakṣīta | tadvrataṃ | āpo vā annaṃ | jyotirannādaṃ | appu*)
ज्योतिः प्रतिष्ठितं । ज्योतिष्यापः प्रतिष्ठिताः । तदेतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं । (*jyotiḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ | jyotiṣyāpaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ | tadetadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ |*)
स य एतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति । अन्नवानन्नादो भवति । (*sa ya etadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati | annavānannādo bhavati |*)
महान्भवति प्रजया पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन । महान्कीर्त्या ॥ (*mahānbhavati prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena | mahānkīrtyā ‖*)
(कृ. उ. ३-८) (*(kṛ. u. 3-8)*)

One should not despise food. Take that as a vow. Water is food; fire (*jyotis*) eats food. Fire is established in water; water is established in fire. These two, fire and water, are established in food (in food are heat and water). One who knows that food is established in food (in food-form Parabrahman) is honoured. He becomes rich in food and an enjoyer of food. He becomes endowed with offspring (children and the like), cattle, the radiance of Brahman and fame, and eminent and honoured among men.

There are also many Śruti proofs on the matter that one should give food to guests and visitors and only then eat oneself.

मोघमन्नं विंदते अप्रचेताः सत्यं ब्रवीमि वध इत्स तस्य । (*moghamannaṃ viṃdate apracetāḥ satyaṃ bravīmi vadha itsa tasya |*)
नार्यमणं पुष्यति नो सखायं केवलाघो भवति केवलादी ॥ (*nāryamaṇaṃ puṣyati no sakhāyaṃ kevalāgho bhavati kevalādī ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-११७-६) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-117-6)*)

... that is, the food (nourishment) won by a miser who gives nothing to anyone is in vain. No benefit comes to him from the food he gains; it becomes the cause of his death (ruin). "I say this is true." It is said that the man who does not offer oblations and the like to the deities Aryaman and the rest, that is, does not give food to the gods, and does not satisfy with food a friend or a guest coming to the house like a friend, but eats alone, is a great sinner. And:

न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानाय पित्वः । (*na sa sakhā yo na dadāti sakhye sacābhuve sacamānāya pitvaḥ |*)
अपास्मात्पेयान्न तदोको अस्ति पृणंतमन्यमरणं चिदिच्छेत् ॥ (*apāsmātpeyānna tadoko asti pṛṇaṃtamanyamaraṇaṃ cidicchet ‖*)
(म. सं १०-११७-४) (*(ma. saṃ 10-117-4)*)

One who does not give food to a friend, to his companion, to one near him, is no friend at all. Therefore one should leave the house of such a man; it is not the only house; there are surely houses of generous people who give food, and it is good to go there: so the ṛṣi describes. For this reason good householders should prepare in the house somewhat more food than is enough for themselves, for the entertainment of guests and visitors. On this matter:

अन्नं बहु कुर्वीत । तद्व्रतं । पृथिवी वा अन्नं । आकाशोऽन्नादः । (*annaṃ bahu kurvīta | tadvrataṃ | pṛthivī vā annaṃ | ākāśo 'nnādaḥ |*)

प्रतिष्ठितं । स य एतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति । अन्नवानन्नादो (*pratiṣṭhitaṃ | sa ya etadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati | annavānannādo*)

(कृ. उ. ३-९) (*(kṛ. u. 3-9)*)

(the reference is printed twice: "ತ್ರೈ. ಉ. ೩-೯" and "ಕೃ. ಉ. ೩-೯"). One should make much food; one should regard that very thing as a vow. The earth is food; space eats food: that is, the plants, grains and the like that grow on the earth are eaten, in the form of oblations, by the gods of the atmosphere (heaven). (The supplied text has ellipsis dots in the Upaniṣad passage, as in the printed original.) These sentences were spoken by the Veda-puruṣa himself. One should not refuse anyone on the plea that there is no room in the house; one should regard that very thing as a vow. Therefore in whatever way one should obtain much food. They say "prepare food for him (the guest)": this is the preparation of food with great respect. In preparing food and giving it to a worthy person there are three kinds, *sāttvika*, *rājasa* and *tāmasa*, as the Lord himself has said:

दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । (*dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe |*)
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्विकं स्मृतं ॥ (*deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sātvikaṃ smṛtaṃ ‖*)

यदन्नं संपादितमस्त्येतदेवान्नं मुखतो राद्धं भवति । मुख्य देशे (*yadannaṃ saṃpāditamastyetadevānnaṃ mukhato rāddhaṃ bhavati | mukhya deśe*)
तीर्थक्षेत्रविशेषे मुख्यकाले संक्रांत्यमावास्यादिरूपे मुख्यायाभ्यागताय (*tīrthakṣetraviśeṣe mukhyakāle saṃkrāṃtyamāvāsyādirūpe mukhyāyābhyāgatāya*)
वेदशास्त्रतदध्ययनानुष्ठानपराय मुख्यया वृत्ता श्रद्धाप्रणिपातसत्कारादिरूपया (*vedaśāstratadadhyayanānuṣṭhānaparāya mukhyayā vṛttā śraddhāpraṇipātasatkārādirūpayā*)
मुख्यन दात्रा सात्विकेन दत्तमित्यर्थः । यः पुमानेवं सात्विकं दानप्रकारं (*mukhyana dātrā sātvikena dattamityarthaḥ | yaḥ pumānevaṃ sātvikaṃ dānaprakāraṃ*)
वेद विदित्वानुतिष्ठति अस्मै जन्मांतरे मुख्यक्रमणैवान्नं संपद्यते । (*veda viditvānutiṣṭhati asmai janmāṃtare mukhyakramaṇaivānnaṃ saṃpadyate |*)

The *sāttvika* gift means that while giving, one should not keep any expectation of some return from the receiver afterwards. A gift given in truth, without any hope of return, considering place, time, and the worthiness or unworthiness of the receiver, is called *sāttvika*. For example, in sacred places such as *tīrtha*-kṣetras, on special days such as the solstice (*saṃkrānti*) and the new-moon day, food should be given to a guest or visitor, whether invited or coming of his own accord. It is still better if that guest is accomplished in the study of the Veda and śāstras, practises them and is of good conduct. Such a man should be honoured with faith, received and entertained, and given food.

### Printed p. 183

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 6. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 183 (as supplied).*

(The sentence continues:) If food is given to any man afflicted with hunger, and above all to a guest or visitor with the qualities stated above, it becomes a *sāttvika* gift, and the giver in later births lives happily, with abundance of food. That is explained here by the sentences एतद्वै मुखतोऽन्नग्ं राद्धं । मुखतोऽस्मा अन्नग्ं राज्यते [?] (*etadvai mukhato 'nnagṃ rāddhaṃ | mukhato 'smā annagṃ rājyate [?]*) ("this food is prepared at the head; for him food is prepared at the head"). Now the second and third kinds, *rājasa* and *tāmasa* gifts, are as follows:

यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । (*yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |*)
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्राजसमुदाहृतं ॥ (*dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtaṃ ‖*)
आदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते । (*ādeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate |*)
असत्पतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतं ॥ (*asatpatamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtaṃ ‖*)

A gift made by a man who looks for a return is a *rājasa* gift. For example: "If today I give food to this man, tomorrow or some day later he too will honour me in the same way": a gift made with such a thought is called *rājasa*. Such a gift is explained here by the sentences एतद्वै मध्यतोऽन्नग्ं राद्धं । मध्यतोऽस्मा अन्नग्ं राध्यते (*etadvai madhyato 'nnagṃ rāddhaṃ | madhyato 'smā annagṃ rādhyate*) ("this food is prepared in the middle; for him food is prepared in the middle").

Besides, a gift made without considering place, time and worthiness, without proper respect, merely for self-praise, is called *tāmasa*; that is, given in a reproachable place, at an improper time such as midnight, to an unworthy man, that is, one who is not troubled by hunger and has eaten to the throat and has no need of any food, a hospitality or gift made out of conceit, so that another may see and admire one's hospitality, is called unrighteous. This is explained here by the sentences एतद्वा अंततोन्नग्ं राद्धं । अंततोऽस्मा अन्नग्ं राज्यते [?] (*etadvā aṃtatonnagṃ rāddhaṃ | aṃtato 'smā annagṃ rājyate [?]*) ("this food is prepared at the end; for him food is prepared at the end"). Therefore, knowing all these matters well, one should give food at the right time to a worthy recipient.

It is explained that if a man worships food as the form of Parabrahman, he gets the fruit according to his attitude of worship. For example:

### Printed p. 184

तत्पतिष्ठेत्युपासीत । प्रतिष्ठावान्भवति (*tatpatiṣṭhetyupāsīta | pratiṣṭhāvānbhavati*) — if he worships it as "establishment" he becomes endowed with the means of happiness such as food and clothing and has an established position. One who worships it as radiance (*mahaḥ*) becomes rich in wealth and the like, endowed with the qualities of greatness and worthy of honour. One who worships it as mind (*manaḥ*) becomes endowed with the power of thought. One who worships it as *namaḥ* (worthy of salutation) is saluted by all and holds all in his power. All desires of this man, that is, all his wishes, are subject to him, that is, are fulfilled (the supplied text has "ಇவனுக்கு" here, in Tamil script; rewritten in Kannada letters as इवनुक्कु [?] (*ivanukku [?]*) and marked [?]). One who worships it as Brahman becomes a knower of the Vedas and the secret principles of their meaning. One who worships it as तद्ब्रह्मणः परिमर (*tadbrahmaṇaḥ parimara*) ("the dying around of Brahman") finds his enemies, afflictions and diseases around him destroyed; all enemies, haters and unfriendly ones are utterly destroyed. He who is in this man, and he who is in the Sun, is the same. One who has this knowledge, departing from this world, passes beyond the states of the self called *annamaya*, *prāṇamaya*, *manomaya*, *vijñānamaya* and *ānandamaya*, and, becoming a *vidyādhara* (a god with the power of taking whatever forms he wishes), enjoying desires, wanders here and there singing these *sāman* verses (as the Upaniṣad says above). "What a wonder this is! I am food, I am the eater of food, I am the praiser; I was born before the Truth (*ṛta*), and before the gods, in the navel of immortality (in the middle). He who gives to me becomes like me. I am food. I eat him who eats food. I conquer this whole universe, this world. One who knows this becomes like a golden light." There are many such descriptions of food, or of the deity (Brahman) who is the lord of food. There are many more mantras in the Vedas that contain matters about food; for fear of too long a book they cannot all be explained here.

*Gist:* "Pitum nu" is the eighth sūkta of this group, of eleven ṛks, by Agastya, to the deity Food, in *gāyatrī*; the first ṛk is *anuṣṭubh-bṛhatī*, and Śaunaka prescribes its use for honouring food and eating without contempt.

### Printed p. 185

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 185 (as supplied). The window starts at the p. 185 marker, after Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 187 (p. 184).*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with पितुं नु (*pituṃ nu*) is the eighth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Agastya is the seer of this sūkta, the praise of food is the deity, and the metre is *gāyatrī*. The first ṛk has the metre called *anuṣṭubh-garbhoṣṭik* (the supplied text prints "ಗರ್ಭೋಷ್ಟಿಕ್"); in the Anukramaṇikā it is said आद्यः पंचकस्त्रयोऽष्टका अनुष्टुप् गर्भा (*ādyaḥ paṃcakastrayo 'ṣṭakā anuṣṭup garbhā*) ((अनु. ५-७) (*(anu. 5-7)*)). The third, fifth, sixth, seventh and eleventh ṛks of this sūkta are in the *anuṣṭubh* metre; and in the Anukramaṇikā it is said पितुं नन्न स्तुतिर्गायत्रं त्वाद्यानुष्टुब्गर्भा तृतीयांत्ये (*pituṃ nanna stutirgāyatraṃ tvādyānuṣṭubgarbhā tṛtīyāṃtye*) पंचम्याध्याश्च तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभ इति (*paṃcamyādhyāśca tisro 'nuṣṭubha iti*) (the supplied text has "ಪಿತುಂ ನನ್ನ" for the Sanskrit "*pitum nu*"; kept as supplied). On the application (*viniyoga*) of this sūkta Śaunaka says in his work the Ṛgvidhāna:

पितुं नित्युपतिष्ठेत नित्यमन्नमुपस्थितं । (*pituṃ nityupatiṣṭheta nityamannamupasthitaṃ |*)
पूजयेदशनं नित्यं भुंजीत ह्यविकुत्सयन् ॥ (*pūjayedaśanaṃ nityaṃ bhuṃjīta hyavikutsayan ‖*)
नास्य स्यादन्नजो व्याधिर्विषमप्यमृतं भवेत् । (*nāsya syādannajo vyādhirviṣamapyamṛtaṃ bhavet |*)
विषं च पीत्वैतत्तूक्तं जपेद्विषविनाशनं ॥ (*viṣaṃ ca pītvaitattūktaṃ japedviṣavināśanaṃ ‖*)
नावाग्यतस्तु भुंजीत नाशुचिर्न जुगुप्सितं । (*nāvāgyatastu bhuṃjīta nāśucirna jugupsitaṃ |*)
दद्याच्च पूजयेच्चैव जुहुयाच्च हविस्तदा ॥ (*dadyācca pūjayeccaiva juhuyācca havistadā ‖*)
क्षुद्भयं नास्य किंचित्सान्नान्नजं व्याधिमाप्पुयात् ॥ (*kṣudbhayaṃ nāsya kiṃcitsānnānnajaṃ vyādhimāppuyāt ‖*)
(यग्विधान. १-२७) [?] (*(yagvidhāna. 1-27) [?]*)

(the reference is printed "(ಯಗ್ವಿಧಾನ. ೧-೨೭) [?]" for Ṛgvidhāna). This sūkta beginning "pitum nu" should be recited daily at meal-time with devotion, food should be honoured and then one should eat. One should never reproach food. If one does so, the troubles such as disease that can arise from faults of food will not occur; even poison becomes nectar. If, through some other cause, that is, unknowingly, one takes poison, the poison is removed if this sūkta is muttered. While eating one should not chatter but eat with restraint and in purity. One should not eat food that is loathsome, disagreeable or reprehensible. At meal-time one should give a little of the food to others, honour the food, offer an oblation in the fire, and only then eat oneself. For one who does so there is no affliction from hunger, and no disease arising from improper food touches him: thus the greatness of this sūkta is explained.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यस्य (*yasya*) — of which food. ओजसा (*ojasā*) — by the life-giving power. त्रितः (*tritaḥ*) — Indra, famed in the three worlds (*trita*). वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*) — the demon Vṛtra. विपर्वं (*viparvaṃ*) — (making him) one with severed joints. वि आर्दयत् (*vi ārdayat*) — utterly destroyed. (Such food:) महः (*mahaḥ*) — great. धराणं (*dharāṇaṃ*) — all-supporting (or: of the great world, the upholder). तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*) — strong. पितुं (*pituṃ*) — protecting food. नु (*nu*) — quickly. स्तोषं (*stoṣaṃ*) — I praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

I quickly praise that food which is life-giving, great, the upholder of the world, strong and protecting, by whose life-giving power Indra, famed in all three worlds, cut the joints of the demon Vṛtra and destroyed him.

**Printed English translation**

I glorify Pitu, the great, the upholder, the strong, by whose invigorating power Trita slew the mutilated Vritra.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

पितुं—पालकमन्नं (*pituṃ—pālakamannaṃ*) — "the protecting food": the meaning is food that protects us from the affliction of hunger. The word *pitu* is read among the twenty-eight names of food, *andhaḥ*, *vājaḥ* and others ((नि. ३-९) (*(ni. 3-9)*)). Besides, Yāska:

पितुरित्यन्ननाम पातेर्वा, पिबतेर्वा, प्यायतेर्वा । (*piturityannanāma pātervā, pibatervā, pyāyatervā |*)
(सि. ९-२४) (*(si. 9-24)*)
ऎंदु पितु शब्दद निर्वचनवन्नु हेळिद्दारॆ. ऎंदरॆ—पातेर्वा—नम्मन्नु हसिविनिंद कापाडु (*èṃdu pitu śabdada nirvacanavannu heḷiddārè. èṃdarè—pātervā—nammannu hasiviniṃda kāpāḍu*)

has given the derivation of the word *pitu*: that is, *pātervā*: because it protects us from hunger, *pitu* means food; or because it is used for drinking it is called *pitu*, it also applies to liquid food (milk and the like), so it is used for drinking and may be formed from the root *pā* (*pib*) "to drink"; or it may be formed from the root *pyāy* (the supplied text has "ಪ್ರ್ಯಾಯ" for *pyāyate*), which gives the sense "to satisfy". Taking the very ṛk in which this word occurs as the example, he has given its explanation:

पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीं । (*pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīṃ |*)
यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥ (*yasya trito vyojasā vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat ‖*)
तं पितुं स्तौमि महतो धारयितारं बलस्य । तविषीति बलनाम तवतेर्वा (*taṃ pituṃ staumi mahato dhārayitāraṃ balasya | taviṣīti balanāma tavatervā*)
वृद्धिकर्मणः । यस्य त्रित ओजसा बलेन त्रितस्त्रिस्थान इंद्रो वृत्रं विपर्वाणं (*vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ | yasya trita ojasā balena tritastristhāna iṃdro vṛtraṃ viparvāṇaṃ*)
व्यर्दयति ॥ (*vyardayati ‖*)

[the window ends here with the Nirukta passage and its reference (printed "(ನಿ. ೯-೨೫)")].

### Printed p. 188

*Running head: [188 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24. Sū. 187] (the print has "ಆ." for the second abbreviation, as supplied). The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 of Sūkta 187 (the word *pitu*) from p. 187, after the Nirukta passage.*

... having said this: "I praise the food that gives great strength; Indra, pervading the three worlds, having obtained the nourishment of this food and with its help become mighty, crushed and destroyed all the joints of the demon Vṛtra": this is the sense. The word *pitu* (in the sense of food) occurs in the ṛks ऋ. सं. १-६१-७, १-१३२-६, १-१८७-१, ६-२०-४ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-61-7, 1-132-6, 1-187-1, 6-20-4*) and others, and in places such as अथ. वे. ४-६-३ ; तै. सं. ५-७-२-४, वा सं २-२०, १२-६५, ऐ. ब्रा. १-१३ (*atha. ve. 4-6-3 ; tai. saṃ. 5-7-2-4, vā saṃ 2-20, 12-65, ai. brā. 1-13*) (the supplied text has "ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಚ" [?] for "ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದ" in the first line; marked [?]).

महो धर्माणं-महांतं धर्माणं सर्वस्य धारकं । महतो लोकस्य (*maho dharmāṇaṃ-mahāṃtaṃ dharmāṇaṃ sarvasya dhārakaṃ | mahato lokasya*) धारकं (*dhārakaṃ*) — "great, the upholder of all; the upholder of the great world": Sāyaṇa's explanation is "that which sustains the whole, that is, the great world and the beings of the world". Yāska says महतो धारयितारं बलस्य (*mahato dhārayitāraṃ balasya*), "that which produces great strength". Since this is an epithet of the word *pituṃ*, and since food has the power to give nourishment and strength to one who partakes of it, both senses fit.

तविषीं—तविषीति बलनाम (*taviṣīṃ—taviṣīti balanāma*) — "*taviṣī* is a name of strength". Since the word *taviṣī* is read among the twenty-eight names of strength, *ojaḥ*, *pājaḥ* and others ((नि. ३-९) (*(ni. 3-9)*)), *taviṣīṃ* means strength, power. It is known to all that men and other animals get strength and power by taking food. Or the Nirukta-authors have given for the word *taviṣī* the derivation तवतेर्वा वृद्धिकर्मणः (*tavatervā vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ*), so that this word is formed from the root *tavati*, "to make grow", and the sense is explained: by taking food the body grows and prospers.

त्रितः (*tritaḥ*) — the bhāṣyakāra explains the word *tritaḥ* as विस्तीर्णतमः (*vistīrṇatamaḥ*), and the Nirukta-author as त्रितिस्तीर्ण- (*tritistīrṇa-*) तमः (नि ४-६) (*tamaḥ (ni 4-6)*): that is, "pervading all, widely extended". Besides, the Nirukta-author in explaining this ṛk says त्रितस्तिस्थान इंद्रः (*tritastisthāna iṃdraḥ*): "Trita is Indra of three places"; *tristhāna* means earth, atmosphere and heaven: the sense is Indra of unobstructed power in all three worlds. *Tritaḥ* may also mean Trita Āptya. The relation between Trita Āptya and Indra, the meaning of the word *trita*, and other related matters we have explained at length in the Ṛ. Saṃ. part 5, pp. 230-231, in the introduction to part 8, pp. iii-viii, and in part 8, pp. 443-447. In the present ṛk *tritaḥ* means Indra, who is glorious in the threefold places, earth, atmosphere and heaven.

वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् (*vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat*) — among Indra's heroic deeds the slaying of Vṛtra is the most important. This is described:

इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यानि चकार प्रथमानि वज्रे । (*iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yāni cakāra prathamāni vajre |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-३२-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-32-1)*)

### Printed p. 189

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 6 ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 189 (as supplied, "೮. ೨" for "ಅ. ೨").*

in the sūkta ऋ सं १-३२ (*ṛ saṃ 1-32*) that begins thus, and in many other places, in many ways. For this very reason the name *vṛtrahā*, "slayer of Vṛtra", is famous for Indra. That Indra slew Vṛtra by his own power is said in the ṛks ऋ. सं. १-१६५-८ ; ७-२१-६, १०-१३८-६ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-165-8 ; 7-21-6, 10-138-6*) and others. And there are descriptions that for the battle with Vṛtra the gods increased his prowess (ऋ. सं. १०-११३ ८ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-113 8*)), or supplied him with strength and power (ऋ. सं. १०-८०-५, ६-२०-२, १०-४८-३, १०-१२०-३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-80-5, 6-20-2, 10-48-3, 10-120-3*)), or put the thunderbolt in his hand (ऋ. सं २-२०-८ (*ṛ. saṃ 2-20-8*)). Most of all the Maruts are the ones who urge him and support him (ऋ. सं. ३-३२-४, १०-७३-१ (*ṛ. saṃ. 3-32-4, 10-73-1*), etc.); even when all the other gods fled in fear of Vṛtra (ऋ. सं. ८-८५-७, ४-१८-११, ऐ. ब्रा. ३-२० (*ṛ. saṃ. 8-85-7, 4-18-11, ai. brā. 3-20*)) the Maruts alone helped Indra. But it is also said that the Maruts once abandoned him (ऋ. सं. ८-७-३१ (*ṛ. saṃ. 8-7-31*)); and there are descriptions here and there that Agni, Soma and Viṣṇu helped Indra when he fought with Vṛtra. In the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas there is a long history of the slaying of the demon Vṛtra.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

पितुम् (*pitum*) (root पा पाने (*pā pāne*)): by पः किच्च (उ. सू. १-२०) (*paḥ kicca (u. sū. 1-20)*) the suffix *tu*; because it is marked *k*, *i* for the *ā* of the root; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. स्तोषम् (*stoṣam*) (root ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ (*ṣṭuñ stutau*)): Vedic *luṅ*; first person singular; the augment *aṭ* does not occur by the Vedic rule; the verb-*nighāta* accent. धर्माणम् (*dharmāṇam*) (root धृञ् धारणे (*dhṛñ dhāraṇe*)): by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) (*anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyaṃte (pā. sū. 3-2-75)*) the suffix *manin*; by *vyatyaya* the first syllable of the suffix is acute. विपर्वम् (*viparvam*) ("him from whom the joint is gone"): by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) the accent of the earlier member. अर्दयत् (*ardayat*) (root अर्द हिंसायां (*arda hiṃsāyāṃ*)): *curādi*; *luṅ*; third person singular *tip*; loss of *i*; by सत्यापपाश—(पा. सू. ३-१-२५) (*satyāpapāśa—(pā. sū. 3-1-25)*) the suffix *ṇic* in the own sense; because of the *śap* suffix guṇa of *ṇic*; the substitute *ay*; the augment *aṭ* does not occur by the Vedic rule; because of the connection with *yat* there is no *nighāta*; the accent of *ṇic* remains.

#### Ṛk 2

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads संख्याशास्त्र (*saṃkhyāśāstra*); standard label inserted. The Saṃhitā has नवृमहे [?] (*navṛmahe [?]*) against the Pada's *vavṛmahe*; marked [?].]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्वादो॑ पितो॒ मधो॑ पितो व॒यं त्वा॑ नवृमहे [?] ।
> अ॒स्माक॑मवि॒ता भ॑व ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्वादो इति । पितो इति । मधो इति । पितो इति । वयं । त्वा । ववृमहे ।
> अस्माकं । अविता । भव ॥ २ ॥

> *svādo iti | pito iti | madho iti | pito iti | vayaṃ | tvā | vavṛmahe |*
> *asmākaṃ | avitā | bhava ‖ 2 ‖*

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads साह्यभाष्यं (*sāhyabhāṣyaṃ*) (inside the Pada block); standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे स्वादो आस्वादनीय पितो पालक मधो माधुर्योपेत पितो हे
> पानसाधनान्न वयं त्वा त्वां ववृमहे । सेवामहे ॥ अत्र सर्वत्राननुदात्तानां
> पूर्वस्यासामान्यवचनत्वेनानिघातत्वं । अनुदात्तानां तु विशेषवचनत्वान्निघातत्वं ॥
> असकृत्पितुशब्दश्रवणं तस्य प्राशस्त्यज्ञापनार्थं । हे पितो अस्माकमविता तर्पयिता
> भव ॥

*Gist:* O savoury, protecting, sweet food, drink-giving: we serve you; be our satisfier. The repetition of *pito* shows its excellence.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

स्वादो—रुचिकरवू (*svādo—rucikaravū*) (tasty). पितो—पालकवू (*pito—pālakavū*) (protecting). मधो—माधुर्योपेतवू (*madho—mādhuryopetavū*) (sweet). पितो— (*pito—*) पानसाधनवू आद ऎलै अन्नवे (*pānasādhanavū āda èlai annave*) (a means of drink): O food! वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we. त्वा (*tvā*) — you. ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*) — we serve. अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*) — to us. अविता (*avitā*) — protector (satisfier). भव (*bhava*) — be.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads बनार्थ (*banārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O food, worthy of being tasted, protecting, sweet and a means of drink, we serve you. Be our satisfier.

**Printed English translation**

Savoury Pitu ; sweet Pitu ; we worship you : become our protector.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

स्वादो पितो मधो पितो (*svādo pito madho pito*) — *svādu* means tasty, wholesome to eat. That *pito* is addressed here twice shows the extreme regard and esteem the praiser has for food.

अविता-तर्पयिता (*avitā-tarpayitā*) — the bhāṣyakāra's explanation is "one who satisfies". *Avitā* may also be understood as "protector": one who removes the affliction of hunger and protects.

### Printed p. 191

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 191 (as supplied).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 2, noted briefly)

स्वादो (*svādo*): being at the beginning of the pāda, no vocative *nighāta* accent; by आमंत्रितस्य— (*āmaṃtritasya—*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१९८ (*pā. sū. 6-1-198*)) the initial syllable is acute. ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*) (root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*)): *laṭ*, first person plural, suffix *mahiṅ*; by टितआत्मनेपादानां टे— (*ṭitaātmanepādānāṃ ṭe—*) (पा सू. ३-४-७९ (*pā sū. 3-4-79*)) the *ṭi* becomes *e*; by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *śluvikaraṇa* and reduplication of the root; the verb-*nighāta* accent. The supplied text then repeats the final word "it comes" once (dropped). अविता (*avitā*) (root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*)): suffix *tṛc* in the agent sense; by चितः (*citaḥ*) the last syllable is acute. पितो (*pito*): the vocative form of a different noun; since a vocative also precedes, the rule आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmaṃtritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat*) (पा. सू. ८-१-७२ (*pā. sū. 8-1-72*)) would make the earlier one count as non-existent, but by नामंत्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम् (*nāmaṃtrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam*) (पा. सू. ८-१-७९ (*pā. sū. 8-1-79*)) this does not apply; as the head noun is the qualified word and *svādo* the general qualifier, the earlier general word is not treated as absent, so the vocative *nighāta* accent falls on the qualified word. The same holds for the following qualifiers.

> मयोभुः । अद्विषेण्यः । सखा । सुशेवः । अद्वयाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *mayobhuḥ | adviṣeṇyaḥ | sakhā | suśevaḥ | advayāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 192

*Running head: [192 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1 A. 24. Sū. 187] (as supplied).*

> रसः । प्रियरस इत्यर्थः । सखा सखिवत्प्रियकारी सुशेवोऽत एव सुष्टु सुखकरोऽ-
> द्वया द्वयरहित उक्तगुण एव न तु तद्विपरीतो भवेत्यर्थः । अथवा दृष्टांत-
> वादोऽयं । सुशेवोऽद्वया मनःकर्मविसंवादरहितः सखा यथा मयोभुर-
> द्वेष्यश्च भवति तद्वत्त्वमपि भवेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* O Pito, being auspicious, come to us with auspicious aids, giving delight, not distasteful in flavour, friend-like, well respected, free of duplicity; or: as a sincere friend is.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पितो—पालकवाद ऎलै अन्नवे (*pito—pālakavāda èlai annave*) (O protecting food). शिवः—मंगळात्मकनाद नीनु (*śivaḥ—maṃgaḷātmakanāda nīnu*) (you, auspicious). शिवाभिः—मंगळ करगळाद (*śivābhiḥ—maṃgaḷa karagaḷāda*) (auspicious). ऊतिभिः—रक्षणॆगळॊंदिगॆ (*ūtibhiḥ—rakṣaṇègaḷòṃdigè*) (with aids). नः उप—नम्म समीपक्कॆ (*naḥ upa—namma samīpakkè*) (to us, near). आ च—आगमिसु (*ā ca—āgamisu*) (come). सुशेवः—श्रेष्ठवागि गौरविसल्पडुववनू (*suśevaḥ—śreṣṭhavāgi gauravisalpaḍuvavanū*) (greatly respected); अद्वयाः—मनस्सु मत्तु कर्म इवुगळिगॆ ऐक्यतॆ यन्नु संपादिसिरुववनू (*advayāḥ—manassu mattu karma ivugaḷigè aikyatè yannu saṃpādisiruvavanū*) (one who has brought mind and action into unity); सखा—स्नेहितनू (*sakhā—snehitanū*) (friend); मयोभुः—सुखवन्नुंटुमाडुववनू (*mayobhuḥ—sukhavannuṃṭumāḍuvavanū*) (bringer of happiness); अद्विषेण्यः—द्वेषरहितनू आगु (*adviṣeṇyaḥ—dveṣarahitanū āgu*) (be free of hatred). Alternatively: मयोभुः—संतोषकारकनू (*mayobhuḥ—saṃtoṣakārakanū*) (a giver of delight); अद्विषेण्यः— (*adviṣeṇyaḥ—*) अनिष्टवाद रसरहितनागि (प्रियवाद रसवुळ्ळवनू) (*aniṣṭavāda rasarahitanāgi (priyavāda rasavuḷḷavanū)*) (without unpleasant flavour, i.e. of agreeable flavour); सखा—सुहृत्तिनंतॆ प्रियवन्नुंटुमाडु ववनू (*sakhā—suhṛttinaṃtè priyavannuṃṭumāḍu vavanū*) (doing what is dear like a friend); सुशेवः—(आदुदरिंदले) सेविसलु अर्हनू (*suśevaḥ—(ādudariṃdale) sevisalu arhanū*) (therefore worthy of being served); अद्वयाः—पूज्यनू, ग्राह्यनू आद गुणविल्लदे बेरॆ विधवाद गुणविल्लदवनू (आगु) (*advayāḥ—pūjyanū, grāhyanū āda guṇavillade berè vidhavāda guṇavilladavanū (āgu)*) (without any quality other than the stated worshipful and acceptable one; be so).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O auspicious food, come to us with your auspicious aids; be a giver of delight to the sacrificer, of agreeable flavour free of the unpleasant, doing what is dear like a friend, and therefore worthy of worship and of being served.

**Printed English translation**

Come to us, Pitu, auspicious with auspicious aids ; a source of delight not unpalatable, a friend well respected, and having none (bnt [sic] agreeable properties).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

शिवः, शिवाभिः, सुशेवः (*śivaḥ, śivābhiḥ, suśevaḥ*) — the word *śivaḥ* is stated among the twenty names of happiness (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)), so *śivaḥ* means happiness. The bhāṣyakāra explains it as "auspicious". Yāska, in the explanation of the ṛk

अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन् । सखा सुशेव एधि नः । (*amīvahā vāstoṣpate viśvā rūpāṇyāviśan | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ |*)
(म. सं. ७-५५-१) (*(ma. saṃ. 7-55-1)*)

explains the word *śeva* as follows: शेव इति सुखनाम (*śeva iti sukhanāma*), "*śeva* is a name of happiness", शिष्यतेर्नकारो नामकरणोऽन्तस्थांतरोपलिंगी (*śiṣyaternakāro nāmakaraṇo 'ntasthāṃtaropaliṃgī*) and विभाषितगुण शिवमित्यस्य भवति (*vibhāṣitaguṇa śivamityasya bhavati*) (a grammatical-etymological remark which the print leaves in this form; not explained further here).

### Printed p. 193

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 193 (as supplied).*

(नि. १०-१७) (*(ni. 10-17)*): having stated the sense "happiness" for the word *śeva*, he shows that *śiva* has the same sense. In lexicons the word *śiva* is given the sense "auspicious". There is no objection to saying that whatever produces happiness is auspicious. Hence in the present ṛk both senses, "producing happiness" and "auspicious", are suitable.

मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*) — the word *mayaḥ* too, being stated among the twenty names of happiness beginning with शिंबाता, शतरा [?] (*śiṃbātā, śatarā [?]*) (readings uncertain), means happiness. One who produces happiness is named *mayobhuḥ*. The word *mayobhuḥ* in the sense "producing happiness" is used often in the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas.

अद्विषेण्यः—अद्वेष्यरसः (*adviṣeṇyaḥ—adveṣyarasaḥ*) — "of a flavour not hateful"; that is, not causing hatred, or having a beneficial flavour (taste). The sense is: dear and tasty.

सखा-सखिवप्रियकारी (*sakhā-sakhivapriyakārī*) — "doing what is dear, like a friend". Since a friend always desires one's good and does what is dear, food too is desirable to all and does good; so the sage addresses food, out of great affection, with the respectful word *sakhā*, "friend".

अद्वयाः—द्वयरहितः उक्तगुण एव न तु तद्विपरीतो भवेत्यर्थः (*advayāḥ—dvayarahitaḥ uktaguṇa eva na tu tadviparīto bhavetyarthaḥ*) — the bhāṣyakāra explains in one way: without any quality other than the worshipful and acceptable one; and in another way, अद्वयाः मनःकर्मविसंवादरहितः (*advayāḥ manaḥkarmavisaṃvādarahitaḥ*): free from disagreement between mind and action, that is, doing good wholeheartedly, without being of one kind in mind and another in deed. In worldly dealings it is not impossible to see those who pretend to be friends speak good words with the mouth only and in action do the contrary, harm. Therefore food is praised as having the nature of doing good while remaining of one kind in both mind and action.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 3, noted briefly)

चर (*cara*) (root चर गतिभक्षणयोः (*cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*)): *loṭ*, second person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent. शिवः (*śivaḥ*) (शीते अस्मिन् सर्वमिति शिवः (*śīte asmin sarvamiti śivaḥ*), root शीज् स्वप्ने (*śīj svapne*)): formed by सर्व निघृष्टरिष्टलष्टशिव— (*sarva nighṛṣṭariṣṭalaṣṭaśiva—*) (उ. सू. १-१५१ (*u. sū. 1-151*)) with the suffix *va*, irregularly. अद्विषेण्यः (*adviṣeṇyaḥ*) (root द्विष अप्रीत् (*dviṣa aprīt*)): the Uṇādi suffix *eṇya*; *nañ* as first member; in a bahuvrīhi, by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२ (*pā. sū. 6-2-172*)) the last syllable of the final member is acute.

### Printed p. 194

*Running head: [194 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 187] (as supplied).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (continuation of the Ṛk 3 grammar page, noted briefly)

सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*) (root शीज् स्वप्ने (*śīj svapne*)): by इण् शीज्भ्यां वन् (*iṇ śījbhyāṃ van*) (उ. सू. १-१५० (*u. sū. 1-150*)) the suffix *van*; by सार्वधातुकार्ध— (*sārvadhātukārdha—*) guṇa; being marked *n*, the initial syllable is acute. In the compound, overriding the *su* accent, by आद्युदात्तं द्वैच् छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvaic chaṃdasi*) (पा. सू. ६-२-११९ (*pā. sū. 6-2-119*)) the final member gets the acute on its first syllable. अद्वयाः (*advayāḥ*): by तत्पुरुषे तुल्या— (*tatpuruṣe tulyā—*) (पा. सू. ६-२-२ (*pā. sū. 6-2-2*)) the first member *nañ* keeps its natural accent.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तव॒ तै [?] पि॑तो॒ रसा॒ रजां॒स्यनु॒ विष्ठि॑ताः ।
> दि॒वि वाता॑ इव श्रि॒ताः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava tai [?] pito rasā rajāṃsyanu viṣṭhitāḥ |*
> *divi vātā iva śritāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

*[The Saṃhitā has तै [?] (*tai [?]*) against the Pada's *tye*; marked [?].]*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तव । त्ये । पितो इति । रसाः । रजांसि । अनु । विस्थिताः ।
> दिवि । वातार्षइव [?] । श्रिताः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava | tye | pito iti | rasāḥ | rajāṃsi | anu | visthitāḥ |*
> *divi | vātārṣaiva [?] | śritāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

*[The Pada prints वातार्षइव [?] (*vātārṣaiva [?]*) for *vātāḥ iva*; marked [?].]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे पितो तव त्वत्संबंधिनस्ये ते स्वाद्वम्लादिषड्रसा रजांसि लोकाल्लोक-
> स्थानार्थानन्वानुकूल्येन विष्ठिताः । विविधं स्थिताः । विविधस्थितौ दृष्टांतः । दिवि द्युलो-
> केंतरिक्षे श्रिता वाता नायवः ते यथा व्याप्तस्तद्वत् ॥

*Gist:* O Pito, those six flavours of yours, sweet, sour and the rest, are variously spread through the worlds as the winds are spread in the sky.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पितो—ऎलै अन्नवे (*pito—èlai annave*) (O food). दिवि—अंतरिक्षदल्लि (*divi—aṃtarikṣadalli*) (in the atmosphere). श्रिताः—आश्रयिसि प्रसरिसिरुव (*śritāḥ—āśrayisi prasarisiruva*) (spread, resting). वाताः इव—वायुगळु सर्वत्र व्याप्तवागिरुवंतॆ (*vātāḥ iva—vāyugaḷu sarvatra vyāptavāgiruvaṃtè*) (as the winds are diffused everywhere). ते--निन्न (*te--ninna*) (your). त्ये रसाः—प्रसिद्धवाद आम्लादि षड्र सगळू सह (*tye rasāḥ—prasiddhavāda āmlādi ṣaḍra sagaḷū saha*) (the well-known six flavours, sour and the rest). रजांसि—लोकगळन्नॆल्ला (*rajāṃsi—lokagaḷannèllā*) (all the worlds). अनुविष्ठिताः—लोकक्कॆ अनुकूलकरवागिरुवंतॆ विध विधवागि प्रसरिसि व्यापिसिवॆ (*anuviṣṭhitāḥ—lokakkè anukūlakaravāgiruvaṃtè vidha vidhavāgi prasarisi vyāpisivè*) (are spread in many ways, favourably for the world).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O food, as the winds spread in the atmosphere pervade everywhere, so your six flavours, sour and the rest, pervade all the worlds in many ways and are favourable to the world.

### Printed p. 195

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 195 (as supplied).*

**Printed English translation**

Your flavours, Pitu, are diffused through the regions, as the winds are spread through the sky.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

त्ये—ते (*tye—te*) — wherever the word *tya* occurs in the Ṛgveda it has the sense of the word *tad*, "that". The Nirukta-authors

त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानां । (*tyamū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānāṃ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-१७८-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-178-1)*)

प्रति त्यं चारुमध्वरं गोपीथाय प्र हूयसे । मरुद्धिरग्न आ गहि ॥ (*prati tyaṃ cārumadhvaraṃ gopīthāya pra hūyase | maruddhiragna ā gahi ‖*)
(ऋ. सं १-१९-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ 1-19-1)*)

in these and other ṛks explain the word *tyaṃ* as *taṃ*, "him" (नि. १०-२९, ३७ (*ni. 10-29, 37*)).

रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) — the word *rajaḥ* is read among the thirty names of night, *śyāvī*, *kṣapā* and others (नि. २-१८ (*ni. 2-18*)), and Yāska, explaining the sense of *rajaḥ*, says:

रजः । रजो रजतेर्जोर्यती रज उच्यते । उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका (*rajaḥ | rajo rajaterjoryatī raja ucyate | udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā*)
रजांस्युच्यंते ॥ (*rajāṃsyucyaṃte ‖*)
(नि. ४-१९) (*(ni. 4-19)*)

Since it is derived from the root *rajati* in the sense "to shine", *rajaḥ* means light; *rajaḥ* also means water; the plural *rajāṃsi* also means worlds: so Yāska explains, and as an example

भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश्च नेता यत्रा नियुद्भिः सचसे शिवाभिः । (*bhuvo yajñasya rajasaśca netā yatrā niyudbhiḥ sacase śivābhiḥ |*)
दिवि मूर्धानं दधिषे स्वर्षां जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहं ॥ (*divi mūrdhānaṃ dadhiṣe svarṣāṃ jihvāmagne cakṛṣe havyavāhaṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-८-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-8-6)*)

shows that in this ṛk the word *rajasaḥ* has the sense "water", and in

रजांसि चित्रा विचरंति तान्यवः । (*rajāṃsi citrā vicaraṃti tānyavaḥ |*)
अद्या चिन्नू चित्रदपो नदीनां यदाभ्यो अरदो गातुमिंद्र । (*adyā cinnū citradapo nadīnāṃ yadābhyo arado gātumiṃdra |*)
नि पर्वता अद्मसदो न सेदुस्त्वया दृळ्हानि सुकृतो रजांसि ॥ (*ni parvatā admasado na sedustvayā dṛḷhāni sukṛto rajāṃsi ‖*)
ऋ. सं. (६-३०-३) (*ṛ. saṃ. (6-30-3)*)

and other ṛks that the word *rajāṃsi* has the sense "worlds". In the present ṛk the sense is "worlds".

रसाः दिवि वाता इव श्रिताः (*rasāḥ divi vātā iva śritāḥ*) — just as the wind in the atmosphere spreads evenly everywhere, so the six flavours, sweet and the rest, pervade food and produce flavours of many kinds: the sage here gives this as an illustration.

> मत्तारोऽसंख्यातग्रीवा इव भवंति रसानां बाहुल्यादिति भावः । एवं बहुरसो-
> पेतमन्नमिति तस्य स्तुतिः ॥

*Gist:* O Pito, men who seek you become your eaters and givers by your favour; the eaters of your flavours go out like men with swelling necks, since fasting makes the neck hang down.

### Printed p. 197

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 197 (as supplied).*

**Pratipadārtha** (Ṛk 5)

स्वादिष्ट—अत्यंत स्वादुकरनाद (*svādiṣṭa—atyaṃta svādukaranāda*) (most sweet). पितो—पालकनाद अन्नवे,  (*pito—pālakanāda annave, *)(protecting food). त्ये—निन्नन्नु अन्वेषण माडतक्क नररु (*tye—ninnannu anveṣaṇa māḍatakka nararu*) (the men who seek you). तव—निन्नन्नु सेविसि सुखपडुत्तारॆ. (*tava—ninnannu sevisi sukhapaḍuttārè.*) (they enjoy by partaking of you). पितो—रक्षकनाद अन्नवे (*pito—rakṣakanāda annave*) (O protecting food). तव--निन्न अनुग्रहदिंद (*tava--ninna anugrahadiṃda*) (by your favour). ते—अवरु (यज्ञकर्तरु) (*te—avaru (yajñakartaru)*) (they, the sacrificers). ददतः—निन्नन्नु (इतररिगू) हंचुत्तारॆ (*dadataḥ—ninnannu (itararigū) haṃcuttārè*) (they distribute you, to others also). रसानां- निन्न षड्रसगळ (*rasānāṃ- ninna ṣaḍrasagaḷa*) (of your six flavours). स्वाद्मानः—भोक्तृगळु (निन्न रसास्वादनॆयन्नु माडि सुखपडतक्कवरु ) (*svādmānaḥ—bhoktṛgaḷu (ninna rasāsvādanèyannu māḍi sukhapaḍatakkavaru )*) (enjoyers, those who are happy relishing your flavours). तुविग्रीवा इव—वृद्धियन्नु हॊंदि पुष्टवाद कत्तुळ्ळवरंतॆ (*tuvigrīvā iva—vṛddhiyannu hòṃdi puṣṭavāda kattuḷḷavaraṃtè*) (like those grown and with stout necks). प्र ईरते—आनंदवन्नु व्यक्तपडि सुत्ता संचरिसुत्तारॆ (*pra īrate—ānaṃdavannu vyaktapaḍi suttā saṃcarisuttārè*) (they move about expressing joy).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O most sweet, protecting food: the sacrificers who partake of you find happiness in you, and not only that, they share that happiness with others. All who relish your six flavours and enjoy happiness, grown and with stout necks as it were, move about expressing joy.

**Printed English translation**

Those (men), Pitu, (are the enjoyers of your bounty), who are your distributors, most sweet Pitu, (to others): they who are relishers, of your flavours, are as if they had stiff necks.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

*[In the Special Topics of this Ṛk the supplied text has तै [?] (*tai [?]*) (apparently *te*) in the line on *svādmānaḥ rasānām*; marked [?].]*

त्ये—ते (*tye—te*) — we explained the sense of this word under the previous ṛk. Here *te* means men (or animals?) who desire food and partake of it; this is the intended sense.

तव (*tava*) — since the word *tava* is read twice in this ṛk, according to the Nirukta-authors' statement अभ्यासे हि भूयांसमर्थं मन्यंते (*abhyāse hi bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyaṃte*) ("in repetition they take the sense to be greater"), the repetition indicates respect and affection for food.

ददतः तव (*dadataḥ tava*) — those who give (you) food to others, by your favour, who make gifts; and

स्वाद्मानः रसानां (*svādmānaḥ rasānāṃ*) — those who relish the many kinds of flavours in food, or who eat food of this kind: both are qualifiers of the word तै [?] (नराः) (*tai [?] (narāḥ)*), "men". The main sense is: men who eat food endowed with the six flavours themselves and also give it to others (become strong).

### Printed p. 198

*Running head: [198 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24. Sū. 187] (as supplied).*

तुविग्रीवा इव (*tuvigrīvā iva*) — तुवि (*tuvi*) means "much" (नि ३-१३ (*ni 3-13*)); ग्रीव (*grīva*) means neck, throat. Sāyaṇa has given this word *tuvigrīvā* two kinds of meaning. One: प्रवृद्धग्रीवाः (*pravṛddhagrīvāḥ*), "those with well-grown, stout and firm necks". Having stout necks means being firm-limbed. It is well known in the world that by taking good food not the neck alone but the whole body grows strong. Although only the word *grīva*, "neck", is used here, it indicates the other limbs of the body or the whole body; therefore *tuvigrīvā iva* is explained as "moving about firm-limbed". The bhāṣyakāra has explained that the word *iva* here has the sense of *eva*, or that it has no definite sense and is used only to fill the pāda. And explaining the second meaning of the word *tuvigrīvā iva* he says:

तव रसानामत्तारोऽसंख्यातग्रीवा इव भवंति रसानां बाहुल्यादिति भावः । अन्नद (*tava rasānāmattāro 'saṃkhyātagrīvā iva bhavaṃti rasānāṃ bāhulyāditi bhāvaḥ | annada*)

The one who eats food of many kinds of flavours is like one eating with many throats (mouths), that is, becomes a great eater: this is the other kind of meaning given. In this matter the English scholar Wilson explains Sāyaṇa's view in this way:

तुविग्रीवा इवेरते (*tuvigrīvā iverate*)—तुवि (*tuvi*) is ordinarily, a synonyme of बहु (*bahu*) much, many ; Sayana explains it by प्रवृद्ध (*pravṛddha*), enlarged; because, he says, when people eat, they are दृढांग (*dṛḍhāṃga*), firm ; and when they are without food, the neck is bent, bends down ; or it may mean that they are great eaters, as if they had many throats.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 5, noted briefly)

ददतः (*dadataḥ*) (root डुदाञ् दाने (*ḍudāñ dāne*)): the participle substituted for *laṭ*, *śluvikaraṇa*, reduplication of the root; by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-४-११२ (*pā. sū. 6-4-112*)) the *ā* of the root is dropped; in the nominative plural by नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः (*nābhyastācchatuḥ*) the augment *num* does not occur; by अभ्यस्तानामादि: (*abhyastānāmādi:*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१८९ (*pā. sū. 6-1-189*)) the first syllable is acute. स्वादिष्ट (*svādiṣṭa*): by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*) the superlative sense after *svādu*; by the rule टेः (*ṭeḥ*) the *ṭi* (*u*) is dropped; the vocative takes the vocative *nighāta* accent. स्वाद्मानः (*svādmānaḥ*) (root स्वाद आस्वादने (*svāda āsvādane*)): by अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anyebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (पा. सू. ३-२-७५ (*pā. sū. 3-2-75*)) the suffix *manin*; being marked *n*, the first syllable is acute; nominative plural. ईरते (*īrate*) (root ईर गत् प्रेरणे च (*īra gat preraṇe ca*)): *adādi*, *laṭ*, third person plural; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वे पि॑तो म॒हानां॑ दे॒वानां॒ मनो॑ हि॒तं ।
> अका॑रि॒ चारु॑ के॒तुना॒ तवाहि॒मव॑सावधीत् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tve pito mahānāṃ devānāṃ mano hitaṃ |*
> *akāri cāru ketunā tavāhimavasāvadhīt ‖ 6 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading हडपाटॆ (*haḍapāṭè*) stands inside the Saṃhitā block where the Pada label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वे इति । पितो इति । महानां । देवानां । मनः । हितं ।
> अकारि । चारु । केतुना । तव । अहिं । अवसा । अवधीत् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tve iti | pito iti | mahānāṃ | devānāṃ | manaḥ | hitaṃ |*
> *akāri | cāru | ketunā | tava | ahiṃ | avasā | avadhīt ‖ 6 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading स:यणभाष्यं (*sa:yaṇabhāṣyaṃ*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे पितो महानां पूज्यानां महतां ना देवानामिंद्रादीनां मनस्त्वे
> त्वयि हितं निहितमकारि । कृतं । अमृतमपि विहाय त्वय्येव वर्तते । हे पितो तव
> चारु समीचीनेन केतुना त्वत्कृतेन प्रज्ञानलक्षणेनावसा रक्षणेनाहिं मेघं वृत्रं
> नावधीत् । हतवानिंद्रः । अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । छां. ६ ५-४ । इति श्रुतेः ।
> अथवा त्वत्केतुना जगद्रक्षणेन निमित्तेनेति योज्यं । जगद्रक्षणार्थं हींद्रेणाहि-
> र्भिद्यते ॥

*Gist:* The minds of the great gods are set on you, Pito; by your guarding wisdom Indra slew Ahi, for mind is made of food (Chāndogya).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पितो—ऎलै अन्नवे (*pito—èlai annave*) (O food). महानां—पूज्यराद (*mahānāṃ—pūjyarāda*) (venerable). देवानां—इंद्रादि देवतॆगळ (*devānāṃ—iṃdrādi devatègaḷa*) (of the gods, Indra and others). मनः—मनस्सु (*manaḥ—manassu*) (mind). त्वे—निन्नल्ले (*tve—ninnalle*) (in you alone). हितं अकारि—इडल्पट्टिदॆ (*hitaṃ akāri—iḍalpaṭṭidè*) (has been placed). तव—निन्न (*tava—ninna*) (your). चारु—रम्यवादुदू (*cāru—ramyavādudū*) (pleasant). केतुना—प्रज्ञानरूपवादुदू आद (*ketunā—prajñānarūpavādudū āda*) (of the nature of wisdom). अवसा—रक्षणदिंद (*avasā—rakṣaṇadiṃda*) (by protection). अहिं—मेघवन्नु (अथवा वृत्र नन्नु) (*ahiṃ—meghavannu (athavā vṛtra nannu)*) (the cloud, or Vṛtra). अवधीत्—इंद्रनु कॊंदनु (*avadhīt—iṃdranu kòṃdanu*) (Indra slew).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O food, even the venerable gods, Indra and the rest, have their minds fixed on you alone. By your pleasant protection, of the nature of wisdom, Indra slew Vṛtra.

**Printed English translation**

The thoughts of the mighty gods are fixed. Pitu, upon you, by your kind and intelligent assistance, (Indra) slew Ahi.

### Printed p. 200

*Running head: [200 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 25. Sū. 187] (as supplied, the print has "೨೫" for the adhyāya).*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 reads विशेषयगळु (*viśeṣayagaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 6)**

महानां (*mahānāṃ*) — "of the great" or "of the venerable". The words *mahat* and *mahaḥ* are also read among the names of water (नि. २-२४ (*ni. 2-24*)); and Yāska, giving the explanation of the first ṛk of this sūkta, पितुं नु स्तोषं (*pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ*), explains the word *mahaḥ* in it as *mahataḥ*. Hence in the present ṛk the sense of *mahānāṃ* as "possessing greatness, of great glory, great, that is venerable" is suitable. The use of the word *mahānāṃ* here raises the importance of food. How? The phrase महानां देवानां मनः त्वे हितं (*mahānāṃ devānāṃ manaḥ tve hitaṃ*) says that the very mind of the gods of great glory, not much regarding their natural food, the nectar, rests in you (in food). That is: even the gods of great glory desire food; as to men and other animals, there is no need to say how necessary food is. Thus the use of the word *mahānāṃ* stresses the greatness of food.

केतुना (*ketunā*) — the word *ketu* has the sense "wisdom" (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)). The bhāṣyakāra's explanation is "(protection) marked by wisdom": that is, the excellent knowledge or intelligence arising from partaking of food.

अहिं अवधीत् (*ahiṃ avadhīt*) — although the word *ahi* has several senses, here it means Vṛtra. Although the sentence has no noun indicating the subject, it must be supplied; since the slayer of Vṛtra is Indra, the word *indraḥ* is to be supplied as subject. The latter half of this ṛk says the very thing stated in the first ṛk of this sūkta: that Indra slew the demon Vṛtra by the abundant strength of food.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 6, noted briefly)

महानाम् (*mahānām*) (root मह पूजायां (*maha pūjāyāṃ*)): by नंदिग्रहिपचादिभ्य— (*naṃdigrahipacādibhya—*) (पा सू. ३-१-१३४ (*pā sū. 3-1-134*)) the suffix *ac*; being marked *c*, the last syllable is acute; genitive plural. हितम् (*hitam*) (root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*)): by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) the suffix *kta*; by दधातेर्हिः (*dadhāterhiḥ*) (पा. सू. ७-४-४२ (*pā. sū. 7-4-42*)) the substitute *hi* before the suffix; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. आकारि (*ākāri*) (root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*)): *luṅ* in the passive; by चिण्‌भावकर्मणोः (*ciṇbhāvakarmaṇoḥ*) (पा. सू. ३-१-६६ (*pā. sū. 3-1-66*)) the substitute *ciṇ* for *cli*; by अचोञ्णति (*acoñṇati*) vṛddhi of the root vowel *ṛ*;

### Printed p. 201

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2 Adhyāya 5. Varga 7] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 201 (as supplied).*

by चिणोलुक् (*ciṇoluk*) (पा. सू. ६-४-१०४ (*pā. sū. 6-4-104*)) the *ta* suffix is dropped; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; being at the beginning of the pāda, no *nighāta*; since the augment is acute, the first syllable is acute. अवधीत् (*avadhīt*) (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*)): third person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यद॒दो पि॑तो॒ अज॑गन्वि॒वस्व॒ पर्व॑तानां ।
> अत्रा॑ चिन्नो मधो पि॒तो ऽरं॑ भ॒क्षाय॑ गम्याः ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यत् । अदः । पितो इति । अजगन् । विवस्व । पर्वतानां ।
> अत्र । चित् । नः । मधो इति । पितो इति । अरं । भक्षाय । गम्याः ॥ ७ ॥

> *yat | adaḥ | pito iti | ajagan | vivasva | parvatānāṃ |*
> *atra | cit | naḥ | madho iti | pito iti | araṃ | bhakṣāya | gamyāḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading कायणभाष्यं (*kāyaṇabhāṣyaṃ*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे पितो अन्न त्वां यद्यदा विवस्व ॥ सुपो लुक् । अंत्यलोपश्रांदसः ॥
> विवासनवतां विद्युद्रूपप्रकाशनवतां । विवो धनमुदकलक्षणं । धनवतां वा पर्व-
> तानां मेघानां संबंध्यदः प्रसिद्धं तदुदकमजगन् अगमत् गच्छेत्. अत्र चिदस्मि-
> न्नाले नोऽस्मान् हे मधो हे पितो माधुर्योपेतान्न त्वं नोऽस्मानरमलं
> संपूर्णं भक्षाय भक्षणाय गम्याः । गच्छ । संनिहितो भव ॥

*Gist:* O Pito, when the water of the lightning-bright clouds comes to you, then, O sweet food, be present with us in sufficiency for eating.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पितो—ऎलै अन्नवे (*pito—èlai annave*) (O food). यत्—यावाग (*yat—yāvāga*) (when). विवस्व—(उदकरूपवाद) धनदिंद युक्त वाद अथवा विद्युद्रूपवाद प्रकाशदिंद कूडिद (*vivasva—(udakarūpavāda) dhanadiṃda yukta vāda athavā vidyudrūpavāda prakāśadiṃda kūḍida*) (endowed with wealth in the form of water, or with the light of lightning). पर्वतानां—मेघगळ (*parvatānāṃ—meghagaḷa*) (of the clouds). अदः—प्रसिद्धवाद उदकवु (*adaḥ—prasiddhavāda udakavu*) (the well-known water). अजगन्—(निन्नन्नु) सेरिकॊळ्ळुत्तदॆयो (*ajagan—(ninnannu) serikòḷḷuttadèyo*) (reaches you). आत्र चित्—आ कालदल्लि (*ātra cit—ā kāladalli*) (at that time; the print has "ಆತ್ರ" for *atra*, as supplied). मधो— माधुर्योपेतनाद (*madho— mādhuryopetanāda*) (sweet). पितो—ऎलै अन्नवे (*pito—èlai annave*) (O food). नः—नमगॆ (*naḥ—namagè*) (to us). अरं—पूर्णवाद (*araṃ—pūrṇavāda*) (full). भक्षाय— भक्षणक्कॆ अर्हवागि (*bhakṣāya— bhakṣaṇakkè arhavāgi*) (fit for eating). गम्याः—सन्निहितनागु (*gamyāḥ—sannihitanāgu*) (be present).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O food, when the water, the wealth of the clouds bright with the light of lightning, reaches you, then, O sweet food, be present with us as fit for our eating, in sufficiency (the print has "ಪುಷ್ಪಲವಾದ", as supplied).

### Printed p. 202

*Running head: [202 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24 Sū. 187] (as supplied).*

**Printed English translation**

When, Pitu, this (product) of the water-wealthy clouds, (the rain), arrives ; then do you, sweet Pitu, be at hand with sufficiency for our eating.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 7)**

विवस्व (*vivasva*) — here the genitive plural of *vivasvat*, विवस्वतां (*vivasvatāṃ*), must be meant; since the final syllable तां (*tāṃ*) is dropped in the Vedic manner, only *vivasva* remains. For the word *vivasvat* Yāska gives विवस्वान् विवासनवान् (*vivasvān vivāsanavān*) (नि. ७-२६ (*ni. 7-26*)), "that which dispels darkness", and the bhāṣyakāra explains it here in the same way: possessing the light of lightning (flash) which drives away darkness. This word is a qualifier of पर्वतानां (*parvatānāṃ*) (मेघानां (*meghānāṃ*)).

पर्वतानां (*parvatānāṃ*) — the word *parvata* is read among the thirty names of cloud, *adriḥ*, *grāva* and others (नि २-२१ (*ni 2-21*)). For the word *parvata* Yāska gives the explanation पर्ववान् पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा (*parvavān parvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā*) (नि १-२० (*ni 1-20*)): the word *parva* is derived either from the root *pṛ*, "to fill", or from the root *prī*, "to satisfy"; that which has such *parvas* is a *parvata*. If *parvata* is derived from the root *pṛ*, it means that which fills empty regions: the mountain fills the empty regions of the earth, and the clouds (*parvatas*) fill the empty regions of the sky. If it is derived from *prī*, it means that which satisfies the whole world by the release of rain. In this sense too *parvata* means cloud.

*[As supplied, the label line reads व्याकरण पकिया (*vyākaraṇa pakiyā*); standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 7, noted briefly; it continues in the next window)

अजगन् (*ajagan*) (root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*)): in the Vedic manner *laṅ* in the sense of *liṭ*; third person singular *śip*; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) the final *i* is dropped; by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *śap* is replaced by *ślu*; on that basis reduplication of the root; with *jagam-t*, by हल्‌जाभ्यो— (*haljābhyo—*) the suffix is dropped; by मोनोधातोः (*monodhātoḥ*) (पा. सू. ८-२ ६४ (*pā. sū. 8-2 64*)) the final *m* of the root becomes *n*; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; owing to the connection with *yat* the *nighāta* accent is prohibited; since the augment is acute, the first syllable is acute. विवस्व (*vivasva*): विवः धनं. अस्य आस्ति इति विवस्वान् (*vivaḥ dhanaṃ. asya āsti iti vivasvān*); by तदस्यास्ति— (*tadasyāsti—*) the suffix *matup*; by तसौ मत्पर्धे (*tasau matpardhe*) (पा. सू १-१-१९ (*pā. sū 1-1-19*)) the *bha* designation, so that the *s* ... (the print breaks off at the end of the window, "ಸಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ರುತ್ವವಿಸರ್ಗ").

### Printed p. 203

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 7] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 203 (as supplied).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (continuation of the Ṛk 7 grammar page, noted briefly)

Continuing the entry *vivasva*: the *s* does not become *ru*-visarga here; when the genitive plural follows, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (पा सू. ७-१-३९ (*pā sū. 7-1-39*)) the ending is dropped (*luk*); in the Vedic manner the final *n* is dropped; the suffix being marked *p*, the accent is unaccented (*anudātta*). अत्र (*atra*): by निपातस्य चॆ (*nipātasya cè*) (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६ (*pā. sū. 6-3-136*)) the vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā. अरम् (*aram*): by the statement वालमूललघ्व (*vālamūlalaghva*) the substitution of *l* is optional and does not occur here. गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) (root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*)): *liṅ*, second person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

> *| |*
> *vātāpe | pīvaḥ | it ! bhava ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यद्येनापामोषधीनां संबंधि परिंशं परिलेशं परितः सुखकरमन्नमारि-
> शामहे आस्वादयामः भक्षयामः तेनान्नोदकसारेण हे वातापे । वातेन प्राणे-

> पितो त्वमल्पमपि पीवः पीवानेव भव ॥

*Gist:* By the essence of food and water, of which we partake, O body (*vātāpi*), grow fat; or, even if we taste only a little, O all-pervading food, be nourishing.

*[As supplied, a line reading प्रतिपदवर्थ (*pratipadavartha*) stands inside the bhāṣya block as the label; standard label inserted. The Pratipadārtha lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given here as prose.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यत्—याव कारणदिंद (*yat—yāva kāraṇadiṃda*) (since). अपां—अप्पुगळिगू (उदकगळिगू) (*apāṃ—appugaḷigū (udakagaḷigū)*) (of the waters). ओषधीनां—ओषधि गळिगू संबंधिसिदुदू (*oṣadhīnāṃ—oṣadhi gaḷigū saṃbaṃdhisidudū*) (of the plants, related to). परिंशं—पूर्णवागि सुखवन्नुंटुमाडतक्कद्दू आद अन्नवन्नु (*pariṃśaṃ—pūrṇavāgi sukhavannuṃṭumāḍatakkaddū āda annavannu*) (the food that gives complete happiness). अरिशामहे—नावु भक्षिसुत्तेवॆयो (आदुदरिंद) (*ariśāmahe—nāvu bhakṣisuttevèyo (ādudariṃda)*) (we eat, therefore). वातापे—ऎलै शरीरवे (*vātāpe—èlai śarīrave*) (O body). पीव इत् भव— (*pīva it bhava—*)

### Printed p. 204

*Running head: [204 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 187] (as supplied).*

अत्यंत पुष्टवागि बॆळॆ (*atyaṃta puṣṭavāgi bèḷè*) (grow very fat, i.e. well nourished). [Alternatively: अथवा यत्—ऒंदुवेळॆ (*athavā yat—òṃduveḷè*) (if); अपां—अप्पुगळिगू (*apāṃ—appugaḷigū*) (of the waters); ओषधीनां— ओषधिगळिगू संबंधिसिद अन्नदल्लि (*oṣadhīnāṃ— oṣadhigaḷigū saṃbaṃdhisida annadalli*) (in the food related to the plants); परिंशं—अल्पभागवन्नु मात्र (*pariṃśaṃ—alpabhāgavannu mātra*) (only a small part); अरिशामहे—तिंदरू कूड (*ariśāmahe—tiṃdarū kūḍa*) (even if we eat); वातापे—वायुविनंतॆ सर्वव्यापकनाद ऎलै अन्नवे (*vātāpe—vāyuvinaṃtè sarvavyāpakanāda èlai annave*) (O food, all-pervading like the wind); पीव इत् भव— (*pīva it bhava—*) (अल्पवागिद्दरू सह) पुष्टिकारकनागिये आगु (*(alpavāgiddarū saha) puṣṭikārakanāgiye āgu*) (be nourishing even though little). The bracket is not closed in the print.]

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O body, by eating the food related to the waters and plants and giving complete happiness, grow very well nourished.

**Printed English translation**

And since we enjoy, the abundance of the waters aud [sic] the plants; therefore, Body, do you grow fat.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यॆत् अपां ओषधीनां (*yèt apāṃ oṣadhīnāṃ*) — *oṣadhis* are plants and the like, or the grain and other produce obtained from them. Here "related to water and plants" are qualifiers of food: from water come plants, from plants grain and the like, from grain food; so food is said to be related to plants and water.

वातापे (*vātāpe*) — वातेन प्राणेनाप्नोति स्वनिर्वाहमिति वातेनाप्यायत इति वा (*vātena prāṇenāpnoti svanirvāhamiti vātenāpyāyata iti vā*) वातापि शरीरं (*vātāpi śarīraṃ*): since all functions of the body are carried on by the life-breath, *vātāpi* means the body; or, since it is satisfied by air, *vātāpi* means the body: the bhāṣyakāra gives these two meanings of the word *vātāpi*.

पीवः आस्यायितः (*pīvaḥ āsyāyitaḥ*) — "causing satisfaction" is Sāyaṇa's explanation. In the ṛk numbered ७-९१-३ (*7-91-3*) of the Ṛg. Saṃ.

पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधाः श्वेतः सिषक्ति नियुतामभिश्रीः । (*pīvoannā rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhāḥ śvetaḥ siṣakti niyutāmabhiśrīḥ |*)
(म. सं. ७-९१-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 7-91-3)*)

in explaining the words *pīvo annān* the bhāṣyakāra says पीवो अन्नान् पीवांसि स्थूलानि प्रभूतान्यन्नानि येषां तान् (*pīvo annān pīvāṃsi sthūlāni prabhūtānyannāni yeṣāṃ tān*), giving *pīva* the sense "stout, that is, much increased". In

उताहमद्मि पीव इदुभा कुक्षी पृणंति मे विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः । (*utāhamadmi pīva idubhā kukṣī pṛṇaṃti me viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ |*)
(य. सं. १०-८६-१४) (*(ya. saṃ. 10-86-14)*)

the words जीव [?] इत् स्थूल एव (*jīva [?] it sthūla eva*) (the print has *jīva* where *pīva* is expected; marked [?]) he explains as "stout"; and in

ऊर्जं गावो यवसे पीवो अत्तन ऋतस्य याः सदने कोशे आंग्घ्नी । (*ūrjaṃ gāvo yavase pīvo attana ṛtasya yāḥ sadane kośe āṃgghnī |*)
(म सं. १०-१००-१०) (*(ma saṃ. 10-100-10)*)

### Printed p. 205

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 7] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 205 (as supplied).*

the bhāṣyakāra also explains पीवः प्रवृद्धं (*pīvaḥ pravṛddhaṃ*), "increased, causing growth". Hence the word *pīva* may be given the sense "stout" or "nourishing". The body is thus addressed: be satisfied, or grow, by such food. It is a matter of common knowledge that by eating good food the body is satisfied and grows, so there is no need to explain more.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 8, noted briefly)

अपाम् (*apām*): by ऊडिदं पदादि— (*ūḍidaṃ padādi—*) (पा. सू- ६-१-१२१ (*pā. sū- 6-1-121*)) the genitive plural is acute. आरिशामहे (*āriśāmahe*): preverb आज् (*āj*) with the root रिश हिंसायाम् (*riśa hiṃsāyām*); *laṭ*, first person plural; because of the connection with *yat* the *nighāta* accent does not occur; the accent of the stem-suffix remains; by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (पा. सू. ८-१-७१ (*pā. sū. 8-1-71*)) the preverb (*ā*) takes the *nighāta* accent. वातापे (*vātāpe*): वातेन आप्नोति इति वातापिः (*vātena āpnoti iti vātāpiḥ*), root आप्‌ल्य व्याप्त् (*āplya vyāpt*), the Uṇādi suffix *i*; vocative, at the beginning of the pāda so no vocative *nighāta*; by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१९८ (*pā. sū. 6-1-198*)) the first syllable is acute. पीवः (*pīvaḥ*) (root पैज् वृद्धौ (*paij vṛddhau*)): the Uṇādi suffix *van*; *samprasāraṇa* of the root; the following form replaces the preceding; the suffix being marked *n*, the first syllable is acute.
