> गतं ॥

*Gist:* We utter in this Agni, victor over foes and son of the mantra, our fixed praises; by these mantras that reveal what is beyond the senses may we gain boundless wealth, food, strength and long life.

*[As supplied, a line reading प्र, तपदार्थ (*pra, tapadārtha*) with block marks stands where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; standard label inserted. The following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

मानस्य सूनुः—मंत्रदिंद उत्पन्ननाद पुत्रनू (*mānasya sūnuḥ—maṃtradiṃda utpannanāda putranū*) (the son born of the mantra). सहसाने—शत्रुगळन्नु सोलिसुव शक्तियुळ्ळवनू आद (*sahasāne—śatrugaḷannu solisuva śaktiyuḷḷavanū āda*) (possessing the power to defeat foes). अस्मिन् आग्नौ—ई अग्नियल्लि (अग्नियन्नु उद्देशिसि) (*asmin āgnau—ī agniyalli (agniyannu uddeśisi)*) (in this Agni, addressing him). निवचनानि—स्तोत्र रूपवाद वाक्कुगळन्नु (*nivacanāni—stotra rūpavāda vākkugaḷannu*) (words in the form of praise). अवोचाम—पठिसुत्तेवॆ (*avocāma—paṭhisuttevè*) (we recite). वयं—नावु (*vayaṃ—nāvu*) (we). ऋषिभिः—आतींद्रियार्थ वन्नु प्रकाशपडिसतक्क मंत्रगळिंद (*ṛṣibhiḥ—ātīṃdriyārtha vannu prakāśapaḍisatakka maṃtragaḷiṃda*) (by mantras that reveal what is beyond the senses). सहस्रं अपरिमितवाद धनवन्नु (*sahasraṃ aparimitavāda dhanavannu*) (boundless wealth). सनेम—हॊंदुवंता गलि (मत्तु) (*sanema—hòṃduvaṃtā gali (mattu)*) (may we obtain). इषं—अन्नवन्नू (*iṣaṃ—annavannū*) (food). वृजनं—बलवन्नू (*vṛjanaṃ—balavannū*) (strength). जीरदानुं—दीर्घायुष्यवन्नू (*jīradānuṃ—dīrghāyuṣyavannū*) (long life). विद्याम—हॊंदुवंतागलि (*vidyāma—hòṃduvaṃtāgali*) (may we obtain).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भावार्थ- (*bhāvārtha-*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

We recite words of praise addressed to this Agni, the son born of the mantra and possessed of the power to defeat foes. By mantras that reveal what is beyond the senses may we gain boundless wealth, food, strength and long life.

**Printed English translation**

We address our pious prayers to you, Agni, the son of prayer, the subduer of foes; may we procure, by these sacred supplications, infinite wealth that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 8)**

मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*) — मीयत इति मानो मंत्रः । तस्य सूनुरग्निः । मंत्रेणो- त्पद्यमानत्वात् । सप्तम्यर्थे प्रथमा (*mīyata iti māno maṃtraḥ | tasya sūnuragniḥ | maṃtreṇo- tpadyamānatvāt | saptamyarthe prathamā*): here *māna* is explained as *mantra*.

### Printed p. 296

*Running head: [296 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189] (as supplied).*

माज् माने (*māj māne*) — *māna* is formed from the root meaning "to measure"; it means a mantra (a ṛk or metre) with a fixed number of syllables. Since Agni is produced in the *araṇi* with mantras, he is described by the epithet मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*), "produced by the mantra (the son of the mantra)". Here the nominative is used in the sense of the locative; the bhāṣyakāra explains that *mānasya sūnuḥ* should be taken to mean "in Agni".

सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*) — boundless, of great number.

ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*) — ऋषी गत् (*ṛṣī gat*). Since roots of motion are also used in the sense of knowledge, the word *ṛṣi* also has the senses knowledge and understanding. Because the mantra produces knowledge, *ṛṣibhiḥ* here means "by mantras in the nature of knowledge".

जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) — Sāyaṇa at १-१६५-१५ (*1-165-15*) explained this word as जयशीलदानं (*jayaśīladānaṃ*); there is also the variant reading जयशीलं दानं जीवनं वा (*jayaśīlaṃ dānaṃ jīvanaṃ vā*). How the sense "victory" or "victory-bringing" arises here for the word *jīra* is a matter worth considering. The two words *jīra* and *dānu* together form *jīradānu*. Each of these two words is used separately in many places with different senses; and with the word *jīra* other words such as *aśva* and *adhvara* combine to give *jīrāśva*, *jīrādhvara* and the like.

मनुष्यद्देव धीमहि प्रचेतसं जीरं दूतममर्त्यं । (*manuṣyaddeva dhīmahi pracetasaṃ jīraṃ dūtamamartyaṃ |*)
(पु सं. १-४४-११) (*(pu saṃ. 1-44-11)*)

explaining the derivation of the word *jīra* in this ṛk, Sāyaṇa says that the word is formed from the root *ju* (जोरी च. उ. सू. २-१८१ (*jorī ca. u. sū. 2-181*)) and gives the sense "destroying the life (of enemies)"; here *jīram* is an epithet of Agni; from this sense it is understood that the derivation is possible from the root ज्य वयोहानौ (*jya vayohānau*) also. The Nirukta-authors read the word *jīra* among the names of the swift (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*)).

दिविस्पृशं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कृणुतं सुम्मनिष्टये । (*divispṛśaṃ yajñamasmākamaśvinā jīrādhvaraṃ kṛṇutaṃ summaniṣṭaye |*)
प्राचीनरश्मिमाहुतं धृतेन तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥ (*prācīnaraśmimāhutaṃ dhṛtena taddevānāmavo adyā vṛṇīmahe ‖*)
(ऋ सं. १०-३६-६). (*(ṛ saṃ. 10-36-6).*)

In this ṛk the Aśvin deities are prayed to make our rite *jīrādhvara*; here *jīrādhvara* means a sacrifice that is performed unobstructed by hindrances, without violence, and quickly (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 297

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5 Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 297 (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 8 of Sūkta 189, on *jīradānuṃ*.)*

पृषे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय ना सदमा जीरदानवः । (*pṛṣe tā viśvā bhuvanā vavakṣire mitrāya nā sadamā jīradānavaḥ |*)
पृषदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधस ऋजिप्यासो न वयुनेषु धूर्षदः ॥ (*pṛṣadaśvāso anavabhrarādhasa ṛjipyāso na vayuneṣu dhūrṣadaḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. २-३४-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 2-34-4)*)

In this and other places *jīradānavaḥ* is an epithet of the Maruts; the sense is those who very quickly fulfil the wishes of the sacrificer. Likewise the compounds जीराश्वः (*jīrāśvaḥ*) and जीराश्वं (*jīrāśvaṃ*) are epithets of Agni and other deities, or sometimes of their chariot.

आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञियं जीवसे हुवे । (*ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyaṃ manojuvaṃ jīrāśvaṃ yajñiyaṃ jīvase huve |*)
सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टिवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥ (*sahasraketuṃ vaninaṃ śatadvasuṃ śruṣṭivānaṃ varivodhāmabhi prayaḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. १-११९-१) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-119-1)*)

In these and other ṛks the chariot of the Aśvin deities is described as having swiftly running horses. Likewise the word *dānu* too, used separately and also in the compounds *sudānavaḥ* and *jīradānavaḥ*, gives a sense suited to the context. From the context cited by the Nirukta-authors it is known that the word *dānu* gives the sense either "giver" or "demon".

स्तुषेय्यं पुरुवर्ससमृभ्वमिनतममास्त्यमाप्त्यानां । (*stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarsasamṛbhvaminatamamāstyamāptyānāṃ |*)
आ दर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून् प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि ॥ (*ā darṣate śavasā sapta dānūn pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ‖*)
(पु. सं. १०-१२०-६) (*(pu. saṃ. 10-120-6)*)

In explaining this ṛk the Nirukta-authors say that the words सप्त दानून् (*sapta dānūn*) mean सप्त दात्यन् इति वा सप्त दानवान् इति वा (*sapta dātyan iti vā sapta dānavān iti vā*): "seven givers" or "seven demons". But how in such contexts the word *dānu* can have the sense "demon", Max Müller, pointing out his own difficulty (the print has "ತನ್ನ ಕೇಶವನ್ನು" as supplied), says as follows:

It must be confessed that even the meaning of Danu is by no means quite clear. (*It must be confessed that even the meaning of Danu is by no means quite clear.*)
It is clear enough where it means Demon, II. 11, 18 : II. 12. 11 ; IV. 30.7 : (*It is clear enough where it means Demon, II. 11, 18 : II. 12. 11 ; IV. 30.7 :*)
X. 120-6; The seven Demons, in I. 32.9; III. 30.8 ; Danu, Demon is applied to (*X. 120-6; The seven Demons, in I. 32.9; III. 30.8 ; Danu, Demon is applied to*)
the mother of Vritra' the dark cloud; From this Danu we have the derivative (*the mother of Vritra ' the dark cloud; From this Danu we have the derivative*)
Danava, meaning again Demon, why the demons conquered by Indra, were (*Danava, meaning again Demon, why the demons conquered by Indra, were*)
called Danu is not clear, unless they were conceived originally as dark clouds, (*called Danu is not clear, unless they were conceived originally as dark clouds,*)
like Danu, the mother of Indra. Danu might mean wise or even powerful, for (*like Danu, the mother of Indra. Danu might mean wise or even powerful, for*)
this meaning also is ascribed to Danu by the author of Unadi Sutras. (*this meaning also is ascribed to Danu by the author of Unadi Sutras.*)
[ S. B. E. XXXII. P. 114-115 ] (*[ S. B. E. XXXII. P. 114-115 ]*)

### Printed p. 298

*Running head: [298 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. . 24. Sū. 188] (as supplied; the print has the sūkta number 188 and a blank for the adhyāya sign).*

*Dānu* is the name of the mother of Vṛtra, an asura-woman; this scholar asks how her sons should have come to be called *dānu* when they ought to be *dānava*. It is also understood from the Uṇādi sūtra that the word may have the senses "power" and "wise". But the sense "giver" is the better known. So if *jīra* means "swift" and *dānu* "gift", then in the present ṛk "swift gift" would be the sense; but Sāyaṇa has taken "victorious gift". Since the word *jīra* is used in many places in the sense of "impelling", here the sense "victory-impelling gift" may be taken. In general the word *jīradānavaḥ* is mostly used as an epithet of the Maruts.

पृक्षे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय ना सदमा जीरदानवः ॥ (*pṛkṣe tā viśvā bhuvanā vavakṣire mitrāya nā sadamā jīradānavaḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. २-३४-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 2-34-4)*)

In these and other ṛks *jīradānavaḥ* is well known as the Maruts. (The print has "ಪೃಷೇ" in the first quotation on p. 297 and "ಪೃಕ್ಷೇ" here; both as printed.) And:

वृषा न क्रुद्धः पतयद्रजःस्वा यो अर्यपत्नीरकृणोदिमा अपः । (*vṛṣā na kruddhaḥ patayadrajaḥsvā yo aryapatnīrakṛṇodimā apaḥ |*)
स सुन्वते मघवा जीरदानवेऽविंदज्योतिर्मनवे हविष्मते ॥ (*sa sunvate maghavā jīradānave 'viṃdajyotirmanave haviṣmate ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-४३-८) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-43-8)*)

in these and other ṛks the word is also an epithet of the sacrificer who offers oblations and the like.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 8, noted briefly)

अवोचाम (*avocāma*) (root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*)): in the Vedic manner *luṅ* in the present sense; by ब्रुवोवचिः (*bruvovaciḥ*) (पा. सू. २-४-५३ (*pā. sū. 2-4-53*)) the substitute *vac* for the root; by अस्यतिवक्तिख्या— (*asyativaktikhyā—*) (पा. सू. ३-१-८२ (*pā. sū. 3-1-82*)) the substitute *aṅ* for *cli*; when it follows, by वचउम् (*vacaum*) the augment *um*, with guṇa; being at the beginning of the pāda the *nighāta* accent does not occur; by the accent of the augment *aṭ* the first syllable is acute. मानस्य (*mānasya*) (root माज् माने (*māj māne*)): the suffix *ghañ*; being marked *ñ*, the first syllable is acute. In मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*) the nominative has come in the sense of the locative by the statement सुपां सुपो भवंति (*supāṃ supo bhavaṃti*). सहसाने (*sahasāne*) (root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*)): by धात्पादेः षः. सः (*dhātpādeḥ ṣaḥ. saḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-१-६४ (*pā. sū. 6-1-64*)) *s* for the initial; by ऋञ्चिवृधिमंदिसहिभ्यःकित् (*ṛñcivṛdhimaṃdisahibhyaḥkit*) (उ. सू. २-२६४ (*u. sū. 2-264*)) the suffix *asānac*; being marked *c*, by चितः (*citaḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३ (*pā. sū. 6-1-163*)) the last syllable is acute; locative singular. सनेम (*sanema*) (root षण संभक्तौ (*ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*)): as before *s* for the initial; *liṅ*, first person plural; by तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) the *nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 299

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ ೫. ವ. ೧೧.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 299 (as supplied).*

*[As supplied, the heading line reads पि ळिकॆ. (*pi ḷikè.*) (garbled; apparently an introduction, *pīṭhike*, to the next sūkta); no sūkta-number line is printed in the supplied text, so no sūkta number is given here.]*

**Introduction (to the next sūkta)**

The deity of this sūkta is Bṛhaspati. Yāska, in his Nirukta, explaining the derivation of the word *bṛhaspati*, says:

बृहस्पतिः बृहतः पाता ना पालयिता वा । (*bṛhaspatiḥ bṛhataḥ pātā nā pālayitā vā |*)
(सि. १०-११) (*(si. 10-11)*)

and Durgācārya the commentator says बृहतः महतोऽस्य जगतः उदकस्य ना पाता रक्षिता, पाल- यिता अपि रक्षितैव धात्वन्यत्वमर्थैकत्वं (*bṛhataḥ mahato 'sya jagataḥ udakasya nā pātā rakṣitā, pāla- yitā api rakṣitaiva dhātvanyatvamarthaikatvaṃ*): that is, protector or guardian of the great world, or of water. To convey the sense of *pati* the words *pātā* and *pālayitā*, formed from different roots, are given, though the sense is one. Sāyaṇa in many places, explaining *bṛhataḥ pātā*, gives for *bṛhataḥ* the sense बृहतः यज्ञाख्यकर्मणः (*bṛhataḥ yajñākhyakarmaṇaḥ*) or वृष्टाख्यकर्मणः (*vṛṣṭākhyakarmaṇaḥ*), that is, of the work in the form of sacrifice or the work in the form of giving rain. Since Bṛhaspati carries out the sacrificial work as priest of the gods and brings about the rain needed by men, both epithets are natural. The ṛk describing Bṛhaspati's priesthood and the giving of rain:

यद्देवापिः शंतनवे पुरोहितो होत्राय वृतः कृपयन्नदीधेत् । (*yaddevāpiḥ śaṃtanave purohito hotrāya vṛtaḥ kṛpayannadīdhet |*)
देवश्रुतं वृष्टिवनिं रराणो बृहस्पतिर्वाचमस्मा अयच्छत् ॥ (*devaśrutaṃ vṛṣṭivaniṃ rarāṇo bṛhaspatirvācamasmā ayacchat ‖*)
(म सं. १०-९८-७) (*(ma saṃ. 10-98-7)*)

is given by Yāska as an example. In the explanation of this ṛk, बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मा- सीत् सोऽस्मै वाचमयच्छत् (*bṛhaspatirbrahmā- sīt so 'smai vācamayacchat*): Bṛhaspati, as the priest named Brahmā at the sacrifice made by the king Śantanu, taught the mantra in the form of speech, and when the sacrificer praised with that mantra, rain came about: so it is described. Besides, in the Yajurveda and elsewhere:

बृहस्पतिर्देवानां पुरोहित आसीच्छंडामर्कावसुराणां । (*bṛhaspatirdevānāṃ purohita āsīcchaṃḍāmarkāvasurāṇāṃ |*)
(तै. सं. ६-४-१०-१) (*(tai. saṃ. 6-4-10-1)*)

it is said that Bṛhaspati was the priest of the gods and that Śaṇḍa and Marka were the priests of the asuras.

ब्रह्म वै देवानां बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मण्यैव नमभिचरति । (*brahma vai devānāṃ bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇyaiva namabhicarati |*)
(कृ. सं. २-२-९-१) (*(kṛ. saṃ. 2-2-9-1)*)

(the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 300

*Running head: [300 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 189] (as supplied; the print has the sūkta number ೧೮೯ although the page belongs to the next sūkta's introduction).*

*(Continuation of the introduction to the next sūkta, the deity Bṛhaspati.)*

It is also said that Bṛhaspati carried out the sacrifice, as the priest named Brahmā, in the sacrifice made by the gods.

तस्मै विशः स्वयमेवा नमंते यस्मिन् ब्रह्मा राजनि पूर्व एति । (*tasmai viśaḥ svayamevā namaṃte yasmin brahmā rājani pūrva eti |*)
(ऋ. सं. ४-५०-८) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 4-50-8)*)
अवस्यवे यो वरिवः कृणोति ब्रह्मणे राजा तमवंति देवाः ॥ (*avasyave yo varivaḥ kṛṇoti brahmaṇe rājā tamavaṃti devāḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ४-५०-९) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 4-50-9)*)
सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे । (*somaṃ rājānamavase 'gniṃ gīrbhirhavāmahe |*)
आदित्यान्विष्णुं सूर्यं ब्रह्माणं च बृहस्पतिं ॥ (*ādityānviṣṇuṃ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca bṛhaspatiṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-१४१-३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-141-3)*)

In these and other ṛks Bṛhaspati is described as the priest named Brahmā.

In the Ṛgveda Bṛhaspati has a prominent place. Besides being praised in eleven sūktas, he is praised in two sūktas (ऋ. सं. ४-४९ ; ७-९७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 4-49 ; 7-97*)) as a dual deity together with Indra. The word *bṛhaspati* occurs about a hundred and twenty times in the Ṛgveda. In many contexts the deities Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably in a single mantra; yet Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are different deities.

Some Western scholars, and some among modern scholars, have expressed the opinion that, because Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably in the sūkta ऋ. सं. २-२३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 2-23*), the two are one deity. But the ancient Vedic commentators such as Yāska, Śaunaka and Sāyaṇa have stated clearly that Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another. Of the nineteen ṛks in the sūkta ऋ. सं. २ २३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 2 23*) mentioned above, only six, १, ५, ९, ११, १७, १९ (*1, 5, 9, 11, 17, 19*), praise Bṛhaspati; the remaining thirteen ṛks are for Brahmaṇaspati. Yāska too has given different derivations for the word *bṛhaspati* and the word *brahmaṇaspati*; therefore Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another.

Bṛhaspati has a peculiarity wholly different from the other deities. While all other deities are special forms of nature or of the power of nature, Bṛhaspati appears to be connected with the sphere of man's moral and religious life. There are many examples in the Ṛgveda that this deity, the protector of praise, hymns and prayer, exerts his influence on the resolve, will or power of the gods' minds. In the sūkta ऋग्वद १० ने मंडलद ९८ नॆय सूक्तदल्लि (*ṛgvada 10 ne maṃḍalada 98 nèya sūktadalli*) (the print has "ಋಗ್ವದ", as supplied) there is a historical account concerning the royal princes Devāpi and Śantanu of the Kuru line. That Bṛhaspati's part in it is very important the Nirukta-authors describe thus:

### Printed p. 301

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 301 (as supplied).*

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवापिश्चार्ष्टषेणः शंतनुश्च कौरवा भ्रातरा बभूवतुः । (*atretihāsamācakṣate | devāpiścārṣṭaṣeṇaḥ śaṃtanuśca kauravā bhrātarā babhūvatuḥ |*)
स शंतनुः कनीयानभिषेजयांचक्रे । देवापिस्तपः प्रतिपेदे । ततः (*sa śaṃtanuḥ kanīyānabhiṣejayāṃcakre | devāpistapaḥ pratipede | tataḥ*)
शंतनो राज्ये द्वादश वर्षाणि देवो न ववर्ष । तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणा अधर्म (*śaṃtano rājye dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na vavarṣa | tamūcurbrāhmaṇā adharma*)
स्त्वया चरितो ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमंतरित्याभिषेचितं तस्मात्ते देवो न (*stvayā carito jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramaṃtarityābhiṣecitaṃ tasmātte devo na*)
वर्षतीति । स शंतनुर्देवापिं शिशिक्ष राज्येन । तमुवाच देवापिः पुरोहि- (*varṣatīti | sa śaṃtanurdevāpiṃ śiśikṣa rājyena | tamuvāca devāpiḥ purohi-*)
तस्तेऽसानि याजयानि च त्वेति ॥ (*taste 'sāni yājayāni ca tveti ‖*)
(सि. २-११) (*(si. 2-11)*)

In ancient times, in the Kuru line, the king Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa had two sons, Devāpi and Śantanu; Devāpi was the elder and Śantanu the younger. After their father Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa died, his elder son Devāpi wished to become king. But his younger brother Śantanu, giving no opportunity for this and wishing to be the ruler himself, drove away his elder brother Devāpi and began to rule the kingdom himself. The elder brother Devāpi, distressed, went to the forest and spent his time in austerities. Thereupon in Śantanu's country there came a great famine, no rain falling for twelve years. King Śantanu then reflected what should be done and asked the advice of the Brahmins. The Brahmins said to the king: "According to the dharmaśāstra the king's elder son is the one entitled to the kingdom. So the government should have been carried on by your elder brother Devāpi. But you gave no opportunity for this, drove him away and seized the kingdom. Because you are thus practising adharma, the god of rain does not send rain in your kingdom." Repenting of the wrong he had done, King Śantanu called his elder brother Devāpi, who was performing austerities in the forest, and offered him the kingdom. But Devāpi said that he did not want the kingdom, that he would take to the path of renunciation, performing austerities in the forest; that Śantanu should perform a sacrifice to remove the drought that had come in the kingdom, and that he himself would take up the priestly office in it and help the rain to fall. The king agreed, and Devāpi took the part of the priest called *hotṛ* in his sacrifice. Bṛhaspati became the priest called Brahmā. In that sacrifice, performed for rain, the *hotṛ* Devāpi prayed to Bṛhaspati, the Brahmā: "O Bṛhaspati, you have great influence over the minds of the gods; therefore teach me mantras to win them over." Bṛhaspati agreed and taught the *hotṛ* Devāpi the mantras containing the prayers to the gods needed for the fall of rain. By offering oblations to the gods with those mantras, rain fell abundantly: so it is said. Therefore this sūkta is also called the *vṛṣṭikāma* sūkta ("wishing for rain"). This matter, with some differences, is told also in Purāṇic works such as the Viṣṇu Purāṇa ४-२०-७ (*4-20-7*), the Mahābhārata Ādiparva, and the Bhāgavata Purāṇa ९-२२-१४ रिंद १७ (*9-22-14 riṃda 17*).

### Printed p. 302

*Running head: [302 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189] (as supplied).*

In the tenth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, in the sūkta १०८ (*108*), there is another narrative. Asuras called Paṇis stole the cows of the gods (the water-laden clouds) and hid them in an impregnable fortress. Indra sent Saramā, the divine bitch, to search for them. Saramā came to the Paṇis, entered into a dispute with them, and asked them to give back the stolen cows. The Paṇis said: What is Indra's power? We are great heroes and our weapons are very sharp; therefore the gods cannot conquer us, nor can they learn the place where the cows are kept; so if Saramā leaves the gods' side and joins their party, they will give her wealth and the like. Though they urged her in many ways, Saramā did not agree, and returned and told the gods everything. Then Bṛhaspati, by his own power, discovered the place where the cows were hidden. After that the gods subdued them and brought the cows back: such is the narrative.

In many such daring deeds Bṛhaspati's part is very important. In particular, when men need rain, Bṛhaspati's help is indispensable for helping them; this kind of prayer is what is specially seen in the sūktas addressed to Bṛhaspati.

Let us examine carefully what the qualities and achievements of Bṛhaspati are, as described in the Ṛgveda. Bṛhaspati was born of heaven and earth and is nourished by their greatness (ऋ सं ७-९७-८ (*ṛ saṃ 7-97-8*)). But in one place (२-२३-१७ (*2-23-17*)) it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ produced him. He is called the father of the gods (२-२६-३ (*2-26-3*)); it is also said that the gods were produced from him as sparks of fire fly at the blows of a smith's hammer (१०-७२-८ (*10-72-8*)).

He is called Brahmā (the priest called Brahmā) (१०-१४१-३ (*10-141-3*)). He is connected with the priests (७-१०-४ ; १०-१४-३ (*7-10-4 ; 10-14-3*)). He is also called Aṅgiras (४-४०-१ ; ४-७३-१ ; १०-४७-६ (*4-40-1 ; 4-73-1 ; 10-47-6*)). He composes and utters hymns; he is their lord and impeller (२-२३-१, २ ; १-४०-५ (*2-23-1, 2 ; 1-40-5*) and १०-९८-७ (*10-98-7*)); by the mantra alone he accomplishes all his aims (२-२४-३ (*2-24-3*)); mounting the blazing chariot called sacrifice he sets out to conquer the enemies of the gods and of the singers (२-२३ ३ (*2-23 3*)); he is the nourisher and protector of the faithful and their guide; he carries them across calamities (२-२३-४ (*2-23-4*)); he bestows wealth and the like on them (२-२३-९ (*2-23-9*)); he is called the father of all the gods; he is endowed with all divine qualities (३-६२-४ ; ४-५०-६ (*3-62-4 ; 4-50-6*)); he is all-formed; all things that all desire are in him (७-१०-४, ७-९७-४ (*7-10-4, 7-97-4*)); he bears a golden spear (७-९७-७ (*7-97-7*)); together with Indra he is the leader of the armies (१०-१०३-८ (*10-103-8*)).

### Printed p. 303

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 303 (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the introduction to the sūkta whose deity is Bṛhaspati; the list of his qualities from p. 302.)*

...one who prolongs life (१०-१००-५ (*10-100-5*)); plants arose from him (१०-९७-१५ (*10-97-15*) and १९ (*19*)); tawny horses are said to be his vehicle (नि. २-२८ (*ni. 2-28*)). Hearing the distressed cry of Trita, thrown into a well by demons and calling the gods to his help, Bṛhaspati delivered him from that dangerous condition (१-१०५-१७ (*1-105-17*)); it is also said that Bṛhaspati, together with Indra, made the water that was covered in darkness flow again (२-२३-१८ ; १-५६-५ (*2-23-18 ; 1-56-5*)).

Bṛhaspati by his own power broke the rock door of the well filled with honey; the gods drank that honey and sent rain abundantly (२-२४-३, ४ (*2-24-3, 4*)); when Bṛhaspati, with rays spitting fire, broke the strongholds of Vala, the herds of cows became visible; he drove the cows out as one breaks an egg; seeing the honey (water) covered by rock, he split it by his lion-roar alone and brought it out (१०-६८-४ रिंद ९ (*10-68-4 riṃda 9*)); Bṛhaspati brought the cows out of the rocks; he seized Vala's cows and took them in his power (१०-६८-५ (*10-68-5*)). Bṛhaspati is endowed with divinity (२-२३-२ (*2-23-2*)); he is one's own to all the gods (३-६२-४ ; ४-५०-६ (*3-62-4 ; 4-50-6*)) and has the most divinity among the gods; in the form of a god he gathers all the gods and all things into himself (२-२४-११ ; ८-६१-१८ (*2-24-11 ; 8-61-18*)); being capable, he keeps the two ends of the earth far apart (४-५०-१ (*4-50-1*)); the rising of the sun and moon one after the other is his imitable deed (१०-६८-१० (*10-68-10*)). In the Taittirīya-saṃhitā (the Yajurveda) the relation of Bṛhaspati to certain stars is stated: Bṛhaspati is the deity of the Puṣya asterism (तै. सं. ४-४ १०-१ (*tai. saṃ. 4-4 10-1*)); in the Purāṇas and elsewhere Bṛhaspati is described as Vācaspati and as the presiding deity of the planet Jupiter.

Some scholars have held that the deities Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are variant forms of Agni. The scholar M. Langlois in his translation of the Ṛgveda (part I, pp. 249, 254, 578) supports with many examples that these two deities are variant forms of Agni. The scholar Wilson expressed the same opinion in the introduction to the first part of his Ṛgveda translation; and the scholar Max Müller too says:

Brihaspati and Brahmanaspati are both varieties of Agni, the priest and the purohit of the Gods and men and as such he is invoked together with the Maruts &c. (*Brihaspati and Brahmanaspati are both varieties of Agni, the priest and the purohit of the Gods and men and as such he is invoked together with the Maruts &c.*)

That is, Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are both variant forms of Agni, who stand in the position of priest and purohit to the gods and men; for this reason they are invoked together with the Maruts in many places.

### Printed p. 304

*Running head: [304 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189] (as supplied; the print has the sūkta number ೧೮೯).*

We give one or two examples which state the identity of Agni with Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati.

त्वमग्न इंद्रो वृषभः सतामसि त्वं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः । (*tvamagna iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāmasi tvaṃ viṣṇururugāyo namasyaḥ |*)
त्वं ब्रह्मा रयिविद्ब्रह्मणस्पते त्वं विधर्तः सचसे पुरंध्या ॥ (*tvaṃ brahmā rayividbrahmaṇaspate tvaṃ vidhartaḥ sacase puraṃdhyā ‖*)
(म सं. २-१-३) (*(ma saṃ. 2-1-3)*)

"O Agni, you are Indra, the greatest among the good; you are Viṣṇu, the worshipful and of the vast body; O Brahmaṇaspati, you are the wealthy priest called Brahmā": thus Agni is described as the form of many deities.

तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं माशरिश्वानमुक्थं । (*taṃ śubhramagnimavase havāmahe vaiśvānaraṃ māśariśvānamukthaṃ |*)
बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवताशये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदं ॥ (*bṛhaspatiṃ manuṣo devatāśaye vipraṃ śrotāramatithiṃ raghuṣyadaṃ ‖*)
(ऋ सं. ३-२६-२) (*(ṛ saṃ. 3-26-2)*)

"We invoke for our protection the shining Agni, friend of mankind; the Mātariśvan worthy to be addressed by mantra, the wise, the praiser of the gods, the guest-like, the swift Bṛhaspati, to come to the rites such as sacrifice connected with men."

Sāyaṇācārya, in writing the commentary on the ṛk ५-४३-१२ (*5-43-12*), says of the word *bṛhaspati*:

अथवा इयमाग्नेयी। बृहतः परिवृढस्य कर्मणः स्वामाति बृहस्पतिरग्निरुच्यते। तथा नीलवर्णधूमपृष्टत्वसदनसादनहिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलिंगैरप्यग्निरेव बृह- स्पतिः (*athavā iyamāgneyī| bṛhataḥ parivṛḍhasya karmaṇaḥ svāmāti bṛhaspatiragnirucyate| tathā nīlavarṇadhūmapṛṣṭatvasadanasādanahiraṇyavarṇatvādiliṃgairapyagnireva bṛha- spatiḥ*)

That is: or this mantra may be said to address the deity Agni. Because he is the lord of the great work in the form of the sacrifice at hand, Agni is named Bṛhaspati. Likewise, by marks such as the black smoke as his back, the sacrificial altar as his place, and the golden colour, Bṛhaspati too must be said to be Agni.

Now let us examine the examples that state a difference between Agni and Bṛhaspati-Brahmaṇaspati.

सोषामविंदत्स स्वः १ [?] सो अग्निं सो अर्कॆण वि बबाधे तमांसि । (*soṣāmaviṃdatsa svaḥ 1 [?] so agniṃ so arkèṇa vi babādhe tamāṃsi |*)
बृहस्पतिर्गो वपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्ञानं न पर्वणो जभार ॥ (*bṛhaspatirgo vapuṣo valasya nirmajñānaṃ na parvaṇo jabhāra ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-६८-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-68-9)*)

In this ṛk it is said that Bṛhaspati obtained the dawn, heaven and Agni and drove away darkness with a mantra: that Bṛhaspati and Agni are different. (The print has a footnote sign ೧ in the first line, marked [?].)

### Printed p. 305

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 12] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 305 (as supplied).*

इंद्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बृहंतं । (*iṃdraṃ no agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣā rudraṃ rudrebhirā vahā bṛhaṃtaṃ |*)
आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बृहस्पतिमृक्वभिर्विश्ववारं ॥ (*ādityebhiraditiṃ viśvajanyāṃ bṛhaspatimṛkvabhirviśvavāraṃ ‖*)
(म सं. ७-१०-४) (*(ma saṃ. 7-10-4)*)

In this ṛk Agni is prayed to bring Indra with the Vasus, Rudra with the Maruts, Aditi, mother of all, with the Ādityas (gods), and Bṛhaspati with the Aṅgiras sages who praise. Besides, ṛks that indicate that Bṛhaspati or Brahmaṇaspati is different from Agni are many in the Ṛgveda, such as ३-२०-५, ४-४०-१. ५-५१-१२ ७-४१-१, ७-४४-१, ९-५-११, १०-३५-११, १०-६५-१, १०-१३०-४, १०-१४१-३ (*3-20-5, 4-40-1. 5-51-12 7-41-1, 7-44-1, 9-5-11, 10-35-11, 10-65-1, 10-130-4, 10-141-3*) and others. Therefore the doctrine that Agni is one and Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are others is the one supported in the Ṛgveda.

#### Sūkta 190

नूर तॊंभत्तनॆय सूक्तवु. (*nūra tòṃbhattanèya sūktavu.*) — "the hundred-and-ninetieth sūkta."

*[As supplied, Sāyaṇa's introduction to this sūkta has no label line; its lines are printed as plain lines and are given here as a block.]*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> अनर्वाणमित्यष्टर्चमेकादशं सूक्तमागस्त्यं बार्हस्पत्यं त्रैष्टुभं ।
> अनर्वाणं बार्हस्पत्यमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ श्रौतविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ अत्र शौनकः ।
> स्नात्वा जपेदनर्वाणं नमस्कृत्य बृहस्पतिं । वीरान्थनं च प्राप्नोति सोऽश्लोक्यं
> च नियच्छति । ऋग्वि. १-२७ । इति ॥

*Gist:* The sūkta "Anarvāṇam" is the eleventh of this group, of eight ṛks, by Agastya, to Bṛhaspati, in *triṣṭubh* (Anukramaṇikā); its ritual use is *laiṅgika*, according to the sense of the mantra; Śaunaka prescribes bathing and reciting it after saluting Bṛhaspati, to gain sons, wealth and fame.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Agastya is the seer of this sūkta; Bṛhaspati is the deity; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said, beginning अनर्वाणं बार्हस्पत्यं (*anarvāṇaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ*). The Śrauta use of this sūkta is *laiṅgika*, that is, according to the sense of the mantra. On the use of this sūkta the sage Śaunaka in his work Ṛgvidhāna says:

स्नात्वा जपेदनर्वाणं नमस्कृत्य बृहस्पतिं । (*snātvā japedanarvāṇaṃ namaskṛtya bṛhaspatiṃ |*)
वीरान् धनं च प्राप्नोति सुश्लोक्यं च नियच्छति ॥ (*vīrān dhanaṃ ca prāpnoti suślokyaṃ ca niyacchati ‖*)
(ऋग्विधान. १-२७) (*(ṛgvidhāna. 1-27)*)

That is: a person who, having bathed and become pure and saluted the deity Bṛhaspati, recites this sūkta of eight ṛks beginning "Anarvāṇam", Bṛhaspati gives him heroic sons, wealth and fame: so they say.

> *he hotaḥ navyaṃ navataraṃ stutyaṃ nā tamanarvāṇamagaṃtāraṃ | stoturadhīna-*
> *mityarthaḥ | vṛṣabhamapāṃ phalānāṃ varṣitāraṃ maṃdrajihvaṃ mādakavācakaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ*
> *maṃtrasya pālayitārametannāmakaṃ devamarkèrarcanasādhanairmaṃtrairvardhaya | pravṛddhaṃ*
> *kuru | surucaḥ śobhanadīpternavamānasya stūyamānasya | karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ ‖*
> *yasya bṛhaspateḥ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyaḥ ‖ rocamānaṃ stūyamānaṃ gāthānyaḥ | gātheti*
> *vāṅṇāma | stutivacaso netāro devā vyavahartāro martā manuṣyā hotrā-*
> *dayaḥ | yadvā | navamānasya stuvānasya yajamānasya saṃbaṃdhinaste | āśṛṇvaṃti āśrāva-*
> *yaṃti purā taṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vardhaya | atrānarvāṇamapratyṛtamanyasminnityādi niruktaṃ*
> *draṣṭavyaṃ | ni. 6-23 ‖*

*Gist:* O priest, increase with praises the ever-new Bṛhaspati, who does not go away from his worshipper, showerer of fruits, sweet-tongued, guardian of the mantra, of whose bright praise the gods and mortals sing; see the Nirukta नि. ६-२३ (*ni. 6-23*).

*[As supplied, a line reading प्रतिपदार्थ् (*pratipadārth*) with a block mark stands where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; standard label inserted. The following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(ऎलै होतृवे) सुरुचॆः—शोभनात्मकवाद कांतियुळ्ळवनू (*(èlai hotṛve) surucèḥ—śobhanātmakavāda kāṃtiyuḷḷavanū*) (O priest: of beautiful radiance). नवमानस्य—स्तुति सल्पडुववनू आद (*navamānasya—stuti salpaḍuvavanū āda*) (who is praised). यस्य—याव बृहस्पतिय (प्रशंसॆयन्नु) (*yasya—yāva bṛhaspatiya (praśaṃsèyannu)*) (of which Bṛhaspati, his praise). गाथान्यः—स्तुतिवाक्यगळिगॆ कर्तृगळू नेतृगळू आद (*gāthānyaḥ—stutivākyagaḷigè kartṛgaḷū netṛgaḷū āda*) (the makers and leaders of songs of praise). देवाः—देवतॆगळू (*devāḥ—devatègaḷū*) (the gods). मर्ताः—मानवरू (*martāḥ—mānavarū*) (and mortals). आशृण्वंति—घोषिसि पठिसुत्तारॆयो अंतह (*āśṛṇvaṃti—ghoṣisi paṭhisuttārèyo aṃtaha*) (proclaim and recite). नव्यं—स्तुत्यनू (*navyaṃ—stutyanū*) (praiseworthy). अनर्वाणं—(स्तोतृवन्नु बिट्टु) बेरॆ प्रदेशक्कॆ होगदिरुववनू (*anarvāṇaṃ—(stotṛvannu biṭṭu) berè pradeśakkè hogadiruvavanū*) (not going away from the worshipper to another place). वृषभं—इष्टार्थगळन्नु सुरिसुववनू (*vṛṣabhaṃ—iṣṭārthagaḷannu surisuvavanū*) (the showerer of desired things). मंद्रजिह्वं—हर्षदायकवाद वाक्यवुळ्ळवनू आद (*maṃdrajihvaṃ—harṣadāyakavāda vākyavuḷḷavanū āda*) (of joy-giving speech). बृहस्पतिं—मंत्रक्कॆ पालकनू आद बृहस्पतियन्नु (*bṛhaspatiṃ—maṃtrakkè pālakanū āda bṛhaspatiyannu*) (Bṛhaspati, guardian of the mantra). अर्कैः—पूजासाधन गळाद मंत्रगळिंद (*arkaiḥ—pūjāsādhana gaḷāda maṃtragaḷiṃda*) (with the mantras that are means of worship). वर्धय—प्रवृद्धनागुवंतॆ माडु (स्तोत्रमाडु) (*vardhaya—pravṛddhanāguvaṃtè māḍu (stotramāḍu)*) (make him grow, praise him).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Bṛhaspati is of beautiful radiance and praiseworthy; the gods and mortals, leaders of songs of praise, proclaim and recite his praise. Make that praiseworthy Bṛhaspati, who stays with his worshipper, showers desired things, has joy-giving speech and guards the mantra, grow by the mantras that are means of worship.

**Printed English translation**

Priests, augment by your hymns Brihaspati, who deserts not (his worshipper) ; the showerer (of benefits), the pleasant-tongued, the adorable ; of whom resplendent, gods and men, (the ministers) of the institutor of the sacrifice, emulous in sacred songs, proclaim (the praise) (as printed, without a final full stop)

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*) — अगंतारं स्तोतुरधीनमित्यर्थः (*agaṃtāraṃ stoturadhīnamityarthaḥ*): Sāyaṇa explains it as one who does not leave the neighbourhood of the sacrificer who praises, that is, who is subject to the sacrificer who praises. According to the view of the Nirukta-authors for this word: अप्रत्यृतः अप्रतिगतोऽन्यस्मिन् अन्यमनाश्रितः स्वतंत्र इत्यर्थः (*apratyṛtaḥ apratigato 'nyasmin anyamanāśritaḥ svataṃtra ityarthaḥ*) (नि-४-२७ (*ni-4-27*)): one who does not seek another's help, independent. Both senses are possible here.

वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*) — अपां फलानां वर्षितारं (*apāṃ phalānāṃ varṣitāraṃ*). We have explained the derivation of the word *vṛṣabha* at length in the Ṛgveda part five, page 682 (*682*), part eight, page 168 (*168*) and other places. In the present ṛk the sense is one who showers fruits in the form of water. On Bṛhaspati's helping in the giving of rain, see what is said in the introduction to this sūkta (page 301 (*301*)).

### Printed p. 308

*Running head: [308 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190] (as supplied).*

मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*) — मादकवाचं (*mādakavācaṃ*): one who has a tongue that speaks words giving joy to the mind, that is, one who speaks pleasing words so that those who praise are glad.

अर्कै: (*arkai:*) — अर्चनसाधनैर्मंत्रैः (*arcanasādhanairmaṃtraiḥ*): with mantras that are the means of praising. Because they are used for praising, mantras are called *arka*. On the word *arka* Yāska:

अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति (*arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti | arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti*)
अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥ (*arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ‖*)
(नि. ५-४) (*(ni. 5-4)*)

gives four kinds of meaning:

*[List marker in the supplied text: "1."]*

(1) अर्कॊ देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यद्य- स्मादेनं देवं अर्चंति स्तोतारः (*arkò devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti | tāvatsarva evārka ityucyate yadya- smādenaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti stotāraḥ*): *arka* means a deity, because the devotees use it to worship someone; that is, the person or god whom the devotees worship is called *arka*.

(2) अर्कॊ मंत्रो भवति । यद्यस्मात् अनेन मंत्रेण अर्चंति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः (*arkò maṃtro bhavati | yadyasmāt anena maṃtreṇa arcaṃti stotāraḥ tasmādarkaḥ*): *arka* also means a mantra, because those who praise worship the deity with it; hence *arka* is also the name of the mantra.

(3) अर्कमन्नं भवति । तद्दि अर्चति भूतानि यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते पूज्यं च सर्वस्यॆवान्नं (*arkamannaṃ bhavati | taddi arcati bhūtāni yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyèvānnaṃ*): *arka* also means food; since food (nourishment) is necessary to all creatures, everyone honours it with respect and desires it, and so the word *arka* also means food.

(4) अर्कॊ वृक्षो भवतिय एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्मा कटुकभावेन भवति (*arkò vṛkṣo bhavatiya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimmā kaṭukabhāvena bhavati*): the name "tree" for the word *arka* is well known; the *arka* tree is, in the Karnataka language, the plant called *ekka* (the swallow-wort). Since its kindling-sticks are used in sacrifices and it is used in medicines and the like, the *arka* tree is a thing known to all; since it is bitter it is called *kaṭukimmā*. As an example for the explanation of the word *arka*, Yāska gives गायंतित्वा (ऋ सं १-१०-१) (*gāyaṃtitvā (ṛ saṃ 1-10-1)*) (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 309

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ ೫. ವ. ೧೨.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 309 (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 of Sūkta 190, on *arkaiḥ*.)*

...taking the ṛk, he gives its explanation; that explanation is not relevant here. In the present ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has accepted for the word *arka* the sense "mantra".

गाथान्यः (*gāthānyaḥ*) — since the word *gāthā* is read among the fifty-seven names of speech, *ślokaḥ*, *dhārā* and others (नि. २-२३ (*ni. 2-23*)), *gāthā* means speech in the form of praise. गाथा नयंतीति गाथान्यः (*gāthā nayaṃtīti gāthānyaḥ*): the sense is the gods who are leaders of such mantras of praise, and the priests such as the *hotṛ* who recite the mantras.

On the sentence अथवा नवमानस्य (संबंधिनस्ते) गाथान्यः आशृण्वंति आश्रावयंति (*athavā navamānasya (saṃbaṃdhinaste) gāthānyaḥ āśṛṇvaṃti āśrāvayaṃti*) the bhāṣyakāra gives another sense too: the *hotṛ* and other relatives of the sacrificer who praises satisfy Bṛhaspati by reciting mantras.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 1, noted briefly)

अनर्वाणम् (*anarvāṇam*): by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (पा सू. ६-२-१७२ (*pā sū. 6-2-172*)) the last syllable of the final member is acute; accusative singular; since अर्वणस्त्रसावनञ्ः (*arvaṇastrasāvanañḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-४-१७२ (*pā. sū. 6-4-172*), as printed) prohibits, in *anañ*, the substitute *tṛ* as a final does not occur. मंद्रजिह्वम् (*maṃdrajihvam*): मंद्रा जिह्वा यस्य सः (*maṃdrā jihvā yasya saḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौप्रकृत्या— (*bahuvrīhauprakṛtyā—*) (पा. सू. ६-२-१ (*pā. sū. 6-2-1*)) the first member keeps its natural accent. वर्धयॆ (*vardhayè*) (the print): root वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*); since the agency of the causer appears, by हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) (पा. सू. ३-१-२६ (*pā. sū. 3-1-26*)) *ṇic*; *loṭ* after the causative; second person singular; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. गाथान्या (*gāthānyā*) (the print): root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*); by णोनः (*ṇonaḥ*) *n* for the initial; गाथाः नयंति इति गाथान्यः (*gāthāḥ nayaṃti iti gāthānyaḥ*); the suffix *kvip*; by the accent of the final member of the *kṛt* compound the *ī* is acute; when *jas* follows, the substitute *yaṇ*; since an unaccented ending follows the *yaṇ* that has come in the place of the acute, by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः— (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ—*) (पा. सू. ८-२-४ (*pā. sū. 8-2-4*)) the svarita accent comes. आशृण्वंति (*āśṛṇvaṃti*) (root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*)): *laṭ*, third person plural, the ending *jhi*; by झोंतः (*jhoṃtaḥ*) the substitute *anta* for it; by श्रुवः शृच (*śruvaḥ śṛca*) (पा. सू. ३-१-७४ (*pā. sū. 3-1-74*)) the substitute *śṛ* for the root; the stem-suffix *śnu*; *yaṇ*; being at the beginning of the pāda the *nighāta* accent does not occur; the suffix's first syllable is acute; by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (पा सू. ८-१-७१ (*pā sū. 8-1-71*)) the preverb (*ā*) is unaccented. नवमानस्य (*navamānasya*) (root णि स्तुत् (*ṇi stut*), as printed): by शोनः (*śonaḥ*) *n* for the initial; the participle *śānac* for *laṭ*; by *vyatyaya* the agent suffix has come in the passive; the stem-suffix *śap*; by सार्वधातुकार्थ— (*sārvadhātukārtha—*)

#### Ṛk 2

*[As supplied, the label line of the Saṃhitā reads संहार (*saṃhāra*); standard label inserted.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तम्मृ॒त्विया॒ उप॒ वाचः॑ सचंते॒ सर्गो॒ न यो दे॑वय॒ता-॑
> मसर्जि ।
> बृह॒स्पतिः॒ स ह्यंजो॒ वरां॑सि॒ विभ्वाभ॑व॒त्समृ॒ते मा॑त॒रिश्वा॑ ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । ऋत्वियाः । उप । वाचः । सचंते । सर्गः । न । यः । देव्ययतां । असर्जि !
> बृहस्पतिः । सः । हि । अंजः । वरांसि । विभ्वा । अभवत् । सं । ऋते । मातरिश्वा ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> बार्हस्पत्ये पशौ तमृत्वियेत्येषा वपायाज्या । सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते अति
> यदर्यो अर्हात्तमृतिया उप वाचः सचंते । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> तं बृहस्पतिमृत्विया वर्षर्तुसंबंधिन्यो वाचो माध्यमिका उप संचते ।
> समीपे सेवंते । यः सर्गो नोदकस्य स्रष्टापि । नशब्दोऽप्यर्थे । देवयतां
> देवानिच्छतां यजमानानामसर्जि फलं । यद्वा । देवं तमिच्छतां मनुष्याणाम-
> सर्जि सृष्टवान्वृष्टु दकं । यद्वा । ऋत्वियाः प्राप्तकालीना वाचो हॊत्रादिप्रेरिता
> वाच उप सचंते तं यः सर्गो नोदकसृष्टिरिव सः स एव बृहस्पतिरंजो हि
> व्यंजकः खलु । तस्मिन्वर्षति सर्वे भवंति। आत एव विभ्वा विभुर्वाप्नो मातरिश्वा वृष्टि-
> निर्मातर्यंतरिक्षे चेष्टमानो वायुसदृशो वा वरांसि वरणीयानि वृष्टादि-
> फलानि संपादयन्नृत उदके निमित्तभूते सति समभवत् । संभूतः। अथवा । अंजो
> यज्जियानां व्यंजको मातरिश्वा फलस्य निर्मातरि यज्ञे श्वसिता वर्तमानः स बृह-
> स्पतिर्यते यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति वरांसि वरणीयानि हवींशीच्छन् विभ्वा विभुः
> समभवत् ॥

*Gist:* The first lines give the ritual use (Āśvalāyana: the *vapā* yājyā in the Bṛhaspati animal sacrifice). Then: the rain-season speech approaches that Bṛhaspati who, like a creator of water, has produced the fruit for the sacrificers desiring the gods; he is the manifester, pervading, wind-like in the atmosphere, who brings forth desirable fruits such as rain when water is the cause.

### Printed p. 311

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 12] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 311 (as supplied).*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यः—याव बृहस्पतियु (*yaḥ—yāva bṛhaspatiyu*) (who, which Bṛhaspati). सर्गो न—(उदकवन्नु) सृष्टिसुववने आगिद्दानॆयो (मत्तु) (*sargo na—(udakavannu) sṛṣṭisuvavane āgiddānèyo (mattu)*) (is a creator, as it were of water). देवयतां—देवतॆगळन्नु सहायार्थवागि अपेक्षिसुव यजमानरिगॆ (*devayatāṃ—devatègaḷannu sahāyārthavāgi apekṣisuva yajamānarigè*) (to sacrificers who desire the gods' help). असर्जि— फलवन्नु सृष्टिसि ऒदगिसुत्तानॆयो (*asarji— phalavannu sṛṣṭisi òdagisuttānèyo*) (creates and provides the fruit). तं—अंतह बृहस्पतियन्नु (*taṃ—aṃtaha bṛhaspatiyannu*) (him, such a Bṛhaspati). ऋत्वियाः—वर्षर्तुविगॆ संबंधिसिद (*ṛtviyāḥ—varṣartuvigè saṃbaṃdhisida*) (belonging to the rainy season). वाचः—माध्यमिका वाक्कुगळु (*vācaḥ—mādhyamikā vākkugaḷu*) (middle-region speech). उप सचंते—समीपिसि सेविसुत्तवॆ (*upa sacaṃte—samīpisi sevisuttavè*) (approach and serve). सः बृहस्पतिः—अदे बृहस्पतियु (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ—ade bṛhaspatiyu*) (that same Bṛhaspati). अंजः हि—सकलवन्नू आविर्भविसुवंतॆ माडुववनल्लवे ? । (*aṃjaḥ hi—sakalavannū āvirbhavisuvaṃtè māḍuvavanallave ? |*) (is he not the one who makes all things manifest?). विभ्वा—व्यापिसिरुववनू (*vibhvā—vyāpisiruvavanū*) (the all-pervading). मातरिश्वा—अंतरिक्षदल्लि संचरिसुववनू अथवा वायुसदृशनू आद अवनु (*mātariśvā—aṃtarikṣadalli saṃcarisuvavanū athavā vāyusadṛśanū āda avanu*) (he who moves in the atmosphere or is like the wind). वरांसि—अपेक्षितगळाद वृष्टादि फलगळन्नु संपादिसिकॊडुत्ता (*varāṃsi—apekṣitagaḷāda vṛṣṭādi phalagaḷannu saṃpādisikòḍuttā*) (providing the desired fruits such as rain). ऋते—उदकद निमित्तवागि ॥ (*ṛte—udakada nimittavāgi ‖*) (for the sake of water). समभवत्—उत्पन्ननादनु (*samabhavat—utpannanādanu*) (came into being).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Bṛhaspati, who creates water and creates and provides the fruit in the form of rain to the sacrificer who desires the gods' help, is approached and served by the middle-region speech belonging to the rainy season. That same Bṛhaspati makes all things manifest; and by his impulse the wind, pervading everywhere and moving in the atmosphere, provides the desired rain and the like and came into being for the sake of water.

*[As supplied, the label line reads English Translatin (*English Translatin*), run on after the Bhāvārtha; standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

The hymns of the (rainy) season are addressed to him, who is verily the creator (of the rain), and has granted it (to the prayers) of the devout ; for that Brihaspati is the manifester (of all), the expansive wind that (dispensing) blessing has been produced for (the diffusion of water).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

In the animal sacrifice, when the *vapā* offering is made to Bṛhaspati, this ṛk तम्मृतिया (*tammṛtiyā*) (the print) is to be used as the *yājyā* mantra, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra rule बृहस्पते अति यदर्यो आर्हात्तमृतिया उप वाचः सचंते (*bṛhaspate ati yadaryo ārhāttamṛtiyā upa vācaḥ sacaṃte*) (आ. ३-७ (*ā. 3-7*)).

ऋत्वियॊ—वर्षतुर्संबंधिन्यो वाचः (*ṛtviyò—varṣatursaṃbaṃdhinyo vācaḥ*) — since Bṛhaspati has a connection with rain, here it is said "speech connected with the rainy season".

न (*na*) — the word *na* is used here in the sense of combination (the sense *api*). Besides, नेति प्रतिषेधार्थियो भाषायां । उभयमन्वध्यायं (*neti pratiṣedhārthiyo bhāṣāyāṃ | ubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ*): that is, in ordinary speech the word *na* denotes prohibition (denies); in the metrical texts it denotes both, prohibition and comparison: so Yāska's explanation runs (नि. १-४ (*ni. 1-4*)).

### Printed p. 312

*Running head (unmarked page break in the supplied text; printed inside the text): [312 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24. Sū. 190] (the print has "ಸಾಯುಣ" with a misprint).*

मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) — सर्वस्य जगतः निर्मातरि अंतरिक्षे श्वसन् वर्तमानः (*sarvasya jagataḥ nirmātari aṃtarikṣe śvasan vartamānaḥ*): the explanation of the word *mātariśvā*, "existing, breathing, in the atmosphere that is the maker of the whole world". This word may mean deities such as Agni and Vāyu. Here Sāyaṇa explains "wind-like", that is, pervading the atmosphere.

*[As supplied, the label line reads व्याकरण, प्रक्रिया (*vyākaraṇa, prakriyā*); standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 2, noted briefly)

ऋत्वियाः (*ṛtviyāḥ*): by छंदसि घस् (*chaṃdasi ghas*) (पा. सू. ५-१-१०६ (*pā. sū. 5-1-106*)) the suffix *ghas* for the word *ṛtu*; by आयनेयीनी — (*āyaneyīnī —*) (पा. सू. ७-१-२ (*pā. sū. 7-1-2*)) the substitute *iya*; by सितिच (*sitica*) (पा. सू. १-४-१६ (*pā. sū. 1-4-16*)) the *pada* designation, as an exception to the *bha* designation, because the suffix is marked *n*, so that by ओर्गुणः (*orguṇaḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-४-१४६ (*pā. sū. 6-4-146*)) guṇa of the *u* does not occur; *yaṇ*; the suffix's first syllable is acute. सचंते (*sacaṃte*) (root षच समवाये (*ṣaca samavāye*)): *s* for the initial; *laṭ*, third person plural; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. देवयताम् (*devayatām*): देवान् आत्मनः इच्छंतः देवयंतः तेषाम् (*devān ātmanaḥ icchaṃtaḥ devayaṃtaḥ teṣām*); by सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*) the suffix *kyac*; *laṭ* after it with the participle substitute; genitive plural; since an ending beginning with a vowel follows the participle without *num*, by ततुरनुमो नद्यजादी (*taturanumo nadyajādī*) (पा. सू ६-१-१७३ (*pā. sū 6-1-173*)) it is acute. असर्जि (*asarji*) (root सृज विसर्गॆ (*sṛja visargè*)): *luṅ* in the passive, third person singular, suffix *ta*; by चिण् भावकर्मणोः (*ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*) (पा. सू ३-१-६६ (*pā. sū 3-1-66*)) the substitute *ciṇ* for *cli*; on that basis guṇa of the root's penultimate; by चिणोलुक् (*ciṇoluk*) (पा. सू. ६-४-१०४ (*pā. sū. 6-4-104*)) *luk* of the suffix after *ciṇ*; the augment *aṭ*; by यद्वृत्तान्वितम् (*yadvṛttānvitam*) (पा. सू. ८-१-६६ (*pā. sū. 8-1-66*)) because of the connection with *yat* the *nighāta* is prohibited; by the accent of the augment *aṭ* the first syllable is acute. अञ्ज् : (*añj :*) (root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिपु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatipu*), as printed): the suffix *ac* applying to all roots; being marked *n*, the first syllable is acute. वरांसि (*varāṃsi*) (root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*)): as before the suffix *asun*; on that basis by सार्वधातुका— (*sārvadhātukā—*) guṇa of the root's *ṛ*; accusative plural (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

विभ्वा (*vibhvā*) (root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*)): by विप्रसंभो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् (*viprasaṃbho ḍvasaṃjñāyām*) (पा. सू. ३-२-१८० (*pā. sū. 3-2-180*)) the suffix *ḍu* when *vi* is the prefix; because it is marked *ḍ*, the *ṭi* is dropped; the form *vibhu* results; when *su* follows, by सुपांसुलुक्— (*supāṃsuluk—*) (पा. सू. ७-१-३९ (*pā. sū. 7-1-39*)) the substitute *a* for it; then if *yaṇ* were to come by ओः सुपि (*oḥ supi*) (पा सू ६-४-८३ (*pā sū 6-4-83*)), it is prohibited by नभू सुधियोः (*nabhū sudhiyoḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-४-८५ (*pā. sū. 6-4-85*)); by छंदस्युभयथा (*chaṃdasyubhayathā*) (पा. सू. ६-४-८६ (*pā. sū. 6-4-86*)) *yaṇ* comes again; by *vyatyaya* the first syllable is acute. Or, the Uṇādi suffix *ḍun* after the root *bhū* with *vi*; because it is marked *n*, by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१९७ (*pā. sū. 6-1-197*)) the first syllable is acute.

> सामर्थान्मंदेहाद्यसुराञ्चाति तेजस्वी भवति तादृशो महानुभावो यजमान-
> दत्तं हविरादिकं स्वीकरोतीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* This Bṛhaspati strives to accept the praise offered by the sacrificer, the oblation of food and other mantras, as the sun puts forth his arms; by the power of this Bṛhaspati, who is free of hostile demons, the day-sun shines, terrible as a beast and mighty.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सविता—सूर‍्यनु (*savitā—sūryanu*) (the sun). प्र बाहू इव—तन्न हस्त (किरण)गळन्नु प्रसरिसुवंतॆ (*pra bāhū iva—tanna hasta (kiraṇa)gaḷannu prasarisuvaṃtè*) (as he stretches out his arms, the rays). अयं— ई बृहस्पतियु (*ayaṃ— ī bṛhaspatiyu*) (this Bṛhaspati). उपस्तुतिं—(यजमाननिंद) पठितवाद स्तुतियन्नू (*upastutiṃ—(yajamānaniṃda) paṭhitavāda stutiyannū*) (the praise recited by the sacrificer). नमसः—हवीरूपद अन्नद (*namasaḥ—havīrūpada annada*) (of food in the form of an oblation). उद्यंति—अर्पणॆयन्नू (*udyaṃti—arpaṇèyannū*) (the offering). श्लोकं—इतर विधवाद मंत्रविशेषगळन्नू (*ślokaṃ—itara vidhavāda maṃtraviśeṣagaḷannū*) (other special mantras). प्रयं- सत्—आत्मच्छॆयिंद स्वीकरिसलु प्रयत्निसुत्तानॆ (*prayaṃ- sat—ātmacchèyiṃda svīkarisalu prayatnisuttānè*) (strives to accept willingly; the print has "ಆತ್ಮಚ್ಛೆ", as supplied). अथवा सूर‍्यनु किरणगळन्नु प्रसरिसि प्रकाशवन्नु कॊडुवंतॆ यजमाननू सह तन्न बाहुगळन्नु प्रसरिसि स्तुत्यादिगळन्नु अर्पिसुत्तानॆ (*athavā sūryanu kiraṇagaḷannu prasarisi prakāśavannu kòḍuvaṃtè yajamānanū saha tanna bāhugaḷannu prasarisi stutyādigaḷannu arpisuttānè*) (or, as the sun stretches out his rays and gives light, so the sacrificer too, stretching out his arms, offers praise and the like). अरक्षसः— तनगॆ विरोधिगळाद राक्षसरे इल्लदंतॆ माडिरुव (*arakṣasaḥ— tanagè virodhigaḷāda rākṣasare illadaṃtè māḍiruva*) (who has left no hostile demons). अस्य—ई बृहस्पतिय (*asya—ī bṛhaspatiya*) (of this Bṛhaspati). क्रत्वा—सामर्थ्यदिंद (*kratvā—sāmarthyadiṃda*) (by power). अहन्यः—अहस्सन्नुंटुमाडि प्रकाशिसतक्क (*ahanyaḥ—ahassannuṃṭumāḍi prakāśisatakka*) (the day-shining). यः अस्ति—याव सूर‍्यनिद्दानॆयो (*yaḥ asti—yāva sūryaniddānèyo*) (the sun that exists). (सः— अवनु) (*(saḥ— avanu)*) (he). मृगो न—क्रूरमृगदंतॆ (*mṛgo na—krūramṛgadaṃtè*) (like a fierce beast). भीमः—भयंकरनागियू (*bhīmaḥ—bhayaṃkaranāgiyū*) (terrible). तुविष्मान्—बलशालि यागियू आगिद्दानॆ (*tuviṣmān—balaśāli yāgiyū āgiddānè*) (and mighty).

*[As supplied, the label line reads धनार्थ (*dhanārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As the sun stretches out his rays, this Bṛhaspati strives to accept willingly the praise recited by the sacrificer, the food offered by him and other special mantras. By the power of this Bṛhaspati, who has left no hostile demons, the sun who makes and shines by day is terrible as a fierce beast and mighty.

*[As supplied, the label line reads Englih Tranlation (*Englih Tranlation*); standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

He is ready (to accept) the offered praise, the presentation of the homage. the hymn, as the sun (is ready to put forth) his rays ; by the acts of him whom the Rakshasas (oppose not), the daily (revolving sun) exists, and he is strong as a fearful beast of prey.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

For the first half of this ṛk Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning: this Bṛhaspati, hearing the praise made by the sacrificer seated near, accepts the oblation of food in the form of an offering which the sacrificer presents with outstretched hands, and the mantra in the form of praise, as the sun accepts praise and the like

### Printed p. 315

*Running head: [ಅ: ೨. ಅ. ೫ ನ. ೧೨] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 315 (as supplied; the print has "ನ." for the varga sign).*

— this is one sense. Or: while this sacrificer praises Bṛhaspati, as the sun, the cause of the whole world, gives light, heat and the like to the people of the world with his rays that are like arms, so this sacrificer too offers with outstretched hand oblations of food and other mantras in the form of praise to Bṛhaspati: this is the other sense. Both senses are possible here.

In the latter half Bṛhaspati's power and prowess are described. अरक्षसः (*arakṣasaḥ*) means one who has no hostile demons, that is, none among the demons has the strength and power to face this Bṛhaspati; तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*) means very mighty; मृगो न भीमः (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ*) means of a terrible might like beasts such as the lion. The giving of the simile मृगो न भीमः (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ*) to one of great prowess occurs in many places in the Ṛgveda:

प्र तद्विष्णुस्तवते वीर्येण मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः । (*pra tadviṣṇustavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१५४-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-154-2)*)

मृगो न हस्ती तविषीमुषाणः सिंहो न भीमः आयुधानि बिभ्रत् ॥ (*mṛgo na hastī taviṣīmuṣāṇaḥ siṃho na bhīmaḥ āyudhāni bibhrat ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ४-१६-१४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 4-16-14)*)

अश्वो न क्रदो वृषभिर्युजानः सिंहो न भीमो मनसो जवीयान् । (*aśvo na krado vṛṣabhiryujānaḥ siṃho na bhīmo manaso javīyān |*)
(ऋ. सं. ९-९७-२८) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 9-97-28)*)

आशु: शिशानो वृषभो न भीमो घनाघनः क्षोभणश्चर्षणीनां ॥ (*āśu: śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaścarṣaṇīnāṃ ‖*)
(ऋ सं. १०-१०३-१) (*(ṛ saṃ. 10-103-1)*)

In these and other ṛks the word *bhīma* is used in the sense of terrible prowess, with the simile of strong beasts such as the lion and the bull.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 3, noted briefly)

नमसः (*namasaḥ*) (root णमु प्रह्वत्वे शब्दे च (*ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca*)): by नोनः (*nonaḥ*) *n* for the initial; the Uṇādi suffix *asun*; because it is marked *n*, the first syllable is acute; genitive singular. यंसत् (*yaṃsat*) (root यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*)): *leṭ*, third person singular; by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (वा. सू. ३-१-३४ (*vā. sū. 3-1-34*), as printed) *sip*; by तिज्जतिजिः (*tijjatijiḥ*) (as printed) the *nighāta* accent. बाहू (*bāhū*): by *vyatyaya* the nominative dual has been substituted for the instrumental dual; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. अहन्यः (*ahanyaḥ*): अह्नि भवः (*ahni bhavaḥ*) (one who is in the day); the suffix *yat* in the sense of the state; because it is marked *t*, by तित्स्वरितम् (*titsvaritam*) (पा सू ६-१-१८५ (*pā sū 6-1-185*)) it takes the svarita accent (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

*Running head: [316 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. ೧. ೯ಅ. 24. Sū. 190] (as supplied, as printed, with a stray ೯).*

*(Continuation of the Ṛk 3 grammar page of Sūkta 190, after the *ahanyaḥ* entry which ended the previous window.)*

अस्ति (*asti*): because *yaḥ* precedes, by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) (पा. सू. ८-१-६६ (*pā. sū. 8-1-66*)) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited; because the suffix is marked *p*, the accent of the root remains. भीम: (*bhīma:*) (root इंभी भये (*iṃbhī bhaye*), as printed): by भियः सुग्वा (*bhiyaḥ sugvā*) (उ सू १-१४५ (*u sū 1-145*)) the suffix *mak*; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. Yāska has explained भीमः भिभ्यत्यस्मात् (*bhīmaḥ bhibhyatyasmāt*) (निरु. १-२० (*niru. 1-20*)).

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒स्य श्लोको॑ दि॒वीय॑ते पृथि॒व्यामत्यो॒ न यं॑सद्यक्ष॒भृद्वि॑
> चेताः ।
> मृ॒गाणां॒ न हे॒तयो॒ यंति॑ चे॒मा बृह॒स्पते॒रहि॑माया अ॒भि
> द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्य । श्लोकः । दिवि । ईयते । पृथिव्यां । अत्यः । न । यंसत् । यक्षभृत् ।
> विचेताः ।
> मृगाणां । न । हेतयः । यंति । च । इमाः । बृहस्पतेः । अहिमायान् । अभि ।
> द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*[A second, garbled label line शायणभाष्यं (*śāyaṇabhāṣyaṃ*) follows the label in the supplied text; kept as a note in the Kannada text.]*

> अस्य बृहस्पतेः श्लोकः स्तुत्यात्मिका कीर्तिर्गर्जितवाग्वा दिवि द्योतमाने
> द्युलोके पृथिव्यां चेयते । गच्छति । व्याप्ोति । यो बृहस्पतिरत्यो नातनशील
> आदित्य इव यक्षभृत् पूजितं हविरादिकं दधानो विचेता विविधं चेतयिता प्राणिनां
> विशिष्टप्रज्ञायुक्तो वा यंसत् नियच्छति फलु । किंच मृगाणां हंतुमन्विष्यतां
> हेतयो नायुधानीवास्य बृहस्पतेरिमा हेतयो हिंस्राण्यायुधानि यंति ।
> गच्छंति च ॥ चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः ॥ अहिमायानागत्य हंत्रोऽंतरिक्ष-
> चारिण्यो वा माया येषां वृत्रादीनां तानसुरान् द्यून् दिवसान् ॥ काला-
> ध्वनोः । पा. २-३-५ । इति द्वितीया ॥ तान्यायुधान्यभि लक्षयंति च । उपसर्गश्रुते-
> र्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥

*Gist:* The praise of this Bṛhaspati spreads through heaven and earth, and he, like the ever-moving sun, bearing the honoured oblations and discerning, gives fruit; his fierce weapons, like those of hunters, go daily against the deceitful asuras such as Vṛtra.

### Printed p. 317

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೫. ವ. ೧೨ j] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 317 (as supplied, as printed).*

*[As supplied, a line reading प्रसिद्धवाद (*prasiddhavāda*) with a block mark stands where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; standard label inserted. The following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अस्य—ई बृहस्पतिय (*asya—ī bṛhaspatiya*) (of this Bṛhaspati). श्लोकः—स्तुत्यात्मकवाद कीर्तियु (*ślokaḥ—stutyātmakavāda kīrtiyu*) (the glory in the form of praise). दिवि—प्रकाशमानवाद द्युलोकदल्लियू (*divi—prakāśamānavāda dyulokadalliyū*) (in the shining heaven). पृथिव्यां—पृथिवियल्लियू (*pṛthivyāṃ—pṛthiviyalliyū*) (and on earth). ईयते—व्यापिसुत्तदॆ (इवनु) (*īyate—vyāpisuttadè (ivanu)*) (spreads). अत्यो न— (शाश्वतवागि) संचरिसतक्क आदित्यनंतॆ (*atyo na— (śāśvatavāgi) saṃcarisatakka ādityanaṃtè*) (like the sun that ever moves). यक्षभृत्—पूज्यवाद हविस्सुगळन्नु वहिसियू (*yakṣabhṛt—pūjyavāda havissugaḷannu vahisiyū*) (bearing the honoured oblations). विचेताः—प्रज्ञायुक्तनागियू अथवा प्राणिगळन्नु चैतन्ययुक्तवागि माडुत्तलू (*vicetāḥ—prajñāyuktanāgiyū athavā prāṇigaḷannu caitanyayuktavāgi māḍuttalū*) (discerning, or making creatures full of life). यंसत्- फलवन्नु कॊडुत्तानॆ (*yaṃsat- phalavannu kòḍuttānè*) (he gives fruit). मृगाणां—मृगगळन्नु बेटॆयाडुव व्याधर (*mṛgāṇāṃ—mṛgagaḷannu beṭèyāḍuva vyādhara*) (of the hunters who hunt beasts). हेतयः न—(हरितवाद) आयुधगळंतॆ (*hetayaḥ na—(haritavāda) āyudhagaḷaṃtè*) (like the sharp weapons). बृहस्पतेः—बृहस्पतिय (*bṛhaspateḥ—bṛhaspatiya*) (of Bṛhaspati). इमाः—क्रूरवाद आयुधगळु (*imāḥ—krūravāda āyudhagaḷu*) (these cruel weapons). द्यून्—प्रति दिनवू (*dyūn—prati dinavū*) (every day). अहिमायान् अभि—वंचकराद असुररन्नु लक्षिसि (*ahimāyān abhi—vaṃcakarāda asurarannu lakṣisi*) (aiming at the deceitful asuras). यंति च—अट्टिसिकॊंडू होगुत्तवॆ (*yaṃti ca—aṭṭisikòṃḍū hoguttavè*) (and go after them).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The praise of Bṛhaspati spreads through shining heaven and earth. Like the sun that ever moves, he gives fruits, bearing the honoured oblations and discerning. Like the sharp weapons of hunters who hunt beasts, Bṛhaspati's cruel weapons pursue the deceitful asuras every day and harm them.

**Printed English translation**

The glory of this Brihaspati spreads through heaven and earth like the sun : receiving worship, and giving intelligence, he bestows (the rewards of sacrifice) ; like the weapons of the hunters, so these (weapons) of Brihaspati fall daily upon the workers of guile.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषवियरु (*viśeṣaviyaru*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

In this ṛk Bṛhaspati's glory spreading through earth and heaven, his bearing the oblation, and his destroying enemies, asuras and other wicked ones with his weapons are described. In this matter the sūkta ६नॆय मंडलद ७३नॆय सूक्त (*6nèya maṃḍalada 73nèya sūkta*) (the seventy-third sūkta of the sixth maṇḍala) describes the above qualities of Bṛhaspati very well; I give it here as an example:

यो अद्रिभित् प्रथमजा यतावा बृहस्पतिरांगिरसो हविष्मान् । (*yo adribhit prathamajā yatāvā bṛhaspatirāṃgiraso haviṣmān |*)
द्विबर्हज्मा प्राघर्मसत् पिता न आ रोदसी वृषभो रोरवीति ॥ (*dvibarhajmā prāgharmasat pitā na ā rodasī vṛṣabho roravīti ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-२३-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-23-1)*)

### Printed p. 318

*Running head: [318 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. Ā. 24. Sū. 190] (as supplied).*

This Bṛhaspati breaks the mountains into pieces; he is the first-born of Prajāpati (Brahmā); of true vows; a descendant of the sage Aṅgiras; the accepter of oblations or the carrier to the gods; able to cross the two worlds (earth and heaven); dwelling in the shining place of light; like a father to us; the sender of rain; roaring (like a bull) in heaven and earth.

जनाय चिद्य ईवत उ लोकं बृहस्पतिर्देवहूतौ जकार । (*janāya cidya īvata u lokaṃ bṛhaspatirdevahūtau jakāra |*)
घ्नन् वृत्राणि वि पुरो दर्दरीति जयञ्क्तूरमिश्रान् पृत्सु साहन् ॥ (*ghnan vṛtrāṇi vi puro dardarīti jayañktūramiśrān pṛtsu sāhan ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-७३-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-73-2)*)

This Bṛhaspati, for the sacrificer (the man) who invokes him as a god and praises him, prepares the best world; he destroys obstacles and enemies; he defeats in battle the asuras and others who are not friends and destroys their cities.

बृहस्पतिः समजयद्वसूनि महो व्रजान् गोमतो देव एषः । (*bṛhaspatiḥ samajayadvasūni maho vrajān gomato deva eṣaḥ |*)
अपः सिषासन्त्वव १ [?] रप्रतीतो बृहस्पतिर्हंत्यमित्रमर्कॆः ॥ (*apaḥ siṣāsantvava 1 [?] rapratīto bṛhaspatirhaṃtyamitramarkèḥ ‖*)
(मि सं. ६-७२-१) (*(mi saṃ. 6-72-1)*)

This Bṛhaspati won the wealth of the enemies; he also took possession of wide pastures and cattle; to obtain the water of the atmospheric cloud he destroys, with excellent hymns, the enemies in heaven (atmospheric) such as Vṛtra. In the above sūkta all the chief qualities of Bṛhaspati are finely praised. (The print gives a footnote sign ೧ in the first line of the last verse, marked [?], and the reference "ಮಿ ಸಂ.", as printed.)

अहिमायान् (*ahimāyān*) — अगत्य हंत्रः अंतरिक्षचारिणो वा माया येषां वृत्रा- दीनां तानसुरान् (*agatya haṃtraḥ aṃtarikṣacāriṇo vā māyā yeṣāṃ vṛtrā- dīnāṃ tānasurān*): the bhāṣyakāra explains the word *ahimāyān* as enemies who kill by *māyā*, that is, by crooked means, having come running or pursuing; or the asuras such as Vṛtra who move in the atmosphere and cause trouble by *māyā* and the like. Although the word *ahimāya* occurs in the ṛks ऋ. सं. ६-२०-७, ६-५२-१५, १०-६३-४ (*ṛ. saṃ. 6-20-7, 6-52-15, 10-63-4*), since it is there used of the gods, they have explained it differently.

Since Bṛhaspati's weapons are mentioned in this ṛk it is necessary to examine that matter a little. As said in the ṛk given above as an example:

बृहस्पतिर्हंत्यमित्रमर्कॆः (*bṛhaspatirhaṃtyamitramarkèḥ*) — "Bṛhaspati destroys enemies by mantras alone": this is supported in other places also in the Ṛgveda and other works (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

ऋतज्येन क्षिप्रेण ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्यत्र वष्टि प्र तदश्नोति धन्वना । (*ṛtajyena kṣipreṇa brahmaṇaspatiryatra vaṣṭi pra tadaśnoti dhanvanā |*)
तस्य साद्वीरिषवो याभिरस्यति नृचक्षसो दृशये कर्णयोनयः ॥ (*tasya sādvīriṣavo yābhirasyati nṛcakṣaso dṛśaye karṇayonayaḥ ‖*)

Here it is said that Bṛhaspati wears golden weapons.

त्वष्टा माया वेदपसामपस्तमो बिभ्रत्पात्रा देवपानानि शंतमा । (*tvaṣṭā māyā vedapasāmapastamo bibhratpātrā devapānāni śaṃtamā |*)
शिशीते नूनं परशुं स्वायसं येन वृश्चदेतशो ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥ (*śiśīte nūnaṃ paraśuṃ svāyasaṃ yena vṛścadetaśo brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖*)

In this ṛk it is said that Bṛhaspati uses, for the slaying of enemies, the iron axe sharpened and handed over by तृष्टवु (*tṛṣṭavu*) (as printed; Tvaṣṭṛ).

*[As supplied, the label line of the grammar page reads व्याकरणक्रिया (*vyākaraṇakriyā*), run on after the previous line; standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 4, noted briefly)

The page explains the forms of Ṛk 4: ईयते (*īyate*) (a root of motion, middle-voice ending, present third person singular; the *nighāta* accent arises because the word stands after a verb form, printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*)); अत्यः (*atyaḥ*) (suffix *kyap*; the print says the accent falls on the first syllable); यक्षभृत् (*yakṣabhṛt*) (root *bhṛ*, suffix *kvip*, accent of the first element of the compound); विचेताः (*vicetāḥ*) (a possessive compound, with the accent of the first member by the rule बहुप्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuprīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*)); यंति (*yaṃti*) (the *nighāta* is prohibited by the rule च वा योगे प्रथमा (*ca vā yoge prathamā*), because *ca* follows); द्यून् (*dyūn*) (accusative by the rule कालाध्वनो रत्यंत संयोगे (*kālādhvano ratyaṃta saṃyoge*) (पा. सू. २-३-५ (*pā. sū. 2-3-5*)), because the days are constantly connected with the action); अभि (*abhi*) (a preposition; by the rule उपसर्गाःक्रियायोगे (*upasargāḥkriyāyoge*) the name *upasarga* applies only when a verb is connected, so here a verb must be supplied, and the verb लक्षयंति (*lakṣayaṃti*) is supplied; the print reads क्रियापवन्नु (*kriyāpavannu*) for the word for verb, [sic]).

*The word *upasarga* is divided across the page boundary (its first part ends p. 319, the rest begins p. 320); kept as printed.*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ये त्वा॑ देवोश्री॒कं [?] मन्य॑मानाः पा॒पा भ॒द्रमु॑प॒जीवं॑ति॒
> पज्राः ।
> न दू॒ढ्ये॒३॒॑३अनु॑ ददासि वा॒मं बृह॑स्पते॒ चय॑स॒ इप्पिया॑रुं [?]॥

> *ye tvā devośrīkaṃ [?] manyamānāḥ pāpā bhadramupajīvaṃti*
> *pajrāḥ |*
> *na dūḍhye3anu dadāsi vāmaṃ bṛhaspate cayasa ippiyāruṃ [?]‖*
> 

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ये । त्वा । देव । उस्रिकं । मन्यमानाः । पासाः [?] । भद्रं । उपजीवंति । पज्राः ।
> न । दुःध्ये । अनु । ददासि । वामं । बृहस्पते । चयसे । इत् । पियारुं ॥ ५ ॥

> *ye | tvā | deva | usrikaṃ | manyamānāḥ | pāsāḥ [?] | bhadraṃ | upajīvaṃti | pajrāḥ |*
> *na | duḥdhye | anu | dadāsi | vāmaṃ | bṛhaspate | cayase | it | piyāruṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading साहित्यभाष्यं (*sāhityabhāṣyaṃ*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे देव बृहस्पते ये पापाः पापबुद्धयोऽल्पाः पज्रा हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतः
> पापेन जीर्णा वानरा भद्रं कल्याणं त्वा त्वामुस्तिकं । उस्रियेति गोनाम !
> कुत्सितामल्पक्षिरोत्साविणीं गां जीर्णमनड्वाहं वा मन्यमाना उपजीवंति
> उपेत्य प्राणंति । अल्पं याचंत इत्यर्थः । दूढ्यॆ दुर्धिये ॥ वचनव्यत्ययः ॥
> दुर्बुद्धिभ्यस्तेभ्यो वामं वननीयं धनं नानु ददासि । अनुकूलं न वितरसि । हे
> बृहस्पते देव पियारुं सोमपानशीलं सोमेन यष्टारं महाफलरिप्पुं तु
> चयस इत् । गच्छस्यॆवानुग्रहीतुं ॥ चय गतावित्यस्येदं रूपं ॥ यद्वा । हे
> बृहस्पते पियारुं हिंसकं ॥ पीयतेर्हिंसाकर्मण इदं रूपं ॥ तं प्राणिहिंसकं
> चयस इत् । हंस्येव । बृहस्पते यच्चातयसि देवपीयुमिति निरुक्तं । ४-२५ ॥

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati gives no desirable wealth to the sinful, dull men who live thinking him a worn-out cow or ox; he favours the soma-offering sacrificer.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देव—पूज्यनाद ऎलै बृहस्पतिये (*deva—pūjyanāda èlai bṛhaspatiye*) (O revered Bṛhaspati). ये पापाः—याव पापिगळु (*ye pāpāḥ—yāva pāpigaḷu*) (the sinners who). पज्राः—हवि र्लक्षणान्नयुक्तरागि (*pajrāḥ—havi rlakṣaṇānnayuktarāgi*) (possessed of food in the form of oblations). भद्रं—कल्याणात्मकनाद (*bhadraṃ—kalyāṇātmakanāda*) (auspicious). त्वा—निन्नन्नु (*tvā—ninnannu*) (you). हॆच्चु प्रयोजनकारियागदॆ इरुव (*hèccu prayojanakāriyāgadè iruva*) (of little use) उस्रिकं—जीर्णवाद गोवॆंदु (*usrikaṃ—jīrṇavāda govèṃdu*) (as a worn-out cow). मन्यमानाः—तिळिदवरागि (*manyamānāḥ—tiḷidavarāgi*) (thinking). उपजीवंति— जीविसुत्तारॆयो (*upajīvaṃti— jīvisuttārèyo*) (live). दूढ्ये—दुष्टबुद्धियुळ्ळ आ पापिष्ठरिगॆ (*dūḍhye—duṣṭabuddhiyuḷḷa ā pāpiṣṭharigè*) (to those evil-minded sinners). वामं—कांक्षितवाद धनवन्नु (*vāmaṃ—kāṃkṣitavāda dhanavannu*) (the desired wealth). न अनु ददासि—अवरवर अनुकूलक्कॆ बेकागुवंतॆ कॊडुवुदे इल्ल (*na anu dadāsi—avaravara anukūlakkè bekāguvaṃtè kòḍuvude illa*) (you never give as suits each of them). बृहस्पते—ऎलै (*bṛhaspate—èlai*) (O; the entry is divided across the page boundary, as printed).

### Printed p. 321

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १२.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 321 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 12.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 321*).*

बृहस्पतिये ! (*bṛhaspatiye !*) (Bṛhaspati!). पियारुं—सोमवन्नर्पिसि यज्ञमाडतक्कवनन्नु (*piyāruṃ—somavannarpisi yajñamāḍatakkavanannu*) (him who offers soma and performs the sacrifice). चयसे इत्—खंडित वागियू अनुग्रहिसुत्तीयॆ (*cayase it—khaṃḍita vāgiyū anugrahisuttīyè*) (you certainly favour).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Revered Bṛhaspati, those sinners who, worn out by sin, consider you, the auspicious, an aged cow or one of no use, and live so, to those evil-minded sinners you give no desired wealth at all. But him who offers soma and performs the sacrifice you certainly favour.

**Printed English translation**

Divine Brihaspati, you do not bestow desired (wealth) upon those stupid (men), who, sinful and mean, subsist, considering you, who are auspicious, as an old ox, but you favour him who offers (you) libations.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5)**

In this ṛk it is described that Bṛhaspati gives nothing to those who do not desire him and praise him, and destroys those violent ones.

सुनीतिभिर्नयसि त्रायसे जनं यस्तुभ्यं दाशान्न तमंहो अश्ववत् । (*sunītibhirnayasi trāyase janaṃ yastubhyaṃ dāśānna tamaṃho aśvavat |*)
ब्रह्मद्विषस्तपनो मन्युमीरसि बृहस्पते महितत्ते महित्वनं ॥ (*brahmadviṣastapano manyumīrasi bṛhaspate mahitatte mahitvanaṃ ‖*)
(म. सं. २-२३-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 2-23-4)*)

*(The reference is printed म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*), as supplied; kept as printed.)* In this ṛk it is said: to him who satisfies you (Bṛhaspati) with oblations and the like, you are a good guide and you protect him; sins cannot touch him; but those who hate you fall under your wrath; O Bṛhaspati, is this not your greatness?

उस्रिकं—उस्रियेति गोनाम । कुत्सिताल्पक्षीरो स्राविणीं गां जीर्णमनड्वा- हं वा (*usrikaṃ—usriyeti gonāma | kutsitālpakṣīro srāviṇīṃ gāṃ jīrṇamanaḍvā- haṃ vā*): the word *usriyā* is read among the names of the cow (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*)). Yāska has said: उस्रियेति गो नाम उस्राविणोऽस्यां भोगाः उस्रेति च (*usriyeti go nāma usrāviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ usreti ca*) (नि. ४-१९ (*ni. 4-19*)). The milch cow is called *usriyā*, because from such milk the means of enjoyment arise; she is also called *usrā*. Since the word *usrikam* is used here, the bhāṣyakāra explains it as a barren cow that gives very little milk or none, or an aged ox that cannot do any hard work. Nobody expects any return from such a cow or ox; likewise the sinful, like a barren cow or (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 322

*Running head (as supplied): [322 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. १. आ. २४. सू. १९०] (*[322 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 1. ā. 24. sū. 190]*).*

*(Continuation of the *usrikaṃ* note in the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 of Sūkta 190, from the end of the previous page.)*

...like an aged ox, knowing that no use comes from you (Bṛhaspati), they do not worship you. To such wicked ones you give nothing, that is, none of the wealth they want, and you harm them: this is the main purport of the ṛk.

उपजीवंति—उपेत्य प्राणंति । अल्पं याचंत इत्यर्थः (*upajīvaṃti—upetya prāṇaṃti | alpaṃ yācaṃta ityarthaḥ*): they approach you and do not ask for much, they pay no regard to you: this is the purport.

पज्रा: (*pajrā:*) — Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning for this word: हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतः (*havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaḥ*) (those who have food in the form of oblations), or पापेन जीर्णा वा नराः (*pāpena jīrṇā vā narāḥ*) (men worn out by sin, that is, sinful men).

बृहस्पते—चयस इप्पियारुं (*bṛhaspate—cayasa ippiyāruṃ*) (as printed): for these words Yāska says बृहस्पते यच्चातयसि देवपीयुं पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्म (*bṛhaspate yaccātayasi devapīyuṃ pīyatirhiṃsākarma*) (नि. ४-२५ (*ni. 4-25*)), that is, the word *piyāru* is formed from the root *pīyati*, which means an act of harming. So the word means one who harms, that is, a harmer of the gods, one who does not worship the gods and desires only his own enjoyment. Such a harmer of the gods, they have explained, you, Bṛhaspati, destroy.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 5, noted briefly)

The page explains: उस्रिकम् (*usrikam*) (from *usriyā*, with the suffix *ka* in the sense of contempt, a syllable is elided and the acute goes to the end by *vyatyaya*); मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*) (root *man*, *śānac* for the present, *śyan*; initial acute by the rule इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*)); पापाः (*pāpāḥ*) (पापं येषामस्ति इति पापाः (*pāpaṃ yeṣāmasti iti pāpāḥ*), the suffix *āc* in the possessive sense by आर्शआदिभ्योआच् (*ārśaādibhyoāc*), elision of the preceding *a* by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*), final acute by चितः (*citaḥ*) (पा. सू. ६१-१६३ (*pā. sū. 61-163*), as printed)); उपजीवंति (*upajīvaṃti*) (root *jīv*, present third person plural; no *nighāta* because of the connection with *yad*; the prefix is unaccented by the rule तिजिचोदा- त्तम् (*tijicodā- ttam*) (पा. सू. ८-१-७१ (*pā. sū. 8-1-71*))); दूढ्ये (*dūḍhye*) (from दुर्धियः (*durdhiyaḥ*), with the suffix *kvip* by the rule क्विप् च (*kvip ca*), *samprasāraṇa*, the form being accepted through the *pṛṣodarādi* group, and the locative put for the dative by *vyatyaya*).

(The grammar page of Ṛk 5 continues.) चयसे (*cayase*) (root *caya*, present second person singular; no *nighāta* because of the connection with *it*); पियारुं (*piyāruṃ*) (root *pīj*, as printed; since roots have many meanings it is used here in the sense of harming; the desired form is obtained through an Uṇādi suffix marked *n*).
