#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सु॒प्रैतुः॑ सू॒यव॑सो॒ न पंथा॑ दुर्नि॒यंतुः॒ परि॑प्रीतो॒ न॒
> मि॒त्रः ।
> अ॒न॒र्वाणो॑ अ॒भि ये चक्ष॑ते॒ नोऽपी॑वृता अपोर्णु॒वंतो॑
> अस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुप्रैतुः । सुयवसः । न । पंथाः । दुःनियंतुः । परिप्रीतः । न । मित्रः ।
> अनर्वाणः । अभि । ये । चक्षते । नः । अपीवृताः [?] । अपोर्णुवंतः [?] । अस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *supraituḥ | suyavasaḥ | na | paṃthāḥ | duḥniyaṃtuḥ | pariprītaḥ | na | mitraḥ |*
> *anarvāṇaḥ | abhi | ye | cakṣate | naḥ | apīvṛtāḥ [?] | aporṇuvaṃtaḥ [?] | asthuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading सायणभ.पं (*sāyaṇabha.paṃ*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे बृहस्पते त्वं सुप्रैतुः सुष्टु गंतुर्मनुष्यस्य सुयवसः शोभनान्नस्य
> पंथा न मार्ग इव सुष्टु यज्ञमार्गगामिनो सुयवसः पंथा इव । सुखकारी
> भवेत्यर्थः । किंच दुर्नियंतुर्दुःखेन नियमितू राज्यः परिप्रीतः सर्वप्रकारेण
> संतुष्टो द्वेषादिरहितो मित्रो न सुहृन्मंत्रीव । स यथा दुर्नयान्निवर्तयति
> तद्वत् त्वमपि तथास्मभ्यं कुर्वित्यर्थः । सखिवदमार्गान्निवर्त मार्गे यज्ञादिरूपे
> योजयित्वा तत्रापि फलप्रदो भवेत्यर्थः । किंचानर्वाणोऽपापा ये नरा
> नोऽस्मानभ्याभिमुख्येन चक्षते बोधयंति तेऽपीवृता अज्ञानेनावृता अप्य-
> पूर्णुवंतोऽपगतावरणवंतो ज्ञानवंतोऽस्थुः । तिष्ठंतु । यद्वा । अनर्वाण-
> स्वामप्राप्नुवंतो येऽस्मद्विरोधिनो नोऽस्मानभि चक्षते अभिवदंति निंदंति
> तेऽपीवृता आच्छादिता रक्षिता अप्यपूर्णुवंतोऽषगतरक्षणा भवंति ॥

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati is asked to be pleasant to the sacrificer, like a friendly minister to a king, and to free the sinless teachers from ignorance.

### Printed p. 324

*Running head (as supplied): [324 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. १. अ. २४. सू. १९०] (*[324 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 1. a. 24. sū. 190]*).*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सुयेवसः—श्रेष्ठवाद अन्नवन्नु कॊडतक्क यज्ञादि कर्मगळ (*suyevasaḥ—śreṣṭhavāda annavannu kòḍatakka yajñādi karmagaḷa*) (of the sacrificial acts that give excellent food; before it the print has (ऎलै बृहस्पतिये) (*(èlai bṛhaspatiye)*), O Bṛhaspati). पंथाः न—मार्गवु सुखकरवागिरुवंतॆयू (*paṃthāḥ na—mārgavu sukhakaravāgiruvaṃtèyū*) (as a path is pleasant). (मत्तु) दुर्नियंतुः—दुष्टरन्नु निग्रह माडतक्क राजनिगॆ (*(mattu) durniyaṃtuḥ—duṣṭarannu nigraha māḍatakka rājanigè*) (and to the king who restrains the wicked). परिप्रीतः—परिपूर्णवाद प्रेमवुळ्ळवनू (*pariprītaḥ—paripūrṇavāda premavuḷḷavanū*) (full of love). मित्रः न—सुहृत्तू आगिरुव मंत्रियु सुखकरनागिरुवंतॆयू (*mitraḥ na—suhṛttū āgiruva maṃtriyu sukhakaranāgiruvaṃtèyū*) (as a minister who is also a friend is pleasant). सुप्रैतुः—सन्मार्गदल्लि व्यवहरिसि कर्माचरणॆयन्नु माडतक्क यजमाननिगॆ सुखकारियागिरु (*supraituḥ—sanmārgadalli vyavaharisi karmācaraṇèyannu māḍatakka yajamānanigè sukhakāriyāgiru*) (be pleasant to the sacrificer who acts on the good path and performs the rites). ये—यारु (*ye—yāru*) (who). अनर्वाणः—पापरहितरागि (*anarvāṇaḥ—pāparahitarāgi*) (being free of sin). नः—नम्मन्नु (नमगॆ) (*naḥ—nammannu (namagè)*) (us, to us). अभिचक्षते—उपदेशवन्नु कॊट्टु सन्मार्गगामिगळागुवंतॆ माडु त्तारॆयो (अवरु) (*abhicakṣate—upadeśavannu kòṭṭu sanmārgagāmigaḷāguvaṃtè māḍu ttārèyo (avaru)*) (those who instruct and make us follow the good path). अपीवृताः—आज्ञानदिंद आवृतरागिद्दरू सह (*apīvṛtāḥ—ājñānadiṃda āvṛtarāgiddarū saha*) (even though enveloped by ignorance). अपोर्णुवंतः— अज्ञानरूपवाद आवरणदिंद मुक्तरागि (*aporṇuvaṃtaḥ— ajñānarūpavāda āvaraṇadiṃda muktarāgi*) (freed from the covering of ignorance). अस्थुः—आगलि (*asthuḥ—āgali*) (let them be).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Bṛhaspati, be pleasant to the sacrificer who acts on the good path and performs the rites, as the path of sacrificial acts that give excellent food is pleasant, and as a minister who is full of love and a friend is pleasant to a king who restrains the wicked. And since the teachers who show us the good path are sinless, if they are enveloped by ignorance, remove their covering also and make them knowers.

**Printed English translation**

Be a (pleasant) way to him who goes well and makes good offerings, like the affectionate friend of (a ruler who) restrains the bad, and may those sinless men who instruct us, although yet enveloped (by ignorance), stand extricated from their covering.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषयगळु: (*viśeṣayagaḷu:*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 6)**

The matter stated in this ṛk is not clear or is troublesome. Even so, the bhāṣyakāra has explained it so that a meaning fits; the meaning given for the second half does not fit properly.

सुप्रैतुः—सुष्टु गंतुर्मनुष्यस्य (*supraituḥ—suṣṭu gaṃturmanuṣyasya*) । सन्मार्गप्रवर्तकनाद मनुष्यन (*sanmārgapravartakanāda manuṣyana*): that is, here, the man who worships Bṛhaspati with hymns and the like.

सुयवसः (*suyavasaḥ*) — the word यव (*yava*) is read (the print has पतरिवागिदॆ (*patarivāgidè*), [sic]) among the names of food. Hence it means one who gives excellent food. Since food is obtained through sacrifices, यज्ञमार्गगामिनो (*yajñamārgagāmino*) (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 325

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १३ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 325 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 13 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 325*).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 of Sūkta 190, in the *suyavasaḥ* note.)*

पंथा इव (*paṃthā iva*): like the good path of one who wishes to perform sacrifices and the like, that is, like a pleasant path.

दुर्नियंतुः—दुःखेन नियमितुः । अथवा दुर्नयान्निवर्तयति इति दुर्नि- यंता तस्य (*durniyaṃtuḥ—duḥkhena niyamituḥ | athavā durnayānnivartayati iti durni- yaṃtā tasya*): the bhāṣyakāra has explained it as a king who rules with great difficulty, or who punishes those who walk on bad paths and makes them walk on the good path.

परिप्रीतः मित्रः न (*pariprītaḥ mitraḥ na*): satisfied in every way, that is, like a friend full of true love and trust. Although there is no word in this ṛk that denotes a king or a minister, the bhāṣyakāra has explained the words दुर्नियंतुः मित्रः (*durniyaṃtuḥ mitraḥ*) so that the meanings king and minister fit. Or, without giving the meanings king, minister and the like, the words दुर्नियंतुः मित्रो न (*durniyaṃtuḥ mitro na*) may be taken to mean: as a friend, his well-wisher, brings back to the road one who strays on a bad path.

अनर्वाणः (*anarvāṇaḥ*): the bhāṣyakāra has given the meaning अपापाः (*apāpāḥ*), those free from sin, but has not explained how this meaning fits the word. Yāska says in the Nirukta: अनर्वा प्रत्यृतोऽन्यस्मिन् (*anarvā pratyṛto 'nyasmin*) (नि ६-२३ (*ni 6-23*)), and यः अन्यस्मिन् न आश्रितो भवति स्वप्रधान एव सः अनर्वा इत्युच्यते (*yaḥ anyasmin na āśrito bhavati svapradhāna eva saḥ anarvā ityucyate*): the man who does not take shelter in others but is himself chief, that is, independent, is called *anarvā*. Therefore, by the view of the Nirukta authors, *anarvāṇaḥ* (nominative plural) means independent men, those not under another.

अपीवृताः (*apīvṛtāḥ*), अपोर्णुवंतः (*aporṇuvaṃtaḥ*): for these words Sāyaṇa has given in order the explanation अज्ञानेनावृताः अपगतावरण- वंतः (*ajñānenāvṛtāḥ apagatāvaraṇa- vaṃtaḥ*); that is, *apīvṛtāḥ* means those covered by ignorance, blind with ignorance, without understanding; *apōrṇuvantaḥ* means those who have turned away from the covering of ignorance, the free from ignorance, the knowers. Whether these two views are the right meanings of these words remains in doubt. The bhāṣyakāra too, unable to explain the meaning of these words properly, has given another kind of meaning also: यद्वा । अनर्वाणस्त्वामप्राप्नुवंतो येऽस्मद्विरो- धिनो नोऽस्मानभि चक्षते अभिवदंति निंदंति तेऽपीवृता आच्छादिता रक्षिता अप्यपो- र्णुवंतोऽपगतरक्षणा भवंति (*yadvā | anarvāṇastvāmaprāpnuvaṃto ye 'smadviro- dhino no 'smānabhi cakṣate abhivadaṃti niṃdaṃti te 'pīvṛtā ācchāditā rakṣitā apyapo- rṇuvaṃto 'pagatarakṣaṇā bhavaṃti*). That is: those men, our opponents, who without taking shelter in you revile us, even if they have their own protection, may that protection not reach them; so they have said. This meaning too is not very reasonable. In both these kinds of meaning there is room for doubt (the sentence continues on the next page; the word is printed संशयक्कॆ (*saṃśayakkè*) at the end of this page and वकाशविद्दे इदॆ (*vakāśavidde idè*) at the start of the next, as printed).

### Printed p. 326

*Running head (as supplied): [326 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. १. अ. २४ सू. १९०] (*[326 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 1. a. 24 sū. 190]*).*

For how? A man covered by ignorance giving counsel to another does not seem right. Likewise in the second meaning, to say "even if those who do not take shelter in you have protection" is also not right, because those who do not take shelter in you have no protection at all; and, this being so, to say "destroy the protection they have" is also without reason. In short, the right meaning of this ṛk, especially of the second half, remains clouded with doubt.

*Gist:* A yājyā for the cake offering in Bṛhaspati's animal sacrifice: praises reach Bṛhaspati as rivers reach the sea; the wise one watches the waters.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अवनयो न—मानवरु तम्म यजमानरन्नु सुत्तुवरियुवंतॆयू (मत्तु) । (*avanayo na—mānavaru tamma yajamānarannu suttuvariyuvaṃtèyū (mattu) |*) (as men surround their masters, and). रोध- चक्राः—ऎरडु दडगळ नडुवॆ हरियुव नदिगळु (*rodha- cakrāḥ—èraḍu daḍagaḷa naḍuvè hariyuva nadigaḷu*) (the rivers flowing between two banks). समुद्रं—समुद्राभिमुखवागि (*samudraṃ—samudrābhimukhavāgi*) (towards the sea). स्रवतः— (ऒंदे मार्गवन्ननुसरिसि) हरियुवंतॆयू (*sravataḥ— (òṃde mārgavannanusarisi) hariyuvaṃtèyū*) (as they flow, following one course). स्तुभः—सकलस्तुतिगळू सह (*stubhaḥ—sakalastutigaḷū saha*) (all the praises as well). यं—याव बृह स्पतियन्नु (*yaṃ—yāva bṛha spatiyannu*) (which Bṛhaspati). सं यंति—होगि सुत्तुवरिदु सेरुत्तवॆयो (*saṃ yaṃti—hogi suttuvaridu seruttavèyo*) (go to, surround and join). सः बृहस्पतिः—आ बृहस्पतियु (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ—ā bṛhaspatiyu*) (that Bṛhaspati). विद्वान्—प्राज्ञनादवनागियू (*vidvān—prājñanādavanāgiyū*) (being wise). गृध्रः—जलाकांक्षियागियू (*gṛdhraḥ—jalākāṃkṣiyāgiyū*) (desiring water). अंतः—मध्यभागदल्लि निंतु (*aṃtaḥ—madhyabhāgadalli niṃtu*) (standing in the middle). तरः—जलाभिवृद्धियन्नु अथवा दाटुव क्रमवन्नू (*taraḥ—jalābhivṛddhiyannu athavā dāṭuva kramavannū*) (the increase of water, or the manner of crossing). आपः—उदकवन्नू (*āpaḥ—udakavannū*) (the water). उभयं च- ई ऎरडु विषयगळन्नू (*ubhayaṃ ca- ī èraḍu viṣayagaḷannū*) (and both these matters). चष्टे—ध्यानिसि (जलाभिवृद्धियन्नु) उंटुमाडुत्तानॆ (*caṣṭe—dhyānisi (jalābhivṛddhiyannu) uṃṭumāḍuttānè*) (meditating, he brings about the increase of water).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As men surround their masters, and as rivers flowing between two banks flow towards the sea following one course, so all the praises join and surround that Bṛhaspati, who, being wise and desiring water... (the supplied text breaks off here, in the middle of the sentence, at जलाकांक्षि (*jalākāṃkṣi*), at the end of the window).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 7)**

This ṛk सं यं स्तुभः (*saṃ yaṃ stubhaḥ*) is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra सं यं स्तुभोऽवनयो न यंत्येवा पित्रे (*saṃ yaṃ stubho 'vanayo na yaṃtyevā pitre*), as to be used as the *yājyā* mantra in the *puroḍāśa* offering of the animal sacrifice addressed to Bṛhaspati.

The meaning of this ṛk too is not clear. For in the first half the words अवनयो न (*avanayo na*), and in the second half the words उभयं (*ubhayaṃ*), अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*) and तरः आपः (*taraḥ āpaḥ*), do not get a proper meaning.

स्तुभः—स्तोभतीति स्तुतिः (*stubhaḥ—stobhatīti stutiḥ*): the word स्तोभति (*stobhati*) is read among the names of worship (नि. ३-१९ (*ni. 3-19*)). Therefore *stubhaḥ* means hymns.

अवनयः—भूमयो मनुष्याः (*avanayaḥ—bhūmayo manuṣyāḥ*): the word *avanayaḥ* is read among the names of the earth (नि २-५ (*ni 2-5*)), among the names of rivers (नि २-२४ (*ni 2-24*)) and among the names of fingers (नि ३-९ (*ni 3-9*)). Here the word *avani* is used in the sense of earth, that is, men who live on the earth. For the words अवनयो न यंति (*avanayo na yaṃti*) in this ṛk Sāyaṇa's explanation is "as men approach their master". How this meaning is possible for these words has to be guessed and fitted; it is not possible to know the intention of the sage with certainty.

रोधचक्रा (*rodhacakrā*): this word is read among the names of rivers (नि. २-२४ (*ni. 2-24*)). The meaning of its parts is of three kinds: the words *rodha* and *cakra*, formed respectively from the two roots रुधिर् आवरणे (*rudhir āvaraṇe*) and डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*), combine into the word *rodhacakra*.

(1) रोधस्य निरोधस्य चक्रं करणं कृतिरासां विद्यत इति रोधचक्राः (*rodhasya nirodhasya cakraṃ karaṇaṃ kṛtirāsāṃ vidyata iti rodhacakrāḥ*) । नद्यो वृष्ट्या प्राणिनां स्वैरसंचरणनिरोधकारिण्यः (*nadyo vṛṣṭyā prāṇināṃ svairasaṃcaraṇanirodhakāriṇyaḥ*): rivers, by the water in them, obstruct the movement of creatures; that is, creatures are unable to cross a river full of flowing water; therefore rivers are called *rodhacakrāḥ*.

(2) यद्वा । रोधः तीरं तस्य करणं निर्माणमासां विद्यते तीरवत्यो हि नद्यः । सकारलोपश्चांदसः (*yadvā | rodhaḥ tīraṃ tasya karaṇaṃ nirmāṇamāsāṃ vidyate tīravatyo hi nadyaḥ | sakāralopaścāṃdasaḥ*): or, *rodha* means a bank, a shore; as rivers flow they make banks on both their sides; therefore, since they flow between two banks, rivers are called *rodhacakrāḥ*.

### Printed p. 329

*[Unmarked page break in the supplied text: the running head of printed p. 329 stands inside the text and reads अ. २. अ. ५ व. १३ ] सुग्वेदसंहिता 329 (*a. 2. a. 5 va. 13 ] sugvedasaṃhitā 329*), as printed, with ಸುಗ್ವೇದ [sic].]*

(3) यद्वा । रुध्यतेऽनेन जलप्रवाह इति रोधः शब्दः करणं निर्माणमासां विद्यते (*yadvā | rudhyate 'nena jalapravāha iti rodhaḥ śabdaḥ karaṇaṃ nirmāṇamāsāṃ vidyate*): or, the flow of water running in the river is checked from overflowing by the banks at its sides; since rivers make such banks, they are called *rodhacakrāḥ*.

In the present ṛk, in समुद्रं न स्रवतः रोधचक्राः (*samudraṃ na sravataḥ rodhacakrāḥ*), the comparison is apt: as the flowing rivers join the sea, so the hymns we make join Bṛhaspati.

गृध्रः—गर्धनशिलो वृष्टिमाकांक्षमाणः सः बृहस्पतिः (*gṛdhraḥ—gardhanaśilo vṛṣṭimākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*): that is, Bṛhaspati who desires rain. For the word गृध्रस्य (*gṛdhrasya*) in ऋ. सं. १०-१२४-८ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-124-8*) Sāyaṇa has explained रसानभिकांक्षतः (*rasānabhikāṃkṣataḥ*), "desiring water"; and for the word printed वृध्राः (*vṛdhrāḥ*) [sic] in ऋ सं. १-८८-४ (*ṛ saṃ. 1-88-4*) he has explained जलाभिकांक्षायुक्तान् (*jalābhikāṃkṣāyuktān*), "those who desire water".

तरः—तरणं जलाभिवृद्धिं (*taraḥ—taraṇaṃ jalābhivṛddhiṃ*): this is the bhāṣyakāra's explanation, "increase of water". *Taraṇa* means crossing, and "Ferry (*Ferry*)" is the explanation of the Western scholars.

उभयं चष्टे अंतः (*ubhayaṃ caṣṭe aṃtaḥ*): standing in the middle of the two (that is, the water and the manner of crossing it), Bṛhaspati sees or makes. To take उभयमंतर्मध्यॆ (*ubhayamaṃtarmadhyè*) here as "between the water and the crossing" is not so apt; the meaning that उभयं अंतः (*ubhayaṃ aṃtaḥ*) is "in the atmosphere between the earth and heaven" fits properly. For since the water-laden rows of clouds are in the atmosphere, the meaning that Bṛhaspati produced such a mass of water and its manner of crossing (that is, the manner of rain) fits properly here.

*[As supplied, the label line of the grammar page reads व्याकरणक्रिया (*vyākaraṇakriyā*); standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 7, noted briefly)

The page explains: अवनयः (*avanayaḥ*) (root *av*; the suffix *ani* by the rule आर्तिसृधृध (*ārtisṛdhṛdha*) (उ. सू. २-२५९ (*u. sū. 2-259*)); nominative plural; acute on the suffix); यंति (*yaṃti*) (root *iṇ*; present third person plural; prohibition of *nighāta* by यद्वृत्तान्वित्यम् (*yadvṛttānvityam*), as printed); स्रवतः (*sravataḥ*) (root सु गतौ (*su gatau*); by the vārttika सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यः क्विब्वा वक्तव्यः (*sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvibvā vaktavyaḥ*) the suffix *kvip* is added when the action is intended, and the word *sravat* results; acute on the end by the root accent; nominative plural).

रोधचक्राः (*rodhacakrāḥ*) (a possessive compound, with the accent of the first member by the rule बहुप्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuprīhau prakṛtyā*)); चष्टे (*caṣṭe*) (since roots have many meanings, the root चक्षिज् (*cakṣij*) is used here in the sense of seeing; present third person singular; the verbal *nighāta* accent); गृध्रः (*gṛdhraḥ*) (root गृधु अभिकांक्षायां (*gṛdhu abhikāṃkṣāyāṃ*); the suffix *kran* by the rule सुसूधागृधिभ्यःक्रन् (*susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥkran*) (उ. सू. ४-६०० (*u. sū. 4-600*)); because the suffix is marked *n*, an initial acute by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*)).

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ए॒वा म॒हस्तु॑ विजा॒तस्तु वि॑ष्णा॒न्बृह॒स्पति॑र्वृष॒भो [?] धा॑यि दे॒वः ।
> स नः॑ स्तु॒तो वी॒रव॑द्धातु॒ गोम॑द्वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुं ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विव [?] । महः । तुविजातः । तुविष्टान्ः [?] । बृहस्पतिः । वृषभः । धायि । देवः ।
> सः । नः । स्तुतः । वीरवत् । धातु । गोमत् । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> महो महांस्तु विजातो बह्वर्थमुत्पन्नस्तुविष्मान् बलवान् वृषभोs-
> पां वर्षिता देवो बृहस्पतिरेवैवं स्तुतिप्रकारेण धायि । धीयते । स्तूयत
> इत्यर्थः । स स्तुतो देवो नोऽस्माकं वीरवत्पुत्राद्युपेतं गोमद्गोभिर्युक्तं
> फलं धातु । करोत्वित्यर्थः । विद्यामेति गतं ॥

*Gist:* Bṛhaspati, the mighty showerer of water, is thus praised; praised, may he give us heroic sons and cattle.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

महः—महात्मनू (*mahaḥ—mahātmanū*) (the great). तुविजातः—बहुवाद प्रयोजनगळिगागि उत्पन्ननादवनू (*tuvijātaḥ—bahuvāda prayojanagaḷigāgi utpannanādavanū*) (born for many benefits). तुवि- ष्मान्—बलशालियू (*tuvi- ṣmān—balaśāliyū*) (the strong). वृषभः—उदकवन्नु सुरिसतक्कवनू (*vṛṣabhaḥ—udakavannu surisatakkavanū*) (the shower of water). देवः—देवतात्मकनू आद (*devaḥ—devatātmakanū āda*) (the divine). बृहस्पतिः—बृहस्पतियु (*bṛhaspatiḥ—bṛhaspatiyu*) (Bṛhaspati). एव—ई प्रकारवागि (*eva—ī prakāravāgi*) (in this manner). धायि—स्तुतिसल्पडुत्तानॆ (*dhāyi—stutisalpaḍuttānè*) (is praised). स्तुतः स्म—ई विधवागि स्तुतनाद देवनु (*stutaḥ sma—ī vidhavāgi stutanāda devanu*) (the god praised in this way). नः—नमगॆ (*naḥ—namagè*) (to us). वीरवत्—वीरराद पुत्रादिगळिंद कूडिदुदू (*vīravat—vīrarāda putrādigaḷiṃda kūḍidudū*) (accompanied by heroic sons and the like).

### Printed p. 331

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १३ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 331 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 13 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 331*).*

गोमत्—गोवुगळिंद कूडिदुदू आद फलवन्नु (*gomat—govugaḷiṃda kūḍidudū āda phalavannu*) (the fruit accompanied by cows). धातु—उंटुमाडलि (*dhātu—uṃṭumāḍali*) (may he bring about). वयं—नावु (*vayaṃ—nāvu*) (we). इषं—अन्नवन्नू (*iṣaṃ—annavannū*) (food). वृजनं—बलवन्नू (*vṛjanaṃ—balavannū*) (strength). जीरदानुं—दीर्घायुष्यवन्नू (*jīradānuṃ—dīrghāyuṣyavannū*) (long life). विद्याम— पडॆयोण (*vidyāma— paḍèyoṇa*) (let us obtain).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads भाषा (*bhāṣā*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May Bṛhaspati, the great, born for many benefits, strong, the shower of water and divine, who is praised in this manner, give us, thus praised, fruit accompanied by heroic sons and the like and by cows. May we obtain food, strength and long life.

**Printed English translation**

So, Brihaspati, the mighty, the beneficent, the powerful, the showerer (of benefits), the divine, has been glorified : praised by us, may he make us possessed of progeny and cattle, that thence we may obtain food, strength and long life.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 8)**

In this ṛk the sage, concluding the sūkta, prays to Bṛhaspati for the increase of sons and grandsons and for the acquisition of cattle wealth such as cows.

तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*): the word तुवि (*tuvi*) is read among the names for "many" (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)). For the word *tuvijāta* Yāska has said बहुजातः (*bahujātaḥ*), one born in order to bring about many benefits for men.

वीरवत्, गोमत् (*vīravat, gomat*): these words are used as adjectives; a noun to be qualified has to be supplied. Or they may be used as adjectives of the word इषं (*iṣaṃ*). The main purport is that Bṛhaspati may favour valiant sons, grandsons and the like, servants and cows.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 8, noted briefly; the supplied text ends within this page)

एवा (*evā*): lengthening in the Saṃhitā by the rule निपातस्यच (*nipātasyaca*) (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६ (*pā. sū. 6-3-136*)); तुविजातः (*tuvijātaḥ*) (बूहनामुपकारकतया तत्संबंधित्वेन जातः तुविजातः (*būhanāmupakārakatayā tatsaṃbaṃdhitvena jātaḥ tuvijātaḥ*), as printed; a genitive *tatpuruṣa* compound; the acute on the end by the rule षष्ठीतत्पुरुष समासः समासस्य (*ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣa samāsaḥ samāsasya*)).

धायि (*dhāyi*) (डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*), the root, in the passive; *luṅ* in the present sense in the Veda; third person singular; by the rule बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) (पा. सू. ६-४-७५ (*pā. sū. 6-4-75*)) the augment *aṭ* does not occur; the verbal *nighāta* accent arises, the print giving तिजिंतनिघात्वर (*tijiṃtanighātvara*), as printed); धातु (*dhātu*) (the same root; *loṭ*, third person singular; the suffix printed जप् प्रत्यय (*jap pratyaya*); *u* substituted for *i* by the rule एरुः (*eruḥ*); in the Veda the *śnu*-type vikaraṇa, printed श्लविकरण (*ślavikaraṇa*), does not occur, so the root takes no reduplication; because it stands after a verb form, printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*), the *nighāta* accent arises).

#### Sūkta 191

नूर तॊंभत्तॊंदनॆय सूक्तवु. (*nūra tòṃbhattòṃdanèya sūktavu.*) — "the hundred and ninety-first sūkta."

*[As supplied, no label line is printed before Sāyaṇa's introduction; the following lines are the introduction to Sūkta 191, printed as plain lines, and are given here as a block; standard label inserted.]*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> कंकत इति षोडशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं ऋषिरगस्यः अष्टृणसूर्यास्त्रयो
> देवताः त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । सूर्ये विषमित्याद्यास्तिस्रो महापंक्तयः । अष्टकौ
> सप्तकः षट्को दशको नवकश्च । अनु. १०-३ । इत्युक्तलक्षणोपेतत्वात् । नवानामि-
> त्येषा त्रयोदशी महाबृहती । चत्वारोऽष्टका जागतश्च महाबृहती । अनु ९-९ ।
> इति ह्युक्तं । अत्र यद्यप्यक्षराणि न्यूनानि तथापि व्यूहेन पूरणीयानि । अत्रानु-
> क्रमणिका । कंकतः षोळशोपनिषदानुष्टुभमस्पृणसौर्यं विषशंकावानगस्यः
> प्राब्रवीद्धशम्याद्याश्च तिस्रो महापंक्तयो महाबृहती चेति । उपनिषदिति रहस्य-
> मित्यर्थः । विषशंकायुक्तोऽगस्यस्तत्परिहारायेदमुक्तवान् ॥ श्रौतस्य विशेष-
> विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ अत्र शौनकः । कंकतो नेति सूक्तं तु विषार्तः प्रयतो
> जपेत् । विषं न क्रमते चास्य सर्पाद्दृष्टिविषादपि ॥ यत्कीटलूतासु विषं दंष्ट्रि
> वृश्चिकतश्च यत् । मूलं च कृत्रिमं चैव जपन्सर्वमपोहति । ऋग्वि. १-२८ । इति ॥

*Gist:* A sūkta of sixteen ṛks by Agastya to the deities water, grass and sun; a poison-curing hymn, with metres per the Anukramaṇikā; Śaunaka's use is given.

**Anuvāda (Kannada)** of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 191. This sūkta beginning कंकतो न (*kaṃkato na*) is the twelfth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. It has sixteen ṛks. Agastya is the seer of this sūkta. The deities are the अष्टृणसूर्यरु (*aṣṭṛṇasūryaru*) (water, grass, sun), the metre is *triṣṭubh*. The three ṛks beginning सूर्ये विषं (*sūrye viṣaṃ*) (the tenth, eleventh and twelfth ṛks) are of the metre called महाबृहती छंदस्कवु (*mahābṛhatī chaṃdaskavu*) (as printed). In the Anukramaṇikā it is said that in a ṛk of this metre the first two pādas have eight syllables each, the third pāda seven, the fourth six, the fifth ten and the sixth nine (अनु. १०-३ (*anu. 10-3*)). The thirteenth ṛk, beginning नवानां (*navānāṃ*), is of the metre महाबृहती छंद स्ववु (*mahābṛhatī chaṃda svavu*) (as printed); in a ṛk of this metre there are four pādas of eight syllables and one pāda of twelve syllables, as stated in the Anukramaṇikā

### Printed p. 333

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व. १४] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 333 (*[a. 2. a 5. va. 14] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 333*).*

(अनु. ९-९ (*anu. 9-9*)). Generally in metres, even if some syllables are fewer, one must suppose that the syllables have the fixed number, even though they appear fewer by the division of words, by sandhi and the like. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said:

कंकतः षोळशोपनिषदानुष्टुभमप्तृणसौर्यं विषशंकावानगस्यः प्राब्रवीद्द- शम्याद्याश्च तिस्रो महापंक्तयो महाबृहती चेति (*kaṃkataḥ ṣoḷaśopaniṣadānuṣṭubhamaptṛṇasauryaṃ viṣaśaṃkāvānagasyaḥ prābravīdda- śamyādyāśca tisro mahāpaṃktayo mahābṛhatī ceti*).

Here उपनिषत् (*upaniṣat*) means a secret. It is said that the sage Agastya recited this sūkta for the removal of poison, from the doubt that poison might have touched him by a snake bite. In the matter of Śrauta practice, the use of this sūkta is *laiṅgika* (by indication). The great sage Śaunaka, in his work ऋग्विधान (*ṛgvidhāna*), says as follows about the use of this sūkta:

कंकतो नेति सूक्तं तु विषार्तः प्रयतो जपेत् । (*kaṃkato neti sūktaṃ tu viṣārtaḥ prayato japet |*)
विषं न क्रमते चास्य सर्पाद्दृष्टिविषादपि । (*viṣaṃ na kramate cāsya sarpāddṛṣṭiviṣādapi |*)
यत्कीटलूतासु विषं दंष्टिवृश्चिकजं च यत् ॥ (*yatkīṭalūtāsu viṣaṃ daṃṣṭivṛścikajaṃ ca yat ‖*)
मूलं च कृत्रिमं चैव जपन् सर्वं व्यपोहति । (*mūlaṃ ca kṛtrimaṃ caiva japan sarvaṃ vyapohati |*)
धर्मं बुद्धिं धनं पुत्रान् सौभाग्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसं । (*dharmaṃ buddhiṃ dhanaṃ putrān saubhāgyaṃ brahmavarcasaṃ |*)
आरोग्यं पुष्टिमायुष्यं पशून् विद्यां महद्यशः । (*ārogyaṃ puṣṭimāyuṣyaṃ paśūn vidyāṃ mahadyaśaḥ |*)
(मुग्विधान. १-२८) (*(mugvidhāna. 1-28)*)

(The reference is printed मुग्विधान. १-२८ (*mugvidhāna. 1-28*), as supplied.) A man tormented by poison (one in whom poison has risen and who is suffering from a snake bite) should recite with faith and devotion this sūkta beginning कंकतो न (*kaṃkato na*). If he does so, neither the poison spread in the body by a snake bite nor the poison caused by an evil eye will spread further in the body. Besides, the poison caused by reptiles, scorpions and other poisonous creatures will also be removed. Whether that poison has spread in the body by the bite of a poisonous creature, or poison-mixed food and the like have entered the body, all of these will be removed by reciting this sūkta. Besides, by reciting this sūkta all the fruits will be obtained: righteous action, good understanding, wealth, sons and the like, good fortune, Brahmic splendour, health, nourishment, increase of life, cattle wealth, learning, fame and so on.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> कंक॑तो॒ न कंक॒तोs थो॑ सती॒नकं॑कतः ।

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> द्वा । इति । प्लुषी इति । इति । नि । अदृष्टाः । अलिप्सत ॥ १ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> कंकतोऽल्पविषः कश्चित् न कंकतस्तद्विपरीतोऽनल्पविषो महोरगादिः ॥
> तकतेर्गत्यर्थस्य वर्णव्यत्ययेन कंकत इति सरन् भवति ॥ अथो अपि च सतीनकंकतः।
> सतीनमित्युदकनाम । सतीनं गहनमिति तन्नामसु पातात् । उदकचार्यल्पविषवान्
> कश्चिद्दुंदुभादिः । एवं द्वाविति । अल्पविषमहाविषभेदेन जलस्थलभेदेन वा द्विप्रका-
> राविति । प्लुषी इति प्लोषणाविति । प्रकारद्वैविध्यदाहकत्वयोः प्रतिपादनायेशिकार-
> द्वयं । तथादृष्टा अदृश्यमानरूपा एतत्संज्ञकाश्च केचिद्विषधरा एवमुक्तप्रकारा
> ये संति ते नूनं मां न्यलिप्सत विशेषेण लिंपंति । सर्वाण्यंगानि विषमावृणोति।
> केनैवं कृतमिति ज्ञायत इति भावः ॥

*Gist:* Snakes of little poison, those of great poison, and water-snakes, of two kinds, burning, and unseen creatures, smear me thoroughly with poison.

*[As supplied, a line reading प्रसिद्धार्थ (*prasiddhārtha*) stands inside the bhāṣya block where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; the following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

कंकतः—अल्पवाद विषवुळ्ळ सर्पादिगळू (*kaṃkataḥ—alpavāda viṣavuḷḷa sarpādigaḷū*) (snakes and the like with little poison). न कंकतः—आत्यधिकवाद विषवुळ्ळ महो रगादिगळू (*na kaṃkataḥ—ātyadhikavāda viṣavuḷḷa maho ragādigaḷū*) (great serpents and the like with excessive poison). अथो—अदरंतॆये (*atho—adaraṃtèye*) (and likewise). सतीन कंकतः—विषपूरितवाद नीरुहावुगळू (*satīna kaṃkataḥ—viṣapūritavāda nīruhāvugaḷū*) (poison-laden water-snakes). द्वाविति— भूमियमेलॆ संचरिसतक्कवू मत्तु जलचरगळू अथवा अल्पविषवुळ्ळवू मत्तु महाविषवुळ्ळवू आद ऎरडु बगॆयल्लि (*dvāviti— bhūmiyamelè saṃcarisatakkavū mattu jalacaragaḷū athavā alpaviṣavuḷḷavū mattu mahāviṣavuḷḷavū āda èraḍu bagèyalli*) (in two kinds: those moving on the earth and those living in water, or those with little poison and those with great poison). प्लुषी इति—हिंसाकारकवू, नाशकारकगळू आगिरुवुवू (*pluṣī iti—hiṃsākārakavū, nāśakārakagaḷū āgiruvuvū*) (those that cause injury and destruction). अदृष्टाः— कण्णिगॆ गोचरवागद इतर विषजंतुगळू सह (*adṛṣṭāḥ— kaṇṇigè gocaravāgada itara viṣajaṃtugaḷū saha*) (other poisonous creatures not visible to the eye as well). नि अलिप्सत—नन्नन्नु विषदिंद पूरितनन्नागि माडुत्तवॆ (*ni alipsata—nannannu viṣadiṃda pūritanannāgi māḍuttavè*) (they fill me with poison).

*[As supplied, a line reading धनार्थ (*dhanārtha*) stands where the Bhāvārtha label belongs; the following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Snakes and the like with little poison, great serpents and the like with excessive poison, and likewise poison-laden water-creatures, these two kinds of poisonous creatures too, in a manner invisible to me, fill me with poison (the supplied text ends here, at the end of the window; the printed English and the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 follow in the next window).

### Printed p. 335

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १४ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 335 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 14 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 335*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 1 of Sūkta 191, after the Bhāvārtha which ended the previous window.)*

*[As supplied, the label line reads English Translatin (*English Translatin*) (sic), and the printed English carries block marks in the supplied text; given as prose with the standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

Some creature of little venom ; some creature of great venom ; or some venomous aquatic reptile ; creatures of two kinds, both destructive (of life), or (poisonous) unseen creatures, have anointed me with their poison.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

This is the last sūkta in the first maṇḍala. In this sūkta the sage Agastya, suspecting that a snake has bitten him, has spoken of the matter at length; apart from this sūkta there is no other such sūkta on this subject in the Ṛgveda. That by reciting this sūkta the poison caused by snakes and other poisonous creatures is removed, as the sage Śaunaka says in his work ऋग्विधान (*ṛgvidhāna*), has been told in the introduction of this sūkta itself.

In this ṛk two kinds of snakes are indicated: two kinds, snakes with little poison and snakes with great poison; or two kinds, snakes that move on the earth and water-snakes that live in water; so the sage has described them.

कंकतः—अल्पविषः । तकतेर्गत्यर्थस्य वर्णव्यत्ययेन कंकत इति सरन् भवति (*kaṃkataḥ—alpaviṣaḥ | takatergatyarthasya varṇavyatyayena kaṃkata iti saran bhavati*): the bhāṣyakāra explains that the word *kaṅkata* is formed, by transposition of letters (*varṇa*), from the root *takati*, which has the sense of motion, and that since the word gives the sense सरन् (*saran*) (moving) it is a creature that crawls on the ground, so that the meaning "snake" can be given to it. It is well known that there are many varieties in the poisonous power of snakes. Some, if they bite, do not cause much trouble; some, if they bite, the poison spreads and after some time causes distress and afterwards death; still some kinds of snakes, that is cobras, having excessive poison, certainly cause death if they bite. Among these cobras too there are many varieties and sub-varieties; some of them, if they bite, cause death in a few moments (at once). Such snakes are spread in many kinds in various countries. Some kinds of snakes look very large and fearful, yet have no poison; instead of biting animals they swallow them as food. Some kinds, if they merely touch, cause the body of the animal to begin to rot, and then death occurs. Still some kinds, on seeing animals, spray straight into their eyes a kind of poison-mixed fluid, and the animals may lose their eyes and become blind. Since there are such varieties in snakes and in their poison, the sage Agastya has here described their nature as snakes with little poison, snakes with great poison, and snakes that live in water.

न कंकतः—तद्विपरीतोऽनल्पविषः महोरगादिः (*na kaṃkataḥ—tadviparīto 'nalpaviṣaḥ mahoragādiḥ*): not having little poison, that is, cruel serpents such as the cobra, full of great poison; this is the purport.

सतीनकंकतः (*satīnakaṃkataḥ*): since the word सतीनं (*satīnaṃ*) is read among the hundred and one names of water (नि. २-२४ (*ni. 2-24*)), the word *satīnakaṅkataḥ* means a water-snake, a snake that lives in water.

द्वाविति प्लुषी (*dvāviti pluṣī*): the two kinds of snakes spoken of before cause harm; they are dangerous.

अदृष्टा:— अदृश्यमानरूपा एतद्व्यंजकाश्च (*adṛṣṭā:— adṛśyamānarūpā etadvyaṃjakāśca*): not seen by the eye, that is, very small, or these snakes which hide in grass and the like, or in bushes, and so are not seen by the eye; this is the purport. Since snakes are generally in grass, in bushes and in holes, people do not at once notice them; when people are unaware in that way, they deceive them and bite; this is the purport.

अलिप्सत—विशेषण लिंपंति । सर्वाण्यंगानि विषमावृणोति (*alipsata—viśeṣaṇa liṃpaṃti | sarvāṇyaṃgāni viṣamāvṛṇoti*): they smear on the poison so that it spreads to all the limbs, that is, they bite; or, biting, they make the poison spread in the limbs; this is the purport.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 1, noted briefly)

The page explains: कंकत: (*kaṃkata:*) (the root तक गत् (*taka gat*); the desired form is obtained by transposition of letters; the initial acute arises from the same transposition); सतीनकंकतः (*satīnakaṃkataḥ*) (by the rule तत्पुरुषे (*tatpuruṣe*) (पा. सू. ६-२-२ (*pā. sū. 6-2-2*)) the accent of the first member remains; the word *satīna* has the acute on the end by the accent of the nominal stem); अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*) (by the rule न दृष्टाः परादिश्चंदसि बहुलम् (*na dṛṣṭāḥ parādiścaṃdasi bahulam*) (पा. सू. ६ २-१९९ (*pā. sū. 6 2-199*), as printed) the acute on the first syllable of the second member); अलिप्सत (*alipsata*) (root लिप उपदेहे (*lipa upadehe*), as printed, of the *tudādi* class; *luṅ* in the present sense in the Veda; *at* substituted for the third person plural; the augment *āṭ*; because it follows a verb form, printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*), the *nighāta* accent arises).

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒दृष्टा॑न्हंत्याय॒त्यथो॑ हंति पराय॒ती ।
> अथो॑ अवघ्न॒ती हं॒त्यथो॑ पिनष्टि पिंस॒ती [?] ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अदृष्टान् । हंति । आयती । अथो इति । हंति । पर्यायती [?] ।
> आथो [?] इति । अव्यघ्नती [?] । हंति । अथो इति । पिनष्टि । पिंषती ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अनेन विषघ्न्योषधिः स्तूयते । आयती विषदष्टस्य सकाशमागच्छंती विष-
> निर्हरणसाधनौषधिरदृष्टानदृश्यमानान्विषधरान्हंति । हिनस्ति । अथो अपि च परायती
> परागच्छंती सम्मार्जनसमयेऽर्वाक्प्रवृत्ता हंति । नाशयति जलचरविषधरान् ।
> अथो अपि चावघ्नती ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृ प्रत्ययः ॥ अवहन्यमानौषधिः स्वगंधेन हंति
> बहुविषन् । यद्वा । काचिदोषधिर्दंशकान्मारयत्येव । अथो अपि च पिंषती
> पेषणकर्त्रि दृष्टिष्यमाणा नौषधिः पिनष्टि । चूर्णिकरोत्यल्पविषन् । अथवा
> सर्वेषु वाक्येष्टविशेषेण सर्वविषकारिणां नाश उक्तः ॥

*Gist:* The verse praises the poison-destroying herb: coming, going away, being pounded, by its smell or ground to powder, it kills poisonous creatures.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

आयती—(ओषधियु) विषदष्टनादवन हत्तिरक्कॆ बरुवागले (*āyatī—(oṣadhiyu) viṣadaṣṭanādavana hattirakkè baruvāgale*) (the herb, just as it comes near the one bitten by poison). अदृष्टान्—कण्णिगॆ गोचरवागद विषप्राणिगळन्नु (*adṛṣṭān—kaṇṇigè gocaravāgada viṣaprāṇigaḷannu*) (the poisonous creatures not visible to the eye). हंति—कॊल्लुत्तदॆ (*haṃti—kòlluttadè*) (kills). अथो—अनंतर (*atho—anaṃtara*) (afterwards). परायती—(तॊळॆयुव कालदल्लि देहदिंद) हॊरक्कॆ होगतक्क कालदल्लि (*parāyatī—(tòḷèyuva kāladalli dehadiṃda) hòrakkè hogatakka kāladalli*) (at the time of going out, at the time of washing, from the body). हंति—अवुगळन्नु नाशमाडुत्तदॆ (*haṃti—avugaḷannu nāśamāḍuttadè*) (destroys them). अथो— अदू अल्लदॆ (*atho— adū alladè*) (and besides). अवघ्नती—तन्न (गंधदिंदले) नाशकारियाद ओषधियु (*avaghnatī—tanna (gaṃdhadiṃdale) nāśakāriyāda oṣadhiyu*) (the herb that destroys by its own smell). हंति—विषधरगळन्नु नाशमाडुत्तदॆ (*haṃti—viṣadharagaḷannu nāśamāḍuttadè*) (destroys the poison-bearers). अथो—अदर जॊतॆयल्लि (*atho—adara jòtèyalli*) (along with that). पिंषती—चूर्णरूपवाद ओषधियु (*piṃṣatī—cūrṇarūpavāda oṣadhiyu*) (the herb in powder form). पिनष्टि— विषक्रिमिगळन्नु चूर्णमाडुत्तदॆ (*pinaṣṭi— viṣakrimigaḷannu cūrṇamāḍuttadè*) (crushes the poison-worms) (नाशपडिसुत्तदॆ) (*(nāśapaḍisuttadè)*) (destroys them).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The herb, just as it comes near the one bitten by poison, destroys some poison-bearers. Likewise, at the time when it goes out of the body in washing, it destroys some poison-worms. There are also herbs that destroy by their own smell. The herb in powder form crushes the worms to powder and destroys them.

**Printed English translation**

(The antidote), coming (to the bitten person), destroys the nnseen (venomons creatures); departing, (it destroys them) ; deprived (of substance), it destroys them (by its odour); being ground, it pulverises them-

*[The supplied text of the printed English reads "nnseen" and "venomons", apparent misreadings of the print; kept as supplied. The printed English ends with a hyphen, as supplied.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

In this ṛk the nature of herbs that can destroy or remove poison is described.

अदृष्टान् हंति आयती (*adṛṣṭān haṃti āyatī*): the poison-removing herb, even as it comes, kills the poisonous creatures hidden so as not to be seen by the eye; that is, by the power of the herb the poisonous creatures are destroyed at once.

अथो हंति परायती—परागच्छंती सम्मार्जनसमयेऽर्वाक्षप्रवृत्ता हंति (*atho haṃti parāyatī—parāgacchaṃtī sammārjanasamaye 'rvākṣapravṛttā haṃti*) (as printed): they have given the meaning of this sentence as that it destroys the poison which goes out of the body at the time of washing the wound bitten by a snake. This does not appear so fitting. The word परायिती (*parāyitī*) (as printed) means going backward. Therefore the meaning that the herb destroys the serpents and the like who, in fear that the men they have bitten will kill them, escape and run backward out of sight, fits here.

आथो अवघ्नती हंति (*ātho avaghnatī haṃti*) (as printed): the herb kills snakes by its sharp smell. Snakes cannot bear the smell of some herbs (नागदाळीसप्पु (*nāgadāḷīsappu*) and the like); therefore they leave the place where such herbs are. If the word *avaghnatī* is taken as formed with the prefix *ava* from the root घ्रा (जिघ्र) (*ghrā (jighra)*), meaning "smell", the meaning given above fits. Or, if it is taken as formed from the root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*) ("kill"), the word *avaghnatī* may mean the poisonous creatures that bite (men) and kill; that the herb kills (destroys) such poisonous creatures is another way in which the meaning may be given.

अथो पिनष्टि पिंषती (*atho pinaṣṭi piṃṣatī*): some herbs used for medicines are used after being powdered. Such a powder crushes (grinds) and kills the poisonous creatures, that is, destroys them; this is the purport.

The idea stated in the four pādas of this ṛk is all more or less of one kind. For these sentences it may be said that the herbs destroy the poisons spread in the wound, or

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 2, noted briefly)

The page explains: हंति (*haṃti*) (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*), of the *adādi* class; present third person singular; the verbal *nighāta* accent); आयती (*āyatī*) (root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); the suffix *śatṛ*; *ṅīp* when the feminine is intended; the acute on the end by the rule ततुत नुमोनद्यजादी (*tatuta numonadyajādī*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३ (*pā. sū. 6-1-173*)); the same in पराऋती अवघ्नती (*parāṛtī avaghnatī*), as printed); अवघ्नती (*avaghnatī*) (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*); the suffix *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; by *vyatyaya* an agent suffix stands here in the passive; in the sense "being pounded" the form would have to be अवहन्यमाना (*avahanyamānā*), therefore the suffix *śatṛ* itself denotes the object); पिनष्टि (*pinaṣṭi*) (root पिषल्य संचूर्णने (*piṣalya saṃcūrṇane*), as printed, of the *rudhādi* class; present third person singular with the suffix *tip*; the *śnam* vikaraṇa, because marked *m*, comes after the last vowel; the substitution of *ṭ* for the suffix by the rule of *ṣṭutva*; the verbal *nighāta* accent because it follows a verb form).

*Gist:* Other causes of poison: reeds, kuśara, darbha, sairya, muñja and vīraṇa grasses; the unseen poisonous creatures in them together smear me with poison.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

शरासः—शरा ऎंब तृणदल्लडगिरुवुवू (*śarāsaḥ—śarā èṃba tṛṇadallaḍagiruvuvū*) (those hidden in the grass called *śarā*). कुशरासः—कुशवॆंब तृणवन्नाश्रयिसिरुवुवू (*kuśarāsaḥ—kuśavèṃba tṛṇavannāśrayisiruvuvū*) (those lodged in the grass called *kuśa*). दर्भासः—दर्भॆगगळल्लिरुवुवू (*darbhāsaḥ—darbhègagaḷalliruvuvū*) (those in darbha grasses). सैर्य्याः—सैर्य ऎंब जॊंडिनल्लिरुवुवू (*sairyyāḥ—sairya èṃba jòṃḍinalliruvuvū*) (those in the reed called *sairya*). मौंजाः—मुंजद पॊदॆयल्लडगिरुवुवू (*mauṃjāḥ—muṃjada pòdèyallaḍagiruvuvū*) (those hidden in a clump of *muñja*). वैरिणः—वीरणदल्लिरुवुवू आगि (*vairiṇaḥ—vīraṇadalliruvuvū āgi*) (and those in *vīraṇa*). अदृष्टाः—कण्णिगॆ गोचरवागदिरुव (*adṛṣṭāḥ—kaṇṇigè gocaravāgadiruva*) (not visible to the eye). सर्वे—समस्तवाद विषधरगळू सह (*sarve—samastavāda viṣadharagaḷū saha*) (all the poison-bearers too). साकं—जॊतॆयल्लि सेरिकॊंडु (*sākaṃ—jòtèyalli serikòṃḍu*) (joining together). न्यलिस्सत—नन्नन्नु विष पूरितनन्नागि माडुत्तवॆ (*nyalissata—nannannu viṣa pūritanannāgi māḍuttavè*) (they fill me with poison; the word printed as here).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads भाषा (*bhāṣā*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

All the poison-bearers that hide in the grasses *śarā*, *kuśa*, *sairya*, *muñja*, *vīraṇa* and the like, and are not visible to the eye, bite us and make our whole body filled with poison.

*[As supplied, the label line of the printed English reads Englih Tranlation (*Englih Tranlation*) (sic); standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

(Blades of) shara grass, (of) kushara, (of) darbha, (of) sourya, (of) munja, (of) virana, all (the haunt) of unseen (venomous creatures), have together anointed me (with their venom).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

In this ṛk are mentioned the various grasses, darbha and the like, in which snakes hide so as not to be seen by the eye.

शरासः—वेणुदंडसदृशा अंतश्चिद्रास्त्रणविशेषाः (*śarāsaḥ—veṇudaṃḍasadṛśā aṃtaścidrāstraṇaviśeṣāḥ*): a kind of grass or darbha that is tall and straight like a bamboo and looks as if cut in the middle (Sacoharum Sara (*Sacoharum Sara*), as printed). This kind of darbha grows thickly and in regions where there is water. Since they are about waist-high, it is not possible to know what is at their roots; the meaning is that snakes are hiding in such a region where nothing can be seen by the eye.

कुशरासः— कुत्सितशरा अंतश्चिद्राः शरसदृशास्त्रणविशेषाः (*kuśarāsaḥ— kutsitaśarā aṃtaścidrāḥ śarasadṛśāstraṇaviśeṣāḥ*): the darbha called *kuśara* too is just like the darbha *śara* mentioned above, that is, it belongs to the same kind, but it does not grow very tall.

दर्भासः (*darbhāsaḥ*): the grass called darbha, used in sacrifices and in domestic rites. It grows as thick as a हॆंची कड्डि (*hèṃcī kaḍḍi*) (as printed) (Poa cynosuroides (*Poa cynosuroides*)).

### Printed p. 341

*Running head (as supplied): [आ: २. आ ५. व. १४. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 341 (*[ā: 2. ā 5. va. 14. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 341*).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 of Sūkta 191, after the *darbhāsaḥ* entry.)*

सैर्या:—सैर्यास्तटाकादिप्रांतोद्भवास्त्रृणविशेषा अश्ववाला इति प्रसिद्धाः (*sairyā:—sairyāstaṭākādiprāṃtodbhavāstrṛṇaviśeṣā aśvavālā iti prasiddhāḥ*): *sairya* means a reed grass that grows near lakes, tanks or rivers, that is, in places where water stands. It is customarily called "horse's tail". Elephants use it as food. (Saccharum spontaneum (*Saccharum spontaneum*))

मौंजाः—मौंजाः मुंजाः प्रसिद्धाः (*mauṃjāḥ—mauṃjāḥ muṃjāḥ prasiddhāḥ*): *muñja* is a grass that grows long like a stick. It is used for weaving mats. (Saccharum munja (*Saccharum munja*))

वैरिणाः—वीरणप्रकाराः (*vairiṇāḥ—vīraṇaprakārāḥ*): it is not known what a kind of grass called *vīraṇa* is like. (Andropogon muricatum (*Andropogon muricatum*))

Besides these kinds of grass there are many other kinds of grass; only a few are mentioned here. The purport is that snakes hide in them so as not to be seen by people's eyes, and bite those who come near.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 3, noted briefly)

The page explains: शरासः (*śarāsaḥ*) (the suffix *jas* in the nominative plural; the augment *asuk* by the rule आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*); the acute on the middle syllable by the accent of the single substitute); कुशरासः (*kuśarāsaḥ*) (कुत्सिताः शराः कुशरासः (*kutsitāḥ śarāḥ kuśarāsaḥ*); as before the augment *asuk* for *jas*; the accent of the first member by the rule तत्पुरुषे- तुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣe- tulyārtha*) (पा. सू ६-२-२ (*pā. sū 6-2-2*)), where अव्ययेनञ्- कु निपातानाम् (*avyayenañ- ku nipātānām*) is read); न्यलिप्सत (*nyalipsata*) (the prefix *ni*; the root लिप उपदेहे (*lipa upadehe*), as printed; *luṅ*; *at* substituted for the third person plural; the *nighāta* accent because it follows a verb form, printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*)).

### Printed p. 342

*Running head (as supplied): [342 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. अ. २४. सू. १.९१] (*[342 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. a. 24. sū. 1.91]*), as printed.*

*[As supplied, the label line of the bhāṣya reads सायुधभाष्यं (*sāyudhabhāṣyaṃ*); standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> गावो गोष्ठे न्यसदन् । निषीदंति । मृगासो मृगा नृविक्षत । निविष्टाः ।
> स्वस्वस्थान उपरताः । जनानां प्राणिनां केतवः प्रज्ञानानि नि ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेयो-
> ग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । नीचान्यभवन् । एतेऽस्मिन्समयेऽदृष्टा अदृश्यमानरूपाः संतो
> न्यलिप्सत । निलिंपंति विशेषेण ॥

*Gist:* The cows lay in their stalls, beasts at rest in their places, people's senses quiet; at that time unseen creatures smear me with poison.

*[As supplied, a line reading प्रसिद्धार्थ (*prasiddhārtha*) stands inside the bhāṣya block where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; the following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

गावः—गोवुगळु (*gāvaḥ—govugaḷu*) (the cows). गोष्ठे—कॊट्टिगॆयल्लि (*goṣṭhe—kòṭṭigèyalli*) (in the stall). न्यसदन्—कट्टल्पट्टु विश्रांतियन्नु तॆगॆदुकॊळ्ळुत्तिद्दवु (*nyasadan—kaṭṭalpaṭṭu viśrāṃtiyannu tègèdukòḷḷuttiddavu*) (were tied and taking rest). मृगासः—मृगगळु (*mṛgāsaḥ—mṛgagaḷu*) (the beasts). नृविक्षत—तम्म तम्म स्वस्थानगळल्लि विश्रांतियन्नु तॆगॆदुकॊळ्ळुत्तिद्दवु (*nṛvikṣata—tamma tamma svasthānagaḷalli viśrāṃtiyannu tègèdukòḷḷuttiddavu*) (were taking rest each in its own place). जनानां—प्राणिगळ (*janānāṃ—prāṇigaḷa*) (of the creatures). केतवः—प्रज्ञानगळु (*ketavaḥ—prajñānagaḷu*) (the perceptions). नि—प्रशांतवागिद्दवु (इंतह कालदल्लि) (*ni—praśāṃtavāgiddavu (iṃtaha kāladalli)*) (were calm, at such a time). अदृष्टाः—कण्णिगॆ काणदिरुव विषधरगळु (*adṛṣṭāḥ—kaṇṇigè kāṇadiruva viṣadharagaḷu*) (the poison-bearers not visible to the eye). नृलिप्सत—नन्नन्नु कच्चि विषवन्नु नन्न देहदल्लि व्याप्तवागुवंतॆ माडिदवु (*nṛlipsata—nannannu kacci viṣavannu nanna dehadalli vyāptavāguvaṃtè māḍidavu*) (bit me and made the poison spread in my body).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

While the unseen poison-bearers bit me and made my body filled with poison, the cows were tied in the stall, the beasts lay in their own places, and the perceptions of the creatures were calm.

**Printed English translation**

The cows had lain down in their stalls ; the wild beasts had retreated (to their lairs) ; the senses of men were at rest; when the unseen (venomous creatures), anointed me (with their venom).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads कंठपाठि (*kaṃṭhapāṭhi*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

In this ṛk it is explained that snakes generally move about only at night. For the cattle (at night) lie in their stalls, that is, they take rest without movement and chew the cud. The wild beasts too enter their own place, the caves, and sleep. People too, having finished their daily affairs, sleep for rest at night without doing any work. At such a time snakes come unseen and bite people; this is the purport.

Here to say that wild beasts are in their caves at night is not right. For they lie sleeping in their caves all day and move about at night for food (the word is divided by the page boundary: संचरि (*saṃcari*) at the end of p. 342, सुवुवु (*suvuvu*) at the start of p. 343).

### Printed p. 343

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व: १४.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 343 (*[a. 2. a 5. va: 14.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 343*).*

But since this ṛk says only मृगासः (*mṛgāsaḥ*), it need not be understood as wild beasts only; gentle animals such as horses (Domestic Animals (*Domestic Animals*)) may also be meant. Nor is there in this ṛk any word giving the meaning "at night"; but since it indicates a time when people are unconscious (asleep), doing no work, it appears to be night. In the main, whether it is night or day, when people and animals have finished their work and are taking rest, these wicked snakes come unseen and bite them; this is the main purport.

In the first sentence of this ṛk there is the verb नि असदन् (*ni asadan*). In the other sentences, although there is no verb, since the preposition नि (*ni*) is used, a verb has to be supplied for each sentence. Such ṛks are plentiful in the Ṛgveda. For the sake of emphasis (Emphasis (*Emphasis*)) in the sentences, the preposition is sometimes used in this way:

मा नो महांतमुत मा नो अर्भकं मा न उक्षंतमुत मा न उक्षितं । (*mā no mahāṃtamuta mā no arbhakaṃ mā na ukṣaṃtamuta mā na ukṣitaṃ |*)
मा नो वधीः पितरं मोत मातरं मा नः प्रियास्तन्वो रुद्र रीरिषः ॥ (*mā no vadhīḥ pitaraṃ mota mātaraṃ mā naḥ priyāstanvo rudra rīriṣaḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. १-११४-७) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-114-7)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*), as supplied.) In this ṛk the verbs वधीः (*vadhīḥ*) and रीरिषः (*rīriṣaḥ*) are read only once, yet the negative word मा (*mā*) is used in every sentence. Such usages give grace, gravity and rhyme to the poet's skill in composition.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 4, noted briefly)

The page explains: गोष्ठे (*goṣṭhe*) (root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); the suffix *ka* when the word *go* is the upapada, by the rule सुपि स्थः (*supi sthaḥ*) (पा. सू. ३-२-४ (*pā. sū. 3-2-4*)); *ṣatva* of the root's *s* by the rule अंबांबगोभूमि (*aṃbāṃbagobhūmi*) (पा. सू. ८-२९-२ (*pā. sū. 8-29-2*), as printed); elision of the *ā* by आतोलोप इटि च (*ātolopa iṭi ca*); the accent of the verbal-derivative second member; locative singular); आसदन् (*āsadan*) (root षदल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadalya viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*), as printed; *luṅ* in the present sense in the Veda; *aj* substituted for *cli* by the rule पुषादिद्युता (*puṣādidyutā*); *ant* substituted for the plural suffix *jh*; the augment *aṭ*; the verbal *nighāta* accent); अविक्षत (*avikṣata*) (root विश प्रवेशने (*viśa praveśane*); *luṅ*, third person plural; the verbal *nighāta* accent); नि (*ni*) (the name *upasarga* is prescribed when a verb is connected; since here only *ni* is heard, a suitable verb is supplied; the supplied text ends within this grammar page).

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ए॒त उ॒ तै [?] प्रत्य॑दृश्रन्म दो॒षं [?] तस्क॑रा इव ।
> अदृ॑ष्टा॒ विश्व॑दृष्टाः॒ प्रति॑बुद्धा अभूतन ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एते । ऊं इति । त्ये । प्रति । अदृश्रन् । प्रदोषं । तस्कराःइव ।
> अदृष्टाः । विश्वदृष्टाः । प्रतिबुद्धाः । अभूतन ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> त्ये त एते सर्पाः प्रत्यदृश्यन् । प्रतिदृश्यंते रात्रौ श्वासादिलिंगेन । यद्वा ।
> ते रात्रौ हंतारो दिव्यते प्रतिदृश्यंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । प्रदोषं । रात्रिर्दोषा ।
> रात्रिं प्रति तमसाभिभूतासु रात्रिषु तस्करा इव हिंसकाश्चौरा दृश्यंते यथा तद्वत् ।
> कीदृशास्ते । अदृष्टा अपरिदृश्यमाना विश्वदृष्टा विश्वं दृष्टं यैस्ते तादृशाः प्रति-
> दृश्यंते । अतो हे नराः प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन । भवत ॥

*Gist:* These snakes are discovered at night by their breathing, like thieves at dusk; unseen, they see all; so men should be watchful.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

तै ते—मेलॆ वर्णितवाद ई विषधरगळु (*tai te—melè varṇitavāda ī viṣadharagaḷu*) (these poison-bearers described above). प्रदोषं—मब्बिनिंद कूडिद प्रदोष कालदल्लि (*pradoṣaṃ—mabbiniṃda kūḍida pradoṣa kāladalli*) (in the dusky evening time). तस्करा इव—चोररु काणिसिकॊळ्ळुवंतॆ (*taskarā iva—coraru kāṇisikòḷḷuvaṃtè*) (as thieves are discovered). प्रत्यदृश्यन्—(रात्रिकालदल्लि अवुगळ निश्वासादिगळिंद) तिळियल्पडुत्तवॆ अथवा रात्रिय हॊत्तु काणदिद्दरू हगलुहॊत्तु काणल्प डुत्तवॆ (*pratyadṛśyan—(rātrikāladalli avugaḷa niśvāsādigaḷiṃda) tiḷiyalpaḍuttavè athavā rātriya hòttu kāṇadiddarū hagaluhòttu kāṇalpa ḍuttavè*) (are known, at night by their breathing and the like, or, though not seen at night, are seen by day). अदृष्टाः अवुगळु इतररिंद नोडल्पडदिद्दरू (*adṛṣṭāḥ avugaḷu itarariṃda noḍalpaḍadiddarū*) (though they are not seen by others). विश्वदृष्टाः—उळिद समस्तवन्नू सह अवु नोडुत्तवॆ (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ—uḷida samastavannū saha avu noḍuttavè*) (they see everything else as well), (आदुदरिंद ऎलै जनरे) (*(ādudariṃda èlai janare)*) (therefore, O people). प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन—बहळु ऎच्चरदिंदिरि (*pratibuddhā abhūtana—bahaḷu èccaradiṃdiri*) (be very watchful).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads बानार्ध (*bānārdha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The poison-bearers described above are known, in the dusky evening time, at night by their breathing and the like, as thieves are discovered. Although others cannot see them, they can see everything else. Therefore, O people, all of you be watchful.

**Printed English translation**

Or they may be discovered (in the dark), as thieves in the (dusk of) evening; for although they be unseen, yet all are seen by them; therefore, men, be vigilant.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5)**

तै—ते (*tai—te*): in many places in the Ṛgveda it is customary to use the word *tyad* in place of the word *tad*.

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते । (*etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate |*)
(म. सं. १९२१) (*(ma. saṃ. 1921)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. १९२१ (*ma. saṃ. 1921*), as supplied.) In such ṛks त्याः (*tyāḥ*) means ताः (*tāḥ*).

प्रत्यदृशन् प्रदोषं (*pratyadṛśan pradoṣaṃ*) (as printed): are seen at night, that is, in the dark night snakes are generally known by the sound of their breathing; this is the purport.

तस्करा इव (*taskarā iva*): the example of thieves is given with regard to moving in the dark. It is well known that thieves generally steal at night, when darkness has spread, at the time when everyone is asleep, so that nobody may see them. Likewise these wicked snakes, moving about in the dark night, cause danger to people.

अदृष्टाः विश्वदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*): people cannot see the snakes that move or crawl about in the dark; therefore they remain unseen by the eye. Yet they alone can see everyone. Because they have this ability, there is a greater likelihood of danger to people from them. Therefore the sage tells people प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन (*pratibuddhā abhūtana*): O people, you must be very watchful about these snakes.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 5, noted briefly)

The page explains: त्यॆ (*tyè*) (the word *tyad*; *śi* substituted for *jas* in the nominative plural; by the rule त्यदादीनामः (*tyadādīnāmaḥ*) the substitution of *a*, the following form; the printed line ends with गुण (*guṇa*)); अदृश्रन् (*adṛśran*) (root दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे (*dṛśir prekṣaṇe*); *luṅ* in the present sense in the Veda; *aj* substituted for *cli* by the rule इरितोवा (*iritovā*) (पा. सू. ३-१-५७ (*pā. sū. 3-1-57*)); the augment *ruṭ* for *jhi* by the rule बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*) (पा. सू. ७-१-८ (*pā. sū. 7-1-8*)); the *nighāta* accent because it follows a verb form, printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*)); तस्कराः (*taskarāḥ*) (by the rule तद्बृहतोः करपत्यो (*tadbṛhatoḥ karapatyo*) (वा ३७१३ (*vā 3713*), as printed), when the word *pati* follows the word *tad* and the sense of thief appears, the augment *suṭ* in the middle and elision of the *d*); विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*) (विश्वं दृष्टं यैस्ते विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yaiste viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*); since a name is intended, by the rule बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ*) the word *viśva* does not take the acute on the end; by the rule बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपथम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapatham*), as printed, the acute on the first syllable by the accent of the first member).

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> दौर्वः॑ [?] पि॒ता पृ॑थि॒वी मा॒ता सोमो॒ भ्रातादि॑तिः॒ स्वसा॑ ।
> अदृ॑ष्टा॒ विश्व॑दृष्टा॒स्तिष्ठ॑ते॒ळय॑ता॒ सु कं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> द्यौः । वः । पिता । पृथिवी । माता । सोमः । भ्राता । अदितिः । स्वसा ।
> अदृष्टाः । विश्वदृष्टाः । तिष्ठत । इळियत [?] । सु । कं ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अतः परं विषविचिकित्सा । तत्र तावत् हे सर्पाः वो युष्माकं द्यौः पिता ।
> पृथिवी माता । सोमो भ्राता । अदितिर्देवमाता स्वसा । एवंमहानुभावा महो-
> रगाः अदृष्टा अन्यैरदृश्यमानरूपाः स्वयं तु विश्वदृष्टाः सर्वस्य द्रष्टारो
> यूयं तिष्ठत स्वस्वस्थाने । मां प्रति मा गच्छत । सु सुतरां कं सुखं यथा तथे-
> ळयत । ईरयत । गच्छत । सोमशब्देन सोमाधारो द्युलोक उच्यते । पृथिव्यं-
> तरिक्षद्यु स्थानस्थाः सर्पाः स्वस्वस्थानं प्राप्नुतास्मद्बाधं मा कुरतेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* After this, treatment of poison: serpents, heaven is your father, earth mother, Soma brother, Aditi sister; stay in your places, do not harm me.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(ऎलै सर्पगळे) वः—निमगॆ (*(èlai sarpagaḷe) vaḥ—nimagè*) (O serpents, to you). द्यौः—द्युलोकवु (*dyauḥ—dyulokavu*) (heaven). पिता—तंदॆयु (*pitā—taṃdèyu*) (father). पृथिवी—पृथि वियु (*pṛthivī—pṛthi viyu*) (the earth). माता—तायियु (*mātā—tāyiyu*) (mother). सोमः—सोमाधारवाद अंतरिक्षवु (*somaḥ—somādhāravāda aṃtarikṣavu*) (the atmosphere, the support of soma). भ्राता—ऒडहुट्टिदवनु (*bhrātā—òḍahuṭṭidavanu*) (brother). अदितिः—देवमातॆयाद अदितियु (*aditiḥ—devamātèyāda aditiyu*) (Aditi, the mother of the gods). स्वसा—सहोदरियु (*svasā—sahodariyu*) (sister). अदृष्टाः—इतररिंद नीवु नोड ल्पडदिद्दरू (*adṛṣṭāḥ—itarariṃda nīvu noḍa lpaḍadiddarū*) (though you are not seen by others). विश्वदृष्टाः—नीवु सकलवन्नू नोडबल्लिरि (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ—nīvu sakalavannū noḍaballiri*) (you can see everything). तिष्ठत—निम्म निम्म प्रदेशदल्ले सुरक्षितवागिरि (*tiṣṭhata—nimma nimma pradeśadalle surakṣitavāgiri*) (stay safe in your own regions). सु—अतिशयवागि (*su—atiśayavāgi*) (exceedingly). कं—सुखवन्नु हॊंदुवंतॆ (*kaṃ—sukhavannu hòṃduvaṃtè*) (so as to obtain happiness). इलयत—वर्तिसिरि (*ilayata—vartisiri*) (behave).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O serpents, heaven is your father, the earth your mother; Soma (the atmosphere, the support of soma) your brother, Aditi, the mother of the gods, your sister... (the supplied text breaks off here, in the middle of the sentence, at निम्मन्नु इतररु (*nimmannu itararu*), at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 347

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व. १५ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 347 (*[a. 2. a 5. va. 15 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 347*).*

*(Continuation of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 6 of Sūkta 191, from the end of the previous page.)*

...although you cannot be seen by others, you can see everything else. Without coming to us and troubling us, abide in your own places and enjoy happiness.

**Printed English translation**

Heaven, (serpents), is your father, Earth your mother, Soma your brother, Aditi your sister, unseen, all seeing, abide (in your own holes), enjoy (your own) good pleasure.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 6)**

So far the sage Agastya has censured the harm that serpents and the like cause to people and has said that people must be very watchful about them; now, in this ṛk and in the next ṛk, he expresses the wish that they should live happily by themselves without troubling anyone, and prays accordingly.

सोमः (*somaḥ*): here the bhāṣyakāra's view is that the word *soma* means the heavenly world where soma is; that is, the purport is the various kinds of serpents that are on the earth, in the atmosphere and in heaven. This matter is clearly stated in the mantra in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्यो ये के च पृथिवीमनु । (*namo astu sarpebhyo ye ke ca pṛthivīmanu |*)
ये अंतरिक्षे ये दिवि तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥ (*ye aṃtarikṣe ye divi tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*)
(शै. सं. ४-२-८-३) (*(śai. saṃ. 4-2-8-3)*)

(The reference is printed शै. सं. (*śai. saṃ.*), as supplied.) Besides the three principal places, earth, atmosphere and heaven, the matter of the serpents in other places too is told there:

येऽदो रोचने दिवो ये वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिषु । (*ye 'do rocane divo ye vā sūryasya raśmiṣu |*)
येषामप्सुसदः कृतं तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥ (*yeṣāmapsusadaḥ kṛtaṃ tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*)
या इषवो यातुधानानां ये वा वनस्पती ग्ं रनु । (*yā iṣavo yātudhānānāṃ ye vā vanaspatī gṃ ranu |*)
ये वावटेषु शेरते तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥ (*ye vāvaṭeṣu śerate tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*)
(कृ. सं. ४-२-८-३) (*(kṛ. saṃ. 4-2-8-3)*)

(The reference is printed कृ. सं. (*kṛ. saṃ.*), as supplied.) In these mantras the names of many kinds of snakes are given: the serpents that are in the shining heaven; the serpents that wish to be in the rays of the sun (बिसलिनल्लि (*bisalinalli*), in the sunshine); the serpents that are in water (Annaconda (*Annaconda*), as printed); the serpents that are used like the arrows of the rākṣasas; the serpents that live on trees (हसरु हावु (*hasaru hāvu*), as printed); and the serpents that live in ruined wells.

The page explains: शिष्ठत (*śiṣṭhata*) (as printed; the root स्थागतिनिवृत्तौ (*sthāgatinivṛttau*); *loṭ*, second person plural, for which *ta* is substituted; the root takes the substitute printed शिष्ठ (*śiṣṭha*) by the rule पाघ्राध्या- (*pāghrādhyā-*); because it stands at the beginning of a pāda there is no *nighāta*; the acute on the first syllable by the root accent); इळयत (*iḷayata*) (root इल प्रेरणे (*ila preraṇe*), of the *curādi* class; the suffix *ṇic* by the rule printed सत्यापपाक (*satyāpapāka*); in the Veda *guṇa* of the light penultimate does not occur; *loṭ*, second person plural; lengthening in the Saṃhitā by the rule अन्येषामपि- दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi- dṛśyate*) (पा. सू ६-१-१३७ (*pā. sū 6-1-137*)); no *nighāta* because it follows a verb form, printed तिजंत (*tijaṃta*); by the accent of *ṇic* the *ā* after the *l* takes the acute).

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ये अंस्या॒ ये अंग्याः॑ सू॒चीका॒ ये प्र॑ कंक॒ताः ।
> अदृ॑ष्टाः॒ किं च॒नेह वः॒ सर्वे॑ सा॒कं नि ज॑स्यत ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ये । अंस्याः । ये । अंग्याः । सूचीकाः । ये । प्रकंकताः ।
> अदृष्टाः । किं । चन । इह । वः । सर्वे । साकं । नि । जस्यत ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> येऽंस्या अंसार्हा अंसगा अंसे भवा अंसाभ्यां खादंतो वा । तथा
> येऽग्या अंगगा अंगेन शरीरेण हंतारो वा लूतिकादयः । सूचीकाः सूची-
> सदृशपुच्छरोमाणो वृश्चिकाद्याः । ये च प्रकंकताः प्रकृष्टविषाः प्रकृष्टगामिनो
> वा महोरगा अदृष्टा अदृश्यमानाः किं चन यत्किंचित्सर्पजातमस्ति । इहास्मिन्
> समीपे वो युष्माकं किमस्ति । अतो यूयं सर्वे साकं सह नितरां जस्यत ।
> मुंचतास्मान् ॥ जसु मोक्षणे दैवादिकः ॥

*Gist:* Serpents that move on the shoulder or body, needle-tailed scorpions and others of virulent poison, unseen: depart all together from us.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ये—याव विषधरगळु (*ye—yāva viṣadharagaḷu*) (the poison-bearers that). अंस्याः—भुजदिंद सरियुवुवो (*aṃsyāḥ—bhujadiṃda sariyuvuvo*) (glide by the shoulder). ये—यावुवु (*ye—yāvuvu*) (which). अंग्याः—(पूर्णवाद) शरीरदिंद सरियुवुवो (*aṃgyāḥ—(pūrṇavāda) śarīradiṃda sariyuvuvo*) (glide with the whole body). सूचीकाः—सूजियंतॆ पुच्छवू रोमवू उळ्ळ वृश्चिकादिगळू (*sūcīkāḥ—sūjiyaṃtè pucchavū romavū uḷḷa vṛścikādigaḷū*) (scorpions and the like with tail and hair like a needle). ये—यावुवु (*ye—yāvuvu*) (which). प्रकंकताः—उल्बणवाद विषवुळ्ळवो (*prakaṃkatāḥ—ulbaṇavāda viṣavuḷḷavo*) (have virulent poison). अदृष्टाः— (*adṛṣṭāḥ—*) (unseen; the entry is divided across the page boundary)

### Printed p. 349

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व. १५] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 349 (*[a. 2. a 5. va. 15] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 349*).*

गोचरवागद (*gocaravāgada*) (not visible). किंचन—सूक्ष्मवाद विषजंतुगळू आद ऎलै सर्पादिगळे (*kiṃcana—sūkṣmavāda viṣajaṃtugaḷū āda èlai sarpādigaḷe*) (O serpents and the like, and subtle poisonous creatures). इह—इल्लि (*iha—illi*) (here). वः— निम्म गुंपिगॆ सेरिद याव क्रूरजंतुगळिवॆयो (*vaḥ— nimma guṃpigè serida yāva krūrajaṃtugaḷivèyo*) (whatever cruel creatures belong to your group). सर्वे साकं—अवॆल्लवू जॊतॆयल्लि सेरि कॊंडु (*sarve sākaṃ—avèllavū jòtèyalli seri kòṃḍu*) (all of them joining together). जस्यत—नम्मन्नु बिट्टु होगिरि (*jasyata—nammannu biṭṭu hogiri*) (leave us and go).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads धावार्थ (*dhāvārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The poison-bearers that glide by the shoulder and by the body, the scorpions and the like with tail and hair like a needle, and many other subtle poisonous creatures of virulent poison that are not visible to the eye: of these, may all that come near us and are harmful to us go far away, leaving us.

**Printed English translation**

Those (who move with their) shoulders, those (who move with their) bodies, those who sting with sharp fangs, those who are virulently venomous ; what do you here, you unseen, depart together far from us.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषयुक्त: (*viśeṣayukta:*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 7)**

अंस्याः—अंसार्हा, अंसगा, अंसे भवा, अंसाभ्यां खादंतो वा (*aṃsyāḥ—aṃsārhā, aṃsagā, aṃse bhavā, aṃsābhyāṃ khādaṃto vā*): that is, serpents chiefly having shoulders, snakes that make their movements and the like mainly with the shoulders; for this very reason serpents have the names भुजंग (*bhujaṃga*) and भुजग (*bhujaga*); those born from the shoulder, those that bite with the shoulder; thus the nature of four kinds of snakes is explained. Here "those that bite with the shoulder" means that the poison spreads by mere touch; they are to be understood as snakes of that kind. That snakes move by the shoulders is a poetic fancy (*utprekṣā*). That snakes have no legs is known to everyone. Yet, since the structure of their backbone is formed so as to suit moving, they can move very fast. Therefore it is customary to say that snakes move by the shoulder.

अंग्याः—अंगगाः अंगेन शरीरेण हंतारो वा (*aṃgyāḥ—aṃgagāḥ aṃgena śarīreṇa haṃtāro vā*): two kinds of meaning are given: moving by the limb, or killing by the limb. Moving by the limb means moving in a crooked way, as said before; killing by the limb means that, like the snakes belonging to the kind called कॊळकुमंडल (*kòḷakumaṃḍala*) (as printed), they make the poison spread and kill by mere touch; the purport is snakes of that kind.

सूचिका:—सूचीसदृशपुच्छरोमाणो वृश्चिकाद्याः (*sūcikā:—sūcīsadṛśapuccharomāṇo vṛścikādyāḥ*) (printed सूचिका: (*sūcikā:*) against the Saṃhitā सूचीकाः (*sūcīkāḥ*)): the meaning is poisonous creatures such as scorpions that have at the tail hooks sharp like the point of a needle (the supplied text ends here, at the end of the window).

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत्पु॒रस्ता॒त्सूर्य॑ एति वि॒श्वदृ॑ष्टो अदृष्ट॒हा ।
> अ॒दृष्टा॒न्सर्वा॑ ज्॒ञंभय॒न्सर्वा॑श्च [?] यातुधा॒न्यः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत् । पुरस्तात् । सूर्यः । एति । विश्वदृष्टः । अदृष्टहा ।
> आदृष्टान् [?] । सर्वान् । जंभयन् । सर्वाः । च । यात्रुधान्यः [?] ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> असौ सूर्यः पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिश्युदेति । कीदृशः सः । विश्वदृष्टः । विश्वे
> द्रष्टव्या यस्य स तादृशः । अदृष्टहा । अदृष्टा विषविशेषा विषधरविशेषा वा । तेषां
> हंता । यद्वा । अदृष्टमदर्शनमज्ञानमंधकारः । तस्य हंता । सूर्य उदिते सति
> सर्वॆ विषधरा विषाणि वा पलायंते । किं कुर्वन्नुदेतीति चेत् उच्यते । सर्वान-
> दृष्टानद्रष्टव्यान्विषराक्षसादीञ्जंभयन् हिंसयन् । तथा सर्वा यातुधान्यः ।

> *asau sūryaḥ purastātpūrvasyāṃ diśyudeti | kīdṛśaḥ saḥ | viśvadṛṣṭaḥ | viśve*
> *draṣṭavyā yasya sa tādṛśaḥ | adṛṣṭahā | adṛṣṭā viṣaviśeṣā viṣadharaviśeṣā vā | teṣāṃ*
> *haṃtā | yadvā | adṛṣṭamadarśanamajñānamaṃdhakāraḥ | tasya haṃtā | sūrya udite sati*
> *sarvè viṣadharā viṣāṇi vā palāyaṃte | kiṃ kurvannudetīti cet ucyate | sarvāna-*
> *dṛṣṭānadraṣṭavyānviṣarākṣasādīñjaṃbhayan hiṃsayan | tathā sarvā yātudhānyaḥ |*

### Printed p. 351

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १५.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 351 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 15.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 351*).*

*(The bhāṣya block of Ṛk 8 is divided by the page boundary; its remainder follows.)*

> यातवो यातनास्तीव्रवेदनाः । तासां धात्रीरुत्पादयित्रिर्महोरगीराक्षसीर्वा
> जंभयन् पुरस्तादुदेति । अतोऽस्मत्तो नि जस्यतेति संबंधः ॥

*Gist:* The sun rises in the east, seeing all, destroyer of the unseen poisonous creatures and the tormenting demonesses, driving away all.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

विश्वदृष्टः—सकल लोकवन्नू नोडतक्कवनू (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ—sakala lokavannū noḍatakkavanū*) (the one who sees the whole world). अदृष्टहा—कण्णिगॆ काणदिरुव विषध- रादिगळन्नु नाशमाडुववनू अथवा अंधकारवन्नु नाशमाडुववनू आद (*adṛṣṭahā—kaṇṇigè kāṇadiruva viṣadha- rādigaḷannu nāśamāḍuvavanū athavā aṃdhakāravannu nāśamāḍuvavanū āda*) (the destroyer of the unseen poison-bearers and the like, or the destroyer of darkness). सूर‍्यः—सूर‍्यनु (*sūryaḥ—sūryanu*) (the sun). सर्वान् अदृष्टान्—कण्णिगॆ काणद सकलवाद विषजंतुगळन्नू (*sarvān adṛṣṭān—kaṇṇigè kāṇada sakalavāda viṣajaṃtugaḷannū*) (all the unseen poisonous creatures). मत्तु सर्वाश्च यातुधान्यः— अवुगळ उत्पत्तिगॆ कारणवाद सकलवाद स्त्रीजंतुगळन्नू (अथवा असुरस्त्रीयरन्नू) (*mattu sarvāśca yātudhānyaḥ— avugaḷa utpattigè kāraṇavāda sakalavāda strījaṃtugaḷannū (athavā asurastrīyarannū)*) (and all the *yātudhānīs*, the female creatures that are the cause of their birth, or demon-women). जंभयन्— हिंसिसि नाशपडिसुत्ता (*jaṃbhayan— hiṃsisi nāśapaḍisuttā*) (destroying by harming). पुरस्तात्—पूर्वदिक्किनल्लि (*purastāt—pūrvadikkinalli*) (in the east). उदेति—उदयिसुत्तानॆ (*udeti—udayisuttānè*) (rises).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The sun, who sees the whole world and destroys the unseen poison-bearers and the like, rises in the east, destroying by harming all the unseen poisonous creatures and all the female creatures that are the cause of their birth.

**Printed English translation**

The all-seeing sun rises in the east, the destroyer of the unseen, driving away all the unseen (venomous creatures), and all evil spirits.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 8)**

In this ṛk the sage, telling that at the end of the night the darkness is removed and the sun rises, and that thereby the fear that may arise from poisonous creatures is removed, has expressed his joy.

विश्वदृष्टः (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ*): the sun who is seen by all. When the sun rises, everyone sees him. The sun is wanted by everyone; he gives joy to everyone. Since at night the harm from wicked beasts and poisonous creatures is especially great, all creatures and people welcome with great joy the sun rising after such a night has passed and dawn has come. Therefore the purport is that the word *viśvadṛṣṭaḥ* means the sun whom all look at with joy.

अदृष्टहा—अदृष्टा विषविशेषा विषधरविशेषा ना । तेषां हंता । यद्वा । अदृष्टमदर्शनमज्ञानमंधकारः । तस्य हंता । सूर्य उदिते सति सर्वे विषधरा विषाणि वा पलायंते (*adṛṣṭahā—adṛṣṭā viṣaviśeṣā viṣadharaviśeṣā nā | teṣāṃ haṃtā | yadvā | adṛṣṭamadarśanamajñānamaṃdhakāraḥ | tasya haṃtā | sūrya udite sati sarve viṣadharā viṣāṇi vā palāyaṃte*) (the printed विषधरविशेषा ना (*viṣadharaviśeṣā nā*) against the bhāṣya's *vā*): here *adṛṣṭa* means unseen poison, or snakes with poison that hide so as not to be seen. Because he kills these, the sun is praised with the epithet *adṛṣṭahā*. Or *adṛṣṭa* means what is not seen, ignorance, darkness and the like.

### Printed p. 352

*Running head (as supplied): [352 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. १. अ. २४. सू. १९१] (*[352 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 1. a. 24. sū. 191]*).*

Because he destroys these, the sun is also named *adṛṣṭahā*. For as soon as the sun rises, the poisonous serpents and the like run away; they have no special movement in the daytime when there is the light of the sun. Besides, modern scientists agree that the sun's rays (sunshine) have the power to remove poison. Therefore,

अदृष्टान् सर्वान् जंभयन् (*adṛṣṭān sarvān jaṃbhayan*): it is described that the sun rises harming (driving away) with his light all the wicked creatures that hide so as not to be seen.

यातुधान्यः— यातवो यातनास्तीव्रवेदनाः तासां धात्रीरुत्पादयित्रिर्म- होरगी राक्षसीर्वा (*yātudhānyaḥ— yātavo yātanāstīvravedanāḥ tāsāṃ dhātrīrutpādayitrirma- horagī rākṣasīrvā*): *yātu* means very intense pain, torment. Sāyaṇa's explanation is that they are the great serpents full of great poison, or the female rākṣasas, that cause such pain.

*Yātudhānas* are a separate class within the rākṣasa group. Since they cause people many kinds of harm, there are many mantras in the Ṛgveda that pray to Agni (the rākṣasa-destroying Agni, or Agni) to avert their harm. In the ८७नॆय (*87nèya*) sūkta of the १०नॆय (*10nèya*) maṇḍala and in the ११८नॆय (*118nèya*) sūkta, Agni is prayed to protect from their harm. These *yātudhānas* eat the flesh of men and of horses and drink cow's milk (ऋ. सं. १०-८७-१६, १७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-87-16, 17*)). To satisfy their craving for blood and flesh these rākṣasas attack men. This attack is generally by entering into them. Prayer has been made to Agni to prevent them from entering the sacrificers (८-४८-२० (*8-48-20*)). These ghosts and spirits generally enter through our mouth when we eat or drink (अ. वे. ५-२९-६ रिंद ८ (*a. ve. 5-29-6 riṃda 8*)). They also enter by other doors (अ. वॆ. ८-६-३ (*a. vè. 8-6-3*)). As soon as they enter, they tear off and eat a man's flesh and cause disease (अ. वॆ. ५-२९-५, १० (*a. vè. 5-29-5, 10*)), cause madness and destroy eloquence (अ. वे. ६-१११-३, हि. गृ. सू १-१५-५ (*a. ve. 6-111-3, hi. gṛ. sū 1-15-5*)). They invade the dwelling houses of men (कौ. सू. १३५-९ (*kau. sū. 135-9*)). Their time of moving is night or evening (ऋ. सं ७-१०४-८ (*ṛ. saṃ 7-104-8*)). In the eastern direction their play does not go on; the sun rising there drives them away (तै सं. २-६-६-३ (*tai saṃ. 2-6-6-3*)). Many such descriptions of the *yātudhānas* are found here and there in the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas.

*[As supplied, the label line of the grammar page reads व्याकरणपक्रिया (*vyākaraṇapakriyā*); standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 8, noted briefly; the supplied text ends within it)

पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*) (the word *pūrva*; by the rule दिक्‌शब्देभ्यः (*dikśabdebhyaḥ*) (पा. सू. ५-३-२७ (*pā. sū. 5-3-27*)); the form is of the plural ending; the verbal *nighāta* accent); अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*) (root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*); by the rule बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) (पा सू. ३-२-८८ (*pā sū. 3-2-88*)) the suffix *kvip* when *adṛṣṭa* is the upapada; in this all of it is elided).
