*Gist:* Agni, lord and protector of men, is born from sacrificial days, kindled everywhere, from waters, stones, trees and herbs, and is the pure sun.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

नृणां नृपते—मानवरिगॆ प्रभुवू पालकनू आद (*nṛṇāṃ nṛpate—mānavarigè prabhuvū pālakanū āda*) (of men, lord and protector). अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं नीनु (*tvaṃ nīnu*) (you). द्युभिः—यागदिनगळल्लि यागद निमित्तवागि (*dyubhiḥ—yāgadinagaḷalli yāgada nimittavāgi*) (on the sacrificial days, for the sake of the sacrifice). जायसे—उत्पन्ननागुत्तीयॆ (*jāyase—utpannanāguttīyè*) (you are born). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). आशुशुक्षणि:—सर्वत्र दीप्यमाननागियू शत्रुगळन्नु दहिसुववनागियू इद्दीयॆ (*āśuśukṣaṇi:—sarvatra dīpyamānanāgiyū śatrugaḷannu dahisuvavanāgiyū iddīyè*) (you are shining everywhere and a burner of enemies). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अद्भ्यः—उदकगळिंदलू (*adbhyaḥ—udakagaḷiṃdalū*) (from the waters). अश्मनः परि--पाषाणगळिंदलू उत्पन्ननागुत्तीयॆ (*aśmanaḥ pari--pāṣāṇagaḷiṃdalū utpannanāguttīyè*) (from the stones you are born). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). वनेभ्यः—वृक्षादिगळिंद दावानलरूपनागियू (*vanebhyaḥ—vṛkṣādigaḷiṃda dāvānalarūpanāgiyū*) (from trees and the like, in the form of forest fire). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). ओषधीभ्यः— ओषधिगळिंद वैश्वानररूपदल्लियू उत्पन्ननागुत्तीयॆ (*oṣadhībhyaḥ— oṣadhigaḷiṃda vaiśvānararūpadalliyū utpannanāguttīyè*) (from herbs, in the form of Vaiśvānara). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). शुचिः—पवित्रात्मनू प्रकाशमाननू आदआदित्यरूपनू आगिद्दीयॆ (*śuciḥ—pavitrātmanū prakāśamānanū ādaādityarūpanū āgiddīyè*) (the pure, shining one, of the form of the sun).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, lord and protector of men, you are born on the days of sacrifice, for the sake of the sacrifice. You are shining everywhere and a burner of enemies. You are born from the waters and from the stones. You are born from trees and the like in the form of forest fire, and from herbs in the form of Vaiśvānara. You are pure and shining, of the form of the sun.

### Printed p. 381

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १७.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 381 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 17.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 381*).*

**Printed English translation**

Sovereign of men, Agni, you are born for the days (of sacrifice), pure and all-irradiating, from the waters, from the stones, from trees, and from plants.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

In the first ṛk of this first sūkta, seen by the sage Gṛtsamada, the various modes of the origin of Agni are described. We shall explain those modes of origin minutely.

त्वं अग्ने नृणां नृपते (*tvaṃ agne nṛṇāṃ nṛpate*): by these words the sage addresses Agni. We have described at length the etymology and the various meanings of the word *agni* in ऋ. सं. भाग १ पेजु 612-614 (*ṛ. saṃ. bhāga 1 peju 612-614*). Here we shall explain only what the bhāṣyakāra has said, अग्रणीत्वादिगुणविशिष्ट (*agraṇītvādiguṇaviśiṣṭa*). Yāska says in his Nirukta:

अग्निः कस्मादग्रणीर्भवत्यग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयतेङ्गं नयति । (*agniḥ kasmādagraṇīrbhavatyagraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyateṅgaṃ nayati |*)
(सि. ७-१४-) (*(si. 7-14-)*)

(The reference is printed सि. ७-१४- (*si. 7-14-*), as supplied.) In sacrifices and the like Agni has the first place; that is, since the word *agra* denotes the principal, the principal place among the gods befits Agni. In sacrifices, as soon as Agni is produced in the fire-sticks (अरणि (*araṇi*)), they place it in the fire-pit called आहवनीय (*āhavanīya*). From there they carry it to the fire-pit called गार्हपत्य (*gārhapatya*). Therefore Agni has the name अग्रणीः (*agraṇīḥ*). Or *agraṇīḥ* means one who himself leads the army of the gods, or one who is the leader of the army of the gods (नायक or Leader (*nāyaka or Leader*)). This is the first reason for the name of the word *agni*. Besides, in another Brāhmaṇa it is said अग्निर्दॆवानां सेनानीः (*agnirdèvānāṃ senānīḥ*). Following this, the students of the Ṛgveda recite in their Mantra-Brāhmaṇa अग्निर्मुखं प्रथमो देवतानां (*agnirmukhaṃ prathamo devatānāṃ*) (ऐ. ब्रा. १-४ (*ai. brā. 1-4*)). In another part of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it says अग्निर्वैदेवानामवमः (*agnirvaidevānāmavamaḥ*) (ऐ. ब्रा. १-१-१ (*ai. brā. 1-1-1*)). In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa too there is अग्निरग्रे प्रथमो देवतानां (*agniragre prathamo devatānāṃ*) (तै. ब्रा. २-४-३-३ (*tai. brā. 2-4-3-3*)) and अग्निरवमो देवतानां (*agniravamo devatānāṃ*). From these examples it follows that Agni is the first among the gods, the one in the foremost place, the leader, the chief. In the Śukla Yajurveda (वा. सं (*vā. saṃ*)) it is said स वा एषोऽग्रे देवतानामजायत तस्मादग्निर्नामेति (*sa vā eṣo 'gre devatānāmajāyata tasmādagnirnāmeti*), that is, this Agni was born first among all the gods, and therefore he has the name Agni.

नृणां नृपते—मनुष्याणां मध्ये ये नराः यष्टारः संति तेषां विशेषेण पालयितः । यद्वोभाभ्यां पदाभ्यां बहुत्वं नित्यस्वामित्वं च प्रतिपाद्यते । सर्वेषा मपि नराणां नित्यपालकेत्यर्थः (*nṛṇāṃ nṛpate—manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye ye narāḥ yaṣṭāraḥ saṃti teṣāṃ viśeṣeṇa pālayitaḥ | yadvobhābhyāṃ padābhyāṃ bahutvaṃ nityasvāmitvaṃ ca pratipādyate | sarveṣā mapi narāṇāṃ nityapālaketyarthaḥ*): that is, among men, those who perform sacrifices, such sacrificers (the sentence continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 382

*Running head (as supplied): [382 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू.] (*[382 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū.]*).*

...are protected; it means, O Agni who protects them; or, since the two words *nṛṇām nṛpate* both indicate lordship over many people, the main purport is that this Agni is the protector of all people at all times.

त्वमग्ने द्युभिः—यागदिवसैर्निमित्तभूतैर्जायसे । यागार्थं मथनेनो- त्पद्यस इत्यर्थः । यद्वा तादृशैर्दिवसैः सहितो जायसे । तत्तद्यागदिवसेषु प्रसिद्धो भवसीत्यर्थः (*tvamagne dyubhiḥ—yāgadivasairnimittabhūtairjāyase | yāgārthaṃ mathaneno- tpadyasa ityarthaḥ | yadvā tādṛśairdivasaiḥ sahito jāyase | tattadyāgadivaseṣu prasiddho bhavasītyarthaḥ*): O Agni, you are born on the days of the sacrifice; that is, for the sake of the sacrifice (the sacrifice is by Agni itself) you are born by the churning of fire in the fire-sticks; or, on those days of sacrifice, that is, on the days of the sacrifice performed by the sacrificers, you are born together with those days, that is, famous: this too is the meaning.

त्वमाशुशुक्षणि: (*tvamāśuśukṣaṇi:*): the bhāṣyakāra, explaining the meaning of this word, says त्वमाशुशुक्षणिर्जायसे। आ सर्वतो दीप्यमानो भवसि । आज्युपपदे शुच दीप्तानित्येतस्य छांदसमिदं रूपं। यद्वा। आशु शीघ्रं शुच् दीप्तः सन् यतः स सेव्यत इति । आशु शुचं शोकं सनोति ददाति शत्रुभ्यो दाहादिनेत्याशुशुक्षणिः । तादृशो भवति (*tvamāśuśukṣaṇirjāyase| ā sarvato dīpyamāno bhavasi | ājyupapade śuca dīptānityetasya chāṃdasamidaṃ rūpaṃ| yadvā| āśu śīghraṃ śuc dīptaḥ san yataḥ sa sevyata iti | āśu śucaṃ śokaṃ sanoti dadāti śatrubhyo dāhādinetyāśuśukṣaṇiḥ | tādṛśo bhavati*). That is, O Agni, you shine all around. From the root शुच् (*śuc*), which gives the sense "shine", the prefix आ (*ā*) joined, the form *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ* results. Or *āśu* is quickly, *śuc* is shining, *kṣaṇi* is being served; or, by your power of burning, you quickly (*āśu*) give (*sanoti*) grief (*śucam*) to enemies; therefore Agni has the name *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*: thus the meaning of this word is explained. Yāska, to explain the meaning of this word, has taken the very ṛk as the example and has given its etymology:

त्वमग्ने द्युभिरहोभिस्तृमाशुशुक्षणिः । आशु इति च शु इति च क्षिप्रनामनी (*tvamagne dyubhirahobhistṛmāśuśukṣaṇiḥ | āśu iti ca śu iti ca kṣipranāmanī*)
भवतः। क्षणिरुत्तरः क्षणोतेः आशु शुचा क्षणोतीति वा सनोतीति वा ॥ शुक् (*bhavataḥ| kṣaṇiruttaraḥ kṣaṇoteḥ āśu śucā kṣaṇotīti vā sanotīti vā ‖ śuk*)
शोचतेः । पंचम्यर्थे वा प्रथमा । तथा हि वाक्संयोग आ इत्याकार (*śocateḥ | paṃcamyarthe vā prathamā | tathā hi vāksaṃyoga ā ityākāra*)
उपसर्गः पुरस्ताच्चिकीर्षितज उत्तर आशु शोचयिषुरिति । शुचिः शोचते- (*upasargaḥ purastāccikīrṣitaja uttara āśu śocayiṣuriti | śuciḥ śocate-*)
र्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । आयमपीतरः शुचिरेतस्मादेव । निष्पिक्तमस्मात् पापक- (*rjvalatikarmaṇaḥ | āyamapītaraḥ śuciretasmādeva | niṣpiktamasmāt pāpaka-*)
मिति नैरुक्ताः ॥ (*miti nairuktāḥ ‖*)
(नि. ६-१) (*(ni. 6-1)*)

That is: आशु मत्तु शु (*āśu mattu śu*) are *kṣipra* names (names with the meaning "quickly"). The word क्षणः (*kṣaṇaḥ*) is formed from the root क्षणोति (*kṣaṇoti*), which indicates injury; or it may be formed from the root सनेति (*saneti*), meaning "obtain". The syllable शु (*śu*) in the middle is a synonym of the word शुचि (*śuci*), which gives the meaning "shine". Therefore *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ* means that Agni, by his lustre, quickly... (the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, at जाग्रतॆ (*jāgratè*)).

### Printed p. 383

*Running head (as supplied): [अ २ अ. ५. व. १७] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 383 (*[a 2 a. 5. va. 17] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 383*).*

*(Continuation of the Nirukta explanation of *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ* in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1, from mid-sentence at the end of the previous page.)*

...quickly harms (burns) enemies, or quickly provides what the sacrificer needs; this is the meaning.

Or the word *śuk* is formed from the root *śuc*, which gives the sense "shine". Here the nominative case is used in the sense of the ablative. *ā* is the prefix. Therefore, if in आ+शुशुक्षणिः (*ā+śuśukṣaṇiḥ*) the word *śuśukṣaṇi* is taken to indicate the desired meaning (*cikīrṣita*), the word *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ* means one (Agni) who desires to shine all around. Or the word *śuciḥ* may be formed from the root *śocati*, meaning "shine". In this context there is room for the meanings stated above. Besides, the word *śuciḥ* has another meaning: *śuciḥ* means what is sacred, pure, free from sin; this is another meaning. On this view अ+अशुशुक्षणिः==आशुशुक्षणिः (*a+aśuśukṣaṇiḥ==āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) means one free from sin (Agni). (अ denotes negetive. As there are two अ s, two negetives make an affirmative ; Sinless) (*(a denotes negetive. As there are two a s, two negetives make an affirmative ; Sinless)*) (as printed). The Nirukta authors approve this kind of meaning.

द्युभि: अहोभि: (*dyubhi: ahobhi:*): on the days fit for sacrifice, such as the full moon and the new moon, Agni is produced by churning for the sacrifice; therefore, addressing Agni, it is said that you are born on such days.

त्वमद्भ्यः—त्वमद्भ्यो वृष्टुदकेभ्यो जायसे वैद्युतरूपेण वाडव- रू पेण वा समुद्रोदकेभ्यः (*tvamadbhyaḥ—tvamadbhyo vṛṣṭudakebhyo jāyase vaidyutarūpeṇa vāḍava- rū peṇa vā samudrodakebhyaḥ*): "you are born from the waters" means: you are born, when it rains, in the form of lightning arising in the clouds, or in the form of the submarine fire (*bāḍabānala*) seen in the water of the sea; so he is praised.

त्वमश्मनस्परि—अश्मनो मेघात्पाषाणाद्वा (*tvamaśmanaspari—aśmano meghātpāṣāṇādvā*): since the word *aśmā* is read among the thirty names of the cloud (नि. २-२१ (*ni. 2-21*)), you are born in the clouds in the form of lightning. Or, since the word *aśman* also means a stone, it may be said that you are born from the friction of two stones. (Formerly, when matches were not in use, fire was made with flints.) On the matter that Agni is born in the form of lightning from the clouds, the bhāṣyakāra has given as an example the ṛk

यो हत्वाहिमरिणात्सप्त सिंधून्यो गा उदाजदपधा वलस्य । (*yo hatvāhimariṇātsapta siṃdhūnyo gā udājadapadhā valasya |*)
यो अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान संवृक्समत्तु स जनास इंद्रः ॥ (*yo aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna saṃvṛksamattu sa janāsa iṃdraḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. २-१२-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 2-12-3)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. २-१२-३ (*ma. saṃ. 2-12-3*), as supplied.) In explaining the meaning of this ṛk Sāyaṇa says यश्चाश्मनोः अश्नुते व्याप्नोत्यंतरिक्षमिति अश्मा मेघः । अत्यंतमृदुरूपयोर्मे (*yaścāśmanoḥ aśnute vyāpnotyaṃtarikṣamiti aśmā meghaḥ | atyaṃtamṛdurūpayorme*)

### Printed p. 384

*[Unmarked page break in the supplied text: the running head of printed p. 384 stands inside the text, in the middle of the sentence; it reads 384 सायणभाष्पसहिता । मं. २. आ.१ . सू.१. (*384 sāyaṇabhāṣpasahitā | maṃ. 2. ā.1 . sū.1.*), as printed.]*

घयोरंतर्मध्यॆ वैद्युतमग्निं जजान उत्पादयामास (*ghayoraṃtarmadhyè vaidyutamagniṃ jajāna utpādayāmāsa*). That is, the word *aśmā* is formed from the root *aś*, which gives the sense "pervade"; since the cloud pervades the atmosphere, it is called *aśmā*. They have explained the meaning: Indra produced the lightning-fire in the middle of such soft clouds.

त्वं वनेभ्यः—वृक्षादिसमूहेभ्यो दावरूपेण (*tvaṃ vanebhyaḥ—vṛkṣādisamūhebhyo dāvarūpeṇa*): you are born in the forests in the form of forest fire (*kāḍukiccu*). It is well known that in the forest bamboos rub against one another, fire arises from that and burns the whole forest.

त्वमोषधीभ्यः—वैश्वानररूपेण । मथनेनोत्पन्नःसन् सर्वात्मको भवसी- त्यर्थः (*tvamoṣadhībhyaḥ—vaiśvānararūpeṇa | mathanenotpannaḥsan sarvātmako bhavasī- tyarthaḥ*): Agni is in all creatures in the form of the digestive fire (*jāṭharāgni*) and in herbs and trees in the form of the Vaiśvānara fire. When Agni is produced in a sacrifice, two pieces of wood of the aśvattha tree or the śamī tree are placed one on the other and churned strongly; from that Agni is born. In this matter:

शविागर्भादग्निं मंथति । एषा वा अग्नेय्र्यज्जिया तनूः । तामेवास्मै (*śaviāgarbhādagniṃ maṃthati | eṣā vā agneyryajjiyā tanūḥ | tāmevāsmai*)
जनयति ॥ (*janayati ‖*)
(तै. ब्रा. १-१-९-१) (*(tai. brā. 1-1-9-1)*)

There is this Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa sentence. The procedure of producing Agni by churning, with mantras and with rites, in sacrifices and the like is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (ऐ. ब्रा ३-५ (*ai. brā 3-5*)) as follows. Since the matter of the churning of Agni is stated in this ṛk, it is proper to explain that order here. In a sacrifice, after the rite called *somavikrayaṇa* (the purchase of the soma plant, brought from mountains and forests, from those who brought it) is completed, the work of churning Agni begins. Then the priest called the Adhvaryu addresses the priest called the Hotṛ in this way:

अग्नये मध्यमानायानुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युरभि त्वा देव सवितरिति सावित्रि- (*agnaye madhyamānāyānubrūhītyāhādhvaryurabhi tvā deva savitariti sāvitri-*)
मन्वाह तदाहुर्यदग्नये मध्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्मात्सावित्री- (*manvāha tadāhuryadagnaye madhyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmātsāvitrī-*)
मन्वाहेति । सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं तन्न थति (*manvāheti | savitā vai prasavānāmīśe savitṛprasūta evainaṃ tanna thati*)
तस्मात्सावित्री मन्वाह । (*tasmātsāvitrī manvāha |*)

The Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, says the *praiṣa* mantra अग्नये मध्यमानायनुब्रू ३ हि (*agnaye madhyamānāyanubrū 3 hi*) (a *praiṣa* mantra is a recitation of mantras by which, when various rites are performed in a sacrifice, the Adhvaryu and others enjoin, in the form of a command, the persons concerned to perform such and such a rite (or homa)); hearing it, the Hotṛ

### Printed p. 385

*[Unmarked page break in the supplied text: the running head of printed p. 385 stands inside the text, in the middle of the sentence; it reads आ. २. अ. ५ व. १७ ] सुग्वेदसंहिता 385 (*ā. 2. a. 5 va. 17 ] sugvedasaṃhitā 385*), as printed, with ಸುಗ್ವೇದ [sic].]*

recites the verse

अभि त्वा देव सवितरिशानं वार्याणां । सदावन् भागमीमहे ॥ (*abhi tvā deva savitariśānaṃ vāryāṇāṃ | sadāvan bhāgamīmahe ‖*)
(म. सं. १-२४-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-24-3)*)

addressed to the deity Savitṛ (the Sāvitrī ṛk). Here a doubt arises. Although the Adhvaryu has directed the Hotṛ to say the mantra necessary for the churning of Agni, why does the Hotṛ, without doing so, recite a ṛk addressed to the deity Savitṛ? Is this not wrong? It is not so. As in the sentence सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे (*savitā vai prasavānāmīśe*), since Savitṛ is the lord (master) of every production in all rites such as sacrifices, it is natural here to ask the permission of the deity Savitṛ for beginning the work of producing Agni, the churning of Agni. For that reason the Hotṛ first recites the ṛk addressed to the deity Savitṛ.

मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह । तदाहुर्यदग्नये (*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha | tadāhuryadagnaye*)
मध्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्माद्ध्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाहेति द्यावा- (*madhyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmāddhyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāheti dyāvā-*)
पृथिवीभ्यां वा एतं जातं देवाः पर्यगृण्णंस्ताभ्यामेवाद्यापि परिगृहीत- (*pṛthivībhyāṃ vā etaṃ jātaṃ devāḥ paryagṛṇṇaṃstābhyāmevādyāpi parigṛhīta-*)
स्तस्माद्ध्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह ॥ (*stasmāddhyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha ‖*)

Afterwards the Hotṛ, continuing,

मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां । (*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na imaṃ yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ |*)
पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः ॥ (*pipṛtāṃ no bharīmabhiḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२२-१३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-22-13)*)

recites this ṛk addressed to Heaven and Earth. Some raise the objection: when told to say a ṛk about Agni for the churning of Agni, why does this Hotṛ recite a ṛk about Heaven and Earth? The answer is that formerly, when Agni was born, the gods held him between Heaven and Earth (earth and the heavens); therefore the same must be done now. Since the fire called Pāvaka is held by the earth and the fire in the form of the sun is held by heaven, it is proper to recite a ṛk addressed to Heaven and Earth for the holding of Agni.

त्वामग्ने पुष्करादधीति तृचमाग्नेयं गायत्रमन्वाहाग्नौ मध्यमाने स्वयै- (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhīti tṛcamāgneyaṃ gāyatramanvāhāgnau madhyamāne svayai-*)
वैनं तद्भवतया स्वेन छंदसा समर्थयति । अथर्वा निरमंथतेति रूप- (*vainaṃ tadbhavatayā svena chaṃdasā samarthayati | atharvā niramaṃthateti rūpa-*)
समृद्धमेतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाण- (*samṛddhametadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇa-*)
मृगभिवदति. ॥ (*mṛgabhivadati. ‖*)

*[As supplied, a footnote line stands here: बळिक होतृवु अग्निमथनक्कागि अग्नि देवताकवाद— (*baḷika hotṛvu agnimathanakkāgi agni devatākavāda—*) ("Afterwards, for the churning of Agni, the Hotṛ [recites] the ... addressed to Agni"), followed by a stray line [25] Vol. 14 (*[25] Vol. 14*); both are kept as italic notes in the Kannada text.]*

### Printed p. 386

*Running head (as supplied): [386 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २ अ. १ सू. १] (*[386 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2 a. 1 sū. 1]*).*

त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमंथत । मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः । (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhyatharvā niramaṃthata | mūrdhno viśvasya vāghataḥ |*)
तमु त्वा दध्यज् ऋषिः पुत्रः ईधे अथर्वणः । वृत्रहणं पुरंदरं ॥ (*tamu tvā dadhyaj ṛṣiḥ putraḥ īdhe atharvaṇaḥ | vṛtrahaṇaṃ puraṃdaraṃ ‖*)
त मु त्वा पाथ्यो वृषा समीधे दस्युहंतमं । धनंजयं रणेरणे (*ta mu tvā pāthyo vṛṣā samīdhe dasyuhaṃtamaṃ | dhanaṃjayaṃ raṇeraṇe*)
(म. सं ६-१६-१३, १४, १५) (*(ma. saṃ 6-16-13, 14, 15)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं ६-१६-१३, १४, १५ (*ma. saṃ 6-16-13, 14, 15*), as supplied.) He recites these three ṛks. These three ṛks praise the deity Agni, and they are ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre, dear to Agni. For both Agni and the Gāyatrī metre were produced by Prajāpati, and therefore the Gāyatrī metre is said to be his own metre. Now, it is said in the second pāda of the first ṛk अथर्वा निरमंथत (*atharvā niramaṃthata*) that the sage Atharvan churned Agni and produced him. This sage Atharvan, before all others, churned Agni in the fire-sticks and produced him. Therefore there is the prayer that Agni, born as the son of the sage Atharvan, may grow and prosper abundantly in the sacrifice. For this reason it is natural that these ṛks were recited, which give the meaning that Agni, taking form from the fire-sticks and being born (that is, in the complete form of fire), may grow in the sacrificial rite (blaze up greatly) and shine.

स यदि न जायेत यदि चिरं जायेत राक्षोघ्नो गायत्रोऽनूच्याः (*sa yadi na jāyeta yadi ciraṃ jāyeta rākṣoghno gāyatro 'nūcyāḥ*)
अग्ने हंसिन्यत्रिणमित्येताः रक्षसामपहत्यॆ रक्षांसि वा एनं तर्हालभंते (*agne haṃsinyatriṇamityetāḥ rakṣasāmapahatyè rakṣāṃsi vā enaṃ tarhālabhaṃte*)
यर्हि न जायते यर्हि चिरं जायते ॥ (*yarhi na jāyate yarhi ciraṃ jāyate ‖*)

Reciting the five ṛks mentioned before, the churning of Agni must be done in the fire-sticks. If, even though this is done, Agni is not produced, or is produced slowly after a long time, with smoke and the like coming, then the following *rākṣoghna* sūkta of the Gāyatrī metre must be recited:

अग्ने हंसि न्य १ त्रिणं दीद्यन्मर्तेष्णा । स्वे क्षये शुचिव्रत ॥ (*agne haṃsi nya 1 triṇaṃ dīdyanmarteṣṇā | sve kṣaye śucivrata ‖*)
उत्तिष्ठसि स्वाहुतो धृतानि प्रतिमोदसे । यत्वा स्ट्रुचः समस्थिरन् ॥ (*uttiṣṭhasi svāhuto dhṛtāni pratimodase | yatvā sṭrucaḥ samasthiran ‖*)
स आहुतो वि रोचतेऽग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा । स्ट्रुचा प्रतीकमज्यते ॥ (*sa āhuto vi rocate 'gnirīḷenyo girā | sṭrucā pratīkamajyate ‖*)
धृतेनाग्निः समज्यते मधुप्रतीक आहुतः ! रोचमानो विभावसुः । (*dhṛtenāgniḥ samajyate madhupratīka āhutaḥ ! rocamāno vibhāvasuḥ |*)
जरमाणः समिध्यसे देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन । तं त्वा हवंत मर्त्याः ॥ (*jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase devebhyo havyavāhana | taṃ tvā havaṃta martyāḥ ‖*)
तं मर्ता अमर्त्यं धृतेनाग्निं सपर्यत । अदाभ्यं गृहपतिं ॥ (*taṃ martā amartyaṃ dhṛtenāgniṃ saparyata | adābhyaṃ gṛhapatiṃ ‖*)
अदाभ्येन शोचिषाग्ने रक्षस्त्वं दह । गोपा ऋतस्य दीदिहि ॥ (*adābhyena śociṣāgne rakṣastvaṃ daha | gopā ṛtasya dīdihi ‖*)
स त्वमग्ने प्रतीकेन प्रत्योष यातुधान्यः । उरुक्षयेषु दीद्यत् ॥ (*sa tvamagne pratīkena pratyoṣa yātudhānyaḥ | urukṣayeṣu dīdyat ‖*)
तं त्वा गीर्भिरुरुक्षया हव्यवाहं समाधिरे । यजिष्ठं मानुषे जने ॥ (*taṃ tvā gīrbhirurukṣayā havyavāhaṃ samādhire | yajiṣṭhaṃ mānuṣe jane ‖*)
(मि. सं. १०-१८-१ रिंद ९) (*(mi. saṃ. 10-18-1 riṃda 9)*)

(The reference is printed मि. सं. १०-१८-१ रिंद ९ (*mi. saṃ. 10-18-1 riṃda 9*), as supplied.)

### Printed p. 387

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १७ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 387 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 17 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 387*).*

There are nine ṛks in this sūkta. They drive away the rākṣasas and kill them. Therefore, by reciting these ṛks the rākṣasas are destroyed. Why, at the time of churning Agni, Agni is not produced or is produced late: because these rākṣasas obstruct Agni and keep him in their power without releasing him. Therefore the killing of the rākṣasas is necessary in order to set Agni free. For that reason it is said that this *rakṣohanana* sūkta of nine ṛks must be recited.

स यद्येकस्यामेवानूक्तायां जायेत यदि द्वयोरथोत ब्रुवंतु जंतव (*sa yadyekasyāmevānūktāyāṃ jāyeta yadi dvayorathota bruvaṃtu jaṃtava*)
इति जाताय जातवतीमभिरूपामनुब्रूयात् ॥ (*iti jātāya jātavatīmabhirūpāmanubrūyāt ‖*)

While reciting the *rākṣoghna* sūkta, if Agni is born after one ṛk has been recited in the middle, or after two, three and so on, at that very moment

उत ब्रुवंतु जंतव उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि । धनंजयो रणेरणे ॥ (*uta bruvaṃtu jaṃtava udagnirvṛtrahājani | dhanaṃjayo raṇeraṇe ‖*)
(म. सं. १-७४-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-74-3)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. १-७४-३ (*ma. saṃ. 1-74-3*), as supplied.) this ṛk must be recited at once, because the matter propounded in this ṛk is favourable to the birth of Agni. For the very purpose of stating this favourableness the word जातवतीं (*jātavatīṃ*) is used. Afterwards, in the second pāda उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि (*udagnirvṛtrahājani*), the word अजनि (*ajani*), "was born", indicating birth, is read. Therefore it is said that as soon as Agni is born this ṛk, which is appropriate, must be recited at that very moment.

यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं आ यं हस्तेन खादिनमिति हस्ताभ्यां ह्येनं (*yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ ā yaṃ hastena khādinamiti hastābhyāṃ hyenaṃ*)
मंथंति शिशुं जातमिति शिशुरिव वा एष प्रथमजातो यदग्निः न बिभ्रति विशा (*maṃthaṃti śiśuṃ jātamiti śiśuriva vā eṣa prathamajāto yadagniḥ na bibhrati viśā*)
मग्निं स्वध्वरमिति यद्वै देवानां नेति तदेषामो ३ मिति प्र देवं देव- (*magniṃ svadhvaramiti yadvai devānāṃ neti tadeṣāmo 3 miti pra devaṃ deva-*)
वीतये भरता वसुवित्तममिति प्रह्रियमाणायाभिरूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूप- (*vītaye bharatā vasuvittamamiti prahriyamāṇāyābhirūpā yadyajñe 'bhirūpa-*)
तत्समृद्धं आ स्वै योन्‌नौ निषीदत्त्विति एष ह ना अस्य स्वो योनिर्य- (*tatsamṛddhaṃ ā svai yonnau niṣīdattviti eṣa ha nā asya svo yonirya-*)
दग्निरग्नेः ॥ (*dagniragneḥ ‖*)

Up to here the six ṛks used for the churning of Agni (the six ṛks अभित्वा (*abhitvā*), महीद्यौः (*mahīdyauḥ*), त्वामग्ने (*tvāmagne*), तमुत्वा (*tamutvā*) and उत ब्रुवंतु (*uta bruvaṃtu*)) have been stated (as printed); and now

आ यं हस्ते न खादिनं शिशुं जातं न बिभ्रति । विशामग्निं स्वध्वरं ॥ (*ā yaṃ haste na khādinaṃ śiśuṃ jātaṃ na bibhrati | viśāmagniṃ svadhvaraṃ ‖*)
(मि. सं. ६-१६-४०) (*(mi. saṃ. 6-16-40)*)

(The reference is printed मि. सं. ६-१६-४० (*mi. saṃ. 6-16-40*), as supplied.) the Hotṛ recites this as the seventh ṛk. The meaning of this ṛk is as follows. Newly (the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 388

*Running head (as supplied): [388 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ. १. सू १] (*[388 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū 1]*).*

*(Continuation of the Brāhmaṇa rules for churning Agni in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1, from mid-sentence at the end of the previous page.)*

...As a newborn child is lifted in the hands, the priests lift in their hands the Agni born in the fire-stick. The main purport is that this Agni in the form of a child plays the chief part in the sacrifice made by the people and consumes the oblations and the like. The use of the word for "hand" in the first pāda means: the priests churn this Agni with their hands; therefore it is said that they lift him in their hands. In the second pāda the example of a newborn child is given for the Agni that has just been born. The word न (*na*) used here indicates the sense of assent, like ओं (*oṃ*). In ordinary language the word न (*na*) indicates only the sense of prohibition; but in the Vedas this word indicates the sense of prohibition, of comparison and of assent; here the sense of assent is meant. And the word देवानां (*devānāṃ*) may be understood as mantras that propound the deities, or, by the transposition of letters, as वेदानां (*vedānāṃ*), "of the Vedas". Now the eighth ṛk of the churning of Agni, that is,

प्र देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तमं । आ स्वे योन् नि षीदतु ॥ (*pra devaṃ devavītaye bharatā vasuvittamaṃ | ā sve yon ni ṣīdatu ‖*)
(म. सं. ६-१६-४१) (*(ma. saṃ. 6-16-41)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. ६-१६-४१ (*ma. saṃ. 6-16-41*), as supplied.) the Hotṛ recites. "O priests, now place the Agni who has been born in his own place, the fire-pit called Āhavanīya; may he sit there in the place that is Agni's own": this ṛk with that meaning is suited to the rite of placing Agni in the Āhavanīya pit. Here, in accordance with the *praiṣa* mantra recited in every rite, the Hotṛ recites the mantra suited to that rite and of the right meaning. How: as soon as Agni is born, the Adhvaryu says to the Hotṛ the *praiṣa* mantra जातायानुब्रू ३ हि (*jātāyānubrū 3 hi*); in reply the Hotṛ recites the suited ṛk उत ब्रुवंतु जंतवः (*uta bruvaṃtu jaṃtavaḥ*). In the same way, when the Agni that has been born is placed in the pit called Āhavanīya, as soon as the Adhvaryu says the *praiṣa* mantra प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रू३ हि (*prahriyamāṇāyānubrū3 hi*), the Hotṛ recites the ṛk प्र देवं देवनीतये (*pra devaṃ devanītaye*) (as printed), which is right for that occasion. It is to be understood that it goes thus in every rite. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda, on this matter:

आग्नये मध्यमानायानुब्रूहीत्याह सावित्रीमृचमन्वाह सॆवितृप्रसूत (*āgnaye madhyamānāyānubrūhītyāha sāvitrīmṛcamanvāha sèvitṛprasūta*)
एवैनं मंथति जातायानुब्रूहि प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रूहीत्याह (*evainaṃ maṃthati jātāyānubrūhi prahriyamāṇāyānubrūhītyāha*)
कांडेकांड एवैनं क्रियामणे समर्थयति गायत्रिः सर्वा अन्वाह ॥ (*kāṃḍekāṃḍa evainaṃ kriyāmaṇe samarthayati gāyatriḥ sarvā anvāha ‖*)
(तै. सं. ६-३-५-२, ३) (*(tai. saṃ. 6-3-5-2, 3)*)

and so on. This very matter is explained here by the sentence यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं (*yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ*); that is, the main purport is that in each rite the sacrifice should be performed by reciting the mantras appropriate to that rite. At the end, as soon as आ स्वे योन् निषीदतु (*ā sve yon niṣīdatu*) is said,

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १७ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 389 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 17 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 389*).*

they establish Agni in the Āhavanīya pit. For the Āhavanīya place is said to be the place of the churned Agni (the Agni that has just been born).

आजातं जातवेदसीति जात इतरो जातवेदा इतरः प्रियं शिशीतातिथिमित्येष (*ājātaṃ jātavedasīti jāta itaro jātavedā itaraḥ priyaṃ śiśītātithimityeṣa*)
ह वा अस्य प्रियोऽतिथियदग्निरग्नेः स्योन आ गृहपतिमिति शांत्यामेवैनं (*ha vā asya priyo 'tithiyadagniragneḥ syona ā gṛhapatimiti śāṃtyāmevainaṃ*)
तद्दधाति । अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा । हव्यवाड्डुह्वास्य इत्यभि- (*taddadhāti | agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā | havyavāḍḍuhvāsya ityabhi-*)
रूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं । त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण (*rūpā yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ | tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa*)
सन्स्कृतेति विप्र इतरो विप्र इतरः सन्नितरः सन्नितरः सखा सख्या समिध्यस (*sanskṛteti vipra itaro vipra itaraḥ sannitaraḥ sannitaraḥ sakhā sakhyā samidhyasa*)
इत्येष ह वा अस्य स्वः सखा यदग्निरग्नेः ॥ (*ityeṣa ha vā asya svaḥ sakhā yadagniragneḥ ‖*)

Now the Hotṛ recites the ninth ṛk,

आ जातं जातवेदसि प्रियं शिशीतातिथिं । स्कोन आ गृहपतिं ॥ (*ā jātaṃ jātavedasi priyaṃ śiśītātithiṃ | skona ā gṛhapatiṃ ‖*)
(म. सं. ६-१६-४२) (*(ma. saṃ. 6-16-42)*)

(The reference is printed म. सं. ६-१६-४२ (*ma. saṃ. 6-16-42*), as supplied.) The main purport of this ṛk is as follows: in this ṛk two kinds of Agni are indicated. जातं (*jātaṃ*) means the Agni that has just been produced by churning; this is the first, and it is indicated by the word जातं (*jātaṃ*) because it has just been born. The second is the one already established in the Āhavanīya fire-pit; this is called जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Because he knows the nature of the Agni born by churning, the Āhavanīya fire is explained as जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Here, to the Agni called जातवेदस (*jātavedasa*) that was established beforehand in the place of the Āhavanīya fire, the newly churned Agni is like a beloved guest. Therefore the main purport is that this churned Agni, beloved and of the nature of a guest, is established in the Āhavanīya fire-pit for the attainment of a comfortable dwelling. Afterwards the Hotṛ

अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतियुर्वा । हव्यवाड्जु ह्वास्यः ॥ (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiyurvā | havyavāḍju hvāsyaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ सं १-१२-६) (*(ṛ saṃ 1-12-6)*)

recites the tenth ṛk (the reference is printed ऋ सं १-१२-६ (*ṛ saṃ 1-12-6*), as supplied). Its meaning: the newly churned Agni joins the Agni established beforehand in the Āhavanīya pit and blazes well, shining. This churned Agni is the seer who knows all, the protector of the house or of the sacrificer, ever young, the carrier of oblations and the like to the gods, one who keeps the ladle called *juhū*, an instrument of the homa, in his mouth (that is, since ghee and the like are offered in the flame of Agni with the ladle called *juhū*, Agni is called जुह्वास्यः (*juhvāsyaḥ*)). In this way a mantra suited to the occasion is recited here. After this the Hotṛ

त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सता । सखा सख्या समिध्यसे ॥ (*tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsatā | sakhā sakhyā samidhyase ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ८-४३-१४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 8-43-14)*)

recites this ṛk (the reference is printed ऋ. सं. ८-४३-१४ (*ṛ. saṃ. 8-43-14*), as supplied). The purport: O new Agni, you who are wise, joining the wise Āhavanīya fire, be happy as a friend joins a friend and is happy.

तं मर्जयंत सुक्रतुं पुरोयावानमाजिषु । स्वेषु क्षयेषु वाजिनमिति (*taṃ marjayaṃta sukratuṃ puroyāvānamājiṣu | sveṣu kṣayeṣu vājinamiti*)
एष ह ना अस्य स्वः क्षयो यदग्निरग्नेः । यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवा (*eṣa ha nā asya svaḥ kṣayo yadagniragneḥ | yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devā*)
इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । यज्ञेन वै तद्देवा यज्ञमयजंत यदग्निनाग्नि- (*ityuttamayā paridadhāti | yajñena vai taddevā yajñamayajaṃta yadagnināgni-*)
मयजंत ते स्वर्ग० लोकमायन् तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह (*mayajaṃta te svarga0 lokamāyan tāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha*)
नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवा इति छंदासि वै (*nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacaṃta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ saṃti devā iti chaṃdāsi vai*)
साध्या देवास्तेऽग्रेऽग्निनाग्निमयजंत ते स्वर्ग० लोमायन् ॥ (*sādhyā devāste 'gre 'gnināgnimayajaṃta te svarga0 lomāyan ‖*)

Then the Hotṛ recites the ṛk तं मर्जयंत सुक्रतुं (*taṃ marjayaṃta sukratuṃ*) (ऋ. सं. ८-८५-८ (*ṛ. saṃ. 8-85-8*)). Having said this and having established Agni in the Āhavanīya fire, his own dwelling place, he then completes the work of churning Agni by reciting the last ṛk of the churning of Agni, that is, the १३ नॆय (*13 nèya*) ṛk, यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*) (ऋ. सं. १०-९०-१६ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-90-16*)). Here the placing of the churned Agni (the Agni carried forward) joined with the Āhavanīya fire is what is called अग्निनाग्निमय जंत (*agnināgnimaya jaṃta*). Or this very rite is what is stated in the last ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*). Here the word साध्याः (*sādhyāḥ*) means the deities who preside over the metres such as the Gāyatrī. These deities formerly worshipped the Āhavanīya fire with the churned Agni; by that they obtained the world of heaven.

आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नंगिरसश्च तेऽग्रेऽग्निनाग्निमयजंत ते स्वर्गं लोकमा- (*ādityāścaivehāsannaṃgirasaśca te 'gre 'gnināgnimayajaṃta te svargaṃ lokamā-*)
यन् सैषा स्वर्गाहुतिर्यदग्न्याहुतिर्यदि ह ना अप्यब्राह्मणोक्तो (*yan saiṣā svargāhutiryadagnyāhutiryadi ha nā apyabrāhmaṇokto*)
यदि दुरुक्तोक्तो यजतेऽथ हैषाहुतिर्गच्छत्येव देवान पाप्मना (*yadi duruktokto yajate 'tha haiṣāhutirgacchatyeva devāna pāpmanā*)
संसृज्यते गच्छत्यस्याहुतिर्देवान्नास्याहुतिः पाप्मना संसृज्यते य एवं (*saṃsṛjyate gacchatyasyāhutirdevānnāsyāhutiḥ pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate ya evaṃ*)
वेद ॥ (*veda ‖*)

In the same way the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, having performed the sacrifice as said before, went to the world of heaven. This offering to Agni is the direct road to the world of heaven. While such a sacrificial rite is in progress, even if the chief priest is not a Brāhmaṇa as the śāstra requires, or is a bad man, the offering to Agni made in the sacrifice alone takes the sacrificer to heaven. The faults and the like of the priest do not attach to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice; that is, no harm comes to the sacrificer from them. He who knows this order of the offering to Agni, as explained above, joins the gods in heaven. For him there is no contact with sin of any kind.

### Printed p. 391

*Running head (as supplied): [अ: २ अ. ५ व. १७] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 391 (*[a: 2 a. 5 va. 17] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 391*).*

Here it was said in the sentence above "even if he is not a Brāhmaṇa as the śāstra requires". That needs an explanation: even though some Brāhmaṇas have obtained by mere birth the right to officiate at sacrifices, they misuse their right and become guilty of fault; it is said in the Smṛtis that among these non-Brāhmaṇas there are six kinds. How:

अब्राह्मणास्तु षट् प्रोक्ता इति शातातपोऽब्रवीत् ! (*abrāhmaṇāstu ṣaṭ proktā iti śātātapo 'bravīt !*)
आद्यस्तु राजभृत्यः स्याद्द्वितीयः क्रयविक्रया । (*ādyastu rājabhṛtyaḥ syāddvitīyaḥ krayavikrayā |*)
तृतीयो बहुयाज्याख्यश्च तुर्थोऽशौतयाजकः । (*tṛtīyo bahuyājyākhyaśca turtho 'śautayājakaḥ |*)
पंचमो ग्रामयाजी च षष्ठो ब्रह्मबंधुः स्मृतः ॥ (*paṃcamo grāmayājī ca ṣaṣṭho brahmabaṃdhuḥ smṛtaḥ ‖*)

On the question who the non-Brāhmaṇas are, the sage named शातातप (*śātātapa*) has spoken as follows. The first, राजभृत्य (*rājabhṛtya*), are those who depend on the king for their livelihood and serve him. The second are those who live by buying and selling and the like, who keep a shop and live by selling goods. The third are those who, although they have income sufficient for a livelihood, from the greed to earn more wealth make it their occupation to have sacrifices (or priestly work) performed for anyone at all; they are called बहुयाजि (*bahuyāji*). The fourth, अश्लौतयाजक (*aślautayājaka*), are those who, although accomplished in the study of the Veda for performing Śrauta acts, that is, sacrifices and the like, do not engage in the Śrauta rites nor have them performed for others, but engage only in the inferior Smārta rites. The fifth, ग्रामयाजक (*grāmayājaka*), are those who, in villages or cities, for greed of money have sacrifices performed for anyone, whether worthy or unworthy; they are called village-and-city priests (as printed, ग्रामनगरयाजक (*grāmanagarayājaka*)). The sixth, ब्रह्मबंधु (*brahmabaṃdhu*), are those who do not perform at the proper time the twilight rites and the like at sunrise and sunset; they are called *brahmabandhu*. The rite performed by these six kinds of priests is what is called above अब्राह्मणोक्त (*abrāhmaṇokta*) or दुरुक्कोक्त (*durukkokta*) (as printed).

ता एतास्त्रयोदशान्वाह रूपसमृद्धा एतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रू- (*tā etāstrayodaśānvāha rūpasamṛddhā etadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrū-*)
पसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति । तासां त्रिःप्रथमामन्वाह (*pasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati | tāsāṃ triḥprathamāmanvāha*)
त्रिरुत्तमां ताः सप्तदश संपद्यंते सप्तदशो वै प्रजापतिर्द्वादश मासाः (*triruttamāṃ tāḥ saptadaśa saṃpadyaṃte saptadaśo vai prajāpatirdvādaśa māsāḥ*)
पंचर्तवस्तावान्संवत्सरः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापत्यायतनाभिरेवाभी (*paṃcartavastāvānsaṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhirevābhī*)
राध्योति य एवं वेद त्रिः प्रथमां त्रिरुत्तमामन्वाह यज्ञस्यैव तद्बर्सौ (*rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ triruttamāmanvāha yajñasyaiva tadbarsau*)
नह्यति स्थेन्ने बलायाविस्रंसाय ॥ (*nahyati sthenne balāyāvisraṃsāya ‖*)
(इ ब्रा, ३-५) (*(i brā, 3-5)*)

(The reference is printed इ ब्रा, ३-५ (*i brā, 3-5*), as supplied.) Thus the ṛks used in the work of churning Agni are thirteen in all. The nine ṛks addressed to the deity that slays the rākṣasas (the *rākṣoghna* sūkta) are not included in these. By reciting these thirteen ṛks at their proper times (the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 392

*Running head (as supplied): [392 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २ अ. १. सू १] (*[392 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2 a. 1. sū 1]*).*

*(Continuation of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa summary of the thirteen churning ṛks, from mid-sentence at the end of the previous page.)*

...the churning of Agni, the birth of Agni, taking Agni and placing him in the Āhavanīya, and joining him there with the Āhavanīya fire: all these rites being carried out completely by the recitation of ṛks suited to the occasion is called रूपसमृद्धि (*rūpasamṛddhi*). Of these thirteen ṛks the first ṛk (the ṛk अभि त्वा देव सवितः (*abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*)) and the last ṛk (the ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*)) must be recited three times by the Hotṛ. Therefore in all, seventeen ṛks have been recited in this work of churning Agni. Prajāpati is of the nature of the number seventeen. For twelve months and five ṛks (seasons) together make one year; that year is Prajāpati; therefore he who knows the meaning of these ṛks, placed in Prajāpati, attains prosperity. By reciting the first and the last ṛks three times each, the binding (the knots) of the sacrifice becomes firm and tight and has room to stay steady without slipping: so it is set forth in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-५ (*ai. brā. 3-5*)) on the work of churning Agni. The procedure of churning Agni is complete (as printed: अग्नि निर्मंथनविधियु समाप्तवु (*agni nirmaṃthanavidhiyu samāptavu*)).

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. आ ५. व. १७] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 393 (*[a. 2. ā 5. va. 17] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 393*).*

> प्राप्तकालमार्त्विज्यं तवैव । नेष्ट्रं नेष्टुः कर्म प्रस्थितयोज्यादिरूपं तव । हे
> अग्ने त्वमग्नित् अग्नीध्रश्च त्वमेवासि । तथा ऋतायतो यज्ञमिच्छतस्तनैव प्रशास्त्रं
> यत्पशास्तुर्मैत्रावरुणस्य कर्म तत् । हे अग्ने त्वमध्वरीयसि । अध्वरं यज्ञं
> कामयसे । अर्धर्युर्भवसीत्यर्थः । तथाध्वर्युशब्दव्युत्पत्तेः । अध्वर्युरध्वर-
> युरध्वरं कामयत इति वेति हि निरुक्तं । १-८ । तथा ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मणाच्छंस्यप्यसि । तथा
> नो दमेऽस्मदृज्ञगृहे गृहपतिश्चासीति ॥

*Gist:* Agni is addressed: the functions of the Hotṛ, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Ṛtvij, Agnīdhra, Praśāstṛ, Adhvaryu and Brahmā, and the householder, are all yours.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). होत्रं—शस्त्रयाज्यादिगळन्नु पठिसुव होतृविन कर्मवु (*hotraṃ—śastrayājyādigaḷannu paṭhisuva hotṛvina karmavu*) (the office of the Hotṛ who recites the śastras, yājyās and the like). तव—निनगॆ संबंधिसिदुदु (*tava—ninagè saṃbaṃdhisidudu*) (yours). पोत्रं—पोतृविन कर्मवू (*potraṃ—potṛvina karmavū*) (the office of the Potṛ too). तव—निन्नदे ऎंदरॆ निनगोस्करवे (आगिदॆ) (*tava—ninnade èṃdarè ninagoskarave (āgidè)*) (yours, that is, for you). ऋत्वियं—ऋत्विक्कुगळ कर्मवू (*ṛtviyaṃ—ṛtvikkugaḷa karmavū*) (the office of the Ṛtviks too). नेष्ट्रं—नेष्ट्रुविन कर्मवू (*neṣṭraṃ—neṣṭruvina karmavū*) (the office of the Neṣṭṛ too). तव—निन्नदे आगिदॆ (*tava—ninnade āgidè*) (yours). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). ऋतायतः—यज्ञवन्नु इच्छिसतक्क यजमाननिगॆ (*ṛtāyataḥ—yajñavannu icchisatakka yajamānanigè*) (to the sacrificer who desires the sacrifice). अग्नित्—अग्नीध्र- नागिद्दीयॆ (*agnit—agnīdhra- nāgiddīyè*) (you are the Agnīdhra). प्रशास्त्रं—प्रशास्त्रविन कर्मवू (*praśāstraṃ—praśāstravina karmavū*) (the office of the Praśāstṛ too). तव—निन्नदे (*tava—ninnade*) (yours). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अध्वरीयसि— अध्वर्युवागिद्दीयॆ ऎंदरॆ अध्वर्युवु माडुव कॆलसवन्नुमाडुत्तीयॆ (*adhvarīyasi— adhvaryuvāgiddīyè èṃdarè adhvaryuvu māḍuva kèlasavannumāḍuttīyè*) (you are the Adhvaryu, that is, you do the work that the Adhvaryu does). ब्रह्मा च असि—ब्रह्मनू आगिद्दीयॆ (*brahmā ca asi—brahmanū āgiddīyè*) (and you are Brahmā too). नः—नम्म (*naḥ—namma*) (our). दमे—यज्ञगृहदल्लि (*dame—yajñagṛhadalli*) (in the sacrificial house). गृहपतिश्च—गृहपतियू (अथवा यज्ञमाडुव यजमाननू) आगिद्दीयॆ. (*gṛhapatiśca—gṛhapatiyū (athavā yajñamāḍuva yajamānanū) āgiddīyè.*) (and you are the householder (or the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice)).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the office that belongs to the Hotṛ, and to the Potṛ and the Neṣṭṛ, is yours. To the sacrificer who desires the sacrifice you are the Agnīdhra. The office of the Praśāstṛ too is yours. You are the Adhvaryu (the printed word is अध्वरुवू (*adhvaruvū*)) and Brahmā, and you are the householder in our sacrificial house.

**Printed English translation**

Yours, Agni, is the office of the Hotri, of the Potri, of the Ritwij ; of the Neshtri, you are the Agnidhra of the devout, yours is the function of the Prashastri, you are the Adhwaryu and the Brahman, and the householder in our dwelling.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

In this ṛk and in the following ṛks Agni is described in many ways as the form of various deities and priests. When praising the qualities of great men it is the custom to praise them as Indra, Candra, Devendra. In the same way here the sage Gṛtsamada has sung the qualities of Agni by comparing him with various deities. Such description

### Printed p. 394

*Running head (as supplied): [394 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू. १.] (*[394 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 1.]*).*

is found in the Bhagavadgītā verses such as

वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः । (*vedānāṃ sāmavedo 'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ |*)
इंद्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥ (*iṃdriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā ‖*)
(भ. गी. १०=२२) (*(bha. gī. 10=22)*)

(The reference is printed भ. गी. १०=२२ (*bha. gī. 10=22*), as supplied.) and in many other modern works. In the present ṛk Agni is praised as being himself the function or the form of the Hotṛ, Potṛ, Ṛtviks, Neṣṭṛ, Adhvaryu, Brahmā, the householder and others, who play the chief parts in the sacrifice (होतृ, पोतृ, ऋत्विक्कुगळु, नेष्टृ, अध्वर्यु, ब्रह्म, गृहपति (*hotṛ, potṛ, ṛtvikkugaḷu, neṣṭṛ, adhvaryu, brahma, gṛhapati*)). Among the priests who take part in the sacrifice the chief are होतृ, अध्वर्यु, उद्गातृ, ब्रह्म (*hotṛ, adhvaryu, udgātṛ, brahma*). As helpers to them there are twelve more priests. All together they are sixteen: namely, (first) the priests of the Hotṛ group: होतृ, मैत्रावरुण, अच्छावाक, मत्तु ग्रावस्तुत् (*hotṛ, maitrāvaruṇa, acchāvāka, mattu grāvastut*), these four are the priests of the Hotṛ group; (second) those of the Adhvaryu group: अध्वर्यु, प्रतिप्रस्थातृ, नेष्टृ मत्तु उन्नेतृ (*adhvaryu, pratiprasthātṛ, neṣṭṛ mattu unnetṛ*); (third) those of the Udgātṛ group: उद्गातृ, प्रस्तोतृ, प्रतिहर्तृ, मत्तु सुब्रह्मण्य (*udgātṛ, prastotṛ, pratihartṛ, mattu subrahmaṇya*); (fourth) those of the Brahmā group: ब्रह्म, ब्राह्मणाच्छंसि, अग्नीध्र, पोतृ (*brahma, brāhmaṇācchaṃsi, agnīdhra, potṛ*) (the print numbers them with Latin digits).

In these ṛks the chief duty of the Hotṛ group is this: in the sacrifice, as soon as the Adhvaryu says the *praiṣa* mantra and utters which mantra is to be said, the Hotṛ recites, according to the occasion, the mantras of the Ṛgveda, such as the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the śastra mantras, the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras and the mantras to be said in the churning of Agni and the like, and thus helps the sacrificial rites. For them the Ṛgvedic mantras are the chief.

In the sacrifice the part of the Adhvaryu and of his group of helpers is much greater. The Adhvaryu is the leader in all the work, and directs the other priests at the proper times, through *praiṣa* mantras, as to what work they are to do. Therefore it is said अध्वर्युर्वा ऋत्विजां प्रथमो युज्यते (*adhvaryurvā ṛtvijāṃ prathamo yujyate*): among the priests the Adhvaryu is the chief. All his work depends on the Yajurveda.

The Udgātṛ group sing the sāmans suited to the occasion at the time of invoking the deities and at the time of the soma recitation. The Sāmaveda mantras are the chief ones for them. Since it is said अयज्ञो ना एष योऽसामा (*ayajño nā eṣa yo 'sāmā*), that is, a sacrifice without sāman singing is no sacrifice, their part too is very important (the supplied text ends here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 395

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १७] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 395 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 17] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 395*).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 1 of Maṇḍala 2, on the sixteen priests.)*

Brahmā and the priests of his group of helpers see that the works carried on in sacrifices and the like are carried out completely and as the śāstra directs, and if any lapse or fault occurs in the middle, they have the proper expiation and the like performed and see that the sacrifice is completed in good order: this is their duty. They must also have knowledge of the four Vedas. All that has been said above is the general duties of the priests of each group. Besides these, each priest has a special and definite duty of his own. Out of the fear that the book would grow too long by telling all of that here, and because the need for it is not so great, that matter is not told here. Only the subtle details of the works of the priests that are indicated in this ṛk are told here.

The Hotṛ, reciting mantras suited to each time in the sacrifice, invokes the deities. The Potṛ belongs to the Brahmā group; he corrects and purifies the lapses and faults that may occur in the sacrifice. The Neṣṭṛ does such work as bringing the wife of the sacrificer; he belongs to the Adhvaryu group. The Agnīt (अग्नीध्र (*agnīdhra*)) kindles Agni and looks after it; he belongs to the Brahmā group. The Prasthātṛ (मैत्रावरुण (*maitrāvaruṇa*)) is the helper of the Hotṛ and the director of the other priests (there is a Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence, मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्ता- दृत्विग्यो वाचं विभजति (*maitrāvaruṇo hi purastā- dṛtvigyo vācaṃ vibhajati*)). The Adhvaryu proceeds as the leader in all the activities of the sacrifice; whatever work is to be done is only through him or his command. Brahmā sees whether the sacrifice goes on properly and whether any lapse of mantra and tantra happens. *Gṛhapati* here may mean Agni, the lord of the sacrificial house, or the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. All these are the very form of Agni; that is, the sage has described that Agni is of great majesty.

### Printed p. 396

*Running head (as supplied): [396 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २ आ. १. सू. १] (*[396 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2 ā. 1. sū. 1]*).*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । इंद्रः । वृषभः । सतां । असि । त्वं । विष्णुः । उरुगायः । नमस्यॆ [?] ।
> त्वं । ब्रह्मा । रयिवित् । ब्रह्मणः । पते । त्वं । विधर्तरिति विधर्तः । सचसे । पुरंध्या
> ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वं यतः सतां वृषभो वर्षितासि अत इंद्रोऽसि । यद्वा सतां
> साधूनामिंद्रोऽसि । कामानां वर्षितासि । त्वं विष्णुरसि । यत उरुगायो बहु-
> भिर्गीयमानो नमस्को नमस्कार्यश्च भवसि । हे ब्रह्मणस्पते परिवृढस्य कर्मणो
> मंत्रस्य वा पालयितस्त्वं यतो रयिवित् गवादिधनस्य वेत्ता अतो ब्रह्मासि ।
> हे विधर्तर्विविधकारक वैश्वानररूपाग्ने पुरंध्या बहुप्रकारया बुद्ध्या सचसे ।
> सह वर्तसे । सर्वदा बुद्ध्या स्तूयस इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Agni is Indra, showerer on the good; Viṣṇu, widely praised and worthy of homage; Brahmā, rich; lord of rites; endowed with manifold wisdom.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). सतां—सत्पुरुषरिगॆ ! वृषभः—इष्टार्थगळन्नु सुरिसतक्क (*satāṃ—satpuruṣarigè ! vṛṣabhaḥ—iṣṭārthagaḷannu surisatakka*) (to the good men ! the showerer of wishes (the "!" is printed in place of a danda)). इंद्रः—इंद्रनागि (*iṃdraḥ—iṃdranāgi*) (as Indra). असि—इद्दीयॆ (*asi—iddīyè*) (you are). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). उरुगायः—अनेकरिंद स्तुतिसल्पडुववनू (*urugāyaḥ—anekariṃda stutisalpaḍuvavanū*) (praised by many). नमस्यः—नमस्कारार्हनू आद (*namasyaḥ—namaskārārhanū āda*) (worthy of homage). विष्णुः—विष्णुवागिद्दीयॆ (*viṣṇuḥ—viṣṇuvāgiddīyè*) (you are Viṣṇu). ब्रहणस्पते— कर्मपालकनाद अग्निये (*brahaṇaspate— karmapālakanāda agniye*) (O Agni, protector of rites). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). रयिवित्—धनवंतनाद (*rayivit—dhanavaṃtanāda*) (the wealthy). ब्रह्मा—ब्रह्मनागिद्दीयॆ (*brahmā—brahmanāgiddīyè*) (you are Brahmā). विधर्तः—अनेक कार्यगळिगॆ कर्तनाद वैश्वानराग्निये (*vidhartaḥ—aneka kāryagaḷigè kartanāda vaiśvānarāgniye*) (the doer of many works, the Vaiśvānara Agni). पुरंध्या—अनेक विधवाद ज्ञानदिंद (*puraṃdhyā—aneka vidhavāda jñānadiṃda*) (with manifold knowledge). सचसे—युक्तनागिद्दीयॆ (अथवा अनेक विधवाद प्रज्ञॆयिंद स्तुतनागिद्दीयॆ) (*sacase—yuktanāgiddīyè (athavā aneka vidhavāda prajñèyiṃda stutanāgiddīyè)*) (you are endowed (or praised with manifold wisdom)).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you are Indra, the showerer of wishes on good men; you are Viṣṇu, praised by many and worthy of homage; you are the wealthy Brahmā. You are endowed with manifold knowledge.

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are Indra, the showerer (of bounties) on the good ; you are the adorable Vishnu, the hymned of many ; you, Brahmasanapati, are Brahma, the possessor of riches ; you, the author of various (conditions), are associated with wisdom.

### Printed p. 397

*Running head (as supplied): [आ. २. आ ५. व. १७. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 397 (*[ā. 2. ā 5. va. 17. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 397*).*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

वृषभः— कामानां वर्षिता (*vṛṣabhaḥ— kāmānāṃ varṣitā*): the showerer of wishes, one who gives the desired objects.

इंद्रो वृषभः सतां असि (*iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāṃ asi*): you are one who grants desired objects to good men, like Indra. Or इंद्रो सतां असि (*iṃdro satāṃ asi*) (as printed): you are reckoned the best among all good men; this is the purport.

विष्णुरुरुगायः—बहुभिर्गीयमानो विष्णुरसि (*viṣṇururugāyaḥ—bahubhirgīyamāno viṣṇurasi*): like Viṣṇu you are sung by many on the matter of your qualities.

ब्रह्मणस्पते—यज्ञकर्मणः पालयिता (*brahmaṇaspate—yajñakarmaṇaḥ pālayitā*): the protector of sacrificial rites; or, like Bṛhaspati, the lord of the hymns.

पुरंध्या—पुरंधिर्जहुधी (*puraṃdhyā—puraṃdhirjahudhī*): this is Yāska's etymology (नि. ६-१३ (*ni. 6-13*)). बहु प्रकाराया बुद्ध्या सचसे (*bahu prakārāyā buddhyā sacase*): one who has abundant or many kinds of intelligence; or the meaning is also that people praise you with their manifold intelligence.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). धृतव्रतः—सत्यादि व्रतगळिगॆ नियामकनू (*dhṛtavrataḥ—satyādi vratagaḷigè niyāmakanū*) (the regulator of vows such as truth). राजा—प्रभुवादवनू आद (*rājā—prabhuvādavanū āda*) (and lord). वरुणः—वरुणनागिद्दीयॆ (*varuṇaḥ—varuṇanāgiddīyè*) (you are Varuṇa). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). दस्मः—शत्रुनाशकनू (*dasmaḥ—śatrunāśakanū*) (the destroyer of foes). ईड्यः—स्तुत्यनू आद (*īḍyaḥ—stutyanū āda*) (and the adorable). मित्रः—मित्रनागिद्दीयॆ (*mitraḥ—mitranāgiddīyè*) (you are Mitra). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). यस्य—याव आर्यमन दानवु (*yasya—yāva āryamana dānavu*) (of whom, that is, of Aryaman, the gift). संभुजं—सर्वत्र भोग्यवागिदॆयो अंतह (*saṃbhujaṃ—sarvatra bhogyavāgidèyo aṃtaha*) (is everywhere to be enjoyed, such). सत्पतिः—सज्जनर पालकनाद (*satpatiḥ—sajjanara pālakanāda*) (protector of the good). आर्यमा- आर्यमनागि (*āryamā- āryamanāgi*) (you become Aryaman (the entry is printed with a hyphen)). भवसि—आगिद्दीयॆ (*bhavasi—āgiddīyè*) (you become). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अंशशः—अंशदेवनू आगिद्दीयॆ (*aṃśaśaḥ—aṃśadevanū āgiddīyè*) (you are also the god Aṃśa). देवः—देवता, त्मनाद ऎलै अग्निये (*devaḥ—devatā, tmanāda èlai agniye*) (O Agni, whose self is divine). विदथे—नम्म यज्ञदल्लि (*vidathe—namma yajñadalli*) (in our sacrifice). भाजयुः—सत्फलगळन्नु हंचुववनागु. (*bhājayuḥ—satphalagaḷannu haṃcuvavanāgu.*) (be the distributor of good fruits).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you are Varuṇa, the regulator of vows and lord, and Mitra, the destroyer of foes and the adorable. You are Aryaman (the print has अरम्यनू (*aramyanū*)), the protector of the good and the cause of the gift that is enjoyed by all, and Aṃśa. O Agni, whose self is divine, be the distributor of good fruits in our sacrifice.

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are the royal Varuna, observant of holy vows: you are the adorable Mitra, the destroyer (of foes) : you are Aryaman, the protector of the virtuous, whose (liberality) is enjoyed by all : you are a portion (of the sun) : be the distributor (of good things), divine (Agni), at our sacrifice.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

In this ṛk Agni is described as the form of the deities Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman and Aṃśa. These deities Mitra and the others, as Ādityas,

इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । (*imā gira ādityebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi |*)
शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*)
(पु सं. २-२७-१) (*(pu saṃ. 2-27-1)*)

(The reference is printed पु सं. २-२७-१ (*pu saṃ. 2-27-1*), as supplied.)

> त्वं । अग्ने । त्वष्टा । विधते । सुवीर्यं । तव । ग्नावः । मित्रमहः । सजात्यं ।
> त्वं । आशुहेमा । ररिषे । सुअश्व्यं । त्वं । नरां । शर्धः । असि । पुरूवसुः ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वष्टा फलस्य साधु संपादयिता त्वं विधते परिचरते जनाय
> सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्यं । वीर्यं धनर । तद्धेतुर्भवसि । ग्नावो याः स्तुतिवाचः
> संति तास्तव स्वभूताः । हे मित्रमहः हितकारितेजः सजात्यमस्माकं बांधवं भजस
> इत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने आशुहेमा आशु प्रेरयिता त्वं स्वश्वं शोभनाश्वसमूहोपेतं
> फलं ररिषे । ददासि । हे अग्ने पुरूवसुः प्रभूतधनस्त्वं नरां नराणां शर्धो
> बलस्थानीयोऽसि ॥

*Gist:* Agni, as Tvaṣṭṛ, gives his worshipper heroic wealth; praises are his; he is asked for kinship and good horses; he is the strength of men.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वष्टा—फलवन्नु संपादिसिकॊडतक्क (*tvaṣṭā—phalavannu saṃpādisikòḍatakka*) (Tvaṣṭṛ, the one who obtains the fruit). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). विधते— (निन्नन्नु) सेविसतक्क जनरिगॆ (*vidhate— (ninnannu) sevisatakka janarigè*) (to those who serve you). सुवीर‍्यं - श्रेष्ठवाद वीर्यदिंद कूडिद धनवन्नु (कॊडुत्तीयॆ) (*suvīryaṃ - śreṣṭhavāda vīryadiṃda kūḍida dhanavannu (kòḍuttīyè)*) ((you give) wealth endowed with excellent heroism).

### Printed p. 400

*Running head (as supplied): [400 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं २ अ. १. सू १.] (*[400 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ 2 a. 1. sū 1.]*).*

ग्नावः-स्तुतिरूपवाद वाक्कुगळॆल्लवू (*gnāvaḥ-stutirūpavāda vākkugaḷèllavū*) (all the praises in the form of hymns). तव-निन्नवे आगिवॆ (*tava-ninnave āgivè*) (are yours). मित्रमहः-जगत्तिगॆ हितवन्नुंटु माडुव तेजस्सुळ्ळ अग्निये (*mitramahaḥ-jagattigè hitavannuṃṭu māḍuva tejassuḷḷa agniye*) (O Agni of beneficial lustre for the world). सजात्यं--नम्मॊडनॆ बंधुत्ववन्नु पालिसु (*sajātyaṃ--nammòḍanè baṃdhutvavannu pālisu*) (observe kinship with us). आशुहेमा-(कर्तव्य गळल्लि) शीघ्रवागि प्रेरिसतक्क नीनु (*āśuhemā-(kartavya gaḷalli) śīghravāgi prerisatakka nīnu*) (you who urge us promptly (in duties)). स्वश्वं-श्रेष्ठवाद अश्वदिंद कूडिरुव फलवन्नु (*svaśvaṃ-śreṣṭhavāda aśvadiṃda kūḍiruva phalavannu*) (the fruit endowed with excellent horses). ररिषे- कॊडुत्तीयॆ ! पुरूवसुः-प्रभूतवाद धनवुळ्ळ (*rariṣe- kòḍuttīyè ! purūvasuḥ-prabhūtavāda dhanavuḷḷa*) (you give! (the "!" is printed in place of a danda) and, endowed with abundant wealth). त्वं-नीनु (*tvaṃ-nīnu*) (you). नरां--नरर (*narāṃ--narara*) (of men). शर्धः-शक्ति रूपवागि (*śardhaḥ-śakti rūpavāgi*) (as the strength). असि-इद्दीयॆ (*asi-iddīyè*) (you are).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you, in the form of Tvaṣṭṛ, give wealth endowed with excellent heroism to the people who serve you. All the praises in the form of hymns are yours. O Agni of lustre beneficial to the world, observe kinship with us. You who urge us promptly in our duties give the fruit endowed with excellent horses. You, endowed with abundant wealth, are the strength of men.

*[As supplied, the label line of the printed English reads English Translatin (*English Translatin*) (sic), run on without a blank line; standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are Twashtri, (the giver) of great wealth to (your) worshipper : these praises are yours : do you, of benevolent power, (admit) our affinity : you, who are prompt to encourage (us), give us good (store of) horses : you, who abound with opulence, are the strength of men.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5)**

त्वष्टा—फलस्य साधु संपदयिता (*tvaṣṭā—phalasya sādhu saṃpadayitā*) (as printed): for this word the bhāṣyakāra has taken the sense of one who well provides the sacrificers with the fruit of sacrificial rites and the like. Or the word *tvaṣṭā* may also be said to mean the divine craftsman named त्वष्टनामकनाद देवशिल्पि (*tvaṣṭanāmakanāda devaśilpi*). As the divine craftsman (printed तृष्ण (*tṛṣṇa*)) makes for the gods the implements they need, in the same way you (Agni) too are one who gives all kinds of wealth and prosperity to the gods and to men: this is the purport.

ग्नावः— ग्नावो याः स्तुतिवाचः संति तास्तव स्वभूताः (*gnāvaḥ— gnāvo yāḥ stutivācaḥ saṃti tāstava svabhūtāḥ*): the word ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*) is read among the names of speech (नि. २-२३ (*ni. 2-23*); the print has वाज्ञाम (*vājñāma*), as printed). Since all praise sentences are on your behalf, the purport is that you are of the very form of the praise sentences.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). महः—महत्ताद (*mahaḥ—mahattāda*) (great). दिवः—द्युलोकदिंद (लोक त्रयदिंद) असुरः—शत्रुगळन्नु ओडिसतक्क (*divaḥ—dyulokadiṃda (loka trayadiṃda) asuraḥ—śatrugaḷannu oḍisatakka*) (from heaven (from the three worlds), the expeller of foes). रुद्रः—रुद्रनागिद्दीयॆ (*rudraḥ—rudranāgiddīyè*) (you are Rudra). [अथवा रुद्रः त्वं— रुद्ररूपनाद नीनु (*[athavā rudraḥ tvaṃ— rudrarūpanāda nīnu*) ([or: you, of Rudra form). महः—महत्ताद (*mahaḥ—mahattāda*) (great). दिवः - द्युलोकक्कॆ (*divaḥ - dyulokakkè*) (to heaven). असुरः—शक्तिदायकनाद आदित्यनागिद्दीयॆ] (*asuraḥ—śaktidāyakanāda ādityanāgiddīyè]*) (you are the Āditya, giver of strength]). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). मारुतं शर्धः—मरुत्तुगळ संघातरूपवाद शक्तियागि द्धीयॆ (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ—maruttugaḷa saṃghātarūpavāda śaktiyāgi ddhīyè*) (you are the strength in the form of the group of the Maruts). पृक्षः—हविस्सिन रूपद अन्नक्कॆ (*pṛkṣaḥ—havissina rūpada annakkè*) (to the food in the form of oblations). ईशिषे—प्रभुवागिद्दीयॆ (*īśiṣe—prabhuvāgiddīyè*) (you are lord). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अरुणैः— गमनशीलवाद (*aruṇaiḥ— gamanaśīlavāda*) (swift). वातैः—वायुगळिंद (प्रजोदितनागियू) अथवा वायरूपवाद अश्वगळॊड (*vātaiḥ—vāyugaḷiṃda (prajoditanāgiyū) athavā vāyarūpavāda aśvagaḷòḍa*) (by the winds (impelled), or with horses of the form of wind: the entry is divided across the page boundary).

### Printed p. 402

*Running head (as supplied): [402 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ. १. सू. १] (*[402 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 1]*).*

नॆयू (*nèyū*) ((the end of the divided entry)). शंगयः—सुखक्कॆ आवासभूतनागियू (*śaṃgayaḥ—sukhakkè āvāsabhūtanāgiyū*) (and as the abode of happiness). यासि—यज्ञगृहक्कॆ बरुत्तीयॆ (*yāsi—yajñagṛhakkè baruttīyè*) (you come to the sacrificial house). त्वं— नीनु (*tvaṃ— nīnu*) (you). पूषा—सकलक्कू पोषकनागिद्दु (*pūṣā—sakalakkū poṣakanāgiddu*) (as Pūṣan, the nourisher of all). नु—जाग्रतॆयागि (*nu—jāgratèyāgi*) (swiftly). त्मना—निन्न आत्मच्छॆयिंद (*tmanā—ninna ātmacchèyiṃda*) (by your own will). विधतः—निन्नन्नु परचरिसुव यजमानरन्नु (*vidhataḥ—ninnannu paracarisuva yajamānarannu*) (the sacrificers who serve you). पासि—कापाडुत्तीयॆ (*pāsi—kāpāḍuttīyè*) (you protect).

*[As supplied, a line reading धनार्थ (*dhanārtha*) stands, with block marks, where the Bhāvārtha label belongs; the following lines are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you, of the form of Rudra, are the Āditya of the great heaven. You are the strength in the form of the group of the Maruts. You are the lord of all the food in the form of oblations. Impelled by the wind, and as the abode of happiness, you come to the sacrificial house. Being the nourisher of all, you protect, wholeheartedly, the sacrificer who serves you.

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are Rudra, the expeller (of foes) from the expanse of heaven; you are the strength of the Maruts, you are supreme over (sacrificial) food, you, who are pleasantly domiciled (in the hall of sacrifice), go with ruddy horses, (fleet as) the wind ; as Pushan, you cherish, of your own will, those, who offer worship.

*(The printed English reads "sacrifi-cial" with a printed hyphen; joined as "sacrificial".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 6)**

रुद्रः— रुद्दुःखं दुःखरेतुर्वा पापादिः । तस्य द्रावयिता (*rudraḥ— rudduḥkhaṃ duḥkhareturvā pāpādiḥ | tasya drāvayitā*) (as printed): रुत् (*rut*) means sorrow. What is the cause of sorrow is sin. Because he drives away that sin, this god has the name Rudra. Since in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda it is said रुद्रो ना एष यदग्निः (*rudro nā eṣa yadagniḥ*) (तै. सं. ५-४-३ (*tai. saṃ. 5-4-3*)), the purport is that this Agni is of the very form of Rudra. Or रौति मामनिष्टा नरा दुःखे पतिष्यंतीति रुद्रः (*rauti māmaniṣṭā narā duḥkhe patiṣyaṃtīti rudraḥ*): because men, not worshipping me, Agni, with sacrifices and the like, become vessels of sorrow, such an Agni has the name Rudra. In the Nirukta also:

रुद्रो रौतीति सतः । रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा रोदयतेर्वा । यद- (*rudro rautīti sataḥ | rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā rodayatervā | yada-*)
रुदत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं इति काठकं । यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं इति (*rudattadrudrasya rudratvaṃ iti kāṭhakaṃ | yadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvaṃ iti*)
हारिद्रविकं ॥ (*hāridravikaṃ ‖*)
(नि. १०-७) (*(ni. 10-7)*)

Yāska has given the etymology so. Following this, Sāyaṇa has explained the word *rudra* in six ways. The word *rudra* is formed from the root रुद् (*rud*) in the causative. Yāska, as said above, रुद्रो रौतीति सतः रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा रोदयतेर्वा (*rudro rautīti sataḥ rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā rodayatervā*):

### Printed p. 403

*Running head (as supplied): [कि. २. अ. ५. व. १८ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 403 (*[ki. 2. a. 5. va. 18 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 403*), as printed.*

*Rudra* means रौति-स्तनयित्तु शब्दं करोतीति रुद्रः (*rauti-stanayittu śabdaṃ karotīti rudraḥ*): because he makes a sound like the thunder of a cloud, he has the name Rudra; or रोरूयमाणो द्रवति (*rorūyamāṇo dravati*): one who moves about in the midst of the cloud making sound; or रोदयतेर्वा (*rodayatervā*): one who does deeds that make enemies weep and makes them weep; thus the meaning has been explained. And यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रत्वं (*yadarudat tadrudratvaṃ*): following the famous history in the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā that he wept, distressed on seeing his father Prajāpati struck by arrows; or following the idea यदरोदीत् तम्म्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*yadarodīt tammrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) (as printed) belonging to the Maitrāyaṇīya branch, because he wept this god has the name Rudra; thus they have explained the etymology of the word Rudra (नि. १०-७ (*ni. 10-7*)). Sāyaṇa, in giving the meaning of the word Rudra, has put it somewhat differently: because at the time of dissolution he makes everyone weep, or because he destroys the sorrow called *saṃsāra*, or because he is propounded by the Upaniṣads in the form of sound, or because he teaches the knowledge of the self to those who worship by it, or because he destroys ignorance that covers knowledge like pitch darkness that covers light, this god deserves the name Rudra; thus he has explained the meaning of the word Rudra according to the different meanings of the word रुत् (*rut*). We have explained this etymology of the word Rudra and its various meanings, in places suited to the context, in ऋ. सं. भाग 5 पेजु 589, भाग 6 पेजु 350, भाग 9 पेजु 101, भाग 10 पेजु 379; भाग 13 पेजु 541 (*ṛ. saṃ. bhāga 5 peju 589, bhāga 6 peju 350, bhāga 9 peju 101, bhāga 10 peju 379; bhāga 13 peju 541*).

असुरः—शत्रुणां निरसिता (*asuraḥ—śatruṇāṃ nirasitā*) (as printed): "one who repels enemies"; this is an epithet either of Agni or of the word Rudra (the printed word is विशेषणदप (*viśeṣaṇadapa*)). Or असुर्बलं तस्य दातादित्यरूपश्च । त्वमसि (*asurbalaṃ tasya dātādityarūpaśca | tvamasi*): *asu* means strength, and Agni is praised: you are of the Āditya form that gives that strength. The *asuratva* of Agni in relation to heaven is stated in the ṛk

उत वा दिवो आसुराय मन्म प्रान्थांसीव यज्यवे भरध्वं । (*uta vā divo āsurāya manma prānthāṃsīva yajyave bharadhvaṃ |*)
(ऋ. सं. ५-४१-३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-41-3)*)

The word *asura* is a synonym of the word *rākṣasa* in the Purāṇas and the like. But in the Ṛksaṃhitā this word is used in various senses. *Asu* has many meanings, such as life (breath), consciousness, throwing. Therefore the word *asura* too has been used according to these meanings. These must be applied according to the context.

बृहच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कृतः पुरो हरिभ्यां वृषभो रथो हि षः । (*bṛhacchravā asuro barhaṇā kṛtaḥ puro haribhyāṃ vṛṣabho ratho hi ṣaḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-५४-३) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-54-3)*)

In this ṛk the word *asura* is an epithet of Indra. Here too, as said in that ṛk, one meaning is आसुरः— शत्रूणां निरसिता (*āsuraḥ— śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā*) (as printed), and another यद्वा आसुः प्राणो बलं (*yadvā āsuḥ prāṇo balaṃ*) (the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, at the end of the window).

क्षयन्न स्मभ्यमसुर प्रचेता राजन्नेनांसि शिश्रथः कृतानि । (*kṣayanna smabhyamasura pracetā rājannenāṃsi śiśrathaḥ kṛtāni |*)

त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे । (*tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |*)

वि सुपर्णो अंतरिक्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः । (*vi suparṇo aṃtarikṣāṇyakhyadgabhīravepā asuraḥ sunīthaḥ |*)

पृषद्योनिः पंचहोता शृणोत्वतूर्तपंथा असुरो मयोभुः । (*pṛṣadyoniḥ paṃcahotā śṛṇotvatūrtapaṃthā asuro mayobhuḥ |*)

अस्मे वीरो मरुतः शुष्कस्य जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता ॥ (*asme vīro marutaḥ śuṣkasya janānāṃ yo asuro vidhartā ‖*)

शतं कक्षीवा असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवोजरमा ततान । (*śataṃ kakṣīvā asurasya gonāṃ divi śravojaramā tatāna |*)
