### Printed p. 405

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १८. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 405 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 18. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 405*).*

यथा रुद्रस्य सूनवो दिवो वशंत्यसुरस्य वेधसः । (*yathā rudrasya sūnavo divo vaśaṃtyasurasya vedhasaḥ |*)
(म. सं. ८-२०-१७) (*(ma. saṃ. 8-20-17)*)

In this ṛk (the reference is printed म. सं. ८-२०-१७ (*ma. saṃ. 8-20-17*)) the word *asurasya* is used in the sense of a cloud.

अनायुधासो असुरा अदेवाश्च क्रेण ता अस वस यजीषिन् । (*anāyudhāso asurā adevāśca kreṇa tā asa vasa yajīṣin |*)
(म. सं. ८-९६-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 8-96-9)*)

In such ṛks (the reference is printed म. सं. ८-९६-९ (*ma. saṃ. 8-96-9*)) *asuras* are the Daityas belonging to the class of rākṣasas. In the present ṛk the meaning is Agni or Rudra, who repels such rākṣasa enemies. In the Purāṇas and the like, and in modern Sanskrit also, *sura* means a god and *asura* means a rākṣasa who is not a god; this meaning is current. But the word *asura* was not formed as the negation of the word *sura*. The word *asura* itself was current in the Vedas (and especially in the Ṛgveda), and afterwards, by elision of the *a*, the word *sura*, with the opposite meaning, came into use. In the same way the word *aditi* was current, and afterwards, by elision of the *a*, the word *diti* came into use. *Aditi* means the mother of the gods; *diti*, on the contrary, has recently come into use in the sense of the mother of the rākṣasas.

मारुतं शर्धः—मरुत्समूहरूपं बलमसि । वायुरूपश्च त्वमसीत्यर्थः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ—marutsamūharūpaṃ balamasi | vāyurūpaśca tvamasītyarthaḥ*): you are of the form of the wind. Or the purport is that you are the form of the joint strength of the ४९ (*49*) Marut deities. The joint strength of the Marut deities is wonderful. In describing this strength it is the custom to describe it by the words मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*).

इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिं हवामहे । (*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimūtaye mārutaṃ śardho aditiṃ havāmahe |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१०६-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-106-1)*)

In such ṛks (ऋ. सं. १-१०६-१ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-106-1*)), when the Marut deities or the joint strength of the Marut deities is spoken of, the words मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*) are used.

पृक्ष ईशिषे—अन्नस्य हविर्लक्षणस्य त्वं ईश्वरो भवसि (*pṛkṣa īśiṣe—annasya havirlakṣaṇasya tvaṃ īśvaro bhavasi*): the word पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*) is read among the names of food (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*); the print has परितवागिदॆ (*paritavāgidè*) for "is read"). It is described that Agni is lord of food in the form of oblations or in the form of nourishment.

त्वं वातैररुणैर्यासि शंगयः—त्वं वातैर्वायुसदृशैररुणैररुणवर्णॆ- रश्वैः शंगयः सुखस्य गृहरूप आवासभूतः सन् यासि प्राप्नोषि यागगृहं (*tvaṃ vātairaruṇairyāsi śaṃgayaḥ—tvaṃ vātairvāyusadṛśairaruṇairaruṇavarṇè- raśvaiḥ śaṃgayaḥ sukhasya gṛharūpa āvāsabhūtaḥ san yāsi prāpnoṣi yāgagṛhaṃ*): O Agni, endowed with horses of ruddy brown colour that are swift like the wind (that is, seated in a chariot yoked with horses), having a comfortable dwelling, you are to come to our sacrificial house; this is the meaning

### Printed p. 406

*Running head (as supplied): [406 सायणभाष्यसहिता । मं. २. आ १ . सू.१] (*[406 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā | maṃ. 2. ā 1 . sū.1]*), as printed.*

(the sentence continues from the previous page). यद्वा अरुणैर्गमनशीलैर्वायुभिरुत्पन्नः सन् यासि वने (*yadvā aruṇairgamanaśīlairvāyubhirutpannaḥ san yāsi vane*): or it may also mean that, born in the forest from the ever-moving or blowing wind, you grow strong.

पूषा-सर्वस्य पोषकः (*pūṣā-sarvasya poṣakaḥ*): Agni, the nourisher of all, or the well-known deity Pūṣan (the print has अथना (*athanā*) for "or"); you are of the nature of such a deity.

नु-क्षिप्रं (*nu-kṣipraṃ*): "quickly". Yāska says of this word, नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा (*nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā*), that the word *nu* has many kinds of meaning (नि. १-४ (*ni. 1-4*)). This word is used when giving a reason and in comparison and so on. Here it is used in the sense of "quickly".

त्मना विधतः पासि—आत्मना, अनुग्रहरूपया स्वबुद्धैव विधतः परिचरतो यजमानान् पासि (*tmanā vidhataḥ pāsi—ātmanā, anugraharūpayā svabuddhaiva vidhataḥ paricarato yajamānān pāsi*): the *ā* of the word आत्मना (*ātmanā*) is elided for the convenience of the metre, and the word is *tmanā*. In the Ṛgveda, generally, wherever the word *ātmanā* would be expected, the word *tmanā* is used. The prayer to Agni is: protect, by your own mind in the form of favour, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, serving you.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 7 reads संहिता-त्री (*saṃhitā-trī*); standard label inserted. The last word of the second line of the Saṃhitā, split across two lines with a hyphen in the supplied text, is joined.]*

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने द्रविणो॒दा अ॑रं॒कृते॒ त्वं दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता र॑त्न॒धा अ॑सि ।
> त्वं भगो॑ नृपते॒ वस्व॑ ईशिषे॒ त्वं पा॒युर्दमे॒ यस्ते ऽवि॑धत् ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । द्रविणःदाः । अरंकृते । त्वं । देवः । सविता । रत्नधाः । असि ।
> त्वं । भगः । नृपते । वस्वः । ईशिषे । त्वं । पायुः । दमे । यः । ते । अविधत् ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वमरंकृते त्वामलंकुर्वते यजमानाय द्रविणोदाः । हिरण्यस्य
> दातासि । देवो द्योतमानः सविता सर्वस्य सत्कर्मसु प्रेरकस्त्वं रत्नधा रमणी-

> *he agne tvamaraṃkṛte tvāmalaṃkurvate yajamānāya draviṇodāḥ | hiraṇyasya*
> *dātāsi | devo dyotamānaḥ savitā sarvasya satkarmasu prerakastvaṃ ratnadhā ramaṇī-*

*(The bhāṣya of Ṛk 7 breaks off here, in the middle of a word, at रमणी- (*ramaṇī-*), at the end of the window.)*

### Printed p. 407

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. आ. ५. व. १८.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 407 (*[a. 2. ā. 5. va. 18.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 407*).*

*(Continuation of the bhāṣya of Ṛk 7 of Sūkta 1 of Maṇḍala 2, from mid-word at the end of the previous page.)*

> यानां धनानां मणिमुक्तादीनां धारयितासि । तथा हे नृपते नृणां पालकाग्ने
> त्वं भगो भजनीयः सन् वस्वो वसुनो धनस्येशिषे । समर्थो भवसि दातुं । यो
> यजमानो दमे यज्ञगृहे ते त्वामविधत् परिचरति तस्य पायुः पालकस्त्वमसि ॥

*Gist:* Agni gives gold to the sacrificer who adorns him; as Savitṛ he impels deeds, holds jewels; as Bhaga he rules wealth; he protects his servant.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). आरंकृते—निन्नन्नु अलंकरिसुव यजमाननिगॆ द्रविणोदाः—सुवर्णादिगळन्नु कॊडुववनागिद्दीयॆ (*āraṃkṛte—ninnannu alaṃkarisuva yajamānanigè draviṇodāḥ—suvarṇādigaḷannu kòḍuvavanāgiddīyè*) (to the sacrificer who adorns you, you are the giver of gold and the like). रत्नधाः त्वं—रमणीयवाद मणि मुक्तादिगळन्नु धरिसिरुव नीनु (*ratnadhāḥ tvaṃ—ramaṇīyavāda maṇi muktādigaḷannu dharisiruva nīnu*) (you who bear the delightful jewels, pearls and the like). देवः सविता—सकल कर्मगळिगू प्रेरकनादवनू, देवतात्मनू आद सवितृवागि (*devaḥ savitā—sakala karmagaḷigū prerakanādavanū, devatātmanū āda savitṛvāgi*) (as the divine Savitṛ, the impeller of all rites, divine in self). असि—आगिद्दीयॆ (*asi—āgiddīyè*) (you are). नृपते—नररिगॆल्ला पालकनाद ऎलै अग्निये (*nṛpate—nararigèllā pālakanāda èlai agniye*) (O Agni, protector of all men). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). भगः—पूज्यनाद भगनागि (*bhagaḥ—pūjyanāda bhaganāgi*) (as the revered Bhaga). वस्वः—धनक्कॆ (*vasvaḥ—dhanakkè*) (to wealth). ईशिषे—प्रभुवागिद्दीयॆ (*īśiṣe—prabhuvāgiddīyè*) (you are lord). यः—याव यज माननु (*yaḥ—yāva yaja mānanu*) (which sacrificer). दमे—यज्ञगृहदल्लि (*dame—yajñagṛhadalli*) (in the sacrificial house). ते—निन्नन्नु (*te—ninnannu*) (you). अनिधत्—उपचरिसुत्तानॆयो अवन (*anidhat—upacarisuttānèyo avana*) (whoever serves (the printed word is garbled), of him). पायुः—पालकनागि (*pāyuḥ—pālakanāgi*) (as protector). त्वं—नीनु (इद्दीयॆ) (*tvaṃ—nīnu (iddīyè)*) (you are).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you are the giver of wealth, who gives gold and the like to the sacrificer who adorns you. You, who bear delightful jewels, pearls and the like, are the divine Savitṛ, the impeller of all rites. O Agni, protector of all men, you, as the revered Bhaga, are lord of wealth. You are the protector of the sacrificer who serves you.

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are Dravinodas, to him who honours you : you are the divine Savitri, the possessor of precious things : protector of men, you are Bhaga and rule over wealth ; you are the cherisher of him who worships you in his dwelling.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषयगळु (*viśeṣayagaḷu*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 7)**

द्रविणोदाशि (*draviṇodāśi*) (as printed, for the word *draviṇodāḥ*): Yāska has written an extended explanation of this word:

द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्दनं द्रविणमुच्यते । यदेनदभिद्र- (*draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddanaṃ draviṇamucyate | yadenadabhidra-*)
वंति । बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवंति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः । (*vaṃti | balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravaṃti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ |*)
(नि. ८-१) (*(ni. 8-1)*)

Here the derivation of the word *draviṇodāḥ* is द्रविणं ददातीति द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇaṃ dadātīti draviṇodāḥ*): the word *draviṇa* has two meanings, wealth and strength; therefore *draviṇodāḥ* means the giver of wealth or of strength. This is the component meaning of this word.

### Printed p. 408

*Running head (as supplied): [408 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. आ. १ सू. १] (*[408 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. ā. 1 sū. 1]*).*

Besides, Yāska has given the explanation for the ṛk द्रविणोदा द्रवि णसः (*draviṇodā dravi ṇasaḥ*) (ऋ. सं. १-१५-७ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-15-7*)) thus:

द्रविणोदा यस्त्वं । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसानिन इति वा (*draviṇodā yastvaṃ | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasānina iti vā*)
द्रविणसस्तस्मात् पिब त्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचंति स्तुवंति, (*draviṇasastasmāt piba tviti vā | yajñeṣu devamīḷate | yācaṃti stuvaṃti,*)
वर्धयंति पूजयंतीति वा ॥ (*vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃtīti vā ‖*)

That is, the priests who desire wealth, oblations and the like pray to you, called Draviṇodāḥ, in the sacrifices, to drink soma; this is the main meaning. Here, although *draviṇodāḥ* is the nominative singular, how did it become an epithet of the word देवं (*devaṃ*), the accusative singular? The words must be supplied so as to give the sense द्रविणोदा यः देवः तं देवं (*draviṇodā yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devaṃ*), "that god who is the giver of wealth". द्रविणसः (*draviṇasaḥ*): since they pray to the god, for the sake of worshipping the deity, for wealth or oblations, the word द्रविणिसः (*draviṇisaḥ*) (as printed) means priests; and ईळते (*īḷate*) may be said to have many meanings: they beg, praise, extol, worship.

तत्को द्रविणोदा इंद्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः । (*tatko draviṇodā iṃdra iti krauṣṭukiḥ |*)
स बलधनयोर्दातृतमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥ (*sa baladhanayordātṛtamastasya ca sarvā balakṛtiḥ ‖*)

The component meaning of the word *draviṇodāḥ* has been given. But who is the deity called *draviṇodāḥ*? It is Indra who is said to be *draviṇodāḥ*, because the one who gives in excess the strength and wealth indicated by the word *draviṇa* is Indra himself; therefore Indra should be called *draviṇodāḥ*: this is the view of Krauṣṭuki (the print has अभिपाय (*abhipāya*) for "view").

अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहैष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते । (*athāpyagniṃ draviṇodasamāhaiṣa punaretasmājjāyate |*)
यो अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*yo aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*)

And he gives another meaning for this word. Indra created heaven and earth, and in the middle of them created Agni too. Therefore the word *draviṇodāḥ* may also be said to be Agni; to support this meaning they have given as an example the ṛk अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान (*aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna*).

अथाप्यतुयाजेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवंति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्येंद्र- (*athāpyatuyājeṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavaṃti | teṣāṃ punaḥ pātrasyeṃdra-*)
पानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति अथास्याह द्रविणोदाः (*pānamiti bhavati ‖ athāpyenaṃ somapānena stauti athāsyāha draviṇodāḥ*)
पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥ (*pibatu draviṇodasa iti ‖*)

### Printed p. 409

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १८] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 409 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 18] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 409*).*

Because it is said that in the sacrifices offered to the seasons Indra drinks soma from the vessel in the hands of the priests, and because Indra is praised with mantras connected with soma drinking, it is the custom to call the priests by the name द्रविणोदस (*draviṇodasa*) (plural). All this is the opinion of Krauṣṭuki.

अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः । आग्नेयेष्टेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रवि- (*ayamevāgnirdraviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ | āgneyeṣṭeva hi sūkteṣu dravi-*)
णोदसाः प्रवादा भवंति. (*ṇodasāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti.*)

Agni himself is *draviṇodāḥ*: this is the opinion of Śākapūṇi. For in the sūktas related to Agni, the priests, when praising Agni, use the word *draviṇodāḥ* as an epithet of Agni.

यथो एतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतम इति सर्वासु देवतास्वैश्वर्यं विद्यते । (*yatho etatsa baladhanayordātṛtama iti sarvāsu devatāsvaiśvaryaṃ vidyate |*)
यथो “ एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनं” इति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्निरो- (*yatho “ etadojaso jātamutamanya enaṃ” iti cāhetyayamapyagniro-*)
जसा बलेन मध्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं (*jasā balena madhyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ*)
सहसो यहुं ॥ (*sahaso yahuṃ ‖*)

Lordship is found in all the deities. Therefore Agni too gives strength and wealth. Because he gives strength and wealth, Agni too may be called *draviṇodāḥ*. Besides, the word *draviṇa* has the meaning of strength. There is a tradition that when Agni is produced, strength is used (the churning is done strongly), and so Agni was born of strength. For this very reason Agni is praised with the words सहसस्पुत्रं, ( सहसः-बलद, पुत्रं-पुत्रनाद अग्नियन्नु ) सहसः सूनुं, सहसो यहुं (*sahasasputraṃ, ( sahasaḥ-balada, putraṃ-putranāda agniyannu ) sahasaḥ sūnuṃ, sahaso yahuṃ*):

द्र्वन्नः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः । (*drvannaḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ |*)
सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥ (*sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ सं. २-७-६) (*(ṛ saṃ. 2-7-6)*)

त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुत । (*tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnavāhuta |*)
ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥ (*ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं ८-७५-३) (*(ṛ. saṃ 8-75-3)*)

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । (*agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho |*)
अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महिश्रवः ॥ (*asme dhehi jātavedo mahiśravaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२९-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-29-4)*)

In these ṛks the words सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*), सहसःसूनु (*sahasaḥsūnu*) and सहसो यहु (*sahaso yahu*) are used, respectively, in praising Agni. Therefore, although other deities too give strength and wealth, Agni is specially propounded by the word *draviṇodāḥ* (the supplied text ends here, at the end of the window).

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाम॑ग्ने॒ दनु [?]॒ आ वि॒श्वतिं॒ विश॒स्त्वां राजा॑नं सुवि॒दत्र॑मृंजते ।
> त्वं विश्वा॑नि स्वनीक पत्यसे॒ त्वं स॒हस्रा॑णि श॒ता दश॒ प्रति॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वां । अग्ने । दमे । आ । विश्वतिं । विशः । त्वां । राजानं । सुविदत्रं । ऋंजते ।
> त्वं । विश्वानि । सुअनेक [?] । पत्यसे । त्वं । सहस्राणि । शता । दश । प्रति ॥ ८ ॥

> *tvāṃ | agne | dame | ā | viśvatiṃ | viśaḥ | tvāṃ | rājānaṃ | suvidatraṃ | ṛṃjate |*
> *tvaṃ | viśvāni | suaneka [?] | patyase | tvaṃ | sahasrāṇi | śatā | daśa | prati ‖ 8 ‖*

*[As supplied, a line reading सायुणभाष्यं (*sāyuṇabhāṣyaṃ*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted. Two readings of Ṛk 8, one in the Saṃhitā and one in the Pada, are marked with a query, as they differ from the other lines.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने विश्वतिं यजमानानां पालकं त्वां विशो यजमाना दमे स्वकीये
> यज्ञगृह आ ! आसादयंति ॥ उपसर्गवशाद्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । तथा कृत्वा राजानं
> दीप्यमानं सुविदत्रं शोभनज्ञानमस्मदनुकूलचेतस्कं सुधनं वा त्वामृंजते ।
> प्रसाधयंति ॥ ऋंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मेति यास्कः ॥ यत एवं ततो हे स्वनीक शोभन-
> ज्वालारूपसेन त्वं विश्वानि सर्वाणि । हवींशीति शेषः ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया ।
> विश्वेषां हविषामाज्यसोमपुरोडाशादीनां पत्यसे । ईश्वरो भवसि ॥ ईश्वरनामै-
> तत् । इरज्यति पत्यत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ यद्वा पतिभावमाचरसि त्वं तु सहस्राणि
> शता शतानि दश एतत्संख्याकानि प्रति। एतत्संख्याकानामभिमतसाधनानां प्रतिनिधिरित्यर्थः ।
> प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोरिति कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ तैर्यत्पलं भवति तत्त्वया
> लभ्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Sacrificers serve Agni, protector, radiant, wise; he is lord of all oblations and, as substitute, brings about wishes in tens, hundreds, thousands.

*[As supplied, a line reading ॥ त्रैपदार्थ ॥ (*‖ traipadārtha ‖*) stands, with block marks, inside the bhāṣya block where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; the following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). विश्वतिं—यजमानर पालकनाद (*viśvatiṃ—yajamānara pālakanāda*) (of the protector of sacrificers). त्वां—निन्नन्नु (*tvāṃ—ninnannu*) (you). विशः— यजमानरु (*viśaḥ— yajamānaru*) (the sacrificers). दमे—तम्मयज्ञगृहदल्लि (*dame—tammayajñagṛhadalli*) (in their own sacrificial house). आ—उपचरिसुत्तारॆ (*ā—upacarisuttārè*) (serve). राजानं—प्रकाशमाननू (*rājānaṃ—prakāśamānanū*) (the radiant). सुविदत्रं—शोभनात्मकवाद ज्ञान अथवा धनवुळ्ळवनू आद (*suvidatraṃ—śobhanātmakavāda jñāna athavā dhanavuḷḷavanū āda*) (the one with excellent knowledge or wealth). त्वां—निन्नन्नु (*tvāṃ—ninnannu*) (you). यंजते— अलंकरिसि पूजिसुत्तारॆ (*yaṃjate— alaṃkarisi pūjisuttārè*) (adorn and worship). स्वनीक—ज्वालारूपवाद सेनॆयुळ्ळ अग्निये (*svanīka—jvālārūpavāda senèyuḷḷa agniye*) (O Agni with an army in the form of flames). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). विश्वानि- सकल हविस्सुगळिगू (*viśvāni- sakala havissugaḷigū*) (of all oblations). पत्यसे—प्रभुवागिद्दीयॆ (*patyase—prabhuvāgiddīyè*) (you are lord). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). सहस्राणि—सहस्रसंख्याकवू (*sahasrāṇi—sahasrasaṃkhyākavū*) (thousand-fold). शता—शतसंख्याकवू (*śatā—śatasaṃkhyākavū*) (hundred-fold). दश—दशसंख्याकवू आद (ऎंदरॆ) इष्टार्थगळिगॆ (*daśa—daśasaṃkhyākavū āda (èṃdarè) iṣṭārthagaḷigè*) (ten-fold, that is, to the desired objects). प्रति—प्रतिनिधियागि अवुगळन्नु साधिसिकॊडुववनागिद्दीयॆ. (*prati—pratinidhiyāgi avugaḷannu sādhisikòḍuvavanāgiddīyè.*) (as substitute, you are the accomplisher of them).

*[As supplied, a line reading भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*) stands, with block marks, where the Bhāvārtha label belongs; the following lines are given as prose; standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the sacrificers serve you in their sacrificial house. They adorn and worship you, who are radiant and endowed with excellent knowledge or wealth. O Agni, who have an army in the form of flames, you are lord of all oblations (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 411

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २ अ. ५ व. १८] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 411 (*[a. 2 a. 5 va. 18] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 411*).*

You are the accomplisher, as substitute, of the desired objects, tenfold, hundredfold and thousandfold.

**Printed English translation**

The people adore you, Agni, the protector of the people in their dwellings ; they propitiate you as a benevolent sovereign ; leader of a radiant host, you are lord over all offerings ; you are the distributor of tens, and hundreds, and thousands (of good things).

*(The printed English reads "dwel-ings" with a printed hyphen; joined as "dwellings".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 8)**

सुविदत्रं (*suvidatraṃ*): formed with the prefix सु (*su*) from the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*), this word means one with good knowledge.

ऋंजते (*ṛṃjate*): they please, they worship. Yāska says in the Nirukta: ऋंजतिः प्रसाधन- कर्मा । आ व ऋंजसे ऊर्जां व्युष्टिषु इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*ṛṃjatiḥ prasādhana- karmā | ā va ṛṃjase ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (नि. ६-२१ (*ni. 6-21*)).

विश्वानि पत्यसे—सर्वाणि हवींषीति शेषः । षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । विश्वेषां हविषामाज्यसोमपुरोडाशादीनां पत्यसे ईश्वरो भवसि (*viśvāni patyase—sarvāṇi havīṃṣīti śeṣaḥ | ṣaṣṭhyarthe dvitīyā | viśveṣāṃ haviṣāmājyasomapuroḍāśādīnāṃ patyase īśvaro bhavasi*): here the bhāṣyakāra has said that the word हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*) must be supplied with the word *viśvāni*, and that the accusative case has the sense of the genitive. Therefore *viśvāni* means: you are the lord (master) of the sacrificial materials such as oblations, ghee, soma and puroḍāśa; so Agni is praised (the print has ऎनरॆ (*ènarè*) for "means"). Since the word पत्यते (*patyate*) (*patyase* being the second person singular) is read among the four names of lordship beginning with इरज्यति पत्यते (*irajyati patyate*) (नि. ३-११ (*ni. 3-11*)), *patyase* means "you are lord".

सहस्राणि शता दश प्रति (*sahasrāṇi śatā daśa prati*): Agni is praised as the giver of desired objects in tens, hundreds and thousands. Here, although only the prefix *prati* is present, the word प्रतिनिधि (*pratinidhi*) (substitute) corresponding to it must be supplied. Or it may also be understood that you alone provide desired objects that could be obtained from thousands of people.

स्वनीक—शोभनज्वालारूपसेन (*svanīka—śobhanajvālārūpasena*): the best flames are Agni's army; that is, the purport is one who shines with radiant flames. This word is used of Agni in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks ऋ. सं. ४-६-६, ६-१५-१६, ७-१-२३, ७-३-६ (*ṛ. saṃ. 4-6-6, 6-15-16, 7-1-23, 7-3-6*).

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाम॑ेग्ने [?] पि॒तर॑मि॒ष्टिभि॒र्नर॒स्तां भ्रा॒त्राय॒ शम्या॑तनू॒रुचं॑ ।
> त्वं पु॒त्रो भ॑वसि॒ यस्त्ये वि॑ध॒त्त्वं सखा॑ सु॒शेवः॑ पास्त्या॒दृषः॑ [?] ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वां । आग्ने [?] । पितरं । इष्टिभिः । नरः । त्वां । भ्रात्राय । शम्या । तनूरुचं ।
> त्वं । पुत्रः । भवसि । यः । ते । अविधत् । त्वं । सखा । सुशेवः । पासि । अधृषः ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने पितरं पालकं त्वां नरो नेतारो यजमाना इष्टिभिरेषणसाधनै-
> र्यागैर्यजंत इति शेषः । पितृवत्पालनाय यजंत इत्यर्थः । तथा तनूरुचं
> शरीराणां दीपकं शरीरेषु दीप्यमानं वैश्वानरात्मना त्वां भ्रात्राय भ्रातृत्वाय
> सौभ्रात्राय शम्या ॥ कर्मनामृतत् ॥ कर्मणा यजंत इति शेषः । यद्योभयत्र
> वक्ष्यमाणेनाविधदित्यनेन संबंधः । हे अग्ने यो नरस्ते त्वामविधत् परिचरति
> तस्य त्वं पुत्रो भवसि । पुत्रवत्पालयिता भवसि ! तथा त्वं सखा समानख्यानः सखिवद्धित-
> कारी सुशेवः ॥ शेवमिति सुखनाम ॥ सुष्टु सुखकारी सन् आधृष अधर्षकात्मा पासि ।
> रक्षसि । पितृत्वकामाय पितृत्वेन भ्रातृत्वकामाय भ्रातृत्वेन पुत्रत्वकामाय पुत्र-
> स्थानीयो भवसि । त्रिप्रकारेण रक्षसीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Sacrificers serve Agni as father, brother (through rites) and he is son and friend to his servant, protecting in three ways, a mighty helper.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). पितरं पालकनाद (*pitaraṃ pālakanāda*) (the protector (the entry is printed without a dash)). त्वां—निन्नन्नु (*tvāṃ—ninnannu*) (you). नरः—यजमानरु (*naraḥ—yajamānaru*) (the sacrificers). इष्टिभिः—यागादिगळिंद (पितृवन्नु पूजिसुवंतॆ पूजिसुत्तारॆ) (*iṣṭibhiḥ—yāgādigaḷiṃda (pitṛvannu pūjisuvaṃtè pūjisuttārè)*) (by sacrifices and the like (they worship as one worships a father)). तनूरुचं—शरीरक्कॆ कांति यन्नु कॊडतक्क (*tanūrucaṃ—śarīrakkè kāṃti yannu kòḍatakka*) (the one who gives lustre to the body). त्वां—निन्नन्नु (*tvāṃ—ninnannu*) (you). शर्मा—कर्मगळिंद (*śarmā—karmagaḷiṃda*) (by rites). भ्रात्राय—सहोदरनंतॆयू उपचरिसुत्तारॆ (*bhrātrāya—sahodaranaṃtèyū upacarisuttārè*) (as a brother (they serve)). यः—याव यजमाननु (*yaḥ—yāva yajamānanu*) (which sacrificer). ते—निन्नन्नु (*te—ninnannu*) (you). अविधत्—उपचरिसुत्तानॆयो (अवनिगॆ) (*avidhat—upacarisuttānèyo (avanigè)*) (serves (him)). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). पुत्रः - पुत्रनागि (*putraḥ - putranāgi*) (as son). भवसि—आगुत्तीयॆ (*bhavasi—āguttīyè*) (you become). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). सखा—स्नेहित नंतॆ (*sakhā—snehita naṃtè*) (like a friend). सुशेवः—सुखकारियागिरुत्ता (*suśevaḥ—sukhakāriyāgiruttā*) (while being a giver of comfort). अधृषः—आसक्तनागिरुत्तलू (*adhṛṣaḥ—āsaktanāgiruttalū*) (while being attached (as printed)). पासि—रक्षिसुत्तीयॆ. (*pāsi—rakṣisuttīyè.*) (you protect).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads बावार्थ (*bāvārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the sacrificers serve you, the protector, by sacrifices and other rites as one serves a father, and you, the giver of lustre to the body, as a brother; and for the one who serves you (the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 413

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व. १८] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 413 (*[a. 2. a 5. va. 18] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 413*).*

*(Continuation of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 9 of Sūkta 1 of Maṇḍala 2, from mid-sentence at the end of the previous page.)*

...for the sacrificer who serves you, you are a helper in the form of a son; and you protect, remaining attached and giving comfort, like a friend.

**Printed English translation**

(Devout) men (worship) you, Agni, as a father, with secred rites; they (cherish) you, who are the illuminator of the body, with acts (of kindness), as a brother ; you are as a son to him who propitiates you, and you protect us, a faithful and firm friend.

*(The printed English reads "secred" for "sacred" [sic] and ends a line with a printed hyphen in "protect-"; it is reproduced as supplied, the line-end hyphen being joined.)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 9)**

In this ṛk Agni is praised with words that indicate love and trust: father, brother, son, friend.

पितरं—पालकं (*pitaraṃ—pālakaṃ*): one who protects people like a father. The use of the word "father" here indicates Agni's love and trust towards the people who worship him.

तनूरुचं—शरीराणां दीपकं, शरीरेषु दीप्त्यमानं वैश्वानरात्मना (*tanūrucaṃ—śarīrāṇāṃ dīpakaṃ, śarīreṣu dīptyamānaṃ vaiśvānarātmanā*) (as printed): one who shines in the bodies of creatures in the form of heat. The heat in the bodies of creatures is the very form of Agni. The digesting of food and the like in the stomach is also the work of Agni. Agni, being in such a form, has the name Vaiśvānara fire.

त्वं पुत्रो भवसि यस्तेऽविधत् (*tvaṃ putro bhavasi yaste 'vidhat*): the purport is that to the man who serves you with sacrifices and the like you are dear and a protector like a son.

त्वं सखा सुशेवः पासि अधृषः (*tvaṃ sakhā suśevaḥ pāsi adhṛṣaḥ*): you protect us like a friend who gives comfort, that is, who desires our good. That is, the main purport is that you, Agni, protect us in many ways, like a father, like a brother, like a son and like a friend.

*Gist:* Agni is resplendent, honoured when near, lord of renowned food and wealth; he burns for the sacrificer and accomplishes the sacrifice and its fruit.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). ऋभुः—अतिशयवागि प्रकाशिसुववनागिद्दीयॆ (अथवा मेधावियागिद्दीयॆ) (*ṛbhuḥ—atiśayavāgi prakāśisuvavanāgiddīyè (athavā medhāviyāgiddīyè)*) (you are exceedingly resplendent (or you are wise)). आके—नीनु समीपदल्लि प्रत्यक्षनागिरुवागले (*āke—nīnu samīpadalli pratyakṣanāgiruvāgale*) (just when you are present near). नमस्यः— पूजिसल्पडतक्कवनु (*namasyaḥ— pūjisalpaḍatakkavanu*) (one to be worshipped). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). क्षुमतः—सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धवाद (*kṣumataḥ—sarvatra prasiddhavāda*) (of the renowned). वाजस्य—अन्नक्कू (*vājasya—annakkū*) (to food). रायः—धनक्कू (*rāyaḥ—dhanakkū*) (to wealth). ईशिषे—प्रभुवागिद्दीयॆ ॥ (ऎलै प्रभुवे) त्वं—नीनु (*īśiṣe—prabhuvāgiddīyè ‖ (èlai prabhuve) tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you are lord (the entry also contains the printed ॥ and the address "O lord", and the next word "you")). वि भासि—अतिशय वागि प्रज्वलिसुत्तीयॆ (*vi bhāsi—atiśaya vāgi prajvalisuttīyè*) (you shine exceedingly). दावने—अंधकारवन्नु होलाडिसुवुदक्कागि अथवा हविस्सन्नु अर्पिसुव यजमाननिगागि (*dāvane—aṃdhakāravannu holāḍisuvudakkāgi athavā havissannu arpisuva yajamānanigāgi*) (for dispelling darkness, or for the sacrificer who offers oblations). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अनु धक्षि—काष्ठादिगळन्नु दहिसुत्तीयॆ (*anu dhakṣi—kāṣṭhādigaḷannu dahisuttīyè*) (you burn the firewood and the like). यज्ञं—यज्ञवन्नु (*yajñaṃ—yajñavannu*) (the sacrifice). विशिक्षुः—विशेषवाद रीतियल्लि साधिसुववनागि (*viśikṣuḥ—viśeṣavāda rītiyalli sādhisuvavanāgi*) (as the accomplisher in a special way). असि—आगिद्दीयॆ (हागॆये) (*asi—āgiddīyè (hāgèye)*) (you are (likewise)). आतनिः—आ यज्ञक्कॆ फलदातृवागियू आगिद्दीयॆ. (*ātaniḥ—ā yajñakkè phaladātṛvāgiyū āgiddīyè.*) (you are also the giver of fruit to that sacrifice).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you shine exceedingly. You are to be worshipped just when you are present near. You are lord of the renowned food and wealth. You who shine exceedingly burn the firewood and the like for the sacrificer who offers oblations. You are the accomplisher of the sacrifice in a special way, and also the giver of fruit to that sacrifice.

### Printed p. 415

*Running head (as supplied): [५ २. ५ ५. व. १८. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 415 (*[5 2. 5 5. va. 18. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 415*), as printed.*

*[As supplied, the label line of the printed English reads Englih Tranlation (*Englih Tranlation*) (sic), run on without a blank line; standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

You, Agni, are (ever) resplendent, and are to be glorified when present ; you are lord over all renowned food and riches ; you shine brightly, and you consume (the oblation) for him who offers it ; you are the especial accomplisher of the sacrifice, and bestower (of its rewards).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 10)**

ऋभुः—उरुभासमानो मेधावी वा (*ṛbhuḥ—urubhāsamāno medhāvī vā*): very brilliant, or wise (intelligent): this is Sāyaṇa's explanation. It may also be said to be the form of the deity called Ṛbhu, but the meaning given by Sāyaṇa is the fitting one here.

आके नमस्यः (*āke namasyaḥ*): the word आके (*āke*) is read among the names of "near" (नि ३-९ (*ni 3-9*)) and among the names of "far" (नि. ३-२० (*ni. 3-20*)). Here Sāyaṇa says अंतिके सन्निधावेव नमस्को नमस्कार्यः स्तुत्य इत्यर्थः । इतरदेवतावन्मंत्रप्रतिपाद्याकारेण स्तुत्यो न भवसि किंतु प्रत्यक्ष इत्यर्थः (*aṃtike sannidhāveva namasko namaskāryaḥ stutya ityarthaḥ | itaradevatāvanmaṃtrapratipādyākāreṇa stutyo na bhavasi kiṃtu pratyakṣa ityarthaḥ*). The other deities are not visible to our eyes; they are far away. Therefore, as in the śruti sentence परोक्षं वा अन्ये ते वा इज्यंते (*parokṣaṃ vā anye te vā ijyaṃte*) (तै. सं. १-७-३-१ (*tai. saṃ. 1-7-3-1*)), they have to be worshipped indirectly (*parokṣa*) with hymns and the like. But the matter of Agni is not so; since Agni is directly visible close to us, besides praising him with hymns and the like I make a salutation to him as he stands facing me. Therefore the use of the words "near" and "to be saluted" here is proper in the matter of Agni.

त्वं वाजस्य क्षुमतः राय ईशिषे (*tvaṃ vājasya kṣumataḥ rāya īśiṣe*): क्षुमतः (*kṣumataḥ*) means making a sound, that is, that which everybody is asking for as needed. O Agni, you are the lord of the food that everyone asks for and of wealth and other materials: this is the purport.

त्वं वि भास्यनु धक्षि दावने (*tvaṃ vi bhāsyanu dhakṣi dāvane*): for the sacrificer who offers oblations you shine, and burning the firewood and the like and the oblations of ghee and the like that are offered in Agni, you blaze well for the sacrificer's attainment of joy: this is the purport.

त्वं विशिक्षुः असि यज्ञं (*tvaṃ viśikṣuḥ asi yajñaṃ*): one who teaches the sacrificer and the priests, so that they understand well, the programmes that have to be carried out in the sacrifice. Since you know well the duties of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu and the others, you teach them the sacrificial procedure: this is the purport.

आतनिगॆ—फलस्य सर्वतो विस्तारयिता (*ātanigè—phalasya sarvato vistārayitā*) (the print has आतनिगॆ (*ātanigè*) for *ātaniḥ*): one who gives in abundance the fruits that the sacrificial rites and the like should obtain; this is the purport (the supplied text ends here, at the end of the window).

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ अदि॑तिर्देव दा॒शुषे॒ त्वं होत्रा॒भार॑ती वर्धसे गि॒रा।
> त्वमीळा॑ श॒तहि॑मासि॒ दक्ष॑से॒ त्वं वृ॑त्र॒हा व॑सुपते॒ सर॑स्वती ॥ ११ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । अदितिः । देव । दाशुषे । त्वं । होत्रा । भारती । वर्धसे । गिरा ।
> त्वं । इळा । शतहिमा । असि । दक्षसे । त्वं । वृत्रहा । वसुपते । सरस्वती ॥ ११ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने देव त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानायादितिरखंडयिता परि-
> पालयितासि । यद्वा आदीना भूमिरसि । किंच त्वं होत्रा होमनिष्प्रादका भारती
> भरतस्यादित्यस्यादित्यसंबंधिनी रश्मिरूपा सती गिरा स्तुत्या वर्धसे । प्रवृद्दो भवसि ।
> किंच त्वं शतहिमा । हिमशब्दः कालोपलक्षकः । अपरिमितकाला नित्येळा भूमिरसि ।
> तादृशी सती दक्षसे दानाय समर्था भवसि ॥तिज उत्तरत्वादनिघातः ॥तथा हे वसुपते
> धनपालक वृत्रहा पापादेर्हंता त्वं सरस्वती । सरणवान्वायुः । तत्संबंधिन्येतन्नि-
> यामका माध्यमिकासि । आदित्याग्नि वायूनां संबंधिन्नो भारतीळासरस्वत्याख्या
> यास्तिस्रो देव्यः संति ता अपि त्वमेवेत्यर्थः 8

*(The bhāṣya block ends with the printed character 8 (*8*), in place of a danda, as supplied.)*

*Gist:* Agni is Aditi to the donor, Hotrā and Bhāratī (sun's rays), Ilā (earth) of a hundred seasons, and Sarasvatī (wind).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देव—देवतात्मनाद (*deva—devatātmanāda*) (of divine self). अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). दाशुषे—हविस्सन्नु अर्पिसुव यजमाननिगॆ (*dāśuṣe—havissannu arpisuva yajamānanigè*) (to the sacrificer who offers oblations). अदितिः—पूर्णपालकळाद आदितियागि इद्दीयॆ (*aditiḥ—pūrṇapālakaḷāda āditiyāgi iddīyè*) (you are Aditi, the complete protector). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). होत्रा—होमसंपादकियाद होत्रळागियू (*hotrā—homasaṃpādakiyāda hotraḷāgiyū*) (as Hotrā, the accomplisher of homa). भारती—आदित्यसंबंधियाद भारतिया गियू (*bhāratī—ādityasaṃbaṃdhiyāda bhāratiyā giyū*) (as Bhāratī, connected with the Āditya (the entry is divided by a line break in the print)). गिरा—स्तुतियिंद (*girā—stutiyiṃda*) (by praise). वर्धसे—प्रवृद्धनागुत्तीयॆ (*vardhase—pravṛddhanāguttīyè*) (you thrive). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). शतहिमा— शतसंख्याकवाद कालवुळ्ळ ऎंदरॆ नित्यळाद (*śatahimā— śatasaṃkhyākavāda kālavuḷḷa èṃdarè nityaḷāda*) (of a hundred seasons, that is, the eternal one). इळा—इळारूपदल्लि (*iḷā—iḷārūpadalli*) (in the form of Iḷā). आसि—इद्दीयॆ. (मत्तु) (*āsi—iddīyè. (mattu)*) (you are (and)). दक्षसे—दानादिगळिगू समर्थनागिद्दीयॆ (*dakṣase—dānādigaḷigū samarthanāgiddīyè*) (you are capable of giving and the like). वसुपते—धनक्कॆ पालकनाद ऎलै अग्निये वृत्रहा—पापादिगळ हंतकनाद (*vasupate—dhanakkè pālakanāda èlai agniye vṛtrahā—pāpādigaḷa haṃtakanāda*) (O Agni, protector of wealth, destroyer of sin and the like). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). सरस्वती—(वायुसंबंधियाद) (*sarasvatī—(vāyusaṃbaṃdhiyāda)*) ((connected with the wind)). असि— सरस्वतियागियू इद्दीयॆ. (*asi— sarasvatiyāgiyū iddīyè.*) (you are also Sarasvatī).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads भानुवार (*bhānuvāra*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, of divine self, to the sacrificer who offers oblations you are Aditi, the complete protector. You thrive by praise, as Hotrā, the accomplisher of homa, and as Bhāratī, connected with the Āditya (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 417

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. १९ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 417 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 19 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 417*).*

You are in the form of Iḷā (the earth), the eternal; and you are capable of giving and the like. O Agni, protector of wealth, destroyer of sin and the like, you are also Sarasvatī, connected with the wind.

**Printed English translation**

You, divine Agni, are Aditi to the donor of the oblation; you are Hotra and Bharati, and thrive by praise ; you are Ila of a hundred winters to him who makes you gifts ; you, lord of wealth, are the destroyer of Vritra, Saraswati.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 11)**

अदितिः—अखंडयिता परिपालयितासि । यद्वा अदीना भूमिरसि (*aditiḥ—akhaṃḍayitā paripālayitāsi | yadvā adīnā bhūmirasi*): you are an uninterrupted protector, that is, you are always protecting us; or you are a nourisher like the earth. The word *aditi* is read among the names of the earth (नि. २-५ (*ni. 2-5*)), among the names of speech (नि ३-२३ (*ni 3-23*)), among the names of the cow (नि ३-९ (*ni 3-9*)) and among the names of heaven and earth (here *āditī* in the dual) (नि ३-२२ (*ni 3-22*)). Here the bhāṣyakāra has taken the meaning "earth". The extended explanation and discussion of the word *aditi* we have given in ऋ. सं. भाग 8, पुट 559 (*ṛ. saṃ. bhāga 8, puṭa 559*).

भारती भरतस्यादित्यस्य संबंधिनी रश्मिरूपा सती (*bhāratī bharatasyādityasya saṃbaṃdhinī raśmirūpā satī*): Bharata is one of the twelve Ādityas. The lustre of an Āditya is called भा (*bhā*). Therefore *Bhāratī* means the light of the sun, or the Agni that exists in the sun's disc in the form of light. Here a relation of the rays of Agni with the rays of the Āditya is stated. Since it is said that Agni himself exists in the heavenly region in the form of the sun, there is a relation between the rays of the sun and the rays of Agni.

इळा—भूमिरसि (*iḷā—bhūmirasi*): since the word *iḷā* is read among the names of the earth (नि. २-५ (*ni. 2-5*)), the meaning is the earth.

सरस्वती—सरणवान्वायुः । तत्संबंधिन्येतन्नियामका माध्यमिकासि (*sarasvatī—saraṇavānvāyuḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhinyetanniyāmakā mādhyamikāsi*): here the bhāṣyakāra has explained the word *sarasvatī* as the wind, which has a moving nature, and therefore as a deity of the middle region (the atmosphere). आदित्याग्निवायूनां संबंधिन्यो भारतीळासरस्वत्याख्या यास्तिस्रो देव्यः संति ता असि त्वमेवेत्यर्थः (*ādityāgnivāyūnāṃ saṃbaṃdhinyo bhāratīḷāsarasvatyākhyā yāstisro devyaḥ saṃti tā asi tvamevetyarthaḥ*): that is, Agni is praised as being the very form of the three goddesses named Bhāratī, Iḷā and Sarasvatī, connected with the Āditya, fire and wind.

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ सुभृ॑त उत्त॒मं वय॒स्तव॑ स्पा॒र्हे वर्ण॒ आ सं॒दृशि॒ त्रियः॑ [?] ।
> त्वं वाजः॑ प्र॒तर॑णो ब्र॒हन्न॑सि॒ त्वं र॒यिर्ब॑हु॒लो वि॒श्वत॑स्पृ॒थुः ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । सुभृतः । उत्तमं । वयः । तव । स्पार्हे । वर्णे । आ । संदृशि । श्रियः ।
> त्वं । वाजः । प्रतरणः । बृहन् । असि । त्वं । रयिः । बहुलः । विश्वतः । पृथुः ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वं सुभृतः सुष्टु पोषितः सन् उत्तमं निरतिशयं वयोऽन्नमा-
> युष्यं वा त्वमसि । तत्संपादकोऽसित्यर्थः । तथा तव स्पार्हे स्पृहणीये वर्णॆ
> लोहितशुक्लादिलक्षणे संदृशि सम्यग्दर्शनीये श्रिय ऐश्वर्याणि कांतयो वाश्रित्य
> वर्तंते ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ किंच त्वं वाजोऽन्नं । तत्साध-
> कत्वात्ताच्छब्दं । अन्नसाधक इत्यर्थः । प्रतरणः प्रतारयिता पापात् । अत एव बृहन्
> महानसि । तथा त्वं रयिर्धनरूपोऽसि । बहुलः सर्वविषयबाहुल्योपेतो विश्वतः
> पृथुविस्तीर्णः प्रख्यात इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Well nourished, Agni gives the best food or life; fortunes abide in his lovely colour; he is food, saviour from sin, great wealth, renowned.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). सुभृतः—चॆन्नागि पोषितनादाग (*subhṛtaḥ—cènnāgi poṣitanādāga*) (when well nourished). उत्तमं— निरतिशयवाद (*uttamaṃ— niratiśayavāda*) (of the highest). वयः—अन्न (आयुस्स) संपादकवागुवॆ (*vayaḥ—anna (āyussa) saṃpādakavāguvè*) (you are the accomplisher of food (life)). तव—निन्न (*tava—ninna*) (your). स्पार्हे—आकर्षक वादुदू (*spārhe—ākarṣaka vādudū*) (attractive). वर्णे—लोहितादिरूपवुळ्ळद्दू (*varṇe—lohitādirūpavuḷḷaddū*) (having the form red and the like). सुदृशि—दर्शनीयवादुदू आद स्वरूपदल्लि (*sudṛśi—darśanīyavādudū āda svarūpadalli*) (in the visible form (the printed word is "sudṛśi")). श्रियः—ऐश्वर्यगळु अथवा कांतिगळु (*śriyaḥ—aiśvaryagaḷu athavā kāṃtigaḷu*) (fortunes or splendours). आ—अडगिवॆ (*ā—aḍagivè*) (abide). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). वाजः—अन्नवु (अन्नसाध कनु) (*vājaḥ—annavu (annasādha kanu)*) (food (the accomplisher of food)). प्रतरणः—(पापदिंद) दाटिसतक्कवनु (*prataraṇaḥ—(pāpadiṃda) dāṭisatakkavanu*) (the one who carries (across sin)). बृहन्—महात्मनागि (*bṛhan—mahātmanāgi*) (great). असि—आगिद्दीयॆ (*asi—āgiddīyè*) (you are). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). रयिः—धनरूपनागिद्दीयॆ (*rayiḥ—dhanarūpanāgiddīyè*) (you are wealth). बहुलः—नाना स्वरूपवुळ्ळवनू (*bahulaḥ—nānā svarūpavuḷḷavanū*) (of manifold forms). विश्वतः—ऎल्ला कडॆगळल्लू (*viśvataḥ—èllā kaḍègaḷallū*) (everywhere). पृथुः—विस्त्रतवादवनू आगिद्दीयॆ. **भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, when you are well nourished you become the supreme accomplisher of food. In your attractive form, red and the like, pleasing to behold, fortunes lie hidden. You yourself are the accomplisher of food. You carry us across sin; you are great and of the form of wealth, of manifold forms, spread out and extensive everywhere.

**Printed English translation**

When, well-cherished Agni, you are (the giver of) excellent food : in your desirable and delightful hues, beauties (abound) : you (are) food : (you are) the transporter (beyond sin); you are mighty ; you are wealth ; you are manifold, and everywhere diffused.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 12)**

स्पार्हे वर्णे—स्पृहणीये वर्णे लोहितशुक्लादि लक्षणे । (*spārhe varṇe—spṛhaṇīye varṇe lohitaśuklādi lakṣaṇe |*) The flames of Agni are very excellent and are endowed with colours such as red and white.

प्रतरणः—प्रतारयिता पापात् । (*prataraṇaḥ—pratārayitā pāpāt |*) One who carries us across because of sins, that is, one who protects us so that sins do not cover us.

विश्वतः पृथुः (*viśvataḥ pṛthuḥ*): one who is renowned everywhere; or one who is spread out and pervades widely everywhere, that is, one who is pervasive in the three worlds called earth, atmosphere and heaven.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वामादित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रा इंद्रादय आस्यं स्वकीयं मुखं
> भक्षणपानादिसाधनं चक्रिर इति वक्ष्यमाणेन संबंधः । तथा हे कवे क्रांतप्रज्ञ
> त्वामेव शुचयः शुद्धा दीप्ता ना देवा जिह्वां स्वकीयजिह्वास्थानीयमास्वादन-

> रातिषाचः । रातिर्दानं दत्तं हविरादि धनं वा । तेन समवेता देवा अध्वरेषु
> यज्ञेषु सच्चिरे । सेवंते । त्वामेव प्रतीक्ष्यंते विना त्वया स्वेषां हविर्भक्षणायो-
> गात् । एवं कृत्वा त्वे त्वयि देवाः सर्व आहुतिं सर्वतो दत्तं हविरदंति । भक्ष-
> यंति । एवं सर्वदेवोपकारिणं महानुभावं सौमीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The Adityas made Agni their mouth and the gods their tongue; the gods await him at sacrifices and eat the oblation through him.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वां—निन्नन्नु (*tvāṃ—ninnannu*) (you). आदित्यासः—अदितिपुत्रराद इंद्रादिगळु (*ādityāsaḥ—aditiputrarāda iṃdrādigaḷu*) (the Ādityas, Indra and the other sons of Aditi). आस्यः—हविस्सन्नु भक्षिसुव मुखवन्नागि (माडिकॊंडरु) (*āsyaḥ—havissannu bhakṣisuva mukhavannāgi (māḍikòṃḍaru)*) (as the mouth that eats the oblation (made); printed "āsyaḥ", the Pada reads otherwise). कवे—क्रांतप्रज्ञनाद अग्निये (*kave—krāṃtaprajñanāda agniye*) (O Kavi, Agni of far-reaching wisdom). त्वां—निन्नन्ने (*tvāṃ—ninnanne*) (you alone). शुचयः—प्रकाशमानराद देवतॆगळु (*śucayaḥ—prakāśamānarāda devatègaḷu*) (the resplendent gods). जिह्वां—आस्वादनॆमाडतक्क नालिगॆ यन्नागि (*jihvāṃ—āsvādanèmāḍatakka nāligè yannāgi*) (as the tongue with which to taste). चक्रिरे—माडिकॊंडरु (*cakrire—māḍikòṃḍaru*) (they have made). त्वां—निन्नन्ने (*tvāṃ—ninnanne*) (you alone). रातिषाचः—हविस्सिन रूपद धनवन्नु हॊंदिद देवतॆगळु (*rātiṣācaḥ—havissina rūpada dhanavannu hòṃdida devatègaḷu*) (the gods who have obtained wealth in the form of the oblation). अध्वरेषु—यज्ञगळल्लि (*adhvareṣu—yajñagaḷalli*) (at the sacrifices). सश्चिते—सेविसुत्तारॆ (*saścite—sevisuttārè*) (they serve (printed "saścite")). त्वे—निन्नल्लि (निन्न मूलकवे) (*tve—ninnalli (ninna mūlakave)*) (in you (through you)). देवाः—सकल देवतॆगळू (*devāḥ—sakala devatègaḷū*) (all the gods). आहुतं—अर्पितवाद (*āhutaṃ—arpitavāda*) (offered). हविः—हविस्सन्नु (*haviḥ—havissannu*) (the oblation). अदंति— भक्षिसुत्तारॆ. (*adaṃti— bhakṣisuttārè.*) (they eat).

*(The printed Pratipadārtha has the word for "tongue" divided by a line break, joined here in the gloss; two printed forms differ from the Pada and are kept as printed.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Kavi Agni, Indra and the other gods have made you both their mouth that eats the oblation and their tongue that tastes. The gods who have obtained wealth in the form of the oblation serve you alone at the sacrifices. All the gods eat the oblation offered to them through you alone.

**Printed English translation**

The Adityas have made, you Agni, their mouth ; the pure (deities) have made you Kavi, their tongue : the (gods), the givers of wealth, depend upon you at sacrifices ; they eat the offered oblation through you.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 13)**

त्वां अग्ने आदित्यासः आस्यं चक्रिरे (*tvāṃ agne ādityāsaḥ āsyaṃ cakrire*): the Ādityas, that is, the sons of Aditi, the mother of the gods (Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman), or the gods, have made you their mouth. That is, the gods do not come visibly to the sacrificial ground and accept oblations and the like, in a form with a body and so on, so that all may see them. But they accept the oblations and the like that are offered in Agni, accompanied by the respective mantras and addressed to the gods. The oblation offered in Agni goes and reaches the gods; therefore Agni is like a mouth for the gods. The purport is that the gods accept the oblation through him. (The words "having a body and so on" are divided by the page break.)

### Printed p. 421

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५ व. १९.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 421 (*[a. 2. a. 5 va. 19.] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 421*).*

*(The printed words for "therefore" and "oblation" in this passage are misspelt in the print and are left as printed.)*

त्वां जिह्वां शुचयश्च क्रिरे कवे (*tvāṃ jihvāṃ śucayaśca krire kave*): as said before, the resplendent gods have made you, Agni, their tongue. That is, the gods eat the oblations and the like only through your mouth (through offering in you), and they taste with your tongue (flame). Such is the purport.

त्वां रातिषाचः अध्वरेषु सश्चिरे (*tvāṃ rātiṣācaḥ adhvareṣu saścire*): at the sacrifices all the gods assemble, look to you alone and rely on you in order to obtain their oblation. The gods partake of the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer in you.

त्वे देवाः हवि: आदंति आहुतं (*tve devāḥ havi: ādaṃti āhutaṃ*): the gods eat the oblation that is offered in you (in Agni). Although the matters stated in the four pādas of this ṛk are described by different words, the meaning is all one: the gods eat, through Agni, only the oblations and the like offered in Agni.

> हे अग्ने त्वे त्वयि विश्वे सर्वॆऽमृतासोऽमरणधर्माणोऽद्रुहोऽद्रो-

> स्थानात् । वसुः सर्वेषां निवासभूतः सन् जज्जिषे । उत्पादयसि सस्याद्यन्नं ॥

*Gist:* Immortal, benevolent gods eat the offering through Agni's mouth; mortals taste the juicy food through him; he is the embryo of plants, producing food.

*(The bhāṣya ends with a grammatical remark on the form of the third-case singular of the word for "mouth" and on the accent of the case ending; it is transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वे—निन्नल्लि (*tve—ninnalli*) (in you). विश्वे—समस्तवाद (*viśve—samastavāda*) (all). अमृतासः—मरणधर्म रहितरादवरू (*amṛtāsaḥ—maraṇadharma rahitarādavarū*) (the immortals, free from the nature of death). अद्रुहः—लोकक्कॆ हितवन्नॆसगुववरू आद (*adruhaḥ—lokakkè hitavannèsaguvavarū āda*) (the benefactors of the world). देवाः—देवतॆगळु (*devāḥ—devatègaḷu*) (the gods). आसा—निन्न मुखदिंद (*āsā—ninna mukhadiṃda*) (through your mouth). आहुतं—यज्ञदल्लि अर्पिसिद (*āhutaṃ—yajñadalli arpisida*) (offered in the sacrifice). हविः—हविस्सन्नु (*haviḥ—havissannu*) (the oblation). अदंति—भक्षिसुत्तारॆ (*adaṃti—bhakṣisuttārè*) (they eat). मर्ताः—मानवरु (*martāḥ—mānavaru*) (mortals, human beings). त्वया—निन्न सहायदिंदले (*tvayā—ninna sahāyadiṃdale*) (by your help). आसुतिं—रसरूपवाद अन्नादिगळन्नु (*āsutiṃ—rasarūpavāda annādigaḷannu*) (the food and the like in the form of juice). स्वदंतॆ—तिन्नुत्तारॆ (*svadaṃtè—tinnuttārè*) (they taste (printed "svadante")). शुचिः—कांतियुतनाद (*śuciḥ—kāṃtiyutanāda*) (of radiant lustre). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). वीरुधां—लतादिगळ (*vīrudhāṃ—latādigaḷa*) (of the plants and creepers). गर्भः—गर्भरूपदल्लि अवुगळ नडुवॆ इद्दु (*garbhaḥ—garbharūpadalli avugaḷa naḍuvè iddu*) (as the embryo, being in their midst). जज्जिषे—सस्याद्यन्नवन्नु उत्पादनॆमाडुत्तीयॆ. (*jajjiṣe—sasyādyannavannu utpādanèmāḍuttīyè.*) (you produce the food of plants and the like (the word printed is the verb "you are born", with the Saṃhitā and Pada form corrected to the image, as noted)).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the gods, who are free from death and do good to the world, eat through your mouth the oblation offered in the sacrifice. Human beings too eat food and the like in the form of juice only with your help. You, the radiant one, being in the form of the embryo among the plants and creepers, produce the food of plants and the like.

**Printed English translation**

All the benignant immortal gods eat the offered oblation through you, as their mouth ; mortals taste the flavour (of all viands) through you : you are born pure, the embryo of plants.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 14)**

What was stated in the previous ṛk, namely that the gods eat the oblations through your, Agni's, mouth, is stated here too.

अमृतासः— अमरधर्माणः । (*amṛtāsaḥ— amaradharmāṇaḥ |*) Those who are without death; it is a tradition that the gods have no death. In the Ṛgveda the gods are called by the word *amṛta* and human beings by the word *marta* मर्त अथवा (*marta athavā*)

### Printed p. 423

...or मर्त्य (*martya*) (*martya*). Therefore the word *amṛta* in the first half of this ṛk is an adjective of the word *devāḥ* (gods). In the second half the word *martāsaḥ* denotes human beings.

अद्रुहः— अद्रोद्धारः । (*adruhaḥ— adroddhāraḥ |*) (as printed) Since the gods plan harm to no one, they are praised with the adjective *adruhaḥ*.

आसुतिं—रसरूपमन्नादिकं । (*āsutiṃ—rasarūpamannādikaṃ |*) Food, soma and the like, edible or drinkable foodstuffs.

त्वं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्जिषे शुचिः (*tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajjiṣe śuciḥ*): O Agni, you are pure; you are born as the embryo of the herbs. On the word *vīrudh* Yāska has given this etymology: वीरुध ओषधयो भवंति विरोहणात् । वीरुधः पारयिष्ण्वः इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*vīrudha oṣadhayo bhavaṃti virohaṇāt | vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇvaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (the *vīrudhs* are herbs because of growing up; and there is also a Vedic passage, "the *vīrudhs* are those that carry across") (नि ६-३ (*ni 6-3*)). Because these grow on the earth, creepers and the like are called *oṣadhis*; plants and the like may also be called *oṣadhis*. The purport is that Agni, being in the womb of the herbs (or plants), helps their growth and the production of food and the like; or, if the word *vīrudh* is taken to mean "tree", it can be said that Agni arises in the fire-sticks (*araṇi*) that belong to trees.

### Printed p. 424

*Running head (as supplied): [424 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ. १. सू. १] (*[424 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 1]*).*

*[As supplied, the label line of the bhāṣya reads कायणभाष्यं (*kāyaṇabhāṣyaṃ*), inside the quoted block; standard label inserted. A few misprints of the bhāṣya are kept as printed.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वं मज्मना बलेन तान् प्रसिद्धान्देवान् सं चासि । संगच्छसि । तैः
> सहितोऽपि भवसि । तथा सामर्थ्येन प्रति चासि ! प्रत्येकं तैर्विभिन्नः प्रतिनिधिर्वा भवसि ।
> प्रतिस्वीकारसमये तैः सहितो भवसि वियुक्तश्च भवसीत्यर्थः । हे सुजात शोभन-
> जनन । शोभनमंत्रसहितमथनेनोत्पन्नत्वादग्ने: सुजन्मत्वं । तादृशाग्ने हे देव
> परिच्यसे च। तैर्बलेन चाधिको भवसि। आधिक्ये कारणमाह । यत् यस्मादत्रास्मिन्यज्ञे
> पृक्षः सर्वमप्यन्नं ॥ व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं॥ ते तवैव विभुवत् । समर्थं भवति
> महिला माहात्म्येन । यतो महत्त्वमस्ति अत इत्यर्थः । कुत्रॆति तदुच्यते ।
> रोदसी सर्वनिरोदनस्वभावे उभे द्यावापृथिव्यावनु । ते प्रति । तयोर्मध्यॆ
> व्याप्तमित्यर्थः । त्वयि हुतमन्नं त्वन्महत्तेन लोकत्रये व्याप्तमित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* By his strength Agni joins the gods and remains distinct from them, and excels them, since the offered food pervades both worlds by his greatness.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). मज्मना—शक्तियिंद (*majmanā—śaktiyiṃda*) (by strength). तान्—प्रसिद्धराद देवतॆ गळॊडनॆ (*tān—prasiddharāda devatè gaḷòḍanè*) (with the famous gods (the word for "gods" is divided by a line break)). संचासि—सेरिकॊंडिद्दीयॆ (*saṃcāsi—serikòṃḍiddīyè*) (you have joined). प्रतिचासि—विविक्तनागियू इद्दीयॆ (*praticāsi—viviktanāgiyū iddīyè*) (you are also separate (the two entries are divided in the print by an exclamation mark in place of a danda)). यत्—याव निन्न (*yat—yāva ninna*) (by whose). महिना—माहात्म्यदिंद (*mahinā—māhātmyadiṃda*) (greatness). अत्र—ई यज्ञदल्लि (अर्पितवाद) (*atra—ī yajñadalli (arpitavāda)*) (here, in this sacrifice (offered)). पृक्षः—समस्तवाद अन्नवू (*pṛkṣaḥ—samastavāda annavū*) (all the food). ते—निन्न (*te—ninna*) (your). वि भुवत्—अधीनदल्लिये इद्दु (अनंतर) (*vi bhuvat—adhīnadalliye iddu (anaṃtara)*) (being under your control (afterwards)). रोदसी उभे—द्यावा पृथिविगळॆरडु लोकगळन्नू (*rodasī ubhe—dyāvā pṛthivigaḷèraḍu lokagaḷannū*) (both heaven and earth, the two worlds). अनु—व्यापिसुत्तदॆयो (आद्दरिंद) (*anu—vyāpisuttadèyo (āddariṃda)*) (it pervades). सुजात—श्रेष्ठवाद जन्म वुळ्ळवनू (*sujāta—śreṣṭhavāda janma vuḷḷavanū*) (O one of excellent birth). देव—देवतात्मनू आद ऎलै अग्निये (*deva—devatātmanū āda èlai agniye*) (and of divine self, O Agni). परिच्यसे च—नीनु सामर्थ्यदल्लि देवतॆ गळॆल्लरन्नू मीरिये इद्दीयॆ. (*paricyase ca—nīnu sāmarthyadalli devatè gaḷèllarannū mīriye iddīyè.*) (you surpass all the gods in ability).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, of excellent birth and divine self, you have joined the gods by your strength, and you are also separate. By your greatness all the food offered in this sacrifice, being first under your control, afterwards pervades heaven and earth and is distributed to the other gods; therefore you surpass all the other gods in ability.

*[As supplied, the label line of the printed English reads English Translatin (*English Translatin*); standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

You are associated, Agni, by your vigour, with those (goods) [sic] ; divine, well-born Agni, you exceed (them in strength), for the (sacrificial) food that is here prepared is, by your power, subsequently diffused through both regions, heaven and earth.

*(The printed "goods" is evidently a misprint for "gods".)*

### Printed p. 425

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५ व. १९ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 425 (*[a. 2. a. 5 va. 19 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 425*).*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 15)**

त्वं तान् सं च प्रति च असि मज्मना (*tvaṃ tān saṃ ca prati ca asi majmanā*): the word *majmanā* is read among the names of strength. O Agni, in strength you are equal to the gods; or you are in company with the gods. That is, at the time of accepting the oblation you are with the gods. Since the gods eat the oblations offered in you, at the time of offering the oblation you and the gods are together; at other times you remain separate. Such is the purport. (The printed word for "oblations" is misspelt in the print and is left as printed.)

अग्ने सुजात प्र च देव रिच्यसे (*agne sujāta pra ca deva ricyase*): *sujāta* means that since Agni arises at the time of friction (kindling) with the recitation of good mantras, Agni is called *sujāta*, "well-born". Such, O Agni, you surpass the gods in strength (the printed word is "māris-" for "mīris-", left as printed); that is the purport. How is that? —

पृक्षः यदत्र रोदसी उभे (*pṛkṣaḥ yadatra rodasī ubhe*): the food in the form of oblation that is offered in you in this sacrifice pervades, by your greatness, the whole intermediate region between heaven and earth; that is, it goes and reaches all the gods in the earth, the atmosphere and heaven.

*Gist:* Agni is asked to lead the sacrificers, who give cows and horses to praisers, and us to the best place; we shall recite mantras.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). ये—यारु (*ye—yāru*) (those who). सूरयः—सद्बुद्धियिंद प्रेरितरागिद्दारॆयो अंतह यजमानरु (*sūrayaḥ—sadbuddhiyiṃda preritarāgiddārèyo aṃtaha yajamānaru*) (the wise sacrificers, inspired by good intellect). स्तोतृभ्यः—स्तुतिकर्तरिगॆ (*stotṛbhyaḥ—stutikartarigè*) (to the praisers). गोअग्रां—गोवुगळे मुख्यवागिरुवुदू (*goagrāṃ—govugaḷe mukhyavāgiruvudū*) (a gift in which cows are principal). अश्वपेशसं.—अश्वदिंद निरूपिसल्पडुवुदू आद (*aśvapeśasaṃ.—aśvadiṃda nirūpisalpaḍuvudū āda*) (characterised by horses (printed with a full stop before the dash)). रातिं—दानवन्नु (*rātiṃ—dānavannu*) (the gift). उपसृजंति—कॊडुत्तारॆ (*upasṛjaṃti—kòḍuttārè*) (they give). तांश्च—यजमानरन्नू (*tāṃśca—yajamānarannū*) (the sacrificers). आस्मांश्च—ऋत्विक्कुगळाद नम्मन्नू (*āsmāṃśca—ṛtvikkugaḷāda nammannū*) (and us, the priests (printed with a long first vowel)). वस्यः—उत्तमवाद स्वर्गादि स्थानक्कॆ (*vasyaḥ—uttamavāda svargādi sthānakkè*) (to the best place, heaven and the like). आ प्र हि नेषि—=तिशयवाद रीतियल्लि करॆदुकॊंडु होगु (*ā pra hi neṣi—=tiśayavāda rītiyalli karèdukòṃḍu hogu*) (lead us in an excessive manner (the first letter of the word for "excessive" is printed as an equals sign, which is marked with a query in the Kannada text)) [?]. सुवीराः—श्रेष्ठवाद पुत्रादिगळिंद कूडिद नावु (*suvīrāḥ—śreṣṭhavāda putrādigaḷiṃda kūḍida nāvu*) (we, accompanied by excellent sons and the like). विदथे यज्ञदल्लि (*vidathe yajñadalli*) (in the sacrifice (printed without a dash)). बृहत्—महत्तूरितवाद मंत्रवन्नु (*bṛhat—mahattūritavāda maṃtravannu*) (the great, greatness-filled (mantra)). वदेम—पठिसुवॆवु (*vadema—paṭhisuvèvu*) (we shall recite).

*(The doubt in the Pratipadārtha is one printed sign, an equals sign in place of the first letter of the word for "excessive", marked with a query in the Kannada text; the entry is kept as supplied.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the sacrificers, inspired by good intellect, give to the praisers a gift consisting of cows and horses. Lead those sacrificers, and us, the priests, in an excellent manner to the best place, heaven and the like. We, accompanied by excellent sons and the like, will recite a great mantra at the sacrifice.

**Printed English translation**

The pious are they who present, as a gift, to the reciters of your praises, an excellent cow and an excellent horse; do you, Agni, lead both us and them to the best of abodes, (or heaven) ,that we and our worthy descendants may repeat the solemn prayer to you at the sacrifice.

*(The printed English divides "descendants" by a line break and a hyphen, joined here; the printed space before the comma after "(or heaven)" is as supplied.)*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 16)**

In this ṛk, the last of this sūkta, the sage prays to Agni for the fulfilment of his wishes and concludes.

### Printed p. 427

*Running head (as supplied): [आ. २. अ. ५. व. २०] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 427 (*[ā. 2. a. 5. va. 20] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 427*).*

स्तोतृभ्यः गो अग्रामश्वपेशसं रातिं उपसृजंति सूरयः (*stotṛbhyaḥ go agrāmaśvapeśasaṃ rātiṃ upasṛjaṃti sūrayaḥ*): the priests who praise Agni. It is the custom that at the end of the sacrifice the sacrificer gives them, as a fee, cows, horses, goats and the like. Likewise here too the wise sacrificers are said to give cows and the like as a fee to the priests such as the hotṛ, and Agni is prayed to lead such sacrificers and us, the priests, to the best (heavenly and so on) place. Here the meanings of the words are: गोअग्रां (*goagrāṃ*), one in which cows are principal; अश्वपेशसं (*aśvapeśasaṃ*), with the forms of horses, that is, accompanied by horses; रातिं (*rātiṃ*), a gift or a fee.

बृहत् वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhat vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*): we, together with heroic sons, friends, servants and so on, will recite a great, or greatness-filled, hymn in this sacrifice: thus Agni is prayed to. This fourth pāda of this ṛk, बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*), is repeated again and again as the last pāda of the last ṛk of many sūktas seen by this sage Gṛtsamada.

#### Sūkta 2 (Maṇḍala 2)

ऎरडनॆय सूक्तवु. (*èraḍanèya sūktavu.*) ("the second sūkta").

*[As supplied, the label line of the bhāṣya reads । साराणभाष्यं (*| sārāṇabhāṣyaṃ*); standard label inserted. The introduction is printed as plain lines in the supplied text and is given as a quoted block.]*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> यज्ञेन वर्धतेति त्रयोदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं मंडलद्रष्टुर्ग्तृत्समद-
> स्यार्षं । मंडलादिष्टाग्नियमिति परिभाषयाग्नॆयं । तुशब्दानुकर्षादिदमपि
> जागतं । यज्ञेन सप्तोनेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्जागते छंदस्यस्य
> विनियोगः । सूत्रं तु पूर्वसूक्त एवोक्तं ॥ तथा चातुर्विंशिके तृतीयसवने
> जातवेदस्यनिविद्वानीयमिदं । यज्ञेन वर्धतेत्याग्निमारुतं । आ. ७-४ । इति सूत्रित-
> त्वात् ॥ पृष्ट्याभिप्लवषडहयोर्द्वितीयेऽहन्यपि जातवेदस्यनिविद्वानमिदं । चातु-
> र्विंशिकं तृतीयसवनमिति चतुर्विंशादतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

*Gist:* The second sūkta has thirteen ṛks, seer Gṛtsamada, deity Agni, Jagatī metre; its ritual uses are listed (morning litany, Āśvina śastra, twenty-four-day rite).

**Anuvāda (Kannada)** of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 2 of Maṇḍala 2. This sūkta beginning यज्ञेन वर्धत (*yajñena vardhata*) is the second sūkta in the first anuvāka. It contains thirteen ṛks. Gṛtsamada, the seer of the maṇḍala, is also the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is Jagatī; in the Anukramaṇikā it is said: यज्ञेन सप्त (*yajñena sapta*) and so on. This sūkta is used for the ṛks of Jagatī metre at the time of reciting the morning anuvāka mantras and at the time of reciting the Āśvina śastra mantras. The sūtra sentence has been stated before. And in the sacrifice performed for twenty-four days, at the third pressing, this sūkta is used for the nivid mantras recited on behalf of the deity named Jātavedas, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana

*Gist:* Agni is kindled, has good food, leads sacrificers to heaven, shines in heaven, is the hotṛ and the giver of bodily strength.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

समिधानं—प्रज्वलितनादवनू (*samidhānaṃ—prajvalitanādavanū*) (well-kindled). सुप्रयसं—श्रेष्ठवाद अन्नवन्नु हॊंदिदवनू (*suprayasaṃ—śreṣṭhavāda annavannu hòṃdidavanū*) (one with excellent food). स्वर्णरं—(यजमानरन्नु) स्वर्गक्कॆ ऒय्युववनू (*svarṇaraṃ—(yajamānarannu) svargakkè òyyuvavanū*) (one who leads the sacrificers to heaven). द्युक्षं—प्रकाशमाननू अथवा द्युलोक वासियू (*dyukṣaṃ—prakāśamānanū athavā dyuloka vāsiyū*) (radiant, or dwelling in the heaven-world). होतारं—होमसंपादकनू (*hotāraṃ—homasaṃpādakanū*) (the accomplisher of homa). वृजनेषु धूर्षदं—शरीरद शक्तियन्नु वृद्धि माडुववनू (*vṛjaneṣu dhūrṣadaṃ—śarīrada śaktiyannu vṛddhi māḍuvavanū*) (the increaser of bodily strength). जातवेदसं—जातप्रज्ञनू आद (*jātavedasaṃ—jātaprajñanū āda*) (all-knowing). अग्निं—अग्नियन्नु (*agniṃ—agniyannu*) (Agni). यज्ञेन—यागदिंद (*yajñena—yāgadiṃda*) (by the sacrifice). वर्धत—प्रवृद्धनागुवंतॆ माडिरि (*vardhata—pravṛddhanāguvaṃtè māḍiri*) (make him grow (printed "ವರ್ಧತ")). हविषा--हविस्सिनिंदलू (*haviṣā--havissiniṃdalū*) (with the oblation (printed with a double hyphen)). तना—विस्तृतवाद (*tanā—vistṛtavāda*) (extended). गिरा— स्तुतियिंदलू सह (*girā— stutiyiṃdalū saha*) (with praise also). यजध्वं—पूजिसिरि. (*yajadhvaṃ—pūjisiri.*) (worship).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Make Agni, who is well kindled, who has excellent food, who leads the sacrificers to heaven, who is radiant, the accomplisher of homa, the increaser of bodily strength and all-knowing, grow by the sacrifice. Worship him with oblations and with extended praise.

**Printed English translation**

Exalt with sacrifice, Agni, who knows all that has been born ; worship him with oblations, and with ample praise ; him who is well kindled, well fed, much lauded, resplendent, the conveyer of oblations; the giver gf [sic] strength (to the body).

*(The printed "gf" is a misprint for "of" [sic].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

यज्ञेन—यागेन । (*yajñena—yāgena |*) Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning thus: *yajña* is the rite of offering the substance in the form of oblation into Agni with a deity in view, and the sacrificers who satisfy Agni by performing this rite make Agni grow.

Yāska has read the word *yajña* among the fifteen names of sacrifice beginning with यज्ञः वेनः ऎंबिवे (*yajñaḥ venaḥ èṃbive*) (as printed) (नि. ३-१९ (*ni. 3-19*)) and has explained it: यज्ञः कस्मात् प्रख्यातं कर्मेति नैरुक्ताः । या इच्छो भवतीति वा, यजुरुन्नतो भवतीति वा, बहुकृष्णाजिन इत्यौपमन्यवो, यजूंष्येनं नयंतीति वा । (*yajñaḥ kasmāt prakhyātaṃ karmeti nairuktāḥ | yā iccho bhavatīti vā, yajurunnato bhavatīti vā, bahukṛṣṇājina ityaupamanyavo, yajūṃṣyenaṃ nayaṃtīti vā |*) (rendered after the Kannada explanation that follows: "Why is it *yajña*? A famous rite, say the Nairuktas; or ... (the printed second clause is as supplied); or because the *yajus* verses lead it"; the words as printed are kept). In the world and in the Veda it is well known as the rite of worshipping deities such as Agni by the offering of oblations. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 430

*Running head (as supplied): [430 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू. २ (*[430 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 2*).*

And it is said: याचनात् यज्ञः, यजुरुन्नो यज्ञः, बहुकृष्णाजिनो यज्ञः । (*yācanāt yajñaḥ, yajurunno yajñaḥ, bahukṛṣṇājino yajñaḥ |*) That is, it is *yajña* because of begging; because the rite is performed, for the most part from beginning to end, by the Yajurveda, it is *yajña*; and because the black-antelope skin is used much in the respective rites, it is *yajña*. Thus Upamanyu is said to have explained the meaning of the word *yajña* in three ways.

जातवेदसं—जातानां वेदितारं जातधनं जातप्रज्ञं वा । (*jātavedasaṃ—jātānāṃ veditāraṃ jātadhanaṃ jātaprajñaṃ vā |*) Sāyaṇa explains the meaning of this word in three ways: one who knows all that has been born; one who produces substance (wealth); one who produces and increases knowledge and intelligence.

The Nirukta-writer (Yāska) says: जातवेदाः कस्मात्, जातानि वेद, जातानि नैनं विदुः, जाते जाते विद्यत इति वा, जातवित्तो जातधनः, जातविद्यो जातप्रज्ञानः । (*jātavedāḥ kasmāt, jātāni veda, jātāni nainaṃ viduḥ, jāte jāte vidyata iti vā, jātavitto jātadhanaḥ, jātavidyo jātaprajñānaḥ |*) In this world, because everything that is born is known to him, he is omniscient; because all born beings know him, he is called *jātavedas*; because there is no place among the born where he is not, he is one who is in all that is born; he is one who produces wealth; and he is one of naturally unsurpassed knowledge: four kinds of meaning are explained. Durgācārya has explained that the word जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) is formed from the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*) (to come into being) and from the root *vid*, and has cited this sentence of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa: यत्तज्जातः पशूनविंदत तज्जातवेदसो जातवेदस्यं (*yattajjātaḥ paśūnaviṃdata tajjātavedaso jātavedasyaṃ*) (because, having been born, he found the cattle, that is the *jātavedas*-ness of Jātavedas).

अग्निं— (*agniṃ—*) In explaining the meaning of the word *agni* Yāska says: अग्निः कस्मात्, अग्रणीर्भवति, अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयते, अंगं नयति सन्नममानः । अकोपनो भवतीति स्थौलाष्ठीविः । त्रिभ्य आख्यातेभ्यो जायत इति शाकपूणिः । (*agniḥ kasmāt, agraṇīrbhavati, agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate, aṃgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ | akopano bhavatīti sthaulāṣṭhīviḥ | tribhya ākhyātebhyo jāyata iti śākapūṇiḥ |*) (७-१४ (*7-14*)). That is, he explains the word as: the one who is in front in the performance of Vedic and Smārta rites; the commander of the gods; the one who is born first in the sacrifices; the one who, in worldly and Vedic rites, makes the wood and the like on which he rests subject to himself; and he has set out the views of Sthaulāṣṭhīvi and Śākapūṇi.

सुप्रयसम्—शोभनान्नं । (*suprayasam—śobhanānnaṃ |*) Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as one who has food in the form of excellent oblation. Yāska has read the word प्रयस् (*prayas*) among the twenty-eight names of food (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*)).

स्वर्णरं - स्वर्गे नेतव्या यजमाना यस्य तादृशम् । यद्वा स्वरिति सर्वपर्यायः स्तुतीनां नेतारः स्तोतारः बहुस्तोतारं । (*svarṇaraṃ - svarge netavyā yajamānā yasya tādṛśam | yadvā svariti sarvaparyāyaḥ stutīnāṃ netāraḥ stotāraḥ bahustotāraṃ |*) One who is able to make the sacrificers attain heaven (the sentence continues on the next page, the phrase being divided by the page break).

### Printed p. 431

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २ अ. ५ व. १८] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 431 (*[a. 2 a. 5 va. 18] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 431*).*

...or one who is worthy of many kinds of praise; thus the power of Agni is described in two senses of this word. And the meaning that many people praise Agni is also explained. (A line-end hyphen inside the quoted Sanskrit above is joined.)

द्युक्षं—दीप्तं द्युनिवासिनं वा । (*dyukṣaṃ—dīptaṃ dyunivāsinaṃ vā |*) Taking it to mean that Agni is radiant, or dwells in the middle region, and explaining the meaning that without the grace of this Agni living beings would have no bodily strength under the words वृजिनेषु धूर्षदं (*vṛjineṣu dhūrṣadaṃ*) (as printed), Sāyaṇa has also described the experience of the world: अग्निपाटवे सति शारीरं बलं भवतीति प्रसिद्धं (*agnipāṭave sati śārīraṃ balaṃ bhavatīti prasiddhaṃ*) (as printed) (it is well known that when fire is sound, bodily strength exists).

In this ṛk the sage, the seer of the mantra, describes the many kinds of greatness of Agni, addresses the sacrificers and the priests, and instructs them: worship Agni, who is full of such greatness, with oblations and with cakes and cooked rice, and praise him with various kinds of praise.
